items.explanation: Succinate dehydrogenase oxidizes succinate to fumarate (trans-butenedioate) and is the only citric-acid-cycle enzyme that is also Complex II of the electron-transport chain, an inner membrane protein. Its bound FAD is reduced to FADH2, and electrons pass to iron–sulfur centers and then to ubiquinone, forming ubiquinol. Malate dehydrogenase and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase are soluble-matrix NAD+-dependent enzymes (α-KGDH uses NAD+, not NADP+ as the primary acceptor). Fumarase hydrates fumarate to malate and is not a dehydrogenase and not an ETC complex. The dual TCA/ETC identity uniquely identifies SDH.

distractorRationales.A: Malate dehydrogenase is a matrix enzyme that reduces NAD+ to NADH and is not an inner-membrane ETC complex. It also oxidizes a four-carbon hydroxy acid to oxaloacetate, not to a trans-alkene.
distractorRationales.C: α-Ketoglutarate dehydrogenase oxidizes a five-carbon α-keto acid to succinyl-CoA using NAD+, not NADPH, and it is not Complex II.
distractorRationales.D: Fumarase adds water across fumarate’s double bond; it does not reduce NAD+ and is not an electron-transport complex.

items.stem: Which opening uses a reflective first-person without collapsing into solipsism?

choices.text: I am unique and no one else has ever had to choose between speaking and staying.
I kept my mouth closed at that table so the rent would still be paid, and I am still not sure whether that silence was love, cowardice, or both—a question many people inherit with a house.
I hate everyone in my family and this essay will list them.
One must not use “I,” because reflection is only valid in the third person.

items.explanation: Reflective voice is first-person that thinks, not a claim of cosmic uniqueness and not a prosecution file. B names a particular table and rent, admits mixed motives, and then opens the question outward—many people inherit that silence—without pretending the writer is a universal spokesman. A is solipsism. C is a vent. D invents a ban on “I” that would make Task B impossible. The craft is to let the self be a specimen, not a monument. Under time, one honest uncertainty does more than a manifesto of uniqueness.

distractorRationales.A: “No one else has ever” seals the essay against the reader; that is solipsism, not reflection.
distractorRationales.C: A hate-list is expressive, but it does not turn toward a question the reader can share.
distractorRationales.D: Task B expects a personal voice; a third-person-only rule is not ACER’s.

items.stem:
Normal boiling points of four hydrides:

Compound | Mr | bp (°C)
CH4 | 16 | −162
NH3 | 17 | −33
HF | 20 | 20
H2O | 18 | 100

Dispersion forces increase with Mr in the absence of hydrogen bonding. Which explanation of the table is best?

choices.text: CH4, with no N/O/F–H bonding, boils far lower than the three hydrogen-bonded hydrides of similar mass; H2O boils highest because each molecule can form up to four hydrogen bonds in a network
Boiling point simply tracks Mr, so HF must boil below CH4
NH3 has the highest bp because nitrogen is less electronegative than oxygen
All four compounds are hydrogen-bonded equally, so the 262 °C spread is random

items.explanation: Mr values lie in a narrow 16–20 window, so dispersion alone cannot explain a 262 °C spread. CH4 cannot hydrogen-bond and boils at −162 °C. NH3, HF and H2O all hydrogen-bond and boil much higher. Water’s tetrahedral two-donor plus two-acceptor capacity builds a three-dimensional network, placing its bp well above HF (which has a donor/acceptor mismatch) and NH3. Tracking Mr would rank HF highest and CH4 lowest by only a few degrees, not 182 °C. NH3 is not the highest, and the four species are not equivalent in hydrogen-bond inventory.

distractorRationales.B: HF (Mr 20) boils 182 °C above CH4 (Mr 16); mass does not dominate.
distractorRationales.C: NH3 boils at −33 °C, below both HF and H2O.
distractorRationales.D: CH4 cannot form conventional hydrogen bonds; the spread is systematic, not random.

items.stem: The nucleophilic serine of a serine protease is mutated to alanine. Steady-state kinetics show that kcat falls by about six orders of magnitude while Km for a peptide substrate is nearly unchanged. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

choices.text: The serine hydroxyl is required for covalent catalysis but contributes little to ground-state substrate binding
The mutation destroys the S1 specificity pocket, so substrate can no longer bind
Serine was a diffusible cofactor rather than a residue in the polypeptide, and dialysis had already removed it
Km is numerically equal to kcat for hydrolases, so both parameters must fall together; the data are impossible

items.explanation: In the catalytic triad the serine hydroxyl attacks the scissile carbonyl, forming a tetrahedral intermediate and then an acyl-enzyme. Replacing that oxygen with alanine’s methyl group removes the nucleophile and collapses kcat. Km, which for many proteases is dominated by substrate binding to the specificity pockets, can remain similar if those pockets are intact—exactly the pattern reported. A destroyed binding pocket would raise Km substantially. Serine is an amino-acid residue, not a cofactor, and Km is not equal to kcat; they are independent kinetic parameters.

distractorRationales.B: An unchanged Km argues that ground-state binding is largely intact; the defect is chemical step(s), not docking.
distractorRationales.C: The nucleophilic serine is part of the protein sequence; it is not a small-molecule cofactor that dialyzes away.
distractorRationales.D: Km and kcat are independent. A selective kcat drop is the expected signature of a catalytic-residue mutation.

items.stem: Patient S.M. has bilateral amygdala calcification. In delay fear conditioning she shows little potentiation of startle to a colored light that predicts a blast of noise, yet she can later describe the light–noise pairing. A comparison patient with hippocampal damage shows the reverse: intact startle potentiation but no declarative memory of the pairing. Which mapping is best?

choices.text: The amygdala is required for implicit fear learning; the hippocampus is required for declarative memory of the episode
The amygdala stores the explicit narrative; the hippocampus stores the conditioned fear reflex
Either lesion abolishes all emotion, so the double dissociation must be a measurement artifact
An amygdala lesion should spare fear conditioning and impair only language, which is not what was found

items.explanation: The limbic amygdala is central to assigning affective value and supporting Pavlovian fear conditioning, which is expressed as startle potentiation or similar implicit measures. The hippocampus supports forming a declarative record of what happened. A double dissociation of the kind described is the standard mapping in affective neuroscience and in MCAT-level limbic-system teaching: amygdala damage hits the fear response while leaving the story intact, and hippocampal damage hits the story while leaving the conditioned response intact. Swapping those roles, or claiming that any limbic lesion wipes out all emotion and language, contradicts the split.

distractorRationales.B: This swaps the functions: narratives are hippocampal, not amygdalar, in this design; the reflex-like fear response tracks the amygdala.
distractorRationales.C: The point of the dissociation is that emotion-related learning and declarative memory can come apart; it is not evidence that both systems failed.
distractorRationales.D: Amygdala damage is predicted to impair fear conditioning, which is exactly the deficit described for S.M.

items.stem: A thin converging lens has focal length 10 cm. An object stands 20 cm to the left of the lens. The image is:

choices.text: real, inverted, and the same size as the object, 20 cm to the right of the lens
virtual, upright, and enlarged, 20 cm to the left of the lens
real, inverted, and half the size of the object, 10 cm to the right of the lens
real, upright, and the same size as the object, 20 cm to the right of the lens

items.explanation: The thin-lens equation is 1/f = 1/o + 1/i. With f = +10 cm (converging) and o = +20 cm, 1/10 = 1/20 + 1/i, so 1/i = 1/20 and i = +20 cm: a real image on the opposite side of the lens. Magnification m = −i/o = −20/20 = −1, so the image is inverted and the same size as the object. This is the classic object-at-2f geometry, which places the image at 2f. A single converging lens does not produce a real upright image; upright images from this lens are virtual and occur only for o < f.

distractorRationales.B: A virtual upright enlarged image is the o < f (magnifying-glass) case. Here the object is at 2f, outside the focal point, so the image is real and inverted.
distractorRationales.C: An image at f with |m| = 1/2 would require a different object distance (o = 2f is same-size, not half-size). Solving 1/f = 1/o + 1/i with these numbers gives i = 20 cm, not 10 cm.
distractorRationales.D: The location and size are right, but a real image formed by a single converging lens is inverted. Upright and real together would require a second lens or a more elaborate optical system.

items.stem:
A stone is dropped from rest. Taking g = 10 m s−2 downward as positive, the velocity–time graph is a straight line from (t, v) = (0, 0) to (4.0 s, 40 m s−1).

t (s) | v (m s−1)
0 | 0
2.0 | 20
4.0 | 40

Displacement from rest is the triangular area under this v–t graph, equivalently s = (1/2) g t^2. How far has the stone fallen in 4.0 s?
items.explanation: The area of the triangle is (1/2) × 4.0 s × 40 m s−1 = 80 m. The same result is s = (1/2)×10×(4.0)^2 = 80 m. Multiplying the final speed by the elapsed time (40 × 4.0 = 160 m) would be correct only if the stone had travelled at 40 m s−1 for the whole interval; instead the average speed from rest is half of the final speed, 20 m s−1, and 20 × 4.0 = 80 m. 40 m is the numerical value of the final speed with units of metres attached. 200 m would correspond to using g = 25 m s−2 or a 5 s drop at this g. The graph’s linearity already encodes constant acceleration from rest.

distractorRationales.A: 40 m matches the final speed numerically but is not an area. Distance requires integrating v, not reading the last v value as a length.
distractorRationales.C: 160 m is v_final × t, which uses the highest speed as if it applied for all 4 s. The average velocity from rest is 20 m s−1.
distractorRationales.D: 200 m does not match either the triangular area or (1/2)gt^2 with the given g and t.

items.stem: Triiodothyronine (T3) acts on a hepatocyte. Its principal genomic mechanism is to:

choices.text: open a plasma-membrane Na+ channel as its sole action
bind a nuclear receptor and alter transcription of target genes
raise cAMP via a Gs-coupled receptor as the main genomic path
be packaged as a stored peptide in secretory granules inside the target hepatocyte

items.explanation: Thyroid hormones are amino-acid-derived yet act like steroids: they enter cells and bind nuclear receptors (THR) that regulate transcription, matching delayed genomic effects on metabolic enzymes. They are not primarily Gs-cAMP peptides, they are not stored in the target cell's granules as a peptide hormone would be, and opening a Na+ channel is not their defining genomic mechanism (even if some nongenomic effects exist, they do not replace nuclear receptor action as the principal genomic path).

distractorRationales.A: A membrane ion channel is not the textbook genomic mechanism of T3 in hepatocytes.
distractorRationales.C: Gs-cAMP is the peptide/catecholamine pattern. Thyroid hormone receptors are nuclear transcription factors.
distractorRationales.D: The hepatocyte is the target, not a thyroid follicle storing thyroglobulin. T3 is not re-packaged there as a peptide granule hormone.

items.stem: Using t = 0 and t = 20 min, the half-life is

choices.text: 5 min, because 800→200 is two halvings in 20 min.
20 min.
10 min, because 800→400 from 0 to 10 min, and 400→200 from 10 to 20 min.
40 min, the last row.

items.explanation: 800 to 400 in 10 min is one half-life; 400 to 200 in the next 10 min confirms. Two halvings in 20 min therefore mean t½ = 10 min, not 5 min. Choice A states two halvings yet assigns 5 min; that arithmetic does not divide 20 by 2. Choice B treats the two-half-life interval as t½. Choice D is only the last clock time. Points that sit on successive powers of two are the clean interpolation.

distractorRationales.A: Two halvings in 20 min means 10 min per half-life, not 5.
distractorRationales.B: 20 min is the interval containing two half-lives, not t½.
distractorRationales.D: The last clock time is not t½; net rate is still 50, not 400.

passage.title: Counting a short-lived sample
passage.body:
A detector records decays from a small source. Background, measured overnight with the source removed, is 12 counts per minute. The table is net rate after subtracting that background (already done by the software). Clock time starts when the sample is placed.

t / min | net counts per minute
0 | 800
5 | 566
10 | 400
15 | 283
20 | 200
25 | 141
40 | 50

The software also reports a 2-minute count at t = 10 min as 800 counts (raw, including background). A student wants the half-life from any two points and also wants activity in Bq.

items.stem: A 2.00 mg mass of a drug is dissolved in 1.00 kg of water. Density of the dilute solution is 1.00 g mL−1. 1 ppm is 1 mg of solute per kg of solution. The same solution is also described in mol L−1; the drug’s molar mass is 200 g mol−1. Which pair is correct?
items.explanation: 2.00 mg in 1.00 kg is exactly 2.00 ppm by the given definition. The solution volume is 1.00 L at the stated density. Moles of drug = 2.00 × 10−3 g / 200 g mol−1 = 1.00 × 10−5 mol, so molarity is 1.00 × 10−5 mol L−1. Using 2.00 g instead of 2.00 mg would give 0.0100 M. Calling 2.00 mg in 1 kg ‘2000 ppm’ treats the solute as 2 g. 0.00200 ppm would be 2.00 µg in 1 kg.

distractorRationales.A: The ppm figure is 2.00, not 0.00200; the molarity half of the option is right but the ppm is not.
distractorRationales.C: 1.00 × 10−2 M would require 2.00 g of drug in 1 L, a thousand-fold mass error.
distractorRationales.D: 2000 ppm would be 2.00 g per kg, not 2.00 mg.

items.stem: Undocumented patients delay ED care until a surgical emergency. Link and Phelan’s fundamental-cause theory of health disparities would emphasize which point?

choices.text: Once germ theory is known, social position cannot affect infectious risk

SES and socially excluded legal status are flexible resources (money, power, knowledge, beneficial social connections, freedom to choose) that keep reproducing unequal health even as specific diseases and mechanisms change
Only genetic ancestry, not exclusion from insurance, can delay presentation
Parsons’s sick role requires undocumented patients to be blamed for symptoms

items.explanation: Link and Phelan argue that socioeconomic status is a fundamental cause of disease: it commands flexible resources that can be used to avoid risks and minimize consequences no matter which mechanisms are currently salient. Legal exclusion and social exclusion restrict those resources, producing delayed care and worse outcomes. Germ theory did not erase class gradients; mechanisms were replaced. Genetics does not exhaust presentation delay when insurance and deportation fear operate. Parsons’s sick role is a functionalist ideal, not a requirement to blame excluded patients.

distractorRationales.A: Fundamental-cause theory exists because gradients survive mechanism change, including after germ theory.
distractorRationales.C: Access barriers are exactly the sort of resource restriction the theory highlights.
distractorRationales.D: The sick role’s “not responsible” clause is not a license to blame undocumented patients.

items.stem: Erythrocytes metabolize glucose to lactate. When inorganic phosphate is replaced by arsenate, glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase still oxidizes its substrate, but 1-arseno-3-phosphoglycerate hydrolyzes spontaneously and 3-phosphoglycerate forms without generating ATP at phosphoglycerate kinase. What happens to the net ATP yield of anaerobic glycolysis per glucose?

choices.text: Net ATP falls to zero because the two ATP from phosphoglycerate kinase are lost while hexokinase and PFK-1 still consume two ATP
Net ATP doubles because pyruvate kinase is stimulated by arsenate
Net ATP becomes two extra from hexokinase, which now runs in reverse
ATP yield is unchanged because substrate-level phosphorylation occurs only at pyruvate kinase

items.explanation: In anaerobic glycolysis, ATP is spent at hexokinase and phosphofructokinase-1 (−2) and recouped at phosphoglycerate kinase (+2, one per triose) and pyruvate kinase (+2), for a net of +2 ATP per glucose. Arsenate allows GAPDH to proceed but bypasses the acyl-phosphate that PGK uses to make ATP, so those two ATP are lost. Pyruvate kinase still makes two ATP from two PEP, exactly canceling the two ATP invested, and net yield is zero. Hexokinase does not reverse under these conditions, and arsenate is not a PK stimulator that would raise yield. PGK is a genuine substrate-level phosphorylation step that the uncoupler removes.

distractorRationales.B: Arsenate uncouples PGK; it does not double PK flux in a way that increases net ATP above normal.
distractorRationales.C: Hexokinase remains an ATP-consuming step; it does not run in reverse to produce ATP in glycolysis.
distractorRationales.D: Phosphoglycerate kinase is also a substrate-level phosphorylation; ignoring it misses the uncoupling.

items.stem:
Solid calcium carbonate decomposes in a closed, evacuated vessel: CaCO3(s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO2(g). At 1073 K the equilibrium constant is Kp = 0.22 bar, and Kp = P_CO2 because the activities of the pure solids are omitted. The vessel is already at equilibrium with P_CO2 = 0.22 bar and both solids present. An extra 12 g of CaCO3(s) is then added, T held at 1073 K.

Measured P_CO2 (bar) | Condition
0.22 | before adding extra CaCO3
? | after re-equilibration

What is P_CO2 after re-equilibration, and why?

choices.text: 0.44 bar, because doubling the carbonate mass doubles the equilibrium pressure of CO2.
0.22 bar, because Kp depends only on P_CO2 at this T, and extra solid CaCO3 does not appear in Kp.
Much less than 0.22 bar, because added CaCO3 shifts the equilibrium left by mass action on a concentration [CaCO3].
0 bar, because extra CaCO3 reabsorbs all of the CO2.

items.explanation: For this heterogeneous equilibrium the equilibrium law is Kp = P_CO2. At 1073 K that pressure is fixed at 0.22 bar as long as both CaCO3(s) and CaO(s) remain. Adding more solid carbonate does not change the activities of the solids (taken as 1 for pure phases) and does not change T, so P_CO2 is unchanged. Doubling the mass of a solid does not double a gas pressure that is set by Kp. Treating CaCO3 as if it had a molarity in Kp is the usual incorrect homogeneous-style mass-action argument.

distractorRationales.A: Equilibrium pressure of CO2 is set by Kp, not by the mass of solid carbonate, provided some solid remains.
distractorRationales.C: Pure solids are omitted from Kp; there is no [CaCO3] term that would drive the equilibrium backward when extra solid is added.
distractorRationales.D: Reabsorption of all CO2 would require Kp = 0. The given Kp is 0.22 bar, so a finite CO2 pressure remains.

items.stem: An action potential is initiated at the axon hillock of a typical multipolar neuron. Under physiologic conditions the impulse propagates:

choices.text: only backward through the dendritic tree, because axons cannot conduct toward terminals
as a standing wave occupying the entire axon in both directions indefinitely
only after the soma electrically depolarizes a skeletal muscle fiber without using an axon
toward the axon terminals; Na+ channels behind the active region are inactivated, so the spike does not reverse along that axon

items.explanation: Orthodromic conduction runs from the trigger zone toward synaptic terminals. Voltage-gated Na+ channels inactivate shortly after opening, creating a refractory wake that prevents the regenerative depolarization from turning around on the same axon under normal conditions. Dendrites are not the primary regenerative path to the output synapse, a standing wave is not the Hodgkin-Huxley picture, and a CNS neuron does not skip its axon and dump current into a muscle fiber.

distractorRationales.A: The functional output path is the axon to terminals, not exclusive antidromic invasion of dendrites.
distractorRationales.B: The AP is a traveling, self-limited wave with a refractory period, not a persistent bidirectional standing depolarization of the whole axon.
distractorRationales.C: Chemical synaptic transmission at a neuromuscular junction, when it occurs, still requires axonal conduction to the terminal; the soma does not directly pace muscle by volume conduction as the default.

items.stem: A 100 keV diagnostic X-ray photon is compared with a 2 eV visible photon, both in vacuum. The X-ray photon has:

choices.text: longer wavelength and greater speed
shorter wavelength and lower frequency
longer wavelength and higher frequency
shorter wavelength and the same speed

items.explanation: Photon energy E = h f = hc / lambda, so a 100 keV photon has much higher frequency and much shorter wavelength than a 2 eV photon. In vacuum both travel at c; electromagnetic waves do not speed up because they are more energetic. Pairing short wavelength with low frequency, or long wavelength with high frequency, contradicts c = f lambda.

distractorRationales.A: Higher energy means shorter, not longer, wavelength, and vacuum speed is c for both.
distractorRationales.B: Shorter wavelength is correct, but frequency is higher, not lower, because f = c / lambda.
distractorRationales.C: Higher frequency is correct for the X-ray, but that requires a shorter wavelength, not a longer one.

items.stem:
Silica TLC (polar stationary phase, hexane/ethyl acetate 4:1). Distances from origin:

Spot | distance (cm)
Solvent front | 8.0
Compound A | 6.0
Compound B | 2.0
Compound C | 2.0, after staining also UV-active at 254 nm like B

Rf = distance(spot)/distance(front). A is a non-polar hydrocarbon; B is a phenol. Which reading is justified?

choices.text: Rf(A)=0.75, Rf(B)=0.25; A is less polar and travels farther on silica; C co-spots with B so TLC alone does not prove C ≠ B
Rf(A)=0.25 because hydrocarbons stick to silica
B is less polar than A because it moved only 2.0 cm
C must be identical to B because two compounds cannot share an Rf

items.explanation: Rf(A)=6.0/8.0=0.75 and Rf(B)=2.0/8.0=0.25. Polar silica retains the phenol (hydrogen bonding) so B lags; the hydrocarbon A interacts weakly and rides near the solvent front. Compound C has the same Rf as B, so they may be the same or merely coincidentally similar in polarity; co-spotting is necessary but not sufficient for identity. Hydrocarbons do not ‘stick’ on silica relative to phenols. Smaller distance means more polar on this phase, so B is more polar than A. Different compounds can share an Rf, which is why mixed-spot tests and a second method are used.

distractorRationales.B: A travelled 6.0 of 8.0 cm, Rf 0.75, the less retained non-polar compound.
distractorRationales.C: Shorter travel on silica means stronger adsorption, i.e. more polar, not less.
distractorRationales.D: Equal Rf is consistent with identity but does not prove it; many phenols could occupy Rf 0.25.

items.stem:
A mass spectrum of element X shows only three peaks (m/z equal to the mass number, relative intensities summing to 100):
m/z 24, intensity 79; m/z 25, intensity 10; m/z 26, intensity 11.
The average atomic mass is Σ (mass number × relative abundance). What value should be reported?

choices.text: 25.00 u, the middle mass number
24.00 u, the most intense peak
26.00 u, the heaviest isotope

items.explanation: Weighted average = (24 × 79 + 25 × 10 + 26 × 11) / 100 = (1896 + 250 + 286) / 100 = 24.32 u. Relative intensity is the abundance of each isotope, so the mean is pulled toward 24 but not all the way there because of the 25 and 26 peaks. The median mass number 25, the mode 24, and the heaviest mass 26 each ignore that weighting. The arithmetic uses only the tabulated peaks; no external atomic-mass table is required.

distractorRationales.B: An unweighted middle mass number ignores that 79% of the atoms are 24 u.
distractorRationales.C: The most abundant isotope is 24 u, but 21% of the sample is heavier, raising the average to 24.32 u.
distractorRationales.D: The 26 u peak is only 11% of the intensity; it cannot be the average.

items.stem:
Points P and Q lie on the perpendicular bisector and on the line joining two charges, respectively:

Charges: +4.0 μC at x = −1.0 m and +4.0 μC at x = +1.0 m.
P is at (0, 0), the midpoint.
Q is at (3.0 m, 0).

Electric field is a vector; potential V = kq/r is a scalar. Which statement is true?

choices.text: E is maximum at P and zero at Q
At P the fields cancel so E = 0 but V is 2 kq/r = 7.2 × 10^4 V; at Q the fields add in the same direction
E and V are both zero at P because it is halfway
V = 0 at P because the charges are equal

items.explanation: At the midpoint the two E vectors are equal, opposite, and cancel, so E = 0. Potentials add: each is k(4.0×10−6)/1.0 = 3.6×10^4 V, total 7.2×10^4 V. Equal like charges do not make V = 0; that would need opposite signs. At Q, both field arrows point to +x (away from both positives), so they add. E is therefore a minimum (zero) at P, not a maximum. Midpoint cancellation of E for like charges is a vector effect and does not null the scalar potential.

distractorRationales.A: The symmetric point P is where E cancels; Q is off to one side, where the arrows align.
distractorRationales.C: E = 0 at P, but V is the sum of two positive terms, 7.2 × 10^4 V.
distractorRationales.D: V = 0 on a perpendicular bisector of opposite charges, not like charges.

items.stem: A string of length 2.0 m is fixed at both ends. Transverse waves on the string travel at 10 m/s. The frequency of the fundamental standing wave is:

choices.text: 2.5 Hz
5.0 Hz
20 Hz

items.explanation: A string fixed at both ends has a node at each end, so the fundamental fits one-half wavelength into the string: λ/2 = L, or λ = 2L = 4.0 m. Frequency and wavelength are related by v = f λ, so f = v/λ = 10 m/s / 4.0 m = 2.5 Hz. Equivalently, f_n = n v / (2 L) with n = 1 gives 10 / 4 = 2.5 Hz. A closed air column uses v/(4L) for its fundamental, which is a different boundary condition and does not apply to this string.

distractorRationales.A: This is v/(4L), the closed-pipe (node–antinode) fundamental. Both ends of the string are nodes, so the fundamental is v/(2L), not v/(4L).
distractorRationales.C: This is v/L = 5 Hz, which would be the n = 2 harmonic (one full wavelength on the string), not the fundamental.
distractorRationales.D: This is v L or 2 v L with scrambled units. Frequency is speed divided by wavelength, and λ_fundamental = 2L = 4 m, not a product of v and L.

items.stem: Nitronium ion, NO2+, is linear, whereas nitrite, NO2−, is bent. Which pair of hybridizations at nitrogen is consistent with those shapes?

choices.text: NO2+: nitrogen is sp (two electron domains); NO2−: nitrogen is sp2 (three electron domains, including a lone pair).
Both nitrogens are sp3, and the extra charge on nitrite simply compresses the bond angle below 109°.
NO2+: nitrogen is sp3d; NO2−: nitrogen is sp, so nitrite should be linear.
Both nitrogens are sp, so both ions must be linear; packing in the lattice bends nitrite.

items.explanation: Count electron domains at nitrogen. In NO2+ the nitrogen is bonded to two oxygens with no remaining lone pair (the ion is isoelectronic with CO2), so two domains imply sp hybridization and a 180° bond angle. In NO2− nitrogen has two bonding domains plus one lone pair, so three domains imply sp2 hybridization and a bent geometry. Expanding the octet to sp3d is unnecessary for these second-period nitrogen species, and a lattice cannot turn a linear isolated ion into a persistently bent one in the gas-phase or solution description used here.

distractorRationales.B: sp3 would imply four electron domains and a pyramidal or tetrahedral arrangement, which matches neither the linear cation nor the bent anion with only three domains.
distractorRationales.C: This assignment reverses the domain counts and would predict a linear nitrite, contradicting the bent structure.
distractorRationales.D: Nitrite is bent as an isolated ion because of the nitrogen lone pair, not because of crystal packing.

items.stem: A hospital scheduling algorithm shortens appointment slots for ZIP codes that historically overlap with redlined districts, with no individual clerk expressing hostility. Outcome data show longer waits for Black patients. This pattern is best labeled how?

choices.text: Individual discrimination only, because an algorithm cannot be institutional
Institutional discrimination: organizational rules or routines producing systematic unequal treatment, even without a bigoted actor at the desk
Prejudice without discrimination, because no clerk used a slur
Goffman stigma only, which is defined as a ZIP-code variable

items.explanation: Institutional (structural) discrimination is unequal outcomes built into policies, algorithms, or standard operating procedures, and it does not require a prejudiced individual at the moment of action. Individual discrimination is a particular person treating another unequally. The algorithm produces extra wait—discrimination in behavior/outcome—not a mere private attitude. Goffman’s stigma is interactional identity spoilage, not a geocoded slot-length rule. Carmichael and Hamilton’s discussion of institutional racism is the usual MCAT contrast with individual bias.

distractorRationales.A: Institutions can discriminate through routines and code; a smiling clerk is not required.
distractorRationales.C: Unequal waits are discriminatory outcomes, not prejudice-only.
distractorRationales.D: Stigma is not defined as a ZIP-code scheduler.

items.stem:
Vapour pressures at 20 °C:

Liquid | Pvap (kPa) | notable IMF
Pentane | 57 | dispersion only
Propanone | 24 | dipole–dipole + dispersion
Ethanol | 5.8 | hydrogen bonding + dispersion
Water | 2.3 | hydrogen-bond network

A lower vapour pressure at a given temperature means stronger net attractions in the liquid. Which ranking of total intermolecular attraction is supported?

choices.text: Propanone > water, because a carbonyl dipole is always stronger than hydrogen bonding
Water > ethanol > propanone > pentane
Pentane > propanone > ethanol > water, following vapour pressure
All four are equal because each is a molecular liquid at 20 °C

items.explanation: Vapour pressure falls 57 → 24 → 5.8 → 2.3 kPa from pentane to water, so the liquid-phase attractions increase in that same direction: pentane (dispersion only) weakest, then polar propanone, then hydrogen-bonded ethanol, then the water network. Ranking by the vapour-pressure numbers themselves reverses the force order. Being molecular at 20 °C does not equalise escaping tendency. Propanone’s 24 kPa is an order of magnitude above water’s 2.3 kPa, so the carbonyl dipole is not stronger than water’s hydrogen-bond network.

distractorRationales.A: Propanone’s vapour pressure is much higher than water’s, so its net IMF are weaker.
distractorRationales.C: High vapour pressure means weak attractions; that list is the reverse of interaction strength.
distractorRationales.D: A 25-fold range in Pvap shows the liquids are not equivalent.

items.stem: In the trp operon leader, a short ORF contains tandem Trp codons. When charged tRNA^Trp is abundant the ribosome translates the leader without stalling and a terminator hairpin forms; when tryptophan is scarce the ribosome stalls and an antiterminator RNA structure forms. Both leader Trp codons are mutated to alanine. Which phenotype is expected when tryptophan is low but alanine is plentiful?

choices.text: Attenuation still occurs because the ribosome does not stall at alanine codons, the terminator hairpin forms, and trp structural genes remain under-expressed despite tryptophan starvation.
The operon is transcribed constitutively at high levels because the trp aporepressor can no longer bind tryptophan.
Translation of TrpE initiates at the leader alanine codons, producing a functional TrpE fusion enzyme that bypasses regulation.
Uncharged tRNA^Ala stalls the ribosome whenever tryptophan is low, fully relieving attenuation whenever the cell is starved for tryptophan.

items.explanation: trp attenuation couples translation of the leader peptide to a choice between terminator and antiterminator RNA hairpins. Tandem Trp codons stall the ribosome only when charged tRNA^Trp is scarce, favoring the antiterminator and transcription into trpEDCBA. Replacing those codons with alanine removes the tryptophan-specific stall. If alanine-tRNA is available, the ribosome translates the leader smoothly even during tryptophan starvation, the terminator hairpin still forms, and the biosynthetic genes remain attenuated—exactly when the cell needs them. The mutation is in the leader ORF, not in TrpR’s tryptophan-binding site, does not create a TrpE fusion, and does not charge or uncharge tRNA^Ala in response to tryptophan.

distractorRationales.B: TrpR corepression is a separate input; changing leader Trp codons to Ala does not prevent the repressor from binding tryptophan.
distractorRationales.C: The leader peptide is not fused in-frame to TrpE by this codon swap, and attenuation acts on transcription termination, not on creating a new enzyme.
distractorRationales.D: Alanine charging is independent of tryptophan levels, so tRNA^Ala does not stall the leader ribosome specifically when Trp is low.

items.stem:
The Abbe resolution limit is d = 0.61 λ / NA. Two fluorescent point sources are 250 nm apart. Illumination wavelength λ = 500 nm.

Objective | NA | calculated d
Air 10× | 0.25 | 1220 nm
Air 40× | 0.65 | 469 nm
Oil 100× | 1.40 | 218 nm

Which objective can resolve the two sources as separate, and why?

choices.text: The 40× and 100× equally, because both have d listed below 500 nm
Only the oil 100×, because 218 nm < 250 nm while 469 nm and 1220 nm are coarser than the spacing
All three, because 250 nm is larger than the wavelength divided by 2
Only the 10×, because lower magnification reduces diffraction

items.explanation: Two points are resolved when their separation exceeds d. For the oil lens, 250 > 218, so they are just resolved. For the 40× air lens, 250 < 469, so they merge. The 10× is far worse (d = 1.22 µm). Magnification does not appear in the Abbe formula; numerical aperture and wavelength do. Being less than 500 nm (the wavelength) is not the criterion—the 40× d of 469 nm is still larger than 250 nm. The naive λ/2 = 250 nm cutoff is an approximation at NA = 1.22, not a free pass for every lens.

distractorRationales.A: The 40× d of 469 nm still exceeds 250 nm, so that lens cannot split the pair.
distractorRationales.C: λ/2 = 250 nm would require NA ≈ 1.22; the 0.25 and 0.65 objectives do not meet that.
distractorRationales.D: Lower NA at 10× makes d worse (1220 nm), not better; magnification is not in the formula.

items.stem:
rms speed is v_rms = √(3 R T / M). Two flasks of oxygen (same M):
Flask A: 300 K
Flask B: 1200 K
A third flask C holds hydrogen at 300 K; M_H2 = M_O2 / 16. What are the rms-speed ratios vB/vA and vC/vA?

choices.text: All three rms speeds are equal because rms is a universal thermal speed
vB/vA = 2.0; vC/vA = 4.0
vB/vA = 4.0; vC/vA = 16
vB/vA = 2.0; vC/vA = 1/4

items.explanation: v_rms scales as √(T/M). Quadrupling T from 300 to 1200 K multiplies v_rms by 2, so vB/vA = 2. Hydrogen at the same T has M smaller by 16, so √(1/M) larger by 4, hence vC/vA = 4. Scaling as T or as M without the square root produces 4 and 16. Inverting the mass factor would make hydrogen slower. rms speed is not a constant; it is why H2 effuses faster and why hot molecules in a tail of the distribution escape a planet more easily.

distractorRationales.A: v_rms depends on T and M, as the formula in the stem states.
distractorRationales.C: The square root on T and on 1/M is required: √4 = 2 and √16 = 4, not 4 and 16.
distractorRationales.D: Hydrogen is lighter, so it is faster, not four times slower.

items.stem:
Alveolar ventilation VA = f × (VT − VD), with f the respiratory frequency, VT tidal volume, and VD anatomic dead space (150 mL here).

Pattern | f (min−1) | VT (mL)
Quiet breathing | 12 | 500
Slow deep | 6 | 1000
Panting | 24 | 250

Which ranking of VA is correct?

choices.text: Slow deep (5100 mL min−1) > quiet (4200) > panting (2400)
Panting > quiet > slow deep, because frequency dominates
All three equal 4200 mL min−1 because minute ventilation f × VT is 6000 in each row
Quiet 6000; slow deep 6000; panting 6000, ignoring dead space

items.explanation: Quiet: 12 × (500 − 150) = 12 × 350 = 4200 mL min−1. Slow deep: 6 × (1000 − 150) = 6 × 850 = 5100 mL min−1. Panting: 24 × (250 − 150) = 24 × 100 = 2400 mL min−1. Minute ventilation f×VT is 6000 mL min−1 in every pattern, but a larger fraction of each pant is dead-space air, so alveolar ventilation falls. Slow deep breathing spends a larger fraction of each breath below the dead-space threshold, raising VA. Frequency alone does not rank the rows.

distractorRationales.B: Panting has the highest f but the lowest VA because VT is only 100 mL above dead space.
distractorRationales.C: Equal minute ventilation does not imply equal VA once VD is subtracted inside the parentheses.
distractorRationales.D: Ignoring VD quotes minute ventilation, not alveolar ventilation, which is what the stem defines.

items.stem: The equivalence point is best placed near

choices.text: 12.50 mL, the half-equivalence buffer point.
25.00 mL, where pH jumps from the weak-acid/salt region into the excess-OH region.
0.00 mL, the initial pH.
30.00 mL, the last row.

items.explanation: Equal moles: 25.00 mL of 0.100 M HA needs 25.00 mL of 0.100 M NaOH. The table shows a sharp rise between 24 and 26 mL (5.56 to 11.24) with 25.00 mL already 8.72, typical of a weak-acid equivalence (hydrolysing A−), not 12.50 mL which is the half-neutralisation buffer (pH 4.20). Reading a titration curve as a table is graph-reading. The classmate’s “half way on the page” confuses midpoint with equivalence.

distractorRationales.A: 12.50 mL is half-equivalence; pH there equals pKa, not the jump.
distractorRationales.C: Initial pH characterises HA before any OH−.
distractorRationales.D: 30 mL is excess strong base, past equivalence.

passage.title: Unknown weak acid titration
passage.body:
25.00 mL of monoprotic unknown HA (0.100 mol L−1 stated by the stockroom) is titrated with 0.100 mol L−1 NaOH at 25 °C. pH is measured with a probe calibrated at 4.00 and 10.00.

V(NaOH) / mL | pH
0.00 | 2.88
5.00 | 3.46
12.50 | 4.20
20.00 | 4.94
24.00 | 5.56
25.00 | 8.72
26.00 | 11.24
30.00 | 12.15

A classmate says the equivalence volume must be 12.50 mL because that is “half way on the page.” Another wants Ka from the initial pH alone, treating HA as if it were a strong acid.

items.stem: Two otherwise identical eukaryotic mRNAs differ only in 3′ poly(A) length (about 250 adenosines versus about 20). In the cytosol, which difference is expected?

choices.text: The short-tailed mRNA is translated more efficiently because ribosomes bind poly(A) directly as a substitute 5′ cap.
Both mRNAs are equally stable because eukaryotic decay begins exclusively at an internal endonuclease cut that ignores the tail.
The short-tailed mRNA reaches the deadenylation threshold that triggers decapping and 5′–3′ decay more rapidly, shortening its half-life.
The long tail is spliced out in the cytosol, so tail length cannot affect cytoplasmic stability.

items.explanation: Most cytoplasmic eukaryotic mRNAs are degraded by deadenylation-dependent pathways. Poly(A)-binding protein coats a long tail, circularizes the mRNA with eIF4G/eIF4E, and hinders decapping. Once the tail is shortened below a threshold, PABP is lost, the decapping enzyme acts, and Xrn1 degrades the RNA 5′ to 3′ (a 3′–5′ exosome route also exists). An mRNA that already has only ~20 adenosines is close to that threshold and is turned over faster than a 250-A counterpart. Ribosomes do not use poly(A) as a cap substitute, and poly(A) is added after cleavage, not spliced out in the cytosol.

distractorRationales.A: A long poly(A) tail generally supports translation via PABP–eIF4G closed-loop formation. A very short tail reduces, rather than enhances, translation efficiency.
distractorRationales.B: The major decay pathways are deadenylation-dependent; tail length is a primary determinant of mRNA half-life, not an irrelevant decoration.
distractorRationales.D: Splicing removes introns in the nucleus. Poly(A) tails are not exons and are not spliced out in the cytosol.

items.stem: Laminar flow of an incompressible Newtonian fluid through a rigid cylindrical vessel obeys Poiseuille's law. If the radius is halved while pressure drop, length, and viscosity remain the same, the volume flow rate becomes:

choices.text: 1/16 of its original value
1/8 of its original value
1/4 of its original value
1/2 of its original value

items.explanation: Poiseuille's law states that volume flow rate Q is proportional to r to the fourth, Q = (pi r^4 delta P) / (8 eta L). Halving r multiplies Q by (1/2)^4 = 1/16 if every other factor is held fixed. Resistance therefore rises sixteenfold. Scaling with r, r^2 (area), or r^3 (a common incomplete product of area and a single extra r) does not match the derived r^4 dependence of laminar pipe flow.

distractorRationales.B: One-eighth would correspond to an r^3 scaling, which is not Poiseuille flow. The viscous solution of the Navier-Stokes pipe problem yields r^4.
distractorRationales.C: One-fourth is the area ratio. Flow rate for a viscous tube is not simply proportional to cross-sectional area at fixed driving pressure.
distractorRationales.D: One-half is the radius ratio. That would describe a linear geometric scale, not laminar resistance.

items.stem: A phototherapy diode emits 450 nm photons. Compared with each 900 nm photon, each 450 nm photon has:

choices.text: half the energy and half the speed in vacuum
the same energy, because all photons travel at c
twice the energy and the same speed in vacuum
four times the energy, because E scales as 1/lambda^2

items.explanation: Photon energy is E = hc / lambda, so halving wavelength doubles energy: 450 nm photons are twice as energetic as 900 nm photons. In vacuum every photon travels at c regardless of wavelength; frequency and wavelength trade off to keep c = f lambda. Intensity of a beam depends on photon number as well as E and is not asked here. Energy does not scale as 1/lambda squared for a free photon.

distractorRationales.A: Energy is higher, not lower, at shorter wavelength, and vacuum speed is c for both photons.
distractorRationales.B: Equal speed does not imply equal energy. Energy tracks frequency (or 1/lambda), not c.
distractorRationales.D: E is inversely proportional to lambda, not to lambda squared. The extra power of lambda would apply to some intensity or diffraction formulas, not to a single photon's energy.

items.stem: Heat-killed smooth (encapsulated) pneumococci are extracted. The extract transforms live rough cells to smooth, virulent cells. Transforming activity survives protease and RNase treatments but is abolished by DNase. Which conclusion follows most directly?

choices.text: Protein is the genetic material, because the extract came from heat-killed cells in which proteases were inactivated.
Capsular polysaccharide is the gene, because smoothness is a carbohydrate phenotype and sugars survive DNase.
DNA is required for heritable transformation in this system; protein and RNA are dispensable for the transforming principle.
Transformation in this assay requires simultaneous bacteriophage infection, as later shown by Hershey and Chase using the same pneumococcal extracts.

items.explanation: Griffith showed that a heat-stable principle from killed smooth pneumococci can heritably transform rough cells. Avery, MacLeod, and McCarty fractionated that extract and found that DNase destroyed transforming activity whereas protease and RNase did not. The direct inference is that DNA, not protein or RNA, is required for transformation in this assay. Residual activity after proteases argues against protein as the genetic material. The capsule is the transformed phenotype, not the transforming molecule. The experiment did not involve phage infection of pneumococci, which is a different system from Hershey and Chase’s T2 work.

distractorRationales.A: Protease treatment of the extract left transforming activity intact, which is evidence against protein as the hereditary substance.
distractorRationales.B: Smoothness is the phenotype conferred by capsule genes; DNase sensitivity of the extract shows that DNA, not the polysaccharide itself, carries the heritable information.
distractorRationales.D: Avery’s transformation used cell extracts without phage; Hershey and Chase later used labeled T2 bacteriophage, not pneumococcal extracts.

items.stem: Which shift occurs between the poems?

choices.text: From a problem of payment and leaving, toward recognition, return, and uneasy self-division.
From comedy to a weather report.
From the ferryman’s violence to the speaker’s violence.
From prose instructions to a shopping list.

items.explanation: Ticket/change/leaving versus same-boat-as-animal, coins’ edges, and a wave to an unarrived self is the arc. No violence or shopping list appears. A tone shift can be a thematic reorientation on return, not only a mood adjective. B and D are category errors. C invents blows. The pairing is built for that outbound-versus-return turn.

distractorRationales.B: Neither poem is a comedy set or a forecast.
distractorRationales.C: No violence is narrated.
distractorRationales.D: Both are lyrics, not instructions or lists.

passage.title: Two short poems: Ferry
passage.body:
Poem 1 — “Ticket”
I bought a ticket to the other bank
as if the river were a problem in change.
The ferryman took coins that had known other pockets.
He did not ask what I was leaving.
The water did, in small repeated questions
against the hull.

Poem 2 — “Return”
On the way back the same boat
was a different animal.
I recognised the coins by their edges
and not the faces.
Someone on the far jetty waved
at a person I had not yet become
and I, traitor, waved.

items.stem: A leucine that packs in the dehydrated core of a globular protein is mutated to asparagine. The mutant is soluble, but its thermal unfolding midpoint falls by 12 °C relative to wild type. Which thermodynamic explanation is best?

choices.text: Asparagine introduces a new disulfide that over-stabilizes a misfolded state
The mutation increases core hydrophobicity, which always lowers Tm
Placing a polar carboxamide in the hydrophobic core is energetically costly unless new hydrogen bonds fully compensate
Leucine is charged at neutral pH and asparagine neutralizes that charge, loosening the fold

items.explanation: The protein interior is a low-dielectric environment. A buried leucine contributes to the hydrophobic effect and packs with van der Waals contacts. Asparagine’s polar side chain must either satisfy its hydrogen-bonding potential inside the core or pay a large desolvation penalty; incomplete compensation destabilizes the native state and lowers Tm. Asparagine has no thiol, so it cannot make a disulfide. The substitution decreases, rather than increases, hydrophobicity. Leucine is aliphatic and uncharged, so charge neutralization is not the mechanism.

distractorRationales.A: Neither leucine nor asparagine can form disulfides; that chemistry belongs to cysteine.
distractorRationales.B: Asparagine is more polar than leucine, so core hydrophobicity decreases, not increases.
distractorRationales.D: Leucine is not ionized at neutral pH; there is no charge to neutralize.

items.stem:
Mass spectrum of compound W (odd-electron molecular ion):

m/z | interpretation offered
72 | M+•
57 | M − 15 (loss of CH3)
43 | C3H7+ or CH3CO+
29 | C2H5+ or CHO+

IR of W: 1715 cm−1, no 2720 cm−1. Which molecular formula and structure are most consistent?

choices.text: C5H12, pentane: M = 72, but no carbonyl IR is then allowed
C3H4O2, with M = 72, necessarily an aldehyde because of m/z 29
C4H8O, butanal, required by m/z 29 even though 2720 cm−1 is absent
C4H8O, butan-2-one: M = 72, methyl loss to 57, acyl ion CH3CO+ at 43, and a ketone IR

items.explanation: M+• = 72 with a ketone IR is satisfied by C4H8O (72 = 48+8+16). Butan-2-one fragments by α-cleavage to CH3 (M−15 = 57) and to CH3CO+ (43), the standard methyl ketone pattern. Pentane is also Mr 72 but cannot produce 1715 cm−1. C3H4O2 is 72 and could be acrylic acid or similar, but the 1715 cm−1-only description without a broad acid O–H, plus the 57 methyl-loss, fits butanone better; m/z 29 is not uniquely CHO+. Butanal would show the 2720 cm−1 aldehyde C–H that is absent. The IR therefore selects the ketone over the aldehyde isomer of C4H8O.

distractorRationales.A: Pentane has no oxygen and cannot give a 1715 cm−1 carbonyl stretch.
distractorRationales.B: m/z 29 is ambiguous (ethyl or formyl); the missing aldehyde IR and the 57 peak favour a methyl ketone.
distractorRationales.C: Butanal is C4H8O and would give M = 72, but the IR lacks 2720 cm−1, so it is not W.

items.stem: Photons of wavelength 620 nm strike a retinal chromophore. Using the approximation hc = 1240 eV nm, the energy of one photon is:

choices.text: 2.0 eV
1.0 eV
4.0 eV

items.explanation: The photon energy is E = hc / lambda. Substituting the given product hc = 1240 eV nm and lambda = 620 nm yields 1240 / 620 = 2.0 eV, a typical visible-photon energy. Inverting the ratio gives 0.50 eV. Halving or doubling 2.0 eV produces the remaining traps and would correspond to 1240 nm or 310 nm light, not 620 nm.

distractorRationales.B: This is lambda / hc rather than hc / lambda (620 / 1240). Energy must fall as wavelength rises, but the algebraic form is a reciprocal, not this inverted substitution.
distractorRationales.C: This is half the correct value, as if lambda were taken as 1240 nm or an extra factor of two were inserted in the denominator.
distractorRationales.D: This doubles the correct energy, corresponding to 310 nm photons, not 620 nm.

items.stem:
The gas-phase equilibrium A(g) ⇌ 2 B(g) has Kc = 0.40 mol L−1 at temperature T, with Kc = [B]^2 / [A]. A 1.00 L flask at equilibrium contains the concentrations in the first data row. The mixture is then rapidly diluted to 2.00 L at the same T (concentrations instantly halved) before any reaction occurs.

Stage | [A] (mol L−1) | [B] (mol L−1)
At equilibrium in 1.00 L | 0.100 | 0.200
Immediately after dilution to 2.00 L | 0.050 | 0.100

What is Q immediately after dilution, and what net reaction restores equilibrium?

choices.text: Q = 0.40, already equal to Kc, so dilution produces no net chemical change.
Q = 0.80, greater than Kc, so B combines to form A.
Q = 0.20, less than Kc, so A dissociates net to form additional B.
Q = 0.20, less than Kc, so B is consumed because dilution always favours fewer particles.

items.explanation: Check the original row: Q = (0.200)^2 / 0.100 = 0.40 = Kc, so the flask truly started at equilibrium. After doubling the volume, Q′ = (0.100)^2 / 0.050 = 0.010 / 0.050 = 0.20, which is below Kc. The forward reaction therefore proceeds, producing more B. That direction also matches Le Chatelier for a process that increases the number of gas particles when the system is diluted. Q does not remain equal to Kc after a concentration jump of this stoichiometry, because [B] is squared.

distractorRationales.A: Halving both concentrations does not leave Q unchanged when the numerator is a square. Q falls to 0.20, so a net reaction occurs.
distractorRationales.B: Q = 0.80 would require doubling rather than halving concentrations, or inverting the dilution. The actual Q is 0.20, below Kc, so A does not form net.
distractorRationales.D: Q is 0.20, but the restoring reaction produces more particles (A → 2 B), which is the direction favoured by dilution, not consumption of B.

items.stem: A 2 kg stone is released from rest 10 m above the ground. Take g = 10 m/s^2 and neglect air resistance. The speed of the stone just before it hits the ground is closest to:

choices.text: 10 m/s
14 m/s
20 m/s

items.explanation: Mechanical energy is conserved: gravitational potential energy converts entirely into kinetic energy. mgh = (1/2) m v^2, so v = sqrt(2 g h) = sqrt(2 × 10 × 10) = sqrt(200) ≈ 14.1 m/s. The mass cancels, which is why a 2 kg stone and a 1 kg stone hit at the same speed from the same height in vacuum. Using v = g t with an incorrect time, or forgetting the square root of 2 g h, misses this value.

distractorRationales.A: This is sqrt(g h) or the numerical value of g (or of the 10 m height). The free-fall identity is v = sqrt(2 g h), which includes the 2.
distractorRationales.C: This is g t with t = 2 s, but the actual time from rest is t = sqrt(2 h/g) = sqrt(2) s ≈ 1.4 s, giving v ≈ 14 m/s, not 20 m/s.
distractorRationales.D: This is 2 g h without taking the square root. Speed is the square root of 200 m^2/s^2, not 200 m/s.

items.stem:
The Haber equilibrium is N2(g) + 3 H2(g) ⇌ 2 NH3(g) at a fixed temperature where Kc = 0.50, with Kc = [NH3]^2 / ([N2][H2]^3) and concentrations in mol L−1. A reactor is sampled and the instantaneous concentrations are:

Species | Concentration (mol L−1)
N2 | 0.20
H2 | 0.60
NH3 | 0.10

What is the reaction quotient Q, and what net change occurs as the mixture returns to equilibrium?

choices.text: Q = 0.50, so the mixture is already at equilibrium and no net change occurs.
Q ≈ 0.23, which is less than Kc, so ammonia forms net until Q rises to 0.50.
Q ≈ 2.3, which is greater than Kc, so ammonia decomposes net.
Q ≈ 0.083, which is less than Kc, so the reaction shifts to produce N2 and H2.

items.explanation: Q is evaluated with the same expression as Kc but using the instantaneous concentrations: Q = (0.10)^2 / (0.20 × 0.60^3) = 0.010 / (0.20 × 0.216) = 0.010 / 0.0432 ≈ 0.231. Because Q is smaller than Kc, the forward reaction is favoured and ammonia is produced until Q = Kc. Failing to cube [H2] or to square [NH3] gives the distractor values. Kc itself is unchanged at constant temperature, so the comparison of Q with the given Kc fully determines the net direction.

distractorRationales.A: Q equals Kc only if the plugged-in concentrations already satisfy Kc. Here Q ≈ 0.23, not 0.50, so the mixture is not at equilibrium.
distractorRationales.C: Q ≈ 2.3 is obtained if [NH3] is not squared. The correctly computed Q is below Kc, so the net reaction is forward, not reverse.
distractorRationales.D: Q ≈ 0.083 comes from omitting the cube on [H2]. Even with a Q below Kc, the net change is ammonia formation, not production of N2 and H2.

items.stem: A toxin constitutively locks Gs in the GTP-bound state in hepatocytes that use Gs-coupled receptors to mobilize glucose. The expected effect is:

choices.text: persistent adenylyl cyclase activity, high cAMP, and increased glycogen breakdown
a fall in cAMP and net glycogen synthesis
cleavage of the insulin receptor as the toxin's only target
ligand-independent translocation of steroid receptors onto DNA

items.explanation: Gs stimulates adenylyl cyclase while GTP is bound. A lock in the active state (as in cholera toxin on Gs) keeps cAMP high. In hepatocytes, cAMP-dependent protein kinase phosphorylates phosphorylase kinase and promotes glycogenolysis (the glucagon/epinephrine Gs pathway). That is the opposite of lowering cAMP and building glycogen. The toxin is not an insulin-receptor protease, and steroid-receptor nuclear entry is a separate, ligand-regulated path.

distractorRationales.B: Active Gs raises, not lowers, cAMP. High cAMP in liver favors breakdown, not synthesis, of glycogen.
distractorRationales.C: Gs-directed toxins modify G proteins, not by default cleaving the insulin receptor as their sole action.
distractorRationales.D: Steroid receptors are not the Gs-cAMP module. Constitutive Gs does not substitute for steroid ligand in nuclear targeting.

items.stem: The author's central claim is best stated as

choices.text: Parks should be ticketed like venues so the ledger can finally close.

A park is not a leak from private order but a condition of urban inhabitability; defend it with a more complete ledger, including maintenance and the people priced off adjacent blocks, rather than with mere poetry of the unowned.
Ledgers are evil, and gardeners in winter betray the commons.
Developers are wrong that parks have any price.

items.explanation: The opening denies that a park is a leak, the middle rejects fencing-or-neglect and weak poetry, and the close demands maintenance plus the displaced neighbors. B holds those parts. A is the crude policy attacked. C inverts the adult defense. D ignores the grant that developers are not wrong about a price. Main idea answers must include both the inhabitability thesis and the incomplete-ledger politics, not only a slogan about green space.

distractorRationales.A: Ticketing until the park behaves like a venue is named as a crude refusal to count the park's effects.
distractorRationales.C: The author says planting, toilets, and a winter gardener are how openness lasts, not betrayals.
distractorRationales.D: The first paragraph says developers are not wrong that the gift has a price.

passage.title: The ledger of the commons
passage.body:
When a city puts a park on a map, it appears to have given something away: land that could have been lots, hours that could have been tolls. Developers are not wrong that the gift has a price. They are wrong when they treat the price as a leak from an otherwise watertight private order. The private order is already subsidized by streets, courts, pipes, and the patience of people who do not sue every time a stranger walks past a porch. A park is not the exception to property. It is one of the ways a dense city remains inhabitable enough for property to be worth wanting.

Accountants prefer a ledger in which every square metre has a named owner and a yield. Parks embarrass the ledger because their yield is a crowd that does not pay at the gate, a cooling that does not send an invoice, a child who learns a city can include her without a purchase. The embarrassment produces two crude policies. One is to fence and ticket until the park behaves like a venue. The other is to neglect the park until the crowd looks like a problem that only private security can solve. Both policies claim to be realistic. Both are ways of refusing to count the effects that made the park rational in the first place.

Friends of the park sometimes answer with a poetry of the unowned. The poetry is moving and strategically weak. A commons that cannot speak in maintenance budgets will lose to a spreadsheet that can. The more adult defense is to insist that the ledger is incomplete, not that ledgers are evil. Planting, lighting, toilets, and a gardener who is paid in winter are not betrayals of openness. They are how openness lasts past a ribbon-cutting.

There is a further honesty. Parks are not innocent. They have been used to raise adjacent rents, to move unhoused people out of sight, to display a city’s kindness to visitors who will never need the toilets. Naming those uses does not hand the land to the highest bidder. It prevents the park’s defenders from pretending that green on a map is already justice. Justice would be a park whose ledger includes the people who were priced off the blocks around it.

If urban politics cannot hold that thought, it will keep oscillating between the venue and the ruin, and calling the oscillation pragmatism.

items.stem:
A beam of radiation is absorbed according to I = I0 e^{−μ x}. Taking the natural log gives ln I = ln I0 − μ x, so a graph of ln I versus x is linear with slope −μ. Count rates versus absorber thickness are:

x (cm) | I (counts s−1)
0.0 | 800
2.0 | 400
4.0 | 200
6.0 | 100

What is μ?

choices.text: 0.50 cm−1, using (800 − 100) / 6.0 from the raw I–x table.
2.0 cm−1, the half-thickness itself treated as μ.
0.347 cm−1, because I halves every 2.0 cm and μ = ln 2 / 2.0 cm.
0.125 cm−1, using 100/800 divided by 6.0.

items.explanation: Each additional 2.0 cm of absorber halves the count rate, so the half-thickness x1/2 = 2.0 cm. Then I / I0 = 1/2 = e^{−μ x1/2}, hence μ = ln 2 / x1/2 = 0.693 / 2.0 = 0.347 cm−1. Equivalently, from x = 0 to 6.0 cm there are three halvings, I / I0 = 1/8, ln(I0/I) = ln 8 = 2.079, μ = 2.079 / 6.0 = 0.347 cm−1. The raw I-versus-x graph is exponential, not linear, so (ΔI)/Δx is not μ. The half-thickness is 2.0 cm, which is not the value of μ. A linear fit must be performed on ln I versus x, whose slope is −0.347 cm−1.

distractorRationales.A: Subtracting raw counts and dividing by thickness treats an exponential as a straight line. μ comes from the slope of ln I versus x, not of I versus x.
distractorRationales.B: 2.0 cm is the half-thickness, whose unit is length. μ is ln 2 divided by that length, about 0.35 cm−1.
distractorRationales.D: 100/800 = 0.125 is I(6 cm)/I0, not a value of μ. Dividing that fraction by 6.0 cm also has the wrong algebra for an exponential.

items.stem: A student health campaign first asks residents to sign a one-sentence hand-hygiene pledge at a table, then a week later asks them to staff a four-hour influenza-shot drive. Compliance with the large request is higher among those who signed. This is which sequential technique, as in Freedman and Fraser’s work?

choices.text: Door-in-the-face (Cialdini): a huge request first, then retreat to a smaller one
Foot-in-the-door: a small granted request raises the chance of a later larger one, often via self-perception of being “the kind of person who helps”
Low-balling: the cost is revealed only after commitment to an unchanged request
Cognitive dissonance from a $1 lie about an OSCE, which is the same operational procedure

items.explanation: Foot-in-the-door (Freedman and Fraser) is a small yes followed by a larger related request. Self-perception (Bem) or consistency motives are the usual mediators. Door-in-the-face is the reverse sequence: extreme request refused, then a moderate target. Low-ball changes the cost after a commitment. Festinger’s $1/$20 paradigm is induced compliance with a counter-attitudinal speech, not this two-request campaign.

distractorRationales.A: Door-in-the-face starts large, not with a one-sentence pledge.
distractorRationales.C: The large request is a new, openly described task, not a hidden-price change of the same deal.
distractorRationales.D: Insufficient-justification dissonance is a different experimental recipe than sequential requests.

items.stem: A coding (nontemplate, sense) DNA strand contains 5′-ATG GCA-3′ at the start of an open reading frame. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: The mRNA in this region is 5′-AUG GCA-3′, matching the coding strand except that U replaces T.
The mRNA is 5′-UAC CGU-3′ because RNA polymerase copies the coding strand 3′ to 5′.
The template strand has 5′-ATG GCA-3′ and is copied directly into 5′-AUG GCA-3′.
tRNA, not mRNA, is transcribed from the coding strand of protein-coding genes.

items.explanation: The coding strand has the same sequence as the RNA transcript except that DNA has T where RNA has U. RNA polymerase actually uses the complementary template (antisense) strand as the substrate and polymerizes RNA 5′ to 3′. If the coding strand reads 5′-ATG GCA-3′, the template is 3′-TAC CGT-5′ and the mRNA is 5′-AUG GCA-3′. Calling the coding strand the template, reversing polarity, or asserting that protein-coding genes produce tRNA from that strand all misstate transcription. This relationship is why gene sequences are usually published as the coding strand: it can be read as the mRNA with U for T.

distractorRationales.B: 5′-UAC CGU-3′ is the reverse complement of the coding sequence, not the transcript. Polymerase synthesizes RNA 5′ to 3′ complementary to the template, yielding 5′-AUG GCA-3′.
distractorRationales.C: The template strand is complementary to the coding strand, so it cannot also be 5′-ATG GCA-3′ if the coding strand already has that sequence.
distractorRationales.D: Protein-coding genes are transcribed into mRNA (pre-mRNA in eukaryotes). tRNA genes are separate transcription units, mainly RNA polymerase III products in eukaryotes.

items.stem: A driving simulator has residents keep a car in lane while simultaneously monitoring a second screen for a rare vital-sign alarm. Lane-keeping error jumps when the alarm task is added, even though both tasks are easy alone. Kahneman’s limited-capacity account of divided attention predicts which outcome?

choices.text: Error should not change, because Broadbent’s filter fully protects the driving channel
Only late-selection theory predicts dual-task cost, and only if the alarm is physically identical to engine noise
Habituation of the orienting reflex will abolish lane error after one combined trial
The two tasks compete for a shared pool of attention, so dual-task costs appear when combined demand exceeds available capacity

items.explanation: Kahneman treated attention as a limited, allocatable capacity. Two easy tasks can still interfere when their sum exceeds that pool, which is the classic dual-task cost. Broadbent’s filter is an account of selective, not divided, attention and does not guarantee a protected driving channel. Late selection concerns how far ignored messages are processed, not this resource trade-off. Habituation would reduce responding to a repeated irrelevant stimulus, not erase capacity competition in a first dual-task block.

distractorRationales.A: A selective-attention filter does not imply cost-free divided attention between two attended tasks.
distractorRationales.B: Dual-task costs are the central prediction of capacity models, not a unique late-selection claim about physical identity.
distractorRationales.C: Habituation is non-associative waning to a repeated stimulus, not an explanation of divided-attention interference.

items.stem: 1-Pentanol is oxidized in two separate flasks: flask P with PCC in anhydrous CH2Cl2, and flask J with CrO3 in aqueous H2SO4 (Jones conditions). What are the principal organic products?

choices.text: P: pentanal; J: pentanoic acid, because in water the aldehyde hydrate is further oxidized by chromic acid
P: pentanoic acid; J: pentanal, because PCC is the stronger aqueous oxidant
Both flasks give pentane, because chromium reagents reduce alcohols to alkanes
Neither flask oxidizes a primary alcohol; only secondary alcohols react with Cr(VI)

items.explanation: Primary alcohols are oxidized by Cr(VI) to aldehydes. Under anhydrous PCC conditions the aldehyde is not hydrated and is not rapidly oxidized further, so pentanal is isolated. Jones reagent is aqueous: the aldehyde forms a gem-diol (hydrate) that behaves like a secondary alcohol equivalent and is oxidized to the carboxylic acid. Chromium(VI) is an oxidant, not a reductant, and it certainly oxidizes primary alcohols. The solvent, not a mysterious difference in ‘strength’ of PCC versus Jones as named reagents, is what decides aldehyde versus acid.

distractorRationales.B: This swaps the products. PCC in dry CH2Cl2 is the aldehyde reagent; aqueous chromic acid over-oxidizes to the acid.
distractorRationales.C: Cr(VI) oxidizes alcohols to carbonyls (or acids). It does not deoxygenate them to alkanes (that would be a reduction such as Wolff–Kishner).
distractorRationales.D: Primary and secondary alcohols both react with Cr(VI). Tertiary alcohols lack a C–H on the carbinol carbon and typically do not oxidize.

items.stem: A temperature-sensitive mutation blocks COPII-coated vesicle exit from the ER. Newly synthesized secretory proteins in these cells will:

choices.text: acquire mature Golgi N-glycan modifications on the normal schedule
be imported into mitochondria instead
be translated exclusively on mitochondrial ribosomes
remain in the early secretory pathway and fail to receive Golgi-specific modifications

items.explanation: COPII vesicles carry cargo from ER to Golgi. If they cannot form or fuse, secretory proteins remain ER-associated (or in an ER-Golgi intermediate) and do not encounter Golgi glycosyltransferases, so Golgi-dependent glycan maturation fails. Mitochondrial import uses different targeting peptides and translocons, and secretory proteins are made on cytosolic ribosomes docked at the ER, not on mitochondrial ribosomes. Mature Golgi sugars are precisely what should be missing.

distractorRationales.A: Golgi modifications require arrival at the Golgi. Blocking ER exit prevents that arrival.
distractorRationales.B: ER-retained secretory proteins are not rerouted through TOM/TIM as a default.
distractorRationales.C: Mitochondrial ribosomes translate a handful of OXPHOS subunits, not the cell's secretory proteome.

items.stem: A researcher needs to separate the two strands of genomic DNA for hybridization without hydrolyzing either covalent backbone. Which class of interaction must be disrupted?

choices.text: 3′–5′ phosphodiester bonds within each strand
N-glycosidic bonds linking bases to deoxyribose
Disulfide bonds that covalently crosslink complementary bases
Hydrogen bonds between complementary bases, together with base-stacking interactions

items.explanation: The two strands of a DNA duplex are held together by noncovalent hydrogen bonds between Watson–Crick pairs and by stacking of the aromatic bases. Heat, alkali (which titrates bases and disrupts pairing), or formamide can melt those interactions and yield intact single strands that still have covalent phosphodiester backbones. Breaking phosphodiester or glycosidic bonds would fragment or depurinate the DNA rather than produce hybridizable full-length strands. Complementary bases are not linked by disulfides; those bonds stabilize some proteins, not the DNA double helix. Strand separation for blotting or PCR denaturation therefore targets noncovalent duplex forces only.

distractorRationales.A: Phosphodiester cleavage would nick or degrade each strand. Denaturation for hybridization must leave the covalent backbones intact.
distractorRationales.B: Breaking glycosidic bonds depurinates or depyrimidinates DNA and destroys base-pairing information rather than simply unzipping the duplex.
distractorRationales.C: DNA strands are not covalently crosslinked by disulfides; disulfide bonds are a protein feature. Duplex DNA is noncovalently paired.

items.stem: A junior resident is handed an unfamiliar role in a code. She first judges the event as a threat to the patient’s life and to her reputation. She then asks whether she has the skills, attending backup, and time to manage it. According to Lazarus, these two judgments are:

choices.text: Primary appraisal of stakes (threat) followed by secondary appraisal of coping resources
Secondary appraisal of harm followed by primary appraisal of challenge, which must occur in that order
The alarm and resistance stages of the general adaptation syndrome
Problem-focused coping then emotion-focused coping, which are mandatory sequential stages

items.explanation: Lazarus distinguishes how a person construes what is at stake from how the person construes what can be done. Primary appraisal classifies an encounter as irrelevant, benign-positive, or stressful (harm/loss, threat, or challenge). Secondary appraisal evaluates coping options and resources. The resident’s first judgment is about threat to valued ends; the second is about skills and backup. GAS stages are physiological, not these two cognitive steps. Coping styles are attempts to manage the stressor after appraisal, not the names of the two appraisals.

distractorRationales.B: The first judgment is about stakes (primary), not resources; reversing the labels and forcing harm-then-challenge as a law misstates the model.
distractorRationales.C: Alarm and resistance are Selye’s physiological stages, not Lazarus’s appraisal steps.
distractorRationales.D: Problem- and emotion-focused coping are strategies, not a required two-step sequence that replaces appraisal.

items.stem:
50.0 mL of 1.00 M HCl is mixed with 50.0 mL of 1.00 M NaOH in a coffee-cup calorimeter. Treat the mixture as 100.0 g of solution with c = 4.18 J g−1 °C−1. Both solutions start at 22.0 °C; the final temperature is 28.8 °C. The limiting reaction is H+ + OH− → H2O (0.0500 mol). q_solution = m c ΔT, and ΔH_rxn = −q_solution / moles.
What is ΔH for the neutralization?

choices.text: −56.8 kJ mol−1
+56.8 kJ mol−1
−28.4 kJ mol−1 (using 0.100 mol as the extent of reaction)
−5.68 kJ mol−1 (using 0.500 mol)

items.explanation: ΔT = 28.8 − 22.0 = 6.8 °C. Heat absorbed by the solution is 100.0 × 4.18 × 6.8 = 2842 J. The reaction released that heat, so q_rxn = −2842 J. Extent is 0.0500 mol (50.0 mL of 1.00 M of each, 1:1 stoichiometry), giving ΔH = −2842 J / 0.0500 mol = −56.8 kJ mol−1. The temperature rise shows an exothermic process, so the sign is negative. Using 0.100 mol (sum of both reagents) halves |ΔH|; using 0.500 mol divides by ten.

distractorRationales.B: Heat flowed into the solution (T rose), so the reaction is exothermic and ΔH is negative.
distractorRationales.C: Only 0.0500 mol of water forms; 50.0 mL of 1.00 M plus 50.0 mL of 1.00 M is not 0.100 mol of reaction.
distractorRationales.D: 0.500 mol is ten times the actual extent, which would give −5.68 kJ mol−1.

items.stem:
Osmotic pressure π = i c RT, with R = 0.080 L atm mol−1 K−1 and T = 300 K. Two intravenous-style solutions:

Solution | formal concentration | i
Glucose | 0.30 M | 1
NaCl | 0.15 M | 2

How do the osmotic pressures compare, and what is π for each?

choices.text: Glucose 7.2 atm; NaCl 3.6 atm, ignoring i of NaCl
Glucose 0.30 atm; NaCl 0.15 atm, omitting RT
Both 2.4 atm, using R = 0.080 without T
Both 7.2 atm, because i c is 0.30 M in each

items.explanation: Particle concentration i c is 0.30 M for glucose and 0.15 × 2 = 0.30 M for NaCl, so they are iso-osmotic. π = 0.30 × 0.080 × 300 = 0.30 × 24 = 7.2 atm for both. Dropping i for NaCl halves its π incorrectly. Omitting RT leaves the molarity numbers with atm painted on. Using R but not T gives 0.30 × 0.080 = 0.024, not 2.4; a 2.4 atm figure is 0.30 × 8 without the 300/100 bookkeeping. Clinically this is why 0.15 M NaCl (half-molar salt) matches 0.30 M glucose.

distractorRationales.A: NaCl’s i = 2 doubles 0.15 M to the same 0.30 M particles as glucose.
distractorRationales.B: RT = 24 L atm mol−1 at 300 K with this R, so π is tens of atm per mole per litre, not 0.30 atm.
distractorRationales.C: Forgetting T underestimates by a factor of 300; 2.4 atm is not the correct product.

items.stem:
A stationary observer hears a 400 Hz siren. The speed of sound in the air is 340 m s−1. When the source moves directly toward the observer at 30 m s−1, the observed frequency is given by f′ = f × v / (v − vs), where vs is the source speed toward the observer.

Quantity | Value
f | 400 Hz
v | 340 m s−1
vs toward observer | 30 m s−1

What frequency does the observer hear?

choices.text: 367 Hz
439 Hz
400 Hz
477 Hz

items.explanation: Substitute into the given Doppler formula: f′ = 400 × 340 / (340 − 30) = 400 × 340 / 310. First 340/310 ≈ 1.0968, then 400 × 1.0968 ≈ 439 Hz. Using v + vs in the denominator (340 + 30 = 370) is the receding-source formula and yields 400 × 340/370 ≈ 367 Hz. Leaving the frequency unchanged ignores the approaching source. Putting v + vs in the numerator and v − vs in the denominator (as if both source and observer moved) gives 400 × 370/310 ≈ 477 Hz. The stem specifies a stationary observer and a source moving toward, so only the given f′ = f v / (v − vs) applies.

distractorRationales.A: 367 Hz is 400 × 340 / 370, the formula for a source receding at 30 m s−1. The source is approaching, so the denominator is 310 m s−1.
distractorRationales.C: 400 Hz would be correct only for a source at rest relative to the air and observer. The 30 m s−1 approach is not negligible compared with 340 m s−1.
distractorRationales.D: 477 Hz is 400 × 370 / 310, which inserts an extra (v + vs) factor appropriate to a moving observer as well. The observer is stationary.

items.stem: A single slit of width a = 4.0 × 10−4 m is illuminated with λ = 5.0 × 10−7 m. The first diffraction minimum satisfies a sin θ = λ. For small θ in radians, sin θ ≈ θ ≈ λ/a. A screen is D = 2.0 m away, so the linear distance from centre to the first minimum is y ≈ θ D. The full central-maximum width is 2y. What is that full width?

choices.text: 2.5 mm
8.0 mm
5.0 mm

items.explanation: θ ≈ λ/a = 5.0×10−7 / 4.0×10−4 = 1.25×10−3 rad. Then y = θ D = 1.25×10−3 × 2.0 = 2.5×10−3 m = 2.5 mm to the first minimum. The central bright fringe spans both sides, so the full width is 2y = 5.0 mm. Reporting y itself gives 2.5 mm. Using a = 2.5×10−4 m would widen the pattern. Half of y is 1.25 mm, the angle in milliradians misread as a millimetre distance without multiplying by D correctly. Narrower slits spread the pattern more; this a and λ already fix 5.0 mm.

distractorRationales.A: 2.5 mm is the centre-to-first-minimum distance y, not the full 2y width of the central maximum.
distractorRationales.B: 8.0 mm would require a smaller slit or a larger D than those given.
distractorRationales.C: 1.25 mm is θ in milliradians written as millimetres, or y/2, omitting the screen distance or the two-sided width.

items.stem: Two antibodies bind the same hapten substrate with indistinguishable Kd. Antibody 1 is noncatalytic. Antibody 2, raised against a transition-state analog, accelerates hapten hydrolysis 10^4-fold. Relative to antibody 1, antibody 2 must additionally:

choices.text: Bind the product more tightly than the substrate so that the equilibrium constant of the reaction increases
Raise the activation free energy by straining the substrate into a less reactive geometry
Stabilize the transition state (or align catalytic groups) beyond what ground-state binding affinity reports
Convert the unimolecular reaction into a diffusion-limited bimolecular collision in bulk water

items.explanation: Equal Kd values mean the two antibodies bind the ground-state hapten similarly, so differential ground-state affinity cannot explain a 10^4 rate ratio. Catalytic antibodies selected on transition-state analogs work by binding the altered geometry of the transition state more tightly than the substrate, or by placing catalytic side chains, which lowers ΔG‡. Tighter product binding would risk product inhibition and does not change the reaction equilibrium, which is a property of free substrate and product. Raising the barrier would slow the reaction. Catalysis occurs in the binding site, not by sending the hapten into an uncatalyzed bimolecular solvent path.

distractorRationales.A: Enzymes do not change overall Keq. Excess product affinity causes inhibition, not acceleration.
distractorRationales.B: Increasing the activation energy decreases the rate; the catalytic antibody does the opposite.
distractorRationales.D: The point of a catalytic binding site is to avoid relying on the slow uncatalyzed solution reaction.

items.stem: De novo palmitate synthesis is measured in a liver fractionation experiment. Which combination of compartment, committed step, and reductant is correct?

choices.text: Mitochondrial matrix; thiolase; NADH from the citric acid cycle
