Endoplasmic reticulum lumen; HMG-CoA reductase; NADPH
Cytosol; acetyl-CoA carboxylase producing malonyl-CoA; NADPH from the pentose phosphate pathway and malic enzyme
Peroxisome; CPT-I; FADH2 from acyl-CoA dehydrogenase

items.explanation: De novo fatty-acid synthesis in hepatocytes occurs in the cytosol. The committed step is carboxylation of acetyl-CoA to malonyl-CoA by acetyl-CoA carboxylase (biotin). Fatty acid synthase then uses NADPH, not NADH or FADH2, to reduce the growing chain; NADPH comes largely from the pentose phosphate pathway and from malic enzyme. Acetyl-CoA itself is delivered from mitochondria via citrate and ATP-citrate lyase. Thiolase and FADH2 belong to β-oxidation, HMG-CoA reductase to cholesterol synthesis in the ER, and CPT-I to the mitochondrial uptake of acyl chains for oxidation, the opposite pathway.

distractorRationales.A: Mitochondrial thiolase and NADH are features of β-oxidation/ketogenesis, not of de novo palmitate synthesis, which is cytosolic and NADPH-dependent.
distractorRationales.B: HMG-CoA reductase is the committed enzyme of cholesterol synthesis in the ER, not of palmitate synthesis, even though it also uses NADPH.
distractorRationales.D: CPT-I and acyl-CoA dehydrogenase belong to fatty-acid oxidation, not synthesis, and peroxisomal β-oxidation is not the cytosolic de novo path measured here.

items.stem: Two monomeric proteins are compared by native gel electrophoresis at pH 7.0. Protein A has pI 5.0 and protein B has pI 9.0. Ignoring sieving differences, toward which electrode does each protein migrate?

choices.text: A toward the anode and B toward the cathode
Both toward the anode
Both toward the cathode
A toward the cathode and B toward the anode

items.explanation: In a native gel the running pH sets net charge: below a protein’s pI the net charge is positive and the protein moves to the cathode; above the pI the net charge is negative and it moves to the anode. At pH 7, protein A (pI 5) is net negative and is therefore anodal, while protein B (pI 9) is net positive and cathodal. The two proteins therefore run in opposite directions if the field is applied to a horizontal strip, or they enter a vertical gel only if the polarity matches their charge. This is the same pH-versus-pI logic used for amino acids.

distractorRationales.B: Protein B is below its pI and is cationic; it does not join A toward the anode.
distractorRationales.C: Protein A is above its pI and is anionic; it does not join B toward the cathode.
distractorRationales.D: This choice reverses both signs relative to pH minus pI.

items.stem:
Four weak acids and their pKa values in water at 25 °C are listed. Separate 0.10 M aqueous solutions of the sodium salts NaA, NaB, NaC and NaD are prepared (each salt is the conjugate base of the corresponding HA).

Acid | pKa of HA
HA | 3.80
HB | 4.90
HC | 7.20
HD | 9.10

Which 0.10 M salt solution has the highest pH?

choices.text: NaA, because HA is the strongest acid, so A− is the strongest hydrolysing base.
NaB, because pKa near 5 maximises hydrolysis of a 0.10 M salt.
NaC, because only acids with pKa > 7 give basic salts.
NaD, because HD is the weakest acid, so D− has the largest Kb and produces the most OH−.

items.explanation: The hydrolysis constant of A− is Kb = Kw / Ka = 10^−14 / 10^−pKa = 10^(pKa − 14). The largest pKa therefore gives the largest Kb. HD has pKa 9.10, so Kb of D− is 10^−4.90, much larger than Kb of A− (10^−10.20). For the same 0.10 M concentration, [OH−] ≈ √(Kb C) is therefore greatest for NaD, and that solution has the highest pH. The strongest acid (HA) has the weakest conjugate base, so NaA is the least basic of the four salts, not the most basic. All four conjugate bases hydrolyse to some extent; pKa = 7 is not a switch that turns hydrolysis on.

distractorRationales.A: The strongest acid has the weakest conjugate base. NaA therefore has the smallest Kb and the lowest pH among the four salts.
distractorRationales.B: There is no special maximum in hydrolysis at pKa 5. Hydrolysis of the conjugate base increases monotonically as pKa of HA increases.
distractorRationales.C: Even salts of acids with pKa < 7 (acetate, formate) give pH > 7. The ranking is still set by Kb, which is largest for NaD.

items.stem: An air bubble trapped in a vein has volume 0.20 mL at 2.0 atm. It is carried to the lung, where the surrounding pressure is 1.0 atm. If temperature and the amount of gas are constant, the bubble volume becomes:
items.explanation: Boyle's law at constant n and T is P1 V1 = P2 V2. Halving the pressure doubles the volume: 2.0 atm times 0.20 mL equals 1.0 atm times V2, so V2 = 0.40 mL. The bubble expands as it moves to a lower-pressure region. Inverting the pressure ratio, or assuming volume is pressure-independent, is inconsistent with the ideal-gas law.

distractorRationales.A: This quarters the volume, as if both P and V moved in the same direction or the pressure ratio were squared and inverted incorrectly.
distractorRationales.B: This halves the volume as pressure halves, which is the inverted Boyle relation (V proportional to P instead of 1/P).
distractorRationales.C: Volume is not invariant when pressure changes at fixed T and n; that would require a rigid container, not a bubble.

items.stem: During prolonged fasting, hepatic mitochondria convert acetyl-CoA to acetoacetate and 3-hydroxybutyrate, which are released to blood. Extrahepatic tissues oxidize these ketones, but the liver itself cannot use them as fuel. Which enzymatic gap explains the liver’s inability to consume the ketone bodies it produces?

choices.text: Liver lacks mitochondrial HMG-CoA synthase, so it cannot make ketones in the first place.
Liver lacks succinyl-CoA:acetoacetate CoA-transferase (thiophorase), so it cannot activate acetoacetate to acetoacetyl-CoA.
Liver lacks 3-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase, so 3-hydroxybutyrate cannot be formed or reoxidized.
Liver mitochondria have no succinyl-CoA, so the citric acid cycle cannot run in hepatocytes.

items.explanation: Ketone utilization in muscle, brain, and kidney begins by activating acetoacetate to acetoacetyl-CoA using succinyl-CoA:acetoacetate CoA-transferase (thiophorase). Hepatocytes lack this enzyme, which prevents a futile cycle in which the liver would remake and then re-consume ketones. Liver does contain mitochondrial HMG-CoA synthase (the committed ketogenic enzyme) and 3-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase, which is why it can produce both acetoacetate and 3-hydroxybutyrate. Succinyl-CoA is a normal citric-acid-cycle intermediate in liver; its presence is not the missing factor. Extrahepatic tissues then split acetoacetyl-CoA to acetyl-CoA for the cycle.

distractorRationales.A: Mitochondrial HMG-CoA synthase is present in liver and is required for ketogenesis; its absence would prevent ketone production, contradicting the stem.
distractorRationales.C: Hepatic 3-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase is how liver generates 3-hydroxybutyrate from acetoacetate; the enzyme is not absent.
distractorRationales.D: Liver mitochondria operate the citric acid cycle and contain succinyl-CoA. Lack of succinyl-CoA is not the reason ketones are exported rather than oxidized locally.

items.stem: A patient with influenza stays home from the wards, is not blamed for being ill, is expected to try to get well, and is expected to seek competent medical advice. Parsons’s sick role, as an account of medicine as an institution, includes which pair of rights and obligations?

choices.text: Exemption from normal duties and from blame, plus obligations to want recovery and to seek help
A right to remain ill indefinitely with no obligation to consult a physician
Marx’s claim that medicine exists only to reproduce labor power, which forbids any sick-role rights
The hidden curriculum of K–12 schooling as the definition of the sick role

items.explanation: Parsons modeled the sick role as a patterned, socially controlled deviation: the sick person is exempt from ordinary roles and not held responsible for the condition, but must treat illness as undesirable and cooperate with technically competent healers. That is how medicine as an institution manages illness. Unlimited right to remain ill without help contradicts those obligations. Marxian critiques of medicine are a different theoretical register. The hidden curriculum is a schooling concept (Jackson; Bowles and Gintis), not the sick role.

distractorRationales.B: Parsons required the obligation to seek help and to want to get well.
distractorRationales.C: Conflict critiques do not erase Parsons’s named four-part role as the standard MCAT account.
distractorRationales.D: Hidden curriculum belongs to education, not the influenza sick role.

items.stem: In a minimal-group experiment, strangers are randomly labeled Klee or Kandinsky fans after a coin flip. They then allocate points to unknown others identified only by label. People give more points to in-group members even though no interaction or conflicting interest exists. This result most directly supports:

choices.text: Social identity: mere categorization into a group can create in-group favoritism without a history of realistic conflict
Looking-glass self, because a mirror was required to assign the labels
A theory-of-mind failure, because participants cannot represent that out-group members have minds
Demographic transition among art fans, which predicts point giving in stage 2 only

items.explanation: Social identity theory (and the minimal-group paradigm) holds that self-concept includes group memberships, and that even arbitrary, newly assigned categories can produce in-group bias. No prior competition for scarce resources is required, which distinguishes this from a purely realistic-conflict story. Looking-glass self is about reflected individual appraisals, not coin-flip teams. Favoring an in-group does not mean denying that out-group members have minds. Demographic transition is a population-level birth/death model, not a point-allocation psychology.

distractorRationales.B: No mirror procedure is described; labels came from a coin flip.
distractorRationales.C: Allocating fewer points is bias, not a clinical ToM deficit.
distractorRationales.D: Art-preference labels are not fertility and mortality stages.

items.stem:
Propene is treated in three flasks. Major organic products:

Reagent | major product (after work-up)
HBr | 2-bromopropane
HBr / peroxides | 1-bromopropane
Br2 / CCl4 | 1,2-dibromopropane
H2 / Pt | propane

Markovnikov addition places H on the less substituted carbon. Which statement matches the table?

choices.text: All four reagents give 2-bromopropane
H2/Pt yields 1,2-dibromopropane because platinum brominates
Peroxides reverse Br2 addition, giving 1-bromopropane from Br2/CCl4
Ionic HBr is Markovnikov; peroxide HBr is anti-Markovnikov radical addition; Br2 adds across the double bond; H2/Pt saturates it

items.explanation: Ionic addition of HBr to propene yields the secondary bromide 2-bromopropane (Markovnikov). Peroxides switch the mechanism to bromine-atom addition at the terminal carbon, giving 1-bromopropane. Molecular bromine adds to give the vicinal dibromide. Catalytic hydrogenation removes the π bond entirely, giving propane, not an organobromide. The four rows are four different products, so they cannot all be 2-bromopropane. Platinum is a hydrogenation catalyst here, not a bromine source. Peroxides are specified for HBr, not for Br2/CCl4.

distractorRationales.A: The table lists four different products, only the first of which is 2-bromopropane.
distractorRationales.B: H2/Pt gives propane, the saturated hydrocarbon.
distractorRationales.C: Br2/CCl4 is listed as 1,2-dibromopropane regardless of peroxides, which were used only in the HBr row.

items.stem: A 0.10 M solution of HF (Ka = 6.8 × 10^−4) has [H3O+] ≈ 8.2 × 10^−3 M. Solid NaF is then dissolved to make the solution 0.10 M in F− as well (volume change negligible). What happens to [H3O+]?

choices.text: It increases because NaF is a strong electrolyte that adds extra H3O+.
It decreases because the added fluoride (common ion) shifts HF ⇌ H+ + F− toward undissociated HF.
It is unchanged because Ka is a constant.
It decreases to zero because fluoride completely consumes H3O+.

items.explanation: Le Chatelier’s principle applied to HF ⇌ H3O+ + F− says that adding F− from NaF drives the equilibrium left, lowering [H3O+] and decreasing the percent ionization of HF. After the addition, [H3O+] ≈ Ka [HF]/[F−] ≈ 6.8 × 10^−4, about an order of magnitude below the original 8.2 × 10^−3 M. Ka itself is unchanged; concentrations adjust so that the quotient again equals Ka. NaF is a salt, not a source of H3O+. Residual acid remains, so [H3O+] does not fall to zero.

distractorRationales.A: Na+ and F− are the ions of a salt; fluoride is a base, not an acid, and does not add H3O+.
distractorRationales.C: Ka is constant, but that does not freeze [H3O+]. The ratio [H3O+][F−]/[HF] stays equal to Ka while the individual concentrations change.
distractorRationales.D: The common-ion shift reduces [H3O+] but leaves a weak-acid equilibrium with a small, nonzero [H3O+].

items.stem:
[H+] is measured for two monoprotic acids over a range of formal concentrations C at 25 °C:

C (mol L−1) | Acid X: [H+] (mol L−1) | Acid Y: [H+] (mol L−1)
0.010 | 0.010 | 1.0 × 10^−3
0.040 | 0.040 | 2.0 × 10^−3
0.090 | 0.090 | 3.0 × 10^−3

For a weak acid, [H+] ≈ √(Ka C). Which description fits both columns?

choices.text: X and Y are both strong; the Y column must be a unit error because [H+] should always equal C.
X is weak with Ka = 1.0 × 10^−4 and Y is strong, because only Y has [H+] far below C.
X is a strong monoprotic acid ([H+] = C). Y is a weak acid with Ka = 1.0 × 10^−4, because [H+] = √(Ka C) at each row.
Y is a strong diprotic acid, because [H+] is three times larger at 0.090 M than at 0.010 M.

items.explanation: Acid X matches [H+] = C at every row, which is the hallmark of a fully dissociated monoprotic acid. Acid Y follows [H+] ∝ √C: √0.010 : √0.040 : √0.090 = 0.10 : 0.20 : 0.30, and the table is 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 × 10^−3, the same ratios. Then Ka = [H+]^2 / C. Using the first Y row, (1.0 × 10^−3)^2 / 0.010 = 1.0 × 10^−4, and the other rows give the same Ka. A strong diprotic acid would give [H+] closer to 2C, not a square-root dependence. Swapping which acid is strong contradicts the X column, where [H+] equals C.

distractorRationales.A: Y’s [H+] is far below C and scales as √C, which is incompatible with complete dissociation. The Y column is chemically consistent, not a unit error.
distractorRationales.B: X has [H+] = C, so X is the strong acid. Y is the weak one. This option reverses the assignments.
distractorRationales.D: A factor of three in [H+] when C increases ninefold is the square-root law, not evidence of two protons. A strong diprotic acid would not give [H+] = 0.0030 M from 0.090 M.

items.stem:
Relative catalytic activity of a cysteine protease is plotted against pH:

pH | relative activity (%)
4 | 8
5 | 25
6 | 70
7 | 100
8 | 80
9 | 20
10 | 4

The mechanism requires a histidine (pKa ≈ 6.2) to be deprotonated so it can accept a proton, and a cysteine (pKa ≈ 8.3) to be protonated in the resting enzyme so the thiol is available for activation. Which statement is consistent with the profile and those pKa values?

choices.text: The acidic limb (pH 4–6) tracks protonation of histidine, which removes the required base, while the alkaline limb (pH 8–10) tracks deprotonation of cysteine.
Maximum activity at pH 7 shows that both residues must be fully protonated.
The enzyme is inactive at pH 4 because the peptide substrate is uncharged only in base.
Activity collapses above pH 9 mainly because the essential histidine becomes protonated.

items.explanation: For His to act as a base it must be deprotonated, which becomes true as pH rises through 6.2, matching the climb from 8% at pH 4 to 100% at pH 7. For the thiol to remain in the activatable resting state it must stay protonated, which fails as pH exceeds 8.3, matching the fall to 20% then 4%. Peak activity at pH 7 sits between the two pKa values. The alkaline drop is therefore Cys deprotonation, not His protonation, which would occur on the acidic side.

distractorRationales.B: Fully protonated His would be the inactive acidic form; the pH 7 maximum is the mixed protonation state between the two pKa values.
distractorRationales.C: The stem assigns the pH dependence to catalytic residues, not to a requirement that the substrate be uncharged.
distractorRationales.D: Histidine protonation occurs on the low-pH side of pKa 6.2, not above pH 9.

items.stem: Take hc = 1240 eV nm. Light of wavelength 400 nm falls on a metal with work function φ = 2.0 eV. Photon energy E = hc/λ. Maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons is K_max = E − φ, and the stopping potential satisfies e Vs = K_max. The threshold wavelength is λ0 = hc/φ. Which set is consistent?

choices.text: E = 2.0 eV; K_max = 0; emission at every λ
E = 3.1 eV; K_max = 1.1 eV; λ0 = 400 nm, so 400 nm is already the threshold
E = 3.1 eV; K_max = 1.1 eV; Vs = 1.1 V; λ0 = 620 nm
E = 3.1 eV; K_max = 5.1 eV (adding φ); λ0 = 400 nm

items.explanation: E = 1240/400 = 3.1 eV. Then K_max = 3.1 − 2.0 = 1.1 eV, so Vs = 1.1 V. Threshold: λ0 = 1240/2.0 = 620 nm. Photons less energetic than 2.0 eV (λ > 620 nm) give no emission. Adding φ instead of subtracting would invent 5.1 eV electrons. E is not equal to φ at 400 nm. If 400 nm were threshold, φ would be 3.1 eV, contradicting the given 2.0 eV. Intensity does not appear because K_max is set by one photon’s leftover energy.

distractorRationales.A: E = 3.1 eV at 400 nm, well above φ, so K_max is not zero and emission is not possible at every λ.
distractorRationales.B: K_max = 1.1 eV is right, but that leftover proves 400 nm is above threshold; λ0 is 620 nm.
distractorRationales.D: φ is subtracted, not added; leftover energy is 1.1 eV. Threshold is 620 nm, not the illuminating 400 nm.

items.stem: A radiolabeled, lipid-soluble hormone accumulates in target-cell nuclei and co-immunoprecipitates with a zinc-finger DNA-binding protein that occupies hormone-response elements. The hormone is acting most like:

choices.text: Insulin, which binds a receptor tyrosine kinase at the plasma membrane
Epinephrine, which signals through a Gs-coupled adrenergic receptor
Acetylcholine at nicotinic receptors, opening a ligand-gated cation channel
Cortisol or another steroid, which binds an intracellular receptor that regulates transcription

items.explanation: Steroid hormones are lipid-derived (from cholesterol, a triterpene relative) and cross membranes to bind intracellular receptors. Liganded steroid receptors are transcription factors with zinc-finger DNA-binding domains that sit on hormone-response elements, matching the nuclear co-IP. Peptide hormones and catecholamines bind cell-surface receptors and do not accumulate as nuclear DNA-binding complexes of this type. Nicotinic ACh is an ionotropic neurotransmitter, not a nuclear lipid messenger. The slow genomic actions of steroids follow from this transcriptional mechanism, unlike seconds-scale second-messenger cascades.

distractorRationales.A: Insulin’s receptor is a membrane RTK; the hormone does not co-IP with nuclear zinc-finger receptors as the primary complex.
distractorRationales.B: Epinephrine is a hydrophilic catecholamine acting at GPCRs, not a nuclear steroid receptor ligand.
distractorRationales.C: Nicotinic ACh receptors are ligand-gated channels at membranes, not nuclear DNA-binding proteins.

items.stem: A rigid, massless board is balanced on a fulcrum. A 2 kg mass sits 3 m to the left of the fulcrum. What mass placed 1 m to the right of the fulcrum produces static equilibrium? Take g = 10 m/s^2.

choices.text: 2 kg
3 kg
6 kg
8 kg

items.explanation: Static equilibrium of a rigid body requires zero net torque about the fulcrum (and zero net force, which the fulcrum can supply). Taking counterclockwise as positive, (2 kg)(10 m/s^2)(3 m) = m (10 m/s^2)(1 m), so m = 6 kg. Gravity cancels, leaving the lever rule m1 d1 = m2 d2. A smaller mass on a longer arm balances a larger mass on a shorter arm: 2 kg at 3 m matches 6 kg at 1 m.

distractorRationales.A: Equal masses would balance only if the lever arms were equal. The left arm is three times the right arm, so the right-hand mass must be three times 2 kg.
distractorRationales.B: This averages the given numbers or uses 2 kg times 3 m / 2 m. Torque balance uses the actual 1 m right-hand arm, not an invented 2 m.
distractorRationales.D: This adds 2 + 3 + 3 or otherwise combines the given figures without using torque = force times perpendicular lever arm.

items.stem: As cultural criticism of news, the researcher’s project is closest to saying that

choices.text: style sheets of reporting verbs are already a politics of credibility, not a transparent pane.
newspapers should stop using verbs.
The Signal is the only honest paper because it “revealed.”
talkback is the authentic voice of the city.

items.explanation: Four grammars, one statement, speaking never only speaking: the critic treats verb choice as cultural work on authority. B is a cartoon ban. C treats revealed as truth rather than as another grammar (The Signal stacks it). D contradicts the exercise, which decentres the host. Arts-and-cultural-criticism here is about media form, which this table is built to teach.

distractorRationales.B: The point is how verbs interpret, not that they should vanish.
distractorRationales.C: Revealed is one patterned choice among four, not a halo.
distractorRationales.D: The host is an object of critique, not a gold standard.

passage.title: Table: Verbs in the morning
passage.body:
A media researcher counts finite verbs in the first paragraphs of four papers on the same Monday, all covering the same ministry announcement.

Paper | “said” | “claimed” | “admitted” | “revealed” | “insisted” | Other verbs of speaking
North Evening | 12 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 2
Civic Daily | 3 | 8 | 1 | 0 | 4 | 1
Harbour Post | 7 | 1 | 6 | 0 | 0 | 3
The Signal | 2 | 2 | 0 | 9 | 1 | 2

Caption under the table, written by the researcher: “Speaking is never only speaking. The ministry released one statement. The city woke in four grammars.”

A talkback host that night: “This is just synonyms. Nobody is doing politics with a verb chart. Grow up.”

items.stem: A premed who doubts her ability watches a near-peer master a difficult OSCE station, then raises her own practice time and her predicted score. Bandura’s social-cognitive theory names the reciprocal loop among person, behavior, and environment and would highlight which process here?

choices.text: Oral-stage fixation in Freud’s psychosexual scheme, because watching is a feeding equivalent
Eysenckian extraversion driven by a chronically under-aroused ARAS
Observational learning and a rise in self-efficacy, within reciprocal determinism
Maslowian self-actualization as the only named cause of studying

items.explanation: Bandura’s social-cognitive theory includes observational learning, self-efficacy, and reciprocal determinism (person ↔ behavior ↔ environment). Seeing a similar model succeed can raise efficacy and change study behavior, which then changes the environment of future exams. Freud’s oral stage does not describe OSCE modeling. Eysenck’s biological extraversion is a trait-arousal theory, not vicarious mastery. Maslow’s hierarchy is a need theory of motivation, not this modeling mechanism.

distractorRationales.A: Psychosexual stages do not explain vicarious OSCE mastery.
distractorRationales.B: ARAS extraversion is not the process of watching a peer and then studying more.
distractorRationales.D: Self-actualization is not the specific social-cognitive mechanism named in the stem.

items.stem: A researcher studying anaplerosis in liver mitochondria finds that adding pyruvate plus bicarbonate increases the oxaloacetate pool and accelerates citrate formation from acetyl-CoA. The responsible enzyme requires biotin and is allosterically activated by acetyl-CoA. Which reaction is occurring?

choices.text: Pyruvate kinase converting PEP to pyruvate, which cannot be a net gain of cycle intermediates
Pyruvate dehydrogenase running in reverse to carboxylate acetyl-CoA to pyruvate
Pyruvate carboxylase converting pyruvate plus CO2 to oxaloacetate
ATP-citrate lyase producing oxaloacetate in the mitochondrial matrix from cytosolic citrate

items.explanation: Pyruvate carboxylase is the principal anaplerotic enzyme in liver mitochondria: it carboxylates pyruvate to oxaloacetate using biotin as a CO2 carrier and is allosterically activated by acetyl-CoA, matching every experimental clue. The new four-carbon unit can condense with acetyl-CoA at citrate synthase, so citrate formation rises. Pyruvate kinase makes pyruvate, not OAA, and is not biotin-dependent. PDH is irreversible in animals and does not carboxylate acetyl-CoA. ATP-citrate lyase is cytosolic, generating acetyl-CoA for fatty-acid synthesis, not a mitochondrial biotin enzyme that fills the oxaloacetate pool.

distractorRationales.A: Pyruvate kinase produces pyruvate from PEP and is not a biotin-dependent carboxylase; it does not replenish oxaloacetate.
distractorRationales.B: Pyruvate dehydrogenase is irreversible under physiologic conditions and is inhibited, not reversed, by acetyl-CoA. It does not add CO2 to acetyl-CoA.
distractorRationales.D: ATP-citrate lyase is cytosolic (citrate + ATP + CoA → acetyl-CoA + OAA + ADP + Pi) and does not require biotin or reside in the matrix as the anaplerotic fill reaction described.

items.stem: A straight wire of length 10 m carries a current of 2 A perpendicular to a uniform 1.0 T magnetic field. The magnitude of the magnetic force on the wire is:
items.explanation: A current-carrying wire in a magnetic field feels F = I L B sin θ. With I = 2 A, L = 10 m, B = 1.0 T, and θ = 90° (sin 90° = 1), F = (2)(10)(1) = 20 N. The direction would be given by a right-hand rule, but the question asks only for magnitude. Dropping the length or the current undercounts by a factor of 10 or 2. The formula is linear in I, L, and B; there is no extra trigonometric factor once the current is already perpendicular to B.

distractorRationales.A: This looks like I B / L or a units slip that buried the 10 m. F = I L B uses the product, so the 10 m length raises the force, not lowers it.
distractorRationales.B: This is I B with L omitted (or L taken as 1 m). A 10 m wire has ten times the current-length product of a 1 m wire in the same field.
distractorRationales.C: This combination of 10 + 2 or 10 × 1 + 2 is dimensional nonsense. All three of I, L, and B multiply.

items.stem: HCl infused into the duodenum of a fasting animal raises plasma secretin and pancreatic bicarbonate output. Cutting the vagus does not abolish the bicarbonate response. The dominant mechanism is:

choices.text: CCK released from gastric G cells acting on pancreatic acini to secrete trypsinogen as bicarbonate
Pepsin from pancreatic duct cells, stimulated only by vagal preganglionic fibers
Secretin from duodenal S cells acting hormonally on pancreatic ductal epithelium to secrete HCO3-
Direct titration of pancreatic juice by duodenal acid without any endocrine cell involvement

items.explanation: Duodenal acid is the physiologic stimulus for S cells to release secretin. Secretin travels in blood to pancreatic duct cells, raises cAMP, and drives bicarbonate-rich secretion that neutralizes chyme. Persistence after vagotomy shows a hormonal, not solely neural, reflex. CCK is released from I cells in response to fat and protein and primarily stimulates enzyme secretion and gallbladder contraction, not this acid-bicarbonate pairing. G cells make gastrin in the stomach, pepsin is a gastric protease, and duct cells do not dump pepsin. Acid does not magically become pancreatic juice without secretin.

distractorRationales.A: G cells secrete gastrin, not CCK, and CCK is not the acid-evoked bicarbonate hormone.
distractorRationales.B: Pepsin is gastric; the vagus is unnecessary here by experimental design.
distractorRationales.D: The rise in plasma secretin identifies an endocrine mediator.

items.stem: Unpolarized light of intensity I0 is incident on two ideal linear polarizers placed in series with their transmission axes perpendicular. The intensity after the second polarizer is:

choices.text: essentially zero
I0

items.explanation: An ideal polarizer passes the component of the electric field along its axis. Unpolarized light exits the first polarizer with intensity I0 / 2 and with a definite polarization. Malus's law then gives I = (I0 / 2) cos^2 phi at the second polarizer. For perpendicular axes, phi = 90 degrees and cos phi = 0, so no field component remains to be transmitted. I0 / 4 would describe two 45-degree steps or two independent factors of 1/2 without the 90-degree geometry.

distractorRationales.A: This is the intensity after a single polarizer acting on unpolarized light, before the crossed second polarizer extinguishes the beam.
distractorRationales.C: I0/4 is the crossed-polarizer result only if someone applies two factors of 1/2 and ignores that the second factor is cos^2 90 = 0, or if the axes were at 45 degrees twice in a different setup.
distractorRationales.D: Unpolarized light does not pass a pair of crossed polarizers at full intensity; the second polarizer is orthogonal to the field that leaves the first.

items.stem: Ouabain blocks Na+/K+ ATPase in a neuron that still has Na+ and K+ leak pathways. Over the following minutes, the most direct effect is that:

choices.text: intracellular Na+ falls because extrusion of Na+ continues
the Na+ electrochemical gradient dissipates as Na+ leaks inward and is not pumped out
intracellular K+ rises above its usual steady-state value
the lipid bilayer becomes freely permeable to cytosolic proteins

items.explanation: The pump continuously extrudes three Na+ ions and imports two K+ ions, maintaining steep gradients against leak. When the pump is blocked, leak is unopposed: Na+ runs down its gradient into the cell and K+ leaks out, so both gradients run down and the membrane slowly depolarizes. The bilayer's permeability to proteins is unchanged. Intracellular Na+ therefore rises rather than falls, and intracellular K+ falls rather than rises.

distractorRationales.A: Extrusion of Na+ is what the ATPase does. Blocking it stops extrusion, so intracellular Na+ rises as Na+ leaks in.
distractorRationales.C: Without the pump, K+ is not reaccumulated; it leaks out, so intracellular K+ falls.
distractorRationales.D: Cardiac glycosides inhibit the pump protein; they do not punch nonspecific holes that dump macromolecules.

items.stem: Mock jurors who individually lean slightly toward conviction become, after deliberation, much more confident that the defendant is guilty. Stoner’s risky shift was an early case of the same family of findings. Which label and mechanism best fit?

choices.text: Groupthink: the jury must have had a mindguard and an illusion of invulnerability, which is required for any extremity shift
Normative social influence as in Asch, which always produces a moderate, never more extreme, consensus
Social facilitation (Zajonc): mere presence of co-actors multiplies the dominant conviction response without discussion
Group polarization: discussion amplifies the group’s already-favored pole via persuasive arguments and social comparison

items.explanation: Group polarization is the finding that like-minded discussion makes the average position more extreme in the initially favored direction. Persuasive-arguments and social-comparison accounts (and the older risky-shift literature Stoner began) explain it. Groupthink is defective decision quality from suppressed dissent, not the same as a lawful extremity shift. Asch conformity can yield a wrong majority, but it is not defined as extremity amplification. Zajonc’s mere-presence facilitation does not require deliberation and is not a jury-discussion theory.

distractorRationales.A: Groupthink is not a required diagnosis for every polarization finding.
distractorRationales.B: Asch-style conformity does not imply that group means cannot become more extreme.
distractorRationales.C: Mere presence without argument exchange is social facilitation, not deliberative polarization.

items.stem: A mixed sample of purified genomic DNA and cellular RNA is incubated in dilute sodium hydroxide at room temperature and then neutralized. Only DNA polymers remain intact. Which structural feature accounts for the selective degradation of RNA?

choices.text: RNA uses uracil, which is deprotonated by hydroxide and leaves the backbone as free base.
DNA lacks a 5′-phosphate, so it cannot undergo nucleophilic cleavage of phosphodiesters.
The C5 methyl of thymine sterically blocks hydroxide attack on DNA phosphodiesters.
The 2′-OH of ribose can be deprotonated and attack the adjacent phosphodiester, forming a 2′,3′-cyclic phosphate.

items.explanation: Alkaline cleavage of RNA is an intramolecular transesterification. Hydroxide deprotonates the ribose 2′-OH, which attacks the 3′-linked phosphorus and displaces the 5′ end of the next nucleotide, producing a 2′,3′-cyclic phosphate that subsequently hydrolyzes. DNA lacks a 2′-OH, so it cannot form that cyclic intermediate and is alkali-stable under the same conditions. Uracil versus thymine and the thymine methyl group do not explain backbone scission, and both polymers have 5′-phosphates in internucleotide linkages. This chemistry is why alkaline lysis can destroy RNA while leaving plasmid DNA intact.

distractorRationales.A: Uracil versus thymine does not make the phosphodiester alkali-labile; RNA with U still requires the 2′-OH for cleavage, and DNA with T is stable because it lacks that hydroxyl.
distractorRationales.B: DNA strands are connected by 5′-phosphates in phosphodiester bonds; the absence of a 2′-OH, not absence of a 5′-phosphate, explains alkali stability.
distractorRationales.C: Thymine’s methyl group is on the base, far from the internucleotide phosphate, and does not account for DNA’s resistance to dilute base.

items.stem: Taken together, the poem, the essay, the table, and the radio line most strongly invite the reader to

choices.text: treat every quoted voice as saying the same thing about citizenship
watch how a figure (kettle, stairs, surplus room) is reused and argued over across genres
compute the exact population of the building
discard the table as unrelated decoration

items.explanation: GAMSAT comparison items ask you to track a motif across quote-sets. Stairs, kettle, and surplus room recur in poem, essay, table, and radio, with disagreement (host vs Okonkwo). The set is not a single slogan, not a census of residents, and the table is thematically tied by the caption on attention.

distractorRationales.A: The host and Okonkwo explicitly diverge.
distractorRationales.C: No building population is given.
distractorRationales.D: The table is captioned into the argument about attention.

passage.title: Two ways of hearing a census
passage.body:
Poem (untitled, 2019)

We counted rooms as if rooms were people.
The spare one kept its coat on.
In the column for language we wrote the kettle.
Nobody asked the stairs their age.

Commentary by L. Okonkwo, catalogue essay for an exhibition of household inventories:
The poem is easy to misread as anti-data. It is not. It notices that a census already poetizes: it decides what may stand for a life (rooms, language, age) and what must remain downstairs, unasked. The coat on the spare room is not a joke about furniture. It is a figure for surplus — the part of a household that official forms cannot rent. When the poem puts a kettle in the language column, it is not claiming kettles speak. It is showing how quickly a form will accept a proxy if the proxy is small and warm.

A table printed beside the poem in the gallery listed visitors by hour and by whether they photographed the stairs:
Hour 10: 14 visitors, 2 photographed stairs
Hour 11: 31 visitors, 18 photographed stairs
Hour 12: 9 visitors, 0 photographed stairs (docent talk in progress)
The curator captioned the table: Attention is not the same as attendance.

A radio host later called the exhibition “political because it made a kettle into a citizen.” Okonkwo's essay had already refused that flattening. The political cut, for her, is not enfranchising objects. It is noticing which human details a state is willing to miss.

items.stem: A mutant citric-acid-cycle enzyme cannot generate GTP (or ATP) even though NADH can still be produced from succinate via later steps. Which enzyme is most likely deficient?

choices.text: Aconitase, which hydrates citrate to isocitrate without phosphoryl transfer
Isocitrate dehydrogenase, which reduces NAD+ but does not form GTP
Succinate dehydrogenase, which reduces enzyme-bound FAD and feeds Complex II
Succinyl-CoA synthetase (succinyl-CoA ligase), which performs substrate-level phosphorylation

items.explanation: The only substrate-level phosphorylation in the citric acid cycle is the conversion of succinyl-CoA to succinate by succinyl-CoA synthetase, which conserves the thioester energy as GTP (or ATP, depending on isoform). Aconitase, isocitrate dehydrogenase, and succinate dehydrogenase do not form GTP. Supplying succinate bypasses succinyl-CoA synthetase and still allows SDH, fumarase, and malate dehydrogenase to generate FADH2/NADH, matching the stem. Loss of isocitrate dehydrogenase would cut NADH from that step and would not be rescued in the GTP phenotype by succinate in the way described. Thus the GTP-specific defect localizes to succinyl-CoA synthetase.

distractorRationales.A: Aconitase isomerizes citrate to isocitrate via cis-aconitate and does not generate GTP or ATP, so its loss would not uniquely explain a missing substrate-level phosphorylation.
distractorRationales.B: Isocitrate dehydrogenase produces NADH and CO2, not GTP. A defect there would reduce NADH from isocitrate, contrary to a GTP-only phenotype with intact succinate oxidation.
distractorRationales.C: Succinate dehydrogenase produces FADH2 equivalents, not GTP. The stem also says NADH from later steps still forms when succinate is supplied, which requires this enzyme to work.

items.stem: A spinal-injury clinic re-interviews adults who had complete thoracic transection years earlier. Compared with their own pre-injury descriptions, patients still classify scenes as frightening or funny, but they say the “heat” of those feelings is weaker, especially for states that used to come with a pounding heart. Autonomic recordings below the lesion are flat. Which theory most directly predicts the drop in felt intensity?

choices.text: James–Lange theory, because the feeling of emotion depends on detecting bodily change
Cannon–Bard theory, because experience is fully independent of the body, so intensity cannot fall
Schachter–Singer theory, because a missing body makes any situational label impossible
Opponent-process theory, because every emotion automatically elicits its opposite and cancels intensity

items.explanation: James–Lange theory treats conscious emotion as perception of bodily change, including visceral and autonomic feedback that travels in part through the spinal cord. Interrupting that afferent traffic should therefore blunt intensity even when the person can still identify the situation as frightening or amusing. Cannon–Bard theory instead treats the feeling as a parallel central event and does not predict this selective dulling after deafferentation. Two-factor theory emphasizes labeling of unexplained arousal rather than loss of spinal feedback. Opponent-process theory concerns sequential opposite emotions, not bodily deafferentation.

distractorRationales.B: Cannon–Bard holds that feeling and physiology are triggered together by a central process, so cutting spinal autonomic traffic should not systematically weaken the feeling.
distractorRationales.C: Two-factor theory does not claim that a spinal lesion makes labeling impossible; people can still use context. It also does not uniquely predict intensity loss after transection.
distractorRationales.D: Opponent-process theory describes a later opposite reaction (for example, relief after fear), not a requirement for intact viscera.

items.stem: Erythrocytes from a patient with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency maintain near-normal ATP from glycolysis but cannot increase NADPH after an oxidative challenge. After primaquine exposure, hemoglobin is damaged and hemolysis occurs. Which role of the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway best explains the hemolysis?

choices.text: The pathway is the erythrocyte’s main source of ATP, so deficiency causes energy failure first
The pathway produces NADH that directly reduces methemoglobin via complex I
The pathway decarboxylates pyruvate, and loss of that step starves the TCA cycle in red cells
The pathway supplies NADPH that keeps glutathione reduced so that peroxides do not damage hemoglobin

items.explanation: Mature erythrocytes lack mitochondria and rely on glycolysis for ATP, which is intact in G6PD deficiency and therefore not the primary failure. The oxidative PPP, beginning at G6PD, is their principal source of NADPH. NADPH is the reductant for glutathione reductase; reduced glutathione and glutathione peroxidase detoxify H2O2 and lipid peroxides. Without NADPH, oxidative drugs such as primaquine overwhelm hemoglobin (Heinz bodies) and lyse the cell. The PPP produces NADPH, not NADH for a respiratory chain these cells do not have, and it does not decarboxylate pyruvate in red cells.

distractorRationales.A: The vignette states ATP is near normal; hemolysis here is oxidative, not an ATP-depletion syndrome.
distractorRationales.B: G6PD produces NADPH, not NADH, and erythrocytes do not run Complex I.
distractorRationales.C: Red cells have no TCA cycle; pyruvate decarboxylation is not the PPP’s role.

items.stem:
Oxygen evolution of a green algal suspension (relative units) is recorded at equal incident photon flux at each wavelength:

Wavelength (nm) | O2 evolution
430 | 100
480 | 85
550 | 18
650 | 72
680 | 96
700 | 12
720 | 3

Chlorophyll a absorption maxima lie near 430 and 680 nm; chlorophyll b contributes near 480 and 650 nm. Photosystem II photochemistry that splits water declines sharply beyond about 680 nm (Emerson red drop), whereas photosystem I can still absorb near 700 nm. Which conclusion follows?

choices.text: O2 evolution tracks chlorophyll absorption and collapses in far-red light even though PSI can still absorb, so water oxidation is tied to PSII.
The 700 nm point being low proves that chlorophyll does not absorb beyond 680 nm at all.
Equal photon flux at 430 and 700 nm must give equal O2 because both wavelengths are visible light.
The 550 nm trough shows that carotenoids are the main O2-evolving pigments.

items.explanation: High O2 at 430 and 680 nm matches chlorophyll a, with secondary peaks at 480 and 650 nm from chlorophyll b. Green-yellow light at 550 nm is poorly absorbed, so O2 is low. The further collapse at 700–720 nm is the red drop: PSI absorbs there but PSII, which oxidises water, does not drive non-cyclic electron flow efficiently. The action spectrum is therefore a chlorophyll-plus-PSII signature, not a statement that chlorophyll has zero absorbance at 700 nm or that all visible wavelengths are equivalent.

distractorRationales.B: PSI chlorophyll does absorb near 700 nm; the low O2 is a photochemical, not an absorption, failure of PSII.
distractorRationales.C: The table shows 100 versus 12 at those two wavelengths, so equal photon flux does not yield equal O2.
distractorRationales.D: Carotenoids absorb in the blue-green, but O2 is lowest at 550 nm and highest at the chlorophyll peaks, so they are not the O2-evolving pigments.

items.stem: Complete β-oxidation of a saturated odd-chain fatty acid (C17) yields acetyl-CoA plus a three-carbon piece. That piece can support net gluconeogenesis after biotin- and vitamin B12-dependent reactions. Which sequence is correct?

choices.text: Acetyl-CoA is carboxylated to pyruvate in mitochondria and then used for glucose.
The three-carbon piece is acetone, which is transaminated to alanine and then to glucose.
Propionyl-CoA is converted to methylmalonyl-CoA and then to succinyl-CoA, a gluconeogenic citric-acid-cycle intermediate.
Propionyl-CoA is converted to acetoacetate, which is strictly ketogenic and cannot make glucose.

items.explanation: Odd-chain fatty acids leave a terminal propionyl-CoA after the last complete two-carbon cleavage. Propionyl-CoA carboxylase (biotin) makes D-methylmalonyl-CoA, which is racemized and then rearranged by methylmalonyl-CoA mutase (adenosylcobalamin, vitamin B12) to succinyl-CoA. Succinyl-CoA can proceed to oxaloacetate and, via PEPCK, to net glucose, so odd-chain fat is partially glucogenic. Animals cannot convert acetyl-CoA to pyruvate in net amounts (PDH is irreversible; two carbons enter and two leave the cycle). Acetone is a ketone body from acetoacetate decarboxylation, not the three-carbon acyl leftover of odd-chain β-oxidation, and propionyl-CoA is not converted to acetoacetate as its primary fate.

distractorRationales.A: There is no net conversion of acetyl-CoA to pyruvate in human mitochondria; PDH is irreversible, so even-chain acetyl units are not glucogenic.
distractorRationales.B: The leftover of odd-chain β-oxidation is propionyl-CoA, not acetone. Acetone is not transaminated to alanine as a major gluconeogenic path.
distractorRationales.D: Propionyl-CoA is carboxylated and rearranged to succinyl-CoA, which is glucogenic; it is not routed primarily to acetoacetate.

items.stem: Sulfur tetrafluoride, SF4, has a steric number of 5 at sulfur. What molecular geometry (the arrangement of the four fluorines) does VSEPR predict?

choices.text: Tetrahedral
Square planar
Seesaw
Trigonal bipyramidal

items.explanation: Sulfur in SF4 has four bonding pairs and one lone pair, so five electron domains occupy a trigonal bipyramidal electron geometry. The lone pair occupies an equatorial site to minimize 90° lone-pair–bond-pair repulsions. The four fluorine atoms then occupy the remaining two axial positions and two equatorial positions, which is the seesaw molecular shape. Tetrahedral describes four electron domains, square planar describes XeF4 (four bonds plus two axial lone pairs), and trigonal bipyramidal would be the molecular shape only if there were five bonding pairs and no lone pair, as in PF5.

distractorRationales.A: Tetrahedral molecular geometry requires four electron domains and no extra lone pair, as in CH4 or SiF4, not steric number 5.
distractorRationales.B: Square planar is the molecular geometry of XeF4, which has two lone pairs opposite each other, not SF4’s single lone pair.
distractorRationales.D: Trigonal bipyramidal is the electron-domain geometry of SF4 and the molecular geometry of PF5, but it is not the molecular shape once one equatorial site is a lone pair.

items.stem: Eight minutes remain on a typed Task A. The draft has a clear thesis and a half-built example. Which move best protects clarity under timed typing?

choices.text: Begin a new introduction with a dictionary definition, then hope to loop back.
Finish the example in short independent sentences, add one counterargument sentence and one delimiting close; do not open a third example or a nested clause garden.
Write one 180-word sentence so the piece looks dense.
Stop thinking and hold the shift key to add visual emphasis instead of a close.

items.explanation: Timed typing rewards finishing a thought in readable units. Short independent sentences reduce tangle when there is no leisure to recast. A second example will not be earned. Nested gardens hide the thesis. Dictionary restarts waste the remaining clock. Capitals are not a close. The taxonomy’s point is sentence control without relying on later polish: type the claim, the case, the meeting of an objection, stop. B is that sequence. Markers can follow it; they cannot follow a last-minute syntactic monument. Clarity here is a time skill, not a handwriting skill.

distractorRationales.A: A late dictionary opening doubles the unfinished middle rather than closing it.
distractorRationales.C: A giant sentence is how control is lost when there is no time to edit.
distractorRationales.D: Emphasis without a close is panic, not communication.

items.stem: A uniform electric field of 10 N/C is directed from plate L toward plate R. The plates are 2.0 m apart. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: Plate R is at the higher potential, and |ΔV| between the plates is 20 V.
Plate L is at the higher potential, and |ΔV| between the plates is 20 V.
Plate L is at the higher potential, and |ΔV| between the plates is 5 V.
The plates are at equal potential because a uniform field means potential does not change with position.

items.explanation: By definition E points from higher electric potential toward lower potential, so plate L (where the field originates in this description) is at the higher V. In a uniform field the magnitude of the potential difference is |ΔV| = E d = (10 N/C)(2.0 m) = 20 V. A uniform field means E is constant, not that V is constant: V still drops linearly along the field. Dividing E by d instead of multiplying inverts the relation between field and potential difference.

distractorRationales.A: The field direction is high V to low V, so L, not R, is the high-potential plate. The 20 V magnitude is right but assigned to the wrong plate.
distractorRationales.C: L is the high-potential plate, but |ΔV| = E d = 20 V, not E/d = 5 V. Field is potential drop per meter, so you multiply by the 2 m gap.
distractorRationales.D: A uniform field is a constant slope of V versus position, not a flat potential. Only E = 0 would make the plates equipotential.

items.stem: Thesis: “Speed for the already-served is not automatically care.” Which paragraph is a steelman of the opposing view rather than a strawman?

choices.text: Opponents of my view simply enjoy watching the poor wait, which is why they exist.

A serious opposing view is that when delay itself causes harm—an untreated infection, a missed cancer window—then refusing speed is not humility about clocks but a decision to let damage run, and any justice-talk that ignores that harm is aesthetic.
Some people think waiting is fun, which is obviously stupid.
Nobody could disagree with me, so a counterargument would be dishonest.

items.explanation: A steelman states the strongest honest form of the other side before answering it. B uses the set’s own “speed is a form of care when the alternative is neglect” and specifies medical windows, which a waiting-justice thesis must meet. A and C insult motives or intelligence. D refuses the move entirely. Task A essays that never occupy the opposing chair read as sermons. The counterargument topic is not a requirement to surrender; it is a requirement to show that the thesis can survive the best version of “speed is care.” B is that version.

distractorRationales.A: Motive-smearing is a strawman of character, not a reconstruction of the neglect argument.
distractorRationales.C: “Waiting is fun” is not a view present in the set and is too silly to be worth answering.
distractorRationales.D: Disagreement is already staged by the comments; refusing to voice it is not integrity.

items.stem:
A 4000 bp plasmid has a single EcoRI site. A 1000 bp EcoRI fragment is ligated into that site. After ligation, DNA is linearised with EcoRI (complete digestion) and run on a gel.

Sample | observed band(s)
Uncut parental plasmid | fast supercoiled band (apparent ~2500 bp)
Parental plasmid + EcoRI | 4000 bp
Ligation + EcoRI | 4000 bp and 1000 bp
Self-ligated parental recircularised + EcoRI | 4000 bp only

Which conclusion is supported?

choices.text: EcoRI linearisation of recombinants must give a single 5000 bp band because the insert lacks EcoRI ends
A 1000 bp band proves contamination with genomic DNA of that length rather than insert release
Successful recombinants release the 1000 bp insert plus the 4000 bp backbone; empty recircularised plasmid yields only 4000 bp
The uncut apparent 2500 bp band is the true recombinant size (4000 + 1000 − 2500)

items.explanation: Cloning into a unique EcoRI site recreates EcoRI sites at both insert–vector junctions. Complete EcoRI digestion of a recombinant therefore cuts out the 1000 bp insert and leaves the 4000 bp vector, two bands. An empty plasmid cut at its one EcoRI site is a 4000 bp line. Supercoiled uncut DNA migrates anomalously fast (~2500 apparent), which is not a true size and not 4000+1000−2500 arithmetic. The insert was defined as an EcoRI fragment, so it does have EcoRI ends; a 5000 bp linear would appear only if a different enzyme that cuts once in the recombinant were used.

distractorRationales.A: EcoRI ends on the insert restore two EcoRI sites, so the recombinant should fall into 4000 + 1000, not remain 5000.
distractorRationales.B: The 1000 bp band matches the insert length used in the ligation; genomic contamination would not be a single clean 1000 bp species correlated with the ligation lane.
distractorRationales.D: Supercoiled mobility is not a reliable base-pair measure; 2500 is an apparent, not physical, size.

items.stem: An aircraft flies horizontally at 80 m s−1 at a height of 45 m and releases a supply crate. g = 10 m s−2; air resistance is neglected. The crate’s initial vertical velocity is 0. Time to the ground is found from h = (1/2) g t². Horizontal velocity remains 80 m s−1. How far down-range does the crate land, and what is its vertical speed on impact?

choices.text: 45 m down-range; vertical speed 0, because it was released not thrown
240 m down-range; vertical speed 30 m s−1
80 m down-range; vertical speed 45 m s−1
240 m down-range; vertical speed 80 m s−1

items.explanation: From 45 = 5 t², t² = 9, t = 3.0 s. Horizontal distance = 80 × 3.0 = 240 m. Vertical speed vy = g t = 30 m s−1. The horizontal speed is unchanged at 80 m s−1, but that is not the vertical component. Using t = 1 s (as if s = vt with v = 45) gives only 80 m of range. A dropped object still accelerates vertically; impact vertical speed is not zero. Independence of perpendicular components is the whole point of the calculation.

distractorRationales.A: Release with uy = 0 still allows free-fall acceleration; after 3 s, vy = 30 m s−1, and the crate has travelled 240 m horizontally.
distractorRationales.C: 80 m would be the range for a 1.0 s fall; t is 3.0 s from h = 5 t². Vertical speed is gt, not the height number 45.
distractorRationales.D: The range 240 m is right, but 80 m s−1 is the unchanged horizontal speed, not vy.

items.stem: In an oxygen-electrode experiment, mitochondria oxidizing NADH-linked substrates consume O2 rapidly after ADP is added. Oligomycin then arrests O2 consumption. Adding DNP restores O2 consumption without restoring ATP synthesis. Which explanation is consistent with these data?

choices.text: Oligomycin inhibits Complex IV; DNP chemically reduces oxygen, bypassing the chain.
Oligomycin blocks proton flow through ATP synthase, stalling the chain; DNP lets protons re-enter without ATP synthase, restarting electron flow while synthase remains inhibited.
DNP reverses oligomycin binding at the F1 catalytic sites, fully restoring coupled phosphorylation.
Oligomycin uncouples the membrane, and DNP subsequently blocks ATP synthase.

items.explanation: Oligomycin binds the F0 proton channel of ATP synthase, so protons cannot re-enter the matrix through the synthase. The proton-motive force rises until electron transport is thermodynamically stalled and O2 consumption stops, even though Complex IV is intact. DNP provides an alternate proton re-entry path, collapsing the gradient and allowing the respiratory chain to run again, which restores oxygen uptake. ATP synthase remains blocked, so ATP is not restored. That pattern distinguishes ATP-synthase inhibition from Complex IV poisons such as cyanide, which DNP cannot rescue, and from true uncoupling as the primary action of oligomycin.

distractorRationales.A: Oligomycin’s target is ATP synthase, not Complex IV. DNP is a protonophore, not a chemical reductant of O2 that bypasses cytochrome oxidase.
distractorRationales.C: DNP does not competitively displace oligomycin from F1 to restore coupled ATP synthesis; phosphorylation remains inhibited in the experiment.
distractorRationales.D: This choice reverses the two drugs’ mechanisms: oligomycin is the ATP-synthase blocker and DNP is the uncoupler.

items.stem: A reverse-phase C18 HPLC column is equilibrated in 95:5 water/acetonitrile and then eluted with a gradient of increasing acetonitrile. Two peptides are injected: KKKKK (all lysine) and FFFFF (all phenylalanine). Which elution order is expected, and why?

choices.text: FFFFF first, because reverse-phase stationary phases retain polar solutes more strongly than nonpolar ones
KKKKK first, because the hydrophobic C18 phase retains the aromatic peptide while the highly charged oligolysine prefers the aqueous mobile phase
They coelute, because HPLC cannot distinguish peptides of equal residue count
KKKKK first, because C18 silica is a cation-exchange resin that binds lysine and therefore must be eluted last

items.explanation: Reverse-phase chromatography uses a nonpolar stationary phase (typically C18-bonded silica) and a polar aqueous mobile phase. Hydrophobic solutes partition into the alkyl chains and require more organic modifier to elute. Penta-phenylalanine is aromatic and poorly hydrated, so it is retained. Penta-lysine is polycationic and highly water-soluble at acidic or near-neutral pH, so it spends little time on C18 and emerges early in a water-rich gradient. Residue count alone does not set retention. C18 is not an ion-exchange resin; sulfonated or carboxylate resins are.

distractorRationales.A: That statement describes normal-phase (polar) chromatography. Reverse-phase retains hydrophobics, not polars.
distractorRationales.C: Equal length does not imply equal hydrophobicity; lysine and phenylalanine side chains interact very differently with C18.
distractorRationales.D: C18 is a hydrophobic bonded phase, not a cation exchanger. Oligolysine elutes first because it is polar, not because it is ionically stuck.

items.stem: An atom has the ground-state valence configuration 4s^2 4p^5. This element is best classified as:

choices.text: a halogen (group 17)
an alkaline earth metal (group 2)
a noble gas (group 18)
a d-block transition metal

items.explanation: Valence 4s^2 4p^5 means seven valence electrons in period 4, which is the halogen configuration (group 17); the element is bromine. Alkaline earth metals are ns^2 only (here that would be 4s^2 with an empty 4p). Noble gases are ns^2 np^6 (4s^2 4p^6 would be krypton). Transition metals place electrons in (n−1)d subshells; a configuration quoted as 4s^2 4p^5 is p-block, not d-block. Group number for the p-block follows the valence count: 5 + 2 = 7 valence electrons → group 17.

distractorRationales.B: Alkaline earth atoms are ns^2 (two valence electrons), for example 4s^2 for calcium. The additional 4p^5 puts this atom in the p-block halogens.
distractorRationales.C: Noble gases have filled np^6. This configuration is one electron short of 4p^6, which is exactly the halogen pattern.
distractorRationales.D: Transition metals are d-block (incomplete (n−1)d). A 4p^5 count is a main-group p-block element, not a transition metal.

items.stem: The combination of a giant sat-upon stethoscope and a politely typeset postponement is best described as

choices.text: sincere instructional design for new clinic staff.
tragic realism without irony, because cash registers commonly appear in waiting rooms as medical equipment.
satire that uses understatement in the caption and grotesque scale in the image to evaluate whose hearing counts.
affectionate celebration of boards who multitask by listening to receipts.

items.explanation: Satire and understatement: the caption's we'll-call-you is the mild public language of triage; the image is not mild. Grotesque scale (ticket as door, patients as dotted outlines, earpieces on BOARD) evaluates without a ranting label. The tone is not a training poster, not a documentary claim that tills are auscultation devices, and not affection. Non-literal evaluative language is the polite sentence doing the work of a knife. Recognising that pairing is the skill the item tags.

distractorRationales.A: Nothing in the described frame instructs staff in a sincere protocol; the dotted patients and till make mockery, not a handbook.
distractorRationales.B: A cash register as the thing being listened to is ironic substitution, not unironic realism.
distractorRationales.D: Listening to a till while patients remain unfinished is the critique, not a compliment for multitasking.

passage.title: When your number becomes a priority
passage.body:
[Image]
A waiting-room drawn as a long, low shed. The bench is actually the tubing of a giant stethoscope, coiled so that patients must sit on the instrument that is supposed to listen to them. Two figures in dark suits, labelled BOARD, wear the earpieces. They are not facing the patients. They lean together toward a cash register whose receipt paper unspools across the floor like a white carpet. The patients are drawn in broken dotted lines, as if they were still being sketched. One solid figure is a child holding a numbered ticket as tall as a door. The ticket number is 1847. A clock on the wall has no hands.

[Caption, in a polite typeface beneath the frame]
"We'll call you when your number becomes a priority."

items.stem: The Ksp of CaF2 is 4.0 × 10^−11 at 25 °C. Solid CaF2 is stirred with 0.020 M NaF until equilibrium is reached (volume change from the solid is negligible). What is the equilibrium [Ca2+]?

choices.text: 2.2 × 10^−4 M, from 4s^3 = Ksp as if the solid dissolved in pure water

items.explanation: Calcium fluoride dissolves as CaF2(s) ⇌ Ca2+ + 2 F−, so Ksp equals [Ca2+][F−]^2. The 0.020 M fluoride supplied by NaF dwarfs the fluoride that comes from dissolving the salt, so [F−] remains 0.020 M. The dissolved calcium concentration is therefore the molar solubility: [Ca2+] = Ksp / (0.020)^2 = 4.0 × 10^−11 / 4.0 × 10^−4 = 1.0 × 10^−7 M. The pure-water 4s^3 expression ignores the common ion. Taking a square root treats CaF2 as a 1:1 salt. Dividing by [F−] only once uses the wrong stoichiometric exponent.

distractorRationales.A: 4s^3 = Ksp is the mass-action expression in pure water. Added NaF fixes [F−] near 0.020 M, so that cubic relation no longer applies.
distractorRationales.C: Ksp = [Ca2+][F−]^2, not [Ca2+][F−]. Using a single power of fluoride undercounts the common-ion suppression.
distractorRationales.D: √Ksp would be the solubility of an MX salt. CaF2 releases two fluoride ions per formula unit, and the common ion further changes the algebra.

items.stem: The cartoon's principal target of critique is

choices.text: children who play with oversized stationery in clinics.
a governing board that uses the listening tool of medicine while actually attending to revenue, leaving patients unfinished and untimed.
the invention of the stethoscope as a nineteenth-century error.
clockmakers who omit hands as a design fashion.

items.explanation: Political-cartoon reading: the board wears the earpieces of a giant stethoscope but leans toward a cash register; patients are dotted, not fully drawn; the clock has no hands; the child's ticket is 1847. The satire is institutional misdirection of attention, not an attack on children, on auscultation as such, or on furniture design. Symbolism (instrument of listening, unfinished people, frozen time) and the labelled BOARD fix the target. Without the image's arrangement, a caption about priorities could mean several things; the drawing specifies whose ears and whose receipts.

distractorRationales.A: The child is the most solid patient, a victim of scale, not the satiric target.
distractorRationales.C: The stethoscope is ironic because it is sat-upon and mis-aimed, not because the cartoonist wants it uninvented.
distractorRationales.D: The handless clock is a symbol of time that does not move for patients, not a consumer complaint about clocks.

passage.title: When your number becomes a priority
passage.body:
[Image]
A waiting-room drawn as a long, low shed. The bench is actually the tubing of a giant stethoscope, coiled so that patients must sit on the instrument that is supposed to listen to them. Two figures in dark suits, labelled BOARD, wear the earpieces. They are not facing the patients. They lean together toward a cash register whose receipt paper unspools across the floor like a white carpet. The patients are drawn in broken dotted lines, as if they were still being sketched. One solid figure is a child holding a numbered ticket as tall as a door. The ticket number is 1847. A clock on the wall has no hands.

[Caption, in a polite typeface beneath the frame]
"We'll call you when your number becomes a priority."

items.stem: Terminal alkyne C–H bonds (as in acetylene) are substantially more acidic than alkene or alkane C–H bonds. Which orbital argument best accounts for the lower pKa of the alkyne hydrogen?

choices.text: The conjugate-base lone pair of an acetylide sits in an sp orbital, which has 50% s-character and holds electron density closer to the nucleus than sp2 or sp3 orbitals.
Alkyne carbons are sp3 hybridized, so they have weaker bonds and lose hydrogen more easily.
Acetylene has London dispersion forces that stabilize the acetylide anion in water.
The alkyne hydrogen is more acidic because the C≡C bond is longer than a C–C single bond, so the H is farther from carbon.

items.explanation: Acidity of a C–H bond tracks stability of the conjugate-base anion. In an acetylide the lone pair occupies an sp hybrid (50% s-character). Greater s-character concentrates that pair closer to the carbon nucleus, lowering the energy of the anion relative to an sp2 vinyl anion (~33% s) or an sp3 alkyl anion (25% s). That is why typical pKa values run roughly 25 (alkyne), 44 (alkene), and 50 (alkane). The alkyne carbon is sp, not sp3; the C≡C bond is shorter, not longer, than a single bond; and dispersion forces do not explain the hybridization trend.

distractorRationales.B: Alkyne carbons of a terminal C–H are sp, not sp3. An sp3 description would predict the opposite acidity ranking.
distractorRationales.C: London forces are weak intermolecular attractions among neutral molecules; they do not stabilize a specific conjugate-base orbital.
distractorRationales.D: A C≡C triple bond is shorter than a C–C single bond. Bond length is not the reason the alkyne proton is more acidic.

items.stem: Cultured fibroblasts are treated with a membrane-permeable analog of latrunculin that binds G-actin with nanomolar affinity and drops free monomer below the critical concentration for barbed-end assembly. Fifteen minutes later, which structure is expected to disassemble first?

choices.text: Nuclear lamina, because lamins are actin polymers that treadmill rapidly
Keratin tonofilaments, because intermediate filaments require a high G-actin pool
Stress fibers and the cortical actin meshwork, which are F-actin arrays in equilibrium with G-actin
Centrioles, because the nine triplet blades are unstabilized actin bundles

items.explanation: Latrunculin-like ligands sequester G-actin so the monomer concentration falls below the critical concentration. Filamentous actin therefore net-depolymerizes, collapsing stress fibers, lamellipodia, and cortical F-actin within minutes. Intermediate filaments (lamins, keratins) are nonpolar coiled-coil polymers of unrelated subunits and do not require an actin monomer pool. Centrioles are highly stable microtubule-based organelles. The kinetic selectivity of the drug therefore reports which cytoskeletal polymer is actin, not which structure looks fibrous by light microscopy.

distractorRationales.A: Nuclear lamins are intermediate filaments, not actin polymers, so sequestering G-actin does not dismantle the lamina on this timescale.
distractorRationales.B: Keratin filaments are intermediate filaments assembled from keratin subunits; they are not in rapid equilibrium with G-actin.
distractorRationales.D: Centrioles are microtubule triplets plus accessory proteins, not actin bundles, and they are unusually stable.

items.stem: The clerk’s remark that “surrender had already occurred in the timetable” assumes that

choices.text: a published schedule without runnable service is already a loss, so lights are a remainder of display.
generators cannot fail.
overseas papers never print photographs.
children wrote the timetable.

items.explanation: Without bitterness he separates timetable surrender from the order to keep lights on so darkness would not look like surrender. The unstated assumption is that the timetable is the real service-commitment, already broken, leaving illumination as look. B and C and D are unrelated. Unstated-assumption items should name the premise that makes his contrast coherent.

distractorRationales.B: He says the generator complained; failure is imaginable.
distractorRationales.C: An overseas paper is cited as printing the photograph.
distractorRationales.D: No such authorship is hinted.

passage.title: Note on a cancelled tram
passage.body:
In the third week of the lockout the company ran a single tram, brightly lit, along the route at dusk, with no passengers permitted. Officials called it a demonstration of service. Strikers called it a lantern on a coffin. Children ran beside it anyway, as they had when the cars were working, and were photographed. The photograph was printed in the morning paper under the heading NORMALITY RETURNS, and in an overseas paper under the heading CHILDREN MOCK THE DEAD LINE.

A clerk in the tram office, years later, wrote that he had been told to leave the lights on even if the generator complained, because darkness would look like surrender. He added, without apparent bitterness, that surrender had already occurred in the timetable. What remained was a moving argument about who owned the look of a street at evening.

Historians still disagree whether the empty tram lengthened the dispute by humiliating the men or shortened it by frightening the board with the cost of theatre. The clerk’s sentence is more useful than either camp: the fight had become, for a night, a question of illumination.

items.stem: A horizontal artery widens into an aneurysm whose cross-sectional area is twice that of the adjacent vessel. For steady incompressible flow at constant height, the pressure inside the dilated segment is:

choices.text: lower than adjacent pressure because speed is higher there
higher than adjacent pressure because speed is lower there
higher than adjacent pressure because speed is higher there
equal to adjacent pressure because the vessel is still horizontal

items.explanation: Continuity forces speed to fall where area rises, so the aneurysm is a slow region. Bernoulli's relation at constant gravitational height then requires hydrostatic pressure to rise where dynamic pressure 1/2 rho v squared falls. The elevated transmural pressure, together with Laplace's law for wall tension, is why a dilation can progress. Equal height alone does not equalize pressure if speeds differ along the streamline.

distractorRationales.A: Speed is lower, not higher, in the wider segment. A fast, low-pressure region describes a stenosis, the opposite geometry.
distractorRationales.C: This pairs the correct pressure change with the wrong speed change. Higher speed would lower pressure, not raise it.
distractorRationales.D: Horizontal flow removes the rho g h term from the comparison but does not cancel the 1/2 rho v^2 term. Pressure still tracks speed.

items.stem: A researcher titrates free histidine (pKa values: α-carboxyl 1.8, imidazole 6.0, α-ammonium 9.2) and asks at which pH the amino acid has a time-averaged net charge closest to zero. Which pH should be chosen for an isoelectric precipitation trial?

choices.text: 3.9, the average of 1.8 and 6.0
5.5, the average of 1.8 and 9.2
7.6, the average of 6.0 and 9.2
9.2, equal to the α-ammonium pKa

items.explanation: Fully protonated histidine carries a net charge of +2 (carboxylic acid, imidazolium, and ammonium). Loss of the carboxyl proton (pKa 1.8) yields net +1; loss of the imidazole proton (pKa 6.0) yields the zwitterion of net charge 0; loss of the ammonium proton (pKa 9.2) yields net −1. The isoelectric point of a basic amino acid is the average of the two pKa values that bound the net-zero form, here (6.0 + 9.2)/2 = 7.6. Averaging the two lowest pKa values is the rule for acidic residues such as aspartate, not for histidine, and the pI is not equal to a single pKa.

distractorRationales.A: Averaging the two lowest pKa values gives the pI of acidic amino acids (Asp, Glu), not of histidine.
distractorRationales.B: Averaging the α-carboxyl and α-ammonium pKa values is the rule for amino acids with uncharged side chains.
distractorRationales.D: At the α-ammonium pKa the side chain is already deprotonated, so the net charge is negative, not zero.

items.stem: A proliferating culture is treated with a microtubule-depolymerizing drug. Flow cytometry shows a 4C DNA peak. Live imaging shows condensed chromosomes and a disassembled nuclear envelope that persist for hours. The cells are arrested primarily in:

choices.text: G1, when unreplicated 2C nuclei wait for mitogen
Early S phase, when DNA content is still near 2C
Mitosis, because the spindle assembly checkpoint blocks anaphase until kinetochores attach to microtubules
Cytokinesis of a haploid cell, which has 1C DNA

items.explanation: After S phase, G2 and mitotic cells both have 4C DNA, so DNA content alone cannot separate them. Condensed chromosomes and nuclear-envelope breakdown are mitotic hallmarks. Without microtubules, kinetochores cannot attach, the spindle assembly checkpoint remains active, separase stays inhibited, and cells arrest in prometaphase with 4C genomes. G1 is 2C with an intact nucleus, early S is between 2C and 4C, and haploid cytokinesis is not the state of these somatic cells. Microtubule poisons used in karyotyping exploit this SAC arrest.

distractorRationales.A: G1 cells are 2C with decondensed chromatin and an intact nucleus.
distractorRationales.B: Early S is not a 4C condensed-chromosome arrest.
distractorRationales.D: These are 4C mitotic somatic cells, not 1C haploids completing cytokinesis.

items.stem: Using only the 0–10 s rates, how many times faster is D’s scatter change than B’s?

choices.text: about 2
about 0.5
about 7
undefined, because A is zero

items.explanation: Rates are −0.060 versus −0.029. The ratio of magnitudes is 0.060/0.029 ≈ 2.1, about 2. Inverse 0.5 would be B/D. 7 would be a misread of 0.060/0.008 (that is D versus C). A being zero is why A is not in the ratio, not why D/B is undefined. Proportional reasoning should use the rate table as stated.

distractorRationales.B: That is B relative to D, the inverse.
distractorRationales.C: That approximates D versus C (−0.060/−0.008), not D versus B.
distractorRationales.D: The question asks D compared with B, both nonzero.

passage.title: Vesicle swelling under osmotic load
passage.body:
A student prepares identical phospholipid vesicles in 300 mOsmol kg−1 sucrose, then dilutes them at t = 0 into the media below. Vesicle volume is inferred from light scatter (larger vesicles scatter less in this geometry). Temperature 25 °C. n = 6 aliquots; scatter reported as mean ± s.d. arbitrary units (higher = smaller vesicles).

Medium after dilution | 10 s | 60 s | 300 s
A: 300 mOsmol sucrose (control) | 1.00 ± 0.02 | 0.99 ± 0.03 | 1.01 ± 0.02
B: 150 mOsmol sucrose | 0.71 ± 0.04 | 0.52 ± 0.05 | 0.48 ± 0.06
C: 150 mOsmol sucrose + 0.1 mM HgCl2 (water-channel blocker in this model) | 0.92 ± 0.03 | 0.80 ± 0.04 | 0.61 ± 0.05
D: 150 mOsmol sucrose + aquaporin proteoliposomes fused at 5 mol% | 0.40 ± 0.06 | 0.33 ± 0.05 | 0.34 ± 0.04

A second table lists initial rates estimated from 0–10 s, treating scatter drop as swelling:

Condition | Δscatter / 10 s
A | ~0
B | −0.029
C | −0.008
D | −0.060

The student claims: “Swelling requires a hypotonic bath, is slowed when water pores are blocked, and is accelerated when extra water pores are added, so the membrane’s phospholipid bilayer is not the main path in B–D.”

items.stem:
Resistance is computed from R = V / I. Independent absolute uncertainties add in quadrature or, as a standard school-level rule used here, relative uncertainties add: δR/R = δV/V + δI/I.

Reading | Value | Absolute uncertainty | Relative uncertainty
V | 12.0 V | 0.3 V | 0.3/12.0 = 2.5%
I | 2.00 A | 0.10 A | 0.10/2.00 = 5.0%

What should be reported for R?

choices.text: 6.00 ± 0.15 Ω, using only the 2.5% voltage uncertainty.
6.00 ± 0.30 Ω, using only the 5.0% current uncertainty.
6.00 ± 0.75 Ω, multiplying the percentages (2.5% × 5.0% is not the combination rule).

items.explanation: R = 12.0 / 2.00 = 6.00 Ω. Adding the given relative uncertainties produces 2.5% + 5.0% = 7.5%. Then δR = 0.075 × 6.00 = 0.45 Ω, so R = 6.00 ± 0.45 Ω. Using only one of the two contributions underestimates the uncertainty. Multiplying 2.5% by 5.0% gives 0.125%, or if the percentages are multiplied as 12.5% one gets 0.75 Ω; neither is the sum rule stated in the stem. Adding the absolute 0.3 V and 0.10 A would mix volts with amperes and is not how a quotient is combined. The current’s 5% dominates, but the voltage’s 2.5% is still required in the sum.

distractorRationales.A: 2.5% of 6.00 Ω is 0.15 Ω, which ignores the larger current uncertainty. Both relative errors must be added for a quotient.
distractorRationales.B: 5.0% of 6.00 Ω is 0.30 Ω, which ignores the voltage uncertainty. The stem’s rule adds both relative contributions.
distractorRationales.D: 0.75 Ω corresponds to 12.5%, as if the percentages were multiplied. The stated rule is to add 2.5% and 5.0%.

choices.text: Lipid solubility (log P) dominates: testosterone is fastest despite the largest MW.
The smallest molar mass always wins, so urea (MW 60) should exceed testosterone.
Glucose is fastest because cells need sugar, and 0.05 is the largest influx.
Charge determines the order; all four solutes must be anions because they cross at all.

items.explanation: Simple diffusion through a bilayer favours hydrophobic solutes. Testosterone’s log P of +3.3 and flux 42 dwarf urea (log P −2.1, flux 0.4) and glucose (log P −3.0, flux 0.05) even though testosterone is the heaviest (MW 288). Ethanol is intermediate (log P −0.3, flux 18). Molecular weight still matters for a given polarity, but in this set polarity outranks size. Need for a metabolite is irrelevant in a protein-free bilayer, and none of the tabulated solutes is an anion.

distractorRationales.B: Urea’s influx is 0.4 versus testosterone’s 42, so smallest MW does not win here.
distractorRationales.C: Glucose has the smallest influx (0.05), not the largest, and a protein-free bilayer has no glucose carriers.
distractorRationales.D: The table gives no charges; urea, ethanol, glucose, and testosterone are not anions, yet they still show very different fluxes.

items.stem:
Glycine (pI 6.0) and lysine (pI 9.7) are spotted at the origin of an electrophoresis strip buffered at pH 6.0. A species with pI < pH is net negative and migrates to the anode; pI > pH is net positive and migrates to the cathode; pI = pH does not migrate. After 20 min the strip is:

Position (towards cathode +) | spot
