Recipients become F+ lac+ (here lac is on the F or cotransferred) while remaining streptomycin-resistant because that chromosomal marker was already theirs. Bacterial recipients do not reverse-transcribe environmental mRNA to gain a stable lac+ genotype.

distractorRationales.A: Transformation uses naked DNA and is blocked by DNase; the high frequency despite DNase excludes it.
distractorRationales.C: No phage was introduced; conjugation between F+ and F- is sufficient to explain the exconjugants.
distractorRationales.D: Stable bacterial alleles are DNA; there is no physiologic reverse transcription of secreted lac mRNA in E. coli.

items.stem: A purified tRNA^Ile bears the anticodon 5′-IAU-3′. In a reconstituted translation system it supports isoleucine incorporation in response to AUU, AUC, and AUA but not AUG. Which statement best explains this codon set?

choices.text: Inosine at the wobble (5′) position of the anticodon pairs with U, C, or A at the third position of the codon, reading the three Ile codons; AUG is Met and would require a G that inosine does not stably pair with.
The genetic code is overlapping, so a single IAU anticodon slides across a window that includes AUG as an isoleucine codon.
Inosine is attached to isoleucine by a mischarging event that converts Met-tRNA to Ile-tRNA, allowing the ribosome to skip AUG.
Each isoleucine codon is recognized only by a perfectly matched anticodon, so the IAU tRNA can read solely AUA.

items.explanation: Wobble pairing occurs between the 5′ base of the anticodon and the 3′ base of the codon. Inosine, produced by deamination of adenosine, hydrogen-bonds with U, C, or A, so anticodon 5′-IAU-3′ decodes AUU, AUC, and AUA—the three isoleucine codons. It does not decode AUG, which specifies methionine and presents a 3′ G that is not a standard inosine wobble partner. The code is nonoverlapping and commaless from a fixed start. Inosine is a tRNA nucleoside modification, not a misacylation of initiator tRNA, and degeneracy plus wobble exist precisely so that one tRNA species can read multiple synonymous codons.

distractorRationales.B: Codons are nonoverlapping triplets; the ribosome advances three nucleotides and does not slide IAU across AUG as Ile.
distractorRationales.C: Inosine is in the anticodon loop of tRNA^Ile; it is not a charging defect that converts Met-tRNA into an Ile carrier.
distractorRationales.D: Wobble exists so that a single tRNA can read several third-position variants; restriction to AUA alone contradicts the incorporation data.

items.stem: Hexokinase catalyzes glucose + ATP → glucose-6-phosphate + ADP. To which Enzyme Commission class does this reaction belong, and why is ‘ligase’ the wrong label?

choices.text: Hydrolase, because water is the phosphoryl acceptor
Lyase, because ATP is cleaved without transferring a group to glucose

Transferase (phosphotransferase): a phosphoryl group is transferred from ATP to glucose; ligases join two substrates with concurrent NTP hydrolysis rather than transferring a preexisting group onto one of them
Oxidoreductase, because the aldehyde of glucose is oxidized to a phosphate ester

items.explanation: The six EC classes are oxidoreductase, transferase, hydrolase, lyase, isomerase, and ligase. Hexokinase moves the γ-phosphoryl of ATP onto glucose’s C6 hydroxyl, which is group transfer (EC 2.7). Ligases (EC 6) catalyze joining of two molecules coupled to NTP hydrolysis, typically forming new C–C, C–O, C–N, or C–S bonds (DNA ligase, glutamine synthetase, pyruvate carboxylase). Water is not the acceptor, so it is not a hydrolase. A lyase would add or remove groups from double bonds without ATP as a phosphoryl donor. The aldehyde of glucose is not oxidized; C6 is a primary alcohol.

distractorRationales.A: A hydrolase would transfer the phosphoryl to water (ATPase). Glucose, not water, is the acceptor in the hexokinase reaction.
distractorRationales.B: A lyase does not use ATP as a phosphoryl donor to an alcohol. The phosphoryl is transferred, not merely eliminated.
distractorRationales.D: No redox change occurs at carbon. Phosphorylation of an alcohol is not oxidation of an aldehyde.

items.stem: A rural county lost its obstetrics ward; EMS times to the nearest labor unit exceed an hour. An urban core eighty miles away has a tertiary hospital, but two of its high-poverty neighborhoods lack night bus service to that campus. Which statement about spatial inequality is most accurate?

choices.text: Spatial inequality includes both rural–urban resource gaps and intra-urban unequal access to existing institutions
Only cities can be spatially unequal; rural closures are a different, nonspatial problem
Rural mortality is lower by definition because of clean air, so ward closures cannot affect outcomes
Demographic transition requires that rural areas have more hospitals than cities

items.explanation: Spatial inequality is unequal distribution of resources and risks across places. That includes the rural–urban gradient (distance to obstetrics, EMS time) and fine-grained intra-urban isolation (transit deserts next to a famous hospital). Restricting the concept to cities, or treating rural health as automatically superior because of air quality, misses both of those geographic mechanisms. Vital-rate stages of the demographic transition do not legislate hospital counts.

distractorRationales.B: Distance and facility closure are spatial by definition, whether the place is rural or urban.
distractorRationales.C: Clean air does not cancel time-to-treatment for obstetric emergencies.
distractorRationales.D: Transition theory does not assign more hospitals to rural areas.

items.stem: A redox titration uses MnO4− + 5 Fe2+ + 8 H+ → Mn2+ + 5 Fe3+ + 4 H2O. 20.0 mL of Fe2+ solution requires 20.0 mL of 0.020 M KMnO4 to reach the first permanent pink. How many moles of Fe2+ were present, and what was the original [Fe2+]?

choices.text: 0.0020 mol Fe2+; 0.020 M (forgetting the 20.0 mL volume of Fe)
0.00040 mol Fe2+; 0.020 M (1:1 mole ratio)

items.explanation: Moles of MnO4− = 0.020 mol L−1 × 0.0200 L = 4.0 × 10−4 mol. The equation consumes 5 Fe2+ per MnO4−, so n(Fe2+) = 5 × 4.0 × 10−4 = 2.0 × 10−3 mol. In 20.0 mL that is 0.0020 / 0.0200 = 0.10 M. A 1:1 assumption undercounts iron by a factor of five. Leaving the iron moles unconverted to molarity with the correct n still needs division by 0.0200 L. Using 1:1 on volumes without the 5:1 ratio can invent other figures such as 0.50 M if 0.020 × 5 / 0.020 is mis-assigned.

distractorRationales.A: 0.0020 mol in 20.0 mL is 0.10 M, not 0.020 M.
distractorRationales.B: 0.010 mol would be 25 times the permanganate moles, not 5 times.
distractorRationales.D: The balanced equation is 5 Fe per MnO4, not 1:1, so n(Fe2+) is five times n(MnO4−).

items.stem: Mischel’s review of trait–behavior correlations (and the later person–situation debate) is presented to a personality journal club. Which statement best captures his critique of a strong global-trait view such as an uncritical Big Five-as-destiny reading?

choices.text: Freud already proved traits are illusions, so Costa and McCrae’s inventory is invalid by definition
Situationism claims that heritability of extraversion is zero, contradicting all twin studies
Humanistic actualization (Rogers) is the only lawful predictor, so traits and situations are both irrelevant
Cross-situational consistency of behavior is often modest, so situations and person–situation interactions must be modeled, not only a five-factor score

items.explanation: Mischel argued that personality coefficients across situations are typically modest; behavior depends on situational features and if–then signatures, not a single global trait score. That launched the person–situation debate; it did not prove Freud, nullify heritability, or crown Rogers as the only predictor. Costa and McCrae’s Big Five can still describe average tendencies; Mischel’s point is that those averages underpredict single-act consistency. Twin data still show genetic influence on traits.

distractorRationales.A: Mischel’s critique is psychometric and situational, not a Freudian disproof of inventories.
distractorRationales.B: Situationism about single-act prediction is not a claim that extraversion heritability is zero.
distractorRationales.C: Rogers is not the punchline of the person–situation debate.

items.stem: Sperm-egg fusion triggers a calcium wave across the oocyte. Cortical granules exocytose, and additional sperm can no longer bind the zona pellucida. This calcium-dependent cortical reaction primarily:

choices.text: Hardens and chemically modifies the zona pellucida to establish a block to polyspermy
Initiates gastrulation within seconds by forming a primitive streak
Completes meiosis I, which in humans is unfinished until after implantation
Fuses male and female pronuclei before DNA replication of either genome

items.explanation: Fertilization must admit exactly one haploid sperm genome. The calcium wave causes cortical granule release; enzymes and structural proteins they contain modify ZP glycoproteins so that additional sperm cannot penetrate, the slow block to polyspermy. Gastrulation occurs days later and is not triggered in seconds by cortical granules. In humans meiosis I is completed at ovulation; fertilization then completes meiosis II, not meiosis I. Pronuclear fusion (syngamy) is a later step and is not the definition of the cortical reaction.

distractorRationales.B: The primitive streak appears at gastrulation, long after the cortical reaction.
distractorRationales.C: Meiosis I is completed before ovulation; fertilization completes meiosis II.
distractorRationales.D: The cortical reaction is a zona/membrane block, not immediate karyogamy.

items.stem: A 72-year-old develops a resting pill-rolling tremor, festinating gait, and masked face; levodopa helps motor signs. Cognition is initially relatively spared. A second patient of the same age has progressive memory loss, hippocampal atrophy, and cortical amyloid plaques. Which pairing of diagnosis and hallmark pathophysiology is correct?

choices.text: First patient Alzheimer disease because tremor is the defining DSM criterion
First patient Parkinson disease (nigrostriatal dopamine loss, Lewy bodies); second Alzheimer disease (amyloid plaques, neurofibrillary tangles, cholinergic deficit)
Second patient Parkinson disease because hippocampus is the substantia nigra
Both are typical-antipsychotic side effects rather than neurodegenerative diseases

items.explanation: Parkinson disease is loss of substantia nigra pars compacta dopaminergic neurons with α-synuclein Lewy bodies; levodopa replaces dopamine and improves motor signs. Alzheimer disease is the amnestic cortical dementia with amyloid plaques, tau tangles, and nucleus-basalis cholinergic loss. Tremor is not an Alzheimer DSM hallmark. The hippocampus is not the nigra. Neurodegenerative histology, not a neuroleptic, is specified in the stem.

distractorRationales.A: Alzheimer disease is not defined by resting tremor; that points to Parkinsonism.
distractorRationales.C: Hippocampal atrophy is an Alzheimer-pattern finding, not a renaming of the nigra.
distractorRationales.D: The stem describes two idiopathic neurodegenerative pictures, not drug-induced Parkinsonism plus plaques.

items.stem: For the condensation-like process A(g) → A(l), ΔH = −40.0 kJ mol−1 and ΔS = −100 J K−1 mol−1 = −0.100 kJ K−1 mol−1. ΔG = ΔH − TΔS. Compute ΔG at 300 K and at 500 K, and the temperature at which ΔG = 0.

choices.text: ΔG(300 K) = −10 kJ mol−1 (spontaneous); ΔG(500 K) = +10 kJ mol−1 (not); crossover T = 400 K
ΔG is −40 kJ mol−1 at both temperatures because ΔH is constant
ΔG(300 K) = +10 kJ mol−1; the process is never spontaneous
Crossover T = 0.25 K, from 40/0.100 without converting ΔS into kJ

items.explanation: At 300 K, TΔS = 300 × (−0.100) = −30 kJ mol−1, so ΔG = −40 − (−30) = −10 kJ mol−1, spontaneous. At 500 K, TΔS = −50 kJ mol−1, ΔG = −40 − (−50) = +10 kJ mol−1, not spontaneous. Setting ΔG = 0 gives T = ΔH/ΔS = 40.0 / 0.100 = 400 K. ΔH alone is not ΔG. The sign at 300 K is negative, not positive. Forgetting to put ΔS in kJ produces a 400-fold temperature error (0.25 K is 40/160, or 40/100 without unit conversion depending on the slip).

distractorRationales.B: The −TΔS term changes by 20 kJ mol−1 between 300 and 500 K, so ΔG is not frozen at ΔH.
distractorRationales.C: ΔG at 300 K is −10 kJ mol−1, so the process is spontaneous below 400 K.
distractorRationales.D: T = 40.0 kJ / 0.100 kJ K−1 = 400 K; using 100 J without converting yields 400 K still if consistent, but 0.25 K is not that quotient.

items.stem: Ethanol (CH3CH2OH) and dimethyl ether (CH3OCH3) are isomers, yet ethanol boils at 78 °C while dimethyl ether boils at −24 °C. Which intermolecular-force difference is the principal reason?

choices.text: Ethanol is ionic and dimethyl ether is covalent.
Only London forces operate in ethanol, whereas dimethyl ether is hydrogen bonded at oxygen.
Dimethyl ether has a much larger surface area, so it should actually boil higher; the listed boiling points must be reversed.
Ethanol molecules form O–H···O hydrogen bonds; dimethyl ether can exert only dipole–dipole and London forces.

items.explanation: Both compounds have similar molar mass, so London forces are comparable. Ethanol has an O–H bond, so it can donate and accept hydrogen bonds, which are much stronger than the dipole–dipole contacts available to the ether. Extra thermal energy is required to separate hydrogen-bonded ethanol molecules, raising the boiling point by about 100 °C. Dimethyl ether’s oxygen can accept a hydrogen bond from water but cannot donate one to another ether molecule. Neither isomer is ionic, and the ether does not have a larger elongated surface that would reverse the boiling-point order.

distractorRationales.A: Both compounds are neutral covalent molecules; ethanol’s elevated boiling point is hydrogen bonding, not an ionic lattice.
distractorRationales.B: This reverses the hydrogen-bond donor ability: the alcohol, not the ether, has the O–H needed for H-bonding between like molecules.
distractorRationales.C: The isomers have similar size; the ether is not the higher-boiling compound. The experimental order is ethanol >> ether.

items.stem:
Boiling points and water solubility of C2H6O constitutional isomers:

Isomer | bp (°C) | miscibility with water
Ethanol | 78 | miscible
Methoxymethane (dimethyl ether) | −25 | modest

Which intermolecular-force account is required?

choices.text: Ethanol’s higher bp shows it has the larger molecular mass
Ethanol hydrogen-bonds to itself and to water, raising bp and conferring miscibility; the ether has only dipole and dispersion forces and cannot donate a hydrogen bond
The ether has the higher boiling point because it is more volatile at −25 °C
Both isomers hydrogen-bond identically, so the 103 °C gap is packing of CH3 groups

items.explanation: Both isomers have Mr = 46, so mass is not the discriminator. Ethanol’s O–H group donates and accepts hydrogen bonds, producing a liquid that boils at 78 °C and mixes in all proportions with water. Dimethyl ether has no O–H bond: it can accept a hydrogen bond from water but cannot form an O–H···O network of its own, so it is a gas at room temperature (bp −25 °C) and only modestly soluble. Volatility is high when boiling point is low, not the reverse. Identical hydrogen bonding cannot open a 103 °C gap.

distractorRationales.A: The isomers are C2H6O, identical mass; mass cannot explain the gap.
distractorRationales.C: −25 °C is a lower boiling point, meaning weaker liquid-phase attractions and higher vapour pressure at a given T.
distractorRationales.D: The ether has no hydrogen-bond donor; the isomers are not equivalent.

items.stem: Oncogenic Ras G12V has greatly reduced GTPase activity and is insensitive to GAPs. In serum-starved fibroblasts this mutant, relative to wild-type Ras, will:

choices.text: Remain GDP-bound and therefore silent at the plasma membrane
Directly phosphorylate tyrosines on growth-factor receptors to mimic ligand
Remain GTP-bound and constitutively activate RAF-MEK-ERK transcription programs even without growth factor
Block all GPCR signaling by sequestering beta-gamma subunits as its only activity

items.explanation: Ras is a molecular switch: GTP-bound Ras-GTP engages RAF, driving the MEK-ERK cascade that promotes proliferation. Intrinsic GTPase activity, stimulated by GAPs, returns Ras to the inactive GDP state. G12V impairs GTP hydrolysis, so the protein accumulates as Ras-GTP independently of upstream RTK occupancy and remains on after serum withdrawal. Ras is not a tyrosine kinase and does not replace receptor autophosphorylation. Although Ras can intersect some GPCR pathways, the defining oncogenic lesion is constitutive RAF activation, not wholesale GPCR blockade.

distractorRationales.A: Failed GTP hydrolysis leaves Ras GTP-bound, not GDP-bound.
distractorRationales.B: Ras binds effectors; it does not phosphorylate receptor tyrosines.
distractorRationales.D: G12V is a gain of Ras-GTP signaling, not a general GPCR antagonist.

items.stem: An ethnographer sits in a diabetes clinic and records how “compliance” is negotiated turn by turn: what a glucometer reading is taken to mean, how a missed dose is excused, how identities of “good patient” are performed. Which pair of approaches is most tightly fitted to this micro-meaning project?

choices.text: Marxist conflict theory, because only class fractions can speak in a clinic
Durkheimian functionalism, because the ethnographer is measuring organic solidarity with a dynamometer
Feminist theory only if no men are present, which is its defining axiom
Symbolic interactionism (Mead, Blumer) and social constructionism (Berger and Luckmann), which treat meanings and “facts” of illness as produced in interaction and institutionalization

items.explanation: Symbolic interactionism holds that people act toward things on the basis of meanings that arise in interaction (Blumer’s premises, from Mead). Social constructionism (Berger and Luckmann) extends that insight: realities, including illness categories, are built and sedimented through social processes. A turn-by-turn clinic study is that program. Conflict theory can study clinics but is not this meaning-negotiation method. Functionalism’s system needs are not measured by dyadic excuses. Feminist theory is not defined by the absence of men.

distractorRationales.A: Class analysis is not implied merely by recording conversational meaning.
distractorRationales.B: Organic solidarity is a macrosocial cohesion type, not a dynamometer reading of excuses.
distractorRationales.C: Feminist approaches analyze gendered power; they are not “no men in the room.”

items.stem: Which of the following, according to the passage, supports the claim that private order is already subsidized?

choices.text: Streets, courts, pipes, and the patience of people who do not sue every stranger at a porch.
Gate receipts from fenced venues.
The poetry of the unowned.
A child who learns that cities require a purchase.

items.explanation: The support is listed in the first paragraph as the existing subsidies of private order. That is the evidence for “not a leak.” B is the venue policy. C is a weak defense the author sets aside. D inverts the child example, which is of inclusion without purchase. Relevance items should pick the listed subsidy, not a neighboring theme.

distractorRationales.B: Fencing and ticketing are a crude policy, not the subsidy evidence.
distractorRationales.C: Poetry is called moving and strategically weak, not evidence of subsidy.
distractorRationales.D: The child learns inclusion without purchase; the option reverses it.

passage.title: The ledger of the commons
passage.body:
When a city puts a park on a map, it appears to have given something away: land that could have been lots, hours that could have been tolls. Developers are not wrong that the gift has a price. They are wrong when they treat the price as a leak from an otherwise watertight private order. The private order is already subsidized by streets, courts, pipes, and the patience of people who do not sue every time a stranger walks past a porch. A park is not the exception to property. It is one of the ways a dense city remains inhabitable enough for property to be worth wanting.

Accountants prefer a ledger in which every square metre has a named owner and a yield. Parks embarrass the ledger because their yield is a crowd that does not pay at the gate, a cooling that does not send an invoice, a child who learns a city can include her without a purchase. The embarrassment produces two crude policies. One is to fence and ticket until the park behaves like a venue. The other is to neglect the park until the crowd looks like a problem that only private security can solve. Both policies claim to be realistic. Both are ways of refusing to count the effects that made the park rational in the first place.

Friends of the park sometimes answer with a poetry of the unowned. The poetry is moving and strategically weak. A commons that cannot speak in maintenance budgets will lose to a spreadsheet that can. The more adult defense is to insist that the ledger is incomplete, not that ledgers are evil. Planting, lighting, toilets, and a gardener who is paid in winter are not betrayals of openness. They are how openness lasts past a ribbon-cutting.

There is a further honesty. Parks are not innocent. They have been used to raise adjacent rents, to move unhoused people out of sight, to display a city’s kindness to visitors who will never need the toilets. Naming those uses does not hand the land to the highest bidder. It prevents the park’s defenders from pretending that green on a map is already justice. Justice would be a park whose ledger includes the people who were priced off the blocks around it.

If urban politics cannot hold that thought, it will keep oscillating between the venue and the ruin, and calling the oscillation pragmatism.

items.stem: Two samples of the same ideal gas have identical molar mass. Sample B is at twice the absolute temperature of sample A. The rms molecular speed in B relative to A is:

choices.text: the same, because rms speed depends only on molar mass
greater by a factor of sqrt(2)
greater by a factor of 2
greater by a factor of 4

items.explanation: The kinetic-theory result is v_rms = sqrt(3RT/M). At fixed molar mass, v_rms scales as the square root of absolute temperature. Doubling T therefore multiplies rms speed by sqrt(2) ≈ 1.41, not by 2 or by 4. Molar mass sets the scale but does not cancel the temperature dependence, and mean-square speed (proportional to T) must not be confused with rms speed (proportional to sqrt(T)).

distractorRationales.A: v_rms depends on both T and M. Equal molar mass still leaves the sqrt(T) factor.
distractorRationales.C: Linear scaling with T would apply to mean kinetic energy, (3/2) kT, not to the speed obtained from the square root of that energy.
distractorRationales.D: A factor of four would match T squared, which does not appear in v_rms.

items.stem: Ammonia has Kb = 1.8 × 10^−5. What is Ka of ammonium ion, NH4+, at 25 °C (Kw = 1.0 × 10^−14)?
items.explanation: For a conjugate pair, Ka(acid) × Kb(base) = Kw. Therefore Ka(NH4+) = Kw / Kb(NH3) = (1.0 × 10^−14) / (1.8 × 10^−5) = 5.6 × 10^−10. That small Ka identifies NH4+ as a weak acid, which is why solutions of NH4Cl are slightly acidic. Copying Kb as Ka ignores the conjugate relationship. 1.8 × 10^−9 is an off-by-factor arithmetic error (dividing by 10^−5 incorrectly). Kw itself is not Ka of ammonium.

distractorRationales.A: 1.8 × 10^−5 is Kb of ammonia, not Ka of ammonium. The conjugate acid must have Ka = Kw/Kb.
distractorRationales.B: 1.8 × 10^−9 would be Kw/Kb with an incorrect power of ten (as if Kw were 10^−14 and Kb were 10^−5 but 1.8 were placed wrong).
distractorRationales.D: 1.0 × 10^−14 is Kw, the autoionization constant of water, not Ka of NH4+.

items.stem: Which of the following is the most defensible limitation of the author's argument as written?

choices.text: It never explains how conversion of dissent into attendance is supposed to work, so no civic implication can be drawn.
It proves that every digital portal is illegal, so further discussion of design is unnecessary.

It implies that photographs of consultation cannot substitute for attributable choice, yet it does not supply criteria for when proceeding-anyway is substantively just—only that consent-narration is a dishonest substitute for that choice.
It shows that democracy is identical with unedited recordings, so a city that publishes audio has thereby exhausted its civic duty.

items.explanation: The passage is strong on a diagnostic implication: legitimacy-by-photograph and coerced averages are not consent. It is modest on substance. The recommended sentence admits a choice; it does not tell a reader how to judge whether the reasons are good. That is a real limitation, not a hole in the conversion mechanism, which is specified through minutes, themes, and ratings. The text also refuses the implication that portals must be abandoned or that recordings exhaust duty. Naming what the argument does not establish is the task; C tracks that gap without inventing a stronger legal claim than the author makes.

distractorRationales.A: The mechanism is specified: crowded-hall photographs, recoding into themes, and averaged stars. The limitation is not absence of mechanism.
distractorRationales.B: The author says a more honest practice would not abandon portals; illegality is never claimed.
distractorRationales.D: Publishing the record is part of honesty, not a completed democracy; reasons for proceeding remain required, and the choice remains attributable.

passage.title: Minutes as consent
passage.body:
City governments have learned to speak the language of invitation. A new waterfront, a bus garage, a night-time licensing scheme: each arrives with a room, a facilitator, sticky notes, and a promise that "your voice will be heard." The promise is not empty in the way cynics assume. People do speak. Minutes are taken. A summary slide later reports that the community was "engaged." What the ritual converts, with almost chemical reliability, is dissent into attendance. The fact of having been in the room is then cited as evidence that the decision which followed was shared.

This conversion is the point, not an accidental side-effect. A planning authority that can display a photograph of a crowded hall has already performed legitimacy. The photograph does not record what was refused, only that refusal was given a chair. Once refusal has a chair, it can be filed. The file then travels upward as proof of consultation, and the project proceeds under the borrowed moral credit of those who came to object. Objectors discover, sometimes only at the groundbreaking, that they were extras in a scene titled participation.

The objection is not that consultation is a trick in every case. Some rooms change designs. A ramp is added; a tree is spared; a night bus is rerouted. Those revisions matter, and it would be a different piety to pretend they never occur. The trouble is the ambient theory that treats any revision as proof that the process is sound, and any remaining grievance as leftover noise from people who "had their chance." Attendance is thereby made to do the work of consent. Consent, if the word still means anything civic, is not the same as having been scheduled.

Oral comments at a microphone illustrate the substitution with painful clarity. Three minutes are allotted. A timer is visible. The speaker is thanked. The next speaker is invited. The form is courteous and the structure is a funnel: complexity is shaved to fit the slot, and what cannot be shaved is classified as repetition. Staff later write that "themes" emerged. Themes are what survive the funnel. They are not necessarily what the speakers thought they had said. A person who came to argue that the garage should not be built at all finds herself listed under "requests for mitigation." The minutes have translated abolition into upholstery.

Digital portals repeat the same conversion with a friendlier interface. A comment box invites "feedback." Character limits and dropdown menus decide in advance which kinds of sentence will count as input. The resident who types a structural objection is asked, before submitting, to rate the project from one to five stars. The rating is the datum that will be averaged; the paragraph is optional texture. When officials later announce that the "average rating was 3.7," they are not lying about the arithmetic. They are treating a coerced metric as a public will.

A more honest practice would not abandon rooms or portals. It would stop narrating them as consent machines. It would publish the unedited record beside the decision, including the proposals that were not adopted, and it would say plainly: we heard you and we are proceeding anyway, for these reasons. That sentence is politically expensive, which is why the photograph of the hall is preferred. The photograph allows a government to be seen listening without being seen choosing. Democracy, however, is not a listening face. It is the willingness to let a choice remain attributable, especially when the choice disappoints the people who were invited to speak.

items.stem: A proton moves parallel to a uniform magnetic field. The magnetic force on the proton is:

choices.text: zero, because F = q v B sin θ and sin 0° = 0
maximum in magnitude and always perpendicular to v
parallel to v, so the proton speeds up
antiparallel to v, so the proton slows down

items.explanation: The magnetic force on a charge is F = q v B sin θ, with θ the angle between velocity and B. Parallel motion means θ = 0°, sin 0° = 0, and F = 0. When the force is not zero it is always perpendicular to v, so magnetic forces never change a charge's speed—only its direction. That perpendicular force is simply absent in this geometry. There is no magnetic analog of a parallel electric force that would accelerate the proton along the field lines.

distractorRationales.B: The maximum force is q v B, which occurs at θ = 90°, not at θ = 0°. Parallel velocity produces no magnetic force at all.
distractorRationales.C: A magnetic force, when it exists, is perpendicular to v and does no work, so it cannot increase speed. Parallel v and B yield F = 0 besides.
distractorRationales.D: Magnetic forces do not act as drag along v. They are either perpendicular to v or zero; they do not reverse the velocity vector by slowing the particle.

items.stem:
g is to be found from T = 2π √(L/g), so g = 4π^2 L / T^2. The length L is known to 0.10% and may be treated as exact compared with the timing error. A student times one oscillation as T = 2.00 ± 0.10 s.

Quantity | Value | Relative uncertainty
L | 1.000 m | 0.10% (neglect)
T | 2.00 ± 0.10 s | 0.10 / 2.00 = 5.0%

Relative uncertainty in a power is the exponent times the relative uncertainty of the base, so δg/g ≈ 2 (δT / T). What is the percentage uncertainty in g?
items.explanation: Because g ∝ 1/T^2, the relative uncertainty doubles: δg/g = 2 × 5.0% = 10%. The 0.10% length error is negligible beside 10%. Using 5.0% copies the timing uncertainty without the exponent 2. Halving 5.0% as if g ∝ √T is the wrong power. Squaring 5% to get 25% confuses the propagation rule (multiply the relative error by the exponent) with squaring the percentage itself. The large timing uncertainty on a single oscillation is why one would instead time many oscillations: timing 25 periods as 50.0 ± 0.10 s would cut δT/T by 25 and the uncertainty in g dramatically.

distractorRationales.A: 5.0% is δT/T. Because T is squared in the denominator of g, that figure must be doubled.
distractorRationales.C: 2.5% would be appropriate if g depended on √T, but g goes as 1/T^2, which increases rather than reduces the relative error.
distractorRationales.D: 25% is (5%)^2 treated as a percentage. Error propagation uses 2 × 5%, not (5%)^2.

items.stem: (2R,3R)-tartaric acid and (2S,3S)-tartaric acid rotate plane-polarized light in opposite directions. (2R,3S)-tartaric acid, however, shows [α] = 0. Which statement explains the optical inactivity of the (2R,3S) isomer?

choices.text: The (2R,3S) isomer is a racemic mixture of the (2R,3R) and (2S,3S) enantiomers.
The (2R,3S) isomer decomposes immediately in water, so no rotation can be measured.
Any molecule with two stereocenters is optically inactive because the two centers cancel.
The (2R,3S) isomer is meso: the two stereocenters are identically substituted and of opposite configuration, so an internal mirror plane makes the molecule achiral.

items.explanation: Tartaric acid’s two carbons each bear CO2H, OH, H, and the other stereocenter. When the configurations are opposite (R,S), a mirror plane (or inversion center) relates the two halves, producing a meso compound that is superposable on its mirror image and therefore optically inactive as a single stereoisomer. It is not a 1:1 mixture of the (R,R) and (S,S) enantiomers; those are a separate racemate. The (R,R) and (S,S) diastereomers lack that internal plane and are optically active. Having two stereocenters does not automatically cancel rotation.

distractorRationales.A: A racemate is an equimolar mixture of enantiomers. Meso-tartaric acid is one achiral stereoisomer, not a mixture of (R,R) and (S,S).
distractorRationales.B: Meso-tartaric acid is a stable, isolable compound; optical inactivity is a symmetry property, not a result of decomposition.
distractorRationales.C: The chiral (R,R) and (S,S) tartaric acids have two stereocenters and are optically active; cancellation requires a symmetry element, not merely two centers.

items.stem: CO2 is nonpolar while SO2 is polar, even though both molecules contain polar bonds from oxygen to a group-16 atom. Which structural difference accounts for the polarity contrast?

choices.text: CO2 is linear (C is sp), so the two C=O bond dipoles cancel; SO2 is bent because sulfur has a lone pair, so the S–O dipoles do not cancel.
CO2 has ionic bonds and SO2 has covalent bonds, so only SO2 can be polar.
Sulfur is less electronegative than carbon, which forces SO2 to be linear and therefore polar.
Both molecules are tetrahedral; SO2 is polar only because it has a larger molar mass.

items.explanation: Carbon dioxide has two electron domains around carbon, so the carbon is sp hybridized and the molecule is linear. Equal C=O bond dipoles point in opposite directions and cancel, giving a zero molecular dipole. Sulfur dioxide has three electron domains around sulfur (two bonding pairs and one lone pair), so VSEPR predicts a bent geometry. The S–O bond dipoles then have a nonzero resultant. Bond type is covalent in both molecules, and molar mass does not determine whether dipoles cancel.

distractorRationales.B: Both CO2 and SO2 are covalently bonded molecular species; polarity here is a geometry question, not an ionic-versus-covalent classification.
distractorRationales.C: Electronegativity differences create bond dipoles, but they do not force SO2 to be linear. The extra lone pair on sulfur is what bends the molecule.
distractorRationales.D: Neither molecule is tetrahedral (that would require four electron domains). Mass is irrelevant to whether vector dipoles cancel.

items.stem: Coulomb’s law is F = k |q1 q2| / r² with k = 9.0 × 10^9 N m² C−2. Two point charges of +2.0 μC and +2.0 μC are 3.0 m apart. The electric field of a single 2.0 μC charge is E = k q / r². What is F, and what is E at 3.0 m from one of the charges alone?

choices.text: F = 0 because like charges cannot exert forces in a vacuum

items.explanation: q = 2.0 × 10−6 C, r² = 9.0, so k q² / r² = (9.0×10^9)(4.0×10−12)/9.0 = (36×10−3)/9.0 = 4.0×10−3 N. E from one charge is kq/r² = (9.0×10^9)(2.0×10−6)/9.0 = 18×10^3 / 9.0 = 2.0×10^3 N C−1. Dropping the micro- prefix (using 2 C) inflates F by 10^12. E is not equal to F in newtons per coulomb by coincidence of the 4.0×10−3 figure. Like charges repel with that Coulomb force; vacuum is the setting Coulomb’s law assumes.

distractorRationales.B: 2.0 μC is 2.0 × 10−6 C, not 2.0 C; omitting 10−6 twice overstates F catastrophically.
distractorRationales.C: The force 4.0 × 10−3 N is right, but E = kq/r² = 2000 N C−1, not the force copied into N C−1.
distractorRationales.D: Coulomb’s law is a vacuum (or air) law; like charges repel with F = 4.0 mN here.

items.stem: A parathyroid adenoma secretes excess PTH. Serum Ca2+ is high and phosphate is low. PTH raises Ca2+ in part because it:

choices.text: Binds osteoblasts, increasing RANKL expression that activates osteoclasts, and also increases renal Ca2+ reabsorption and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D production
Directly binds osteoclasts as its only receptor-bearing bone cell, with no effect on kidney or vitamin D
Blocks renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase and thereby lowers intestinal Ca2+ absorption as the cause of hypercalcemia
Is identical to calcitonin and inhibits osteoclasts, which paradoxically raises serum Ca2+

items.explanation: PTH receptors on osteoblasts (and osteocytes) induce RANKL, which binds RANK on osteoclast precursors and increases bone resorption, releasing Ca2+ and phosphate. Simultaneously PTH increases distal-tubule calcium reabsorption, decreases phosphate reabsorption (explaining hypophosphatemia), and stimulates renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase to make 1,25-(OH)2D, which increases intestinal Ca2+ absorption. Osteoclasts lack the classical PTH receptor; the osteoblast relay is the MCAT-relevant point. Calcitonin, from thyroid C cells, opposes resorption. Blocking 1-alpha-hydroxylase would lower, not raise, gut Ca2+ uptake.

distractorRationales.B: PTH acts on osteoblasts to control osteoclasts via RANKL, and it has major renal/vitamin D actions.
distractorRationales.C: PTH stimulates, rather than blocks, 1-alpha-hydroxylase; hypercalcemia is not from less vitamin D.
distractorRationales.D: Calcitonin lowers serum Ca2+; PTH is not calcitonin.

items.stem: A researcher compares UTP used by RNA polymerase with dTTP used by DNA polymerase. Which structural statement is accurate?

choices.text: UTP and dTTP are the same molecule; the polymerases merely name them differently
UTP is 2′-deoxy and carries thymine, whereas dTTP is a ribonucleotide that carries uracil
Both sugars are 2′-deoxy; the only difference is the C5 methyl group on uracil versus thymine
UTP has a 2′-OH on ribose and a uracil base that lacks the C5 methyl present on thymine in dTTP, which is 2′-deoxy

items.explanation: Ribonucleoside triphosphates contain D-ribose (hydroxyls at both C2′ and C3′). Deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates lack the C2′ hydroxyl. UTP is therefore a ribose nucleotide; dTTP is a 2′-deoxy nucleotide. The bases also differ: uracil is 2,4-dioxopyrimidine, whereas thymine is 5-methyluracil. RNA polymerases incorporate UTP opposite adenine; DNA polymerases incorporate dTTP. Swapping the sugar identities or claiming the two NTPs are identical contradicts those definitions.

distractorRationales.A: The sugar (ribose vs 2′-deoxyribose) and the pyrimidine (U vs 5-methylU) both differ; the names are not interchangeable.
distractorRationales.B: This inverts both differences: UTP is a ribonucleotide with uracil, and dTTP is 2′-deoxy with thymine.
distractorRationales.C: UTP is not 2′-deoxy. The 2′-OH is the chemical hallmark of RNA building blocks and the reason RNA is alkali-labile relative to DNA.

items.stem: A teenager’s first shoplifting is treated as a one-off (Lemert’s primary deviance). After a public “delinquent” label at school, she is excluded from teams, joins a labeled peer set, and steals more. Becker’s labeling approach and Lemert’s secondary deviance most directly claim which causal order?

choices.text: The later crime is caused only by a biological atavism in Lombroso’s sense, so labels are epiphenomena
Societal reaction can stabilize an outsider identity, making further deviance a career rather than a leftover act
Durkheim proved that labeling reduces crime by clarifying boundaries, so secondary deviance cannot occur
Mertonian rebellion is the only process that can follow a school label

items.explanation: Labeling theory (Becker’s Outsiders; Lemert’s primary vs secondary deviance) argues that official and informal reactions can transform an isolated act into a master status and a deviant career. The stem’s exclusion and peer realignment are that mechanism. Lombroso’s atavism is a 19th-century biological theory, not this sequence. Durkheim did argue that some punishment clarifies norms, but that is not a denial of secondary deviance. Merton’s rebellion is one strain adaptation, not the labeling claim.

distractorRationales.A: Lombroso does not explain identity change after a school label.
distractorRationales.C: Durkheim’s functions of crime do not entail that labels cannot amplify careers in deviance.
distractorRationales.D: Labeling does not require Merton’s rebel cell as the only sequel.

items.stem: A secreted protein contains a single native disulfide between Cys48 and Cys119. Investigators separately mutate each cysteine to serine, express the mutants in oxidizing medium, and compare them with wild type by nonreducing SDS-PAGE and thermal unfolding. Which result is most consistent with the chemistry of cysteine and serine side chains?

choices.text: Each serine spontaneously forms a covalent Ser–Ser cross-link that fully replaces the native cystine
Neither mutant can form the native disulfide; both are more prone to unfolding than wild type
Only the Cys48Ser mutant loses the disulfide, because only the more N-terminal cysteine can oxidize
Both mutants migrate as covalent dimers on nonreducing SDS-PAGE because serine is oxidized by air

items.explanation: A disulfide (cystine) is a covalent bond between two cysteine thiols after oxidation. Serine has a hydroxyl in place of a thiol and cannot form that bond, so either Cys→Ser substitution removes one of the two required sulfurs and abolishes the native inter-residue disulfide. Loss of a structural disulfide commonly lowers conformational stability, so the unfolding temperature typically falls. Serine does not air-oxidize into a covalent Ser–Ser analog of cystine, and both cysteines of a pair are required regardless of sequence order.

distractorRationales.A: Serine hydroxyls do not form a cystine-like covalent cross-link under physiologic oxidizing conditions.
distractorRationales.C: Either cysteine of the pair is required; position in the sequence does not confer a unique ability to oxidize.
distractorRationales.D: Serine is not oxidized to a covalent dimer; nonreducing SDS-PAGE would not report a new intermolecular Ser–Ser bond.

items.stem:
Combustion enthalpies: methane, M = 16.0 g mol−1, ΔH_comb = −890 kJ mol−1; octane, M = 114 g mol−1, ΔH_comb = −5470 kJ mol−1. Heat released per gram is |ΔH_comb| / M.
Which fuel releases more heat per gram?

choices.text: Octane, because 5470 kJ mol−1 is larger than 890 kJ mol−1
Methane, 55.6 kJ g−1 versus 48.0 kJ g−1 for octane
The two fuels are equal per gram, because both are hydrocarbons
Octane, 5470/16.0 = 342 kJ g−1, using methane’s molar mass for octane

items.explanation: Methane: 890 / 16.0 = 55.6 kJ g−1. Octane: 5470 / 114 = 48.0 kJ g−1. Per gram, methane wins even though each octane molecule releases far more heat, because octane’s molar mass is about seven times larger (114 vs 16). Being hydrocarbons does not force equal gravimetric heats. Dividing octane’s molar enthalpy by 16 g mol−1 uses the wrong mass and inflates the octane figure to 342 kJ g−1.

distractorRationales.A: Per-mole enthalpies are not comparable until divided by molar mass; octane’s 5470 kJ is spread over 114 g.
distractorRationales.C: 55.6 and 48.0 kJ g−1 differ by about 16%; they are not equal.
distractorRationales.D: Octane’s molar mass is 114 g mol−1, not 16.0 g mol−1.

items.stem:
β-Galactosidase specific activity (relative units) in four E. coli cultures:

Carbon source | cAMP (relative) | lactose | β-gal
Glucose | 1 | absent | 1
Glucose | 1 | present | 2
Glycerol | 20 | absent | 1
Glycerol | 20 | present | 100

The lac repressor binds the operator unless lactose (allolactose) is present. CAP–cAMP must occupy the promoter for high transcription. Which regulatory logic do the four rows support?

choices.text: High expression requires both a high cAMP (low-glucose) signal and lactose to lift the repressor; either signal alone is insufficient.
Glucose induces the operon because the glucose rows would then be the high-activity ones.
cAMP is a repressor of lac, because activity is high only when cAMP is 1.
Lactose is unnecessary once cAMP is high, because the glycerol-minus-lactose row would then read 100.

items.explanation: Activity is 100 only in the glycerol-plus-lactose row, where cAMP is high and lactose is present. Glucose keeps cAMP low, so even with lactose the activity is 2. High cAMP without lactose leaves the repressor bound (activity 1). AND logic of CAP activation plus repressor removal is the only pattern that fits all four cells. Glucose is not the inducer, cAMP is not a repressor, and lactose remains required when cAMP is already high.

distractorRationales.B: Glucose rows are 1 and 2, not 100, so glucose is not the inducing condition.
distractorRationales.C: The high-cAMP lactose row is 100, so cAMP promotes, rather than represses, expression.
distractorRationales.D: Glycerol without lactose is still 1, so lifting catabolite repression is not enough without inducer.

items.stem: Ubiquinone (coenzyme Q) shuttles reducing equivalents in the inner mitochondrial membrane. Which description of its organic redox chemistry is accurate?

choices.text: The quinone is a peptide cofactor that is hydrolyzed to amino acids when it is ‘reduced’
The para-benzoquinone head accepts two electrons and two protons to give a hydroquinone (ubiquinol), a reversible phenol/quinone redox pair
Reduction of Q requires oxidative cleavage of the isoprenoid tail to acetate
Q is identical to NAD+; both are water-soluble hydride acceptors with nicotinamide rings

items.explanation: Ubiquinone is a lipid-soluble 2,3-dimethoxy-5-methyl-6-polyprenyl-1,4-benzoquinone. Two-electron, two-proton reduction converts the quinone into a p-hydroquinone (ubiquinol), the same phenol/quinone couple that appears in synthetic quinone chemistry and in vitamin K. A one-electron intermediate (semiquinone radical) is also accessible, which is why Q can bridge NADH-like two-electron chemistry and heme/Fe–S one-electron chemistry. The isoprenoid tail is a membrane anchor, not a redox substrate. Q is not a peptide and is not nicotinamide; NAD+ is a hydrophilic hydride acceptor.

distractorRationales.A: CoQ is a small-molecule quinone, not a polypeptide. Reduction does not mean proteolysis.
distractorRationales.C: The polyprenyl chain remains intact during Q/QH2 cycling; redox chemistry is confined to the quinone ring.
distractorRationales.D: NAD+ is a water-soluble nicotinamide nucleotide that accepts a hydride. CoQ is a membrane quinone with a different mechanism and solubility.

items.stem: 1930s HOLC maps graded minority neighborhoods “hazardous” (redlined). Those same census tracts today have less tree canopy, higher land-surface temperature, and more heat-related emergency visits, and the associations remain after contemporary income is included in the model. Which reading is best?

choices.text: Historical lending maps cannot have spatial effects decades later
Heat visits are explained only by individual locus of control
Environmental justice applies only to chemical Superfund sites, not to heat
Legacy residential segregation can persistently structure environmental risk and health, a core spatial-inequality pathway

items.explanation: Redlining is a historical mechanism of residential segregation: credit and investment were withheld from mapped minority neighborhoods. Those investment patterns shape later canopy, housing quality, and heat islands, which are environmental exposures with clinical consequences. Persistence after modern income adjustment is evidence of a place-based legacy, not a claim that class never matters. Environmental justice includes heat and other amenities, not only chemical dumps. Individual locus of control does not plant trees or set 1930s grades.

distractorRationales.A: The empirical pattern in the stem is a decades-later spatial correlation with the historical map.
distractorRationales.B: A tract-level canopy and temperature gap is not an internal-versus-external belief.
distractorRationales.C: Unequal exposure to heat is an environmental-justice outcome even without a Superfund listing.

items.stem: In the taped verse, the speaker who “ticked the milk as if the ticking / could make a future stand up” most nearly implies that

choices.text: household lists are a reliable technology for resurrecting cancelled weeks.
the ritual mark is a superstitious attempt to force continuance that the rest of the poem has already declared failed.
milk was the only item that mattered, and soap and tea are red herrings.
the daughter, not the father, wrote the verse as an instruction to the agent.

items.explanation: Compressed literary implication: the list is “addressed to a week that never arrived,” so the future is already cancelled. Ticking milk “as if” the mark could make a future stand up names a counterfactual, almost magical, use of a household gesture. The as-if is the inference, not a claim that lists work, not a ranking of groceries from the prose list, and not a detective theory about authorship. Reading between the lines here is reading the mood of a failed ignition, which the kettle lines have already prepared.

distractorRationales.A: The as-if construction undercuts reliability; the week never arrived.
distractorRationales.C: Soap and tea belong to the prose list; the poem uses milk as the ticked sign of continuance, not as a shopping hierarchy.
distractorRationales.D: The extract presents the verse as his scrap; nothing licenses reassigning authorship to the daughter as a note to the agent.

passage.title: Vacant possession
passage.body:
The rental had been emptied with the efficiency of people who did not live there. I arrived after the skip had gone. What remained were the marks of remaining: a paler rectangle on the wall where a calendar had blocked the sun, a screw in the kitchen plaster that had held nothing I could remember, a ring on the lino where a bin had sat long enough to become a climate. The agent called it "vacant possession." The phrase was legally tidy. It treated my father as a tenancy that had concluded.

I opened the cupboard above the kettle. Inside, taped to the wood, was a shopping list in his slanted capitals, and beneath it a scrap of verse I had never seen. He was not a man who announced poems. He had been a man who boiled water at the same hour, as if the day were a machine that required a particular ignition. The list wanted milk, soap, and a cheaper brand of tea. The last item was written twice, then crossed out, then written again, as if indecision were a kind of company.

The kettle still knew his hour.
I did not.
The cupboard kept a shopping list
addressed to a week that never arrived.
I ticked the milk as if the ticking
could make a future stand up.

I stood with a pen I had not meant to bring and put a mark beside milk, then stopped, because the gesture had the shape of care and the content of a joke at my own expense. Grief, in the pamphlets, is supposed to be a weather that passes over a landscape. In the cupboard it was more like a task left in a shared kitchen: unclaimed, slightly shameful, still assigned. I wanted, ridiculously, to buy the milk. I wanted not to be the kind of daughter who leaves a list unanswered.

The agent coughed in the hallway and mentioned carpet cleaning, then the bond, then the need to "move on" as if the room were a queue. I heard myself thank him. Courtesy was easier than explaining that the room was not empty, only unpopulated. He was not unkind. He was on a clock I did not share. Vacant possession, I thought, is a legal sentence that cannot conjugate the present tense of objects. The kettle, if it could speak, would not have used it. It would have asked why the hour had been cancelled without notice.

items.stem: In adipocytes and myocytes, insulin binding activates PI3K–Akt. Which coordinated metabolic response follows?

choices.text: GLUT2 is translocated to the muscle plasma membrane, and hormone-sensitive lipase is phosphorylated by PKA.
Glycogen synthase is phosphorylated and inactivated, matching the glucagon/epinephrine phosphorylation program.

GLUT4 vesicles fuse with the plasma membrane, protein phosphatase-1 dephosphorylates glycogen synthase (activating it) and phosphorylase (inactivating it), and hormone-sensitive lipase activity falls, promoting glucose uptake, glycogen synthesis, and fat storage.
cAMP rises, PKA phosphorylates hepatic PFK-2, and ketogenesis accelerates in muscle.

items.explanation: Insulin signaling through PI3K–Akt in fat and muscle translocates GLUT4 to the membrane, increasing glucose uptake. Akt-linked pathways activate protein phosphatase-1, which dephosphorylates glycogen synthase (activating it) and glycogen phosphorylase (inactivating it). Insulin also opposes PKA-driven lipolysis, lowering hormone-sensitive lipase activity. The net program is glucose uptake, glycogen synthesis, and fat storage. GLUT2 is the liver/β-cell transporter, not the insulin-responsive muscle/fat carrier. Phosphorylation of glycogen synthase and a rise in cAMP are glucagon/epinephrine programs. Muscle is not a ketogenic organ, and insulin lowers rather than raises cAMP-dependent fasting pathways.

distractorRationales.A: Insulin-responsive uptake in muscle and fat uses GLUT4, not GLUT2, and insulin reduces rather than PKA-activates hormone-sensitive lipase.
distractorRationales.B: Insulin promotes dephosphorylation and activation of glycogen synthase; phosphorylation/inactivation is the glucagon pathway.
distractorRationales.D: Insulin lowers cAMP-dependent signaling; ketogenesis is hepatic in the fasted state, not an insulin-driven muscle pathway.

items.stem: For ATP hydrolysis, ΔG°′ = −30.5 kJ mol−1. In a resting myocyte the mass-action ratio Q = [ADP][Pi]/[ATP] is much smaller than Keq, and RT ln Q = −22 kJ mol−1 at the relevant temperature. What is ΔG, and what does the comparison to ΔG°′ mean?

choices.text: ΔG = −52.5 kJ mol−1; hydrolysis is more exergonic than the standard-state value because Q ≪ 1
ΔG is always equal to ΔG°′ = −30.5 kJ mol−1, because Q cannot affect a standard free energy
ΔG = +8.5 kJ mol−1; a small Q makes the reaction endergonic
ΔG = 0, because any reaction with a defined Keq is at equilibrium in cells

items.explanation: The living-cell driving force is ΔG = ΔG°′ + RT ln Q, not ΔG°′ alone. Substituting the given values yields −30.5 + (−22) = −52.5 kJ mol−1. A Q far below Keq (high ATP relative to ADP and Pi) makes RT ln Q negative and therefore makes hydrolysis more exergonic than the 1 M standard state. ΔG°′ is the value at Q = 1; it does not freeze ΔG in a cell. A negative RT ln Q cannot flip the sign to endergonic here, and cells maintain ATP hydrolysis far from equilibrium (ΔG ≠ 0) so that the reaction can do useful work.

distractorRationales.B: ΔG°′ is defined at Q = 1. Cellular Q is not 1, so ΔG differs from ΔG°′ by RT ln Q.
distractorRationales.C: RT ln Q is negative, so it adds to the already negative ΔG°′ rather than canceling it. The reaction is more, not less, exergonic.
distractorRationales.D: Keq being large does not place the cell at equilibrium. Homeostasis holds Q ≪ Keq so that ΔG remains strongly negative.

items.stem: A uniform metal wire has resistance 8 Ω. It is drawn through a die so that its length doubles while its volume remains the same. The resistance of the stretched wire is:

choices.text: 4 Ω
8 Ω

items.explanation: Resistance is R = ρ L / A. Volume V = A L is conserved, so doubling L forces A to halve. The new resistance is therefore R' = ρ (2L) / (A/2) = 4 (ρ L / A) = 4 R = 32 Ω. Length in the numerator and area in the denominator each contribute a factor of two. Resistivity ρ is a material property and does not change merely because the wire is longer. Treating only L as doubled while holding A fixed undercounts the increase (16 Ω instead of 32 Ω).

distractorRationales.A: This halves the original resistance, as if stretching made the wire a better conductor. Both the longer path and the thinner cross-section raise R.
distractorRationales.B: Volume and mass are unchanged, but resistance depends on geometry (L/A), which did change. Unchanged ρ is not the same as unchanged R.
distractorRationales.C: This doubles R using only L' = 2L and holding A fixed. Drawing the wire conserves volume, so A also halves and R scales by four, not two.

items.stem: A Doppler ultrasound transducer emits 2.0 MHz ultrasound into tissue. Blood in an artery is moving toward the transducer. Compared with 2.0 MHz, the frequency of the echo returning from that blood is:

choices.text: lower, because a moving reflector always lengthens the received wavelength
higher, because motion of the reflector toward the detector shortens the received wavelength
unchanged, because soft tissue is a linear medium and cannot shift frequency
higher only if the blood speed exceeds the speed of sound in tissue

items.explanation: Doppler shift for a reflector moving toward the source/detector raises the received frequency: the blood acts first as a moving observer (higher frequency intercepted) and then as a moving source (higher frequency re-radiated). Equivalently, successive wavefronts are compressed, so λ decreases and f = v/λ increases. Soft tissue being approximately linear does not cancel first-order Doppler physics; the shift is how clinical Doppler estimates flow toward or away from the probe. The blood speed is much less than the ~1540 m/s tissue sound speed; no sonic-boom threshold is required for a frequency increase.

distractorRationales.A: A reflector receding from the probe would lower frequency. Motion toward the probe compresses, rather than stretches, the returning wavelength.
distractorRationales.C: Linearity of tissue means waves superpose without generating new harmonics as the first approximation; it does not forbid a Doppler shift from a moving reflector.
distractorRationales.D: The ordinary Doppler formula applies at speeds far below the speed of sound. Exceeding the tissue sound speed is neither necessary nor physiologic for a higher echo frequency.

items.stem: A 4.0 x 10^-6 m^3 kidney stone is fully submerged in fluid of density 1000 kg/m^3. The magnitude of the buoyant force is (g = 10 m/s^2):
items.explanation: Archimedes' principle says the buoyant force equals the weight of displaced fluid, rho_fluid V g, and does not depend on the object's own density while the object remains fully submerged. Substituting gives 1000 times 4.0 x 10^-6 times 10, which equals 4.0 x 10^-2 N. Using the stone's density instead of the fluid's, or dropping rho or g, produces the nearby distractors.

distractorRationales.A: This is V g without density (4.0 x 10^-6 x 10). Buoyancy requires multiplying by the fluid density in SI units.
distractorRationales.B: This is rho V without g (1000 x 4.0 x 10^-6). In SI, weight-like forces still include g.
distractorRationales.C: This doubles the correct force, as if the object's density were 2000 kg/m^3 and that density replaced the fluid density in F_b. Displaced-fluid density is what enters Archimedes' law.

items.stem: After a widely televised air-ambulance crash, a premed clinic’s waiting-room survey shows patients now rate dying in a plane crash as likelier than dying in a car, despite contrary base rates. Tversky and Kahneman’s heuristics program names this bias as which process?

choices.text: The representativeness heuristic, because the crash is judged similar to a prototype of “safe commercial aviation”
The availability heuristic, because easily retrieved vivid instances inflate judged probability
Anchoring on the first numeral of the flight number, which is the only named Tversky–Kahneman bias
Piagetian formal operations, which force statistical base-rate use

items.explanation: Availability is judging frequency or probability by ease of retrieval. Media vividness makes the crash easy to bring to mind and inflates its subjective risk relative to mundane car fatalities. Representativeness is judging by similarity to a stereotype or prototype, not by media retrieval. Anchoring is undue influence of an initial number; no such number is supplied. Formal operations would, if anything, support using base rates, which these patients are ignoring.

distractorRationales.A: Representativeness is similarity-to-prototype reasoning, not “what comes to mind after television.”
distractorRationales.C: Anchoring needs a starting value; the stem supplies vivid instances, not a numeric anchor.
distractorRationales.D: Formal-operational competence would predict better, not worse, use of base rates.

items.stem: An antisense DNA oligonucleotide is designed to base-pair with the mRNA sequence 5′-AUG CGA UUC-3′. Which DNA sequence, written 5′ to 3′, is complementary and antiparallel?

choices.text: 5′-ATG CGA TTC-3′
5′-GAA TCG CAT-3′
5′-TAC GCT AAG-3′
5′-TTC AGC GTA-3′

items.explanation: Watson–Crick pairing is complementary and antiparallel, and DNA uses T in place of U. The mRNA 5′-AUG CGA UUC-3′ therefore pairs with DNA 3′-TAC GCT AAG-5′. Rewriting that DNA strand in the conventional 5′ to 3′ direction gives 5′-GAA TCG CAT-3′. Choice A is the coding-strand equivalent of the RNA (T for U) and would run parallel to the mRNA, not pair with it. Writing the complement without reversing polarity (5′-TAC GCT AAG-3′) is a common 5′/3′ error. Getting both complementarity and polarity correct is required for an antisense oligo to hybridize.

distractorRationales.A: This sequence matches the mRNA with T in place of U (coding-like) and would be parallel, not complementary-antiparallel, to the target.
distractorRationales.C: This is the complement written in the same 5′ to 3′ order as the mRNA, which would be parallel rather than antiparallel; the strand must be reversed to 5′-GAA TCG CAT-3′.
distractorRationales.D: This sequence is neither the reverse complement nor a simple T-for-U copy of the mRNA, so it would not form a continuous Watson–Crick duplex with the target.

items.stem: Treating HA as a strong acid from the initial pH would estimate [H+] as

choices.text: 0.100 mol L−1, because the label says 0.100.
about 1.3 × 10−3 mol L−1 from pH 2.88, which already shows the strong-acid assumption is false for 0.100 M HA.

items.explanation: pH 2.88 means [H+] = 10^−2.88 ≈ 1.3 × 10−3, two orders below 0.100, so HA is weak; the classmate’s strong-acid move is contradicted by the first row. 10−7 is neutrality. Dilution arithmetic in D is unrelated. Evaluating the hypothesis “initial pH as strong acid” uses the datum the table actually gives.

distractorRationales.A: That would be full dissociation; pH would be 1.0, not 2.88.
distractorRationales.C: Not the measured pH.
distractorRationales.D: Invented stoichiometry, not [H+] from pH.

passage.title: Unknown weak acid titration
passage.body:
25.00 mL of monoprotic unknown HA (0.100 mol L−1 stated by the stockroom) is titrated with 0.100 mol L−1 NaOH at 25 °C. pH is measured with a probe calibrated at 4.00 and 10.00.

V(NaOH) / mL | pH
0.00 | 2.88
5.00 | 3.46
12.50 | 4.20
20.00 | 4.94
24.00 | 5.56
25.00 | 8.72
26.00 | 11.24
30.00 | 12.15

A classmate says the equivalence volume must be 12.50 mL because that is “half way on the page.” Another wants Ka from the initial pH alone, treating HA as if it were a strong acid.

items.stem:
A comment set reads:
1. “Home is the place that still uses your childhood name.”
2. “I left so that I could speak; I stayed silent so that I could stay.”
3. “Belonging is a practice, not a passport stamp.”
4. “We inherit rooms before we inherit opinions.”
5. “Forgiveness is sometimes just a tired kind of accuracy.”
Which identification correctly treats this as a Task B personal theme rather than a Task A policy brief?

choices.text: Border-security legislation and visa quotas, because “passport” appears once.
Lived belonging, leaving, silence, inherited rooms, and the ordinary work of forgiveness—personal and social experience rather than a program of reform.
Interest-rate policy, because inheritance is mentioned.
The same socio-cultural waiting-time issue as a typical Task A clock set.

items.explanation: Task B comment sets orbit lived experience: love, identity, memory, belonging, failure. This set’s centre is home, silence, inherited rooms, and forgiveness as accuracy—not a ministerial brief. A single word (passport, inherit) does not convert it into immigration law or macroeconomics. Nor is it a waiting-time policy paper. A student who writes Task A rhetoric here (should the state do X) has misidentified the task. B names the personal theme tightly enough that a reflective essay has somewhere to stand.

distractorRationales.A: Passport is a metaphor for belonging, not an invitation to write a visa-quota argument.
distractorRationales.C: Inheritance of rooms is domestic and formative, not a prompt about cash rates.
distractorRationales.D: Clocks and queues are a different set; importing them here abandons these comments.

items.stem: A low-income census tract has no full-service grocery within a mile and a high density of fast-food outlets. An income-matched tract with a supermarket has lower obesity prevalence. Which interpretation is most consistent with spatial inequality?

choices.text: Taste forms independently of retail geography, so the grocery gap cannot matter
This pattern is stage 1 of the demographic transition
Unequal spatial access to healthy food (a food desert) can shape diet and obesity beyond individual income alone
Deindividuation inside supermarkets is what causes obesity

items.explanation: Food deserts are a spatial-inequality pattern: healthy retail is absent or distant in some neighborhoods, while energy-dense outlets cluster there. Matching on income isolates place—how the built food environment is arranged—as a contributor to diet and obesity. That does not claim geography is the only cause, but it does reject the idea that income-matched people must have identical exposure. Demographic transition stages and deindividuation in aisles are the wrong models for a grocery-access gap.

distractorRationales.A: If geography were irrelevant, the income-matched supermarket tract should not differ; the contrast is the evidence that access matters.
distractorRationales.B: Stage 1 is high birth and death rates, not grocery placement.
distractorRationales.D: Anonymity in a crowd does not explain why the tract without a grocery has more obesity.

items.stem: A friend laughs at one comedian: everyone in the room laughs (high consensus), she rarely laughs at other comedians (high distinctiveness), and she always laughs at this one (high consistency). Kelley’s covariation model points to which attribution?

choices.text: Internal: she is a chronically giggly person
External: something about this comedian/situation elicits laughter
Always internal when consistency is high, regardless of consensus and distinctiveness
Fundamental attribution error as a prescriptive rule: ignore consensus by design

items.explanation: Kelley’s covariation rules: high consensus, high distinctiveness, and high consistency yield an external (stimulus/situation) attribution—the comedian is funny. Low consensus, low distinctiveness, high consistency yield an internal attribution (a giggly person). High consistency alone is not diagnostic. FAE is a bias that underuses such situational patterns; it is not Kelley’s prescribed algebra. The stem is the textbook external cell.

distractorRationales.A: A person attribution needs low consensus and low distinctiveness, not the pattern given.
distractorRationales.C: Consistency must be combined with consensus and distinctiveness; it is not sufficient for an internal call.
distractorRationales.D: Kelley’s model uses consensus; FAE is the error of neglecting it.

items.stem:
A population grows logistically: dN/dt = r N (1 − N/K) with r = 0.50 yr−1 and K = 400 individuals. Tabulated states:

N | 1 − N/K | dN/dt (yr−1)
0 | 1.00 | 0
100 | 0.75 | 37.5
200 | 0.50 | 50
400 | 0.00 | 0

If the same r were used in exponential growth dN/dt = rN at N = 200, that rate would be 100 yr−1. Which statement is true?

choices.text: Logistic growth is fastest at N = 0, where unused carrying capacity is greatest
At N = 400 the population still increases at rK = 200 yr−1
Exponential and logistic rates are equal at N = 200 because both contain the factor rN
The maximum logistic recruitment is at N = K/2 = 200, where dN/dt = 50, half the exponential rate at the same N

items.explanation: The logistic term (1 − N/K) is 0.5 at half carrying capacity, so dN/dt = 0.50 × 200 × 0.5 = 50 yr−1, matching the table and equal to half of rN = 100. The product N(1 − N/K) is maximised at N = K/2, not at N = 0 (where N itself is 0, so dN/dt = 0) and not at K (where the bracket is 0). Exponential equality fails because the extra (1 − N/K) factor is 0.5, not 1, at N = 200. At K the population stops growing.

distractorRationales.A: The N = 0 row has dN/dt = 0; an empty habitat has unused K but no parents.
distractorRationales.B: The N = 400 row is 0, the definition of carrying capacity.
distractorRationales.C: The table’s 50 versus the exponential 100 shows they are not equal; (1 − N/K) is missing from the exponential model.

items.stem: Two patients complete the same diabetes-education class. Patient A says “what I do with food and insulin determines my HbA1c” and logs glucose daily. Patient B says “the number is mostly luck and whatever the doctor decides” and rarely logs. At six months, A has the lower HbA1c. Which self-related construct best captures the contrast?

choices.text: A has lower self-efficacy by definition, because internals never believe they can act
B has an internal locus of control, because luck is an internal cause
Looking-glass self explains the HbA1c gap, because no behavior is involved
Internal locus of control (A) is linked to more instrumental health behavior than external locus (B)

items.explanation: Locus of control is the belief that outcomes are caused primarily by one’s own actions (internal) or by luck, fate, or powerful others (external). Patient A’s statement and logging are internal; B’s luck-and-doctor account is external. Internality is associated with taking instrumental steps, which can improve a controllable biomarker such as HbA1c. Self-efficacy is capability belief, not the opposite of internality. Luck is a canonical external cause. Looking-glass self is about reflected appraisals, not glucose logging.

distractorRationales.A: Internal locus typically supports, rather than forbids, the belief that one’s actions matter; that is closer to higher, not lower, efficacy.
distractorRationales.B: Luck and powerful others are external attributions, not internal ones.
distractorRationales.C: The pathway in the stem runs through logging behavior, not through imagined judgments in a mirror.

items.stem: Country Y already has a crude death rate near 8 per 1,000. Over one generation, crude birth rate falls from 35 to 18 as women’s schooling and contraception spread; growth is still positive but slowing. Country Z has CBR ≈ CDR ≈ 10 and TFR near 2.1, with roughly stable size. Which staging is correct?

choices.text: Y is stage 1 and Z is stage 2
Y is stage 3 (fertility falling after mortality already fell); Z is stage 4 (low birth and death, equilibrium)
Both are stage 2, because any positive growth means stage 2
Z is stage 2, because replacement-level TFR indicates a mortality crisis

items.explanation: Stage 3 is the fertility decline that follows the earlier mortality decline of stage 2; Y matches that description. Stage 4 is the subsequent regime of low fertility, low mortality, and little natural increase; Z’s replacement TFR and matched crude rates match stage 4. Stage 1 is high-high, and stage 2 is high birth with falling death, neither of which fits Z. Positive growth can occur in late stage 2 or 3 and does not by itself equal stage 2. Replacement TFR is not a death-rate spike.

distractorRationales.A: Y’s already-low death rate and falling births are not stage 1; Z’s low-low pattern is not stage 2.
distractorRationales.C: Stage 2 is specifically the lag of fertility behind mortality, not any nonzero growth.
distractorRationales.D: TFR near 2.1 with low CDR is controlled fertility, not a mortality crisis.

items.stem: An autosomal dominant disorder has 70% penetrance. An affected heterozygous parent, genotype confirmed by sequencing, has a child with an unaffected, unrelated partner who does not carry the mutant allele. Assuming no de novo mutation, what is the probability that the child is clinically affected?

choices.text: 0.35, because the child has a 1/2 chance of inheriting the mutant allele and, if so, a 0.70 chance of expressing the phenotype.
0.70, because penetrance replaces Mendelian segregation and every child of an affected parent is at the full penetrance risk.
0.50, because complete dominance guarantees that every heterozygote is affected regardless of the stated penetrance.
0.25, the Mendelian fraction of affected offspring from a heterozygous recessive cross.

items.explanation: The child inherits the known mutant allele from the heterozygous parent with probability 1/2; the unrelated partner contributes only wild-type alleles. Incomplete penetrance means that only 70% of heterozygotes manifest the phenotype, so the joint probability of inheriting the allele and expressing disease is 0.5 × 0.70 = 0.35. Penetrance is a conditional probability given genotype; it does not cancel segregation. Dominance describes the phenotype of heterozygotes who do express the trait, not a guarantee of 100% expression when penetrance is 70%. The 0.25 figure applies to affected homozygotes from two heterozygotes for a recessive trait, which this pedigree is not.

distractorRationales.B: Each child still has only a 50% chance of inheriting the mutant allele; 0.70 applies only among those who inherit it.
distractorRationales.C: If penetrance were complete the risk would be 0.50, but the stem specifies 70% penetrance, so many heterozygotes are clinically unaffected.
distractorRationales.D: This mating is dominant with an unaffected noncarrier partner, not a recessive het × het cross.

items.stem: Cyanide is added to cultured cells. Oxygen consumption ceases, the inner-membrane proton gradient collapses, and NADH cannot be reoxidized. Which complex is inhibited, and which reaction fails?

choices.text: Complex I; mammalian cells continue to reduce oxygen through a cyanide-resistant NADH oxidase.
Complex II; molecular oxygen is the physiologic substrate of succinate dehydrogenase.
Complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase); transfer of electrons to O2 to form H2O is blocked.
ATP synthase; cyanide occupies the F0 proton pore in the same way as oligomycin.

items.explanation: Cytochrome c oxidase (Complex IV) transfers electrons from cytochrome c to molecular oxygen, reducing O2 to water and pumping protons. Cyanide binds the heme iron of cytochrome a3 and blocks that terminal step, so oxygen consumption stops. Upstream carriers, including NADH, remain reduced because electrons have nowhere to go, and proton pumping fails as electron flow stops, collapsing Δp. Complex I and II do not reduce O2 as their substrate, and there is no physiologically adequate cyanide-resistant oxidase in typical human cells that would keep respiration going. Cyanide is not an oligomycin-like F0 plug.

distractorRationales.A: Cyanide’s acute lethal target is Complex IV, not Complex I. Human mitochondria do not maintain oxygen consumption via a cyanide-resistant NADH oxidase after Complex IV is blocked.
distractorRationales.B: Succinate dehydrogenase reduces ubiquinone, not O2. Blocking Complex II would not be the cyanide mechanism described.
distractorRationales.D: Oligomycin, not cyanide, blocks the ATP synthase proton channel. Cyanide stops electron flow to oxygen at Complex IV.

items.stem: GFR is 125 mL/min and plasma glucose is 400 mg/dL. The renal glucose Tm is 375 mg/min. Ignoring splay, glucose excretion is closest to:

choices.text: 0 mg/min, because the proximal tubule always reabsorbs 100% of filtered glucose
500 mg/min, equal to the filtered load with no reabsorption
375 mg/min, equal to Tm as if Tm were excreted rather than reabsorbed
125 mg/min, because filtered load is 500 mg/min and reabsorption saturates at 375 mg/min

items.explanation: Filtered load = GFR x plasma concentration. Convert 125 mL/min to 1.25 dL/min and multiply by 400 mg/dL to obtain 500 mg/min (or 125 mL/min x 4 mg/mL). The proximal Na-glucose transporters reabsorb up to Tm = 375 mg/min. Excretion is filtered minus reabsorbed = 125 mg/min once Tm is exceeded. Below threshold, excretion would be ~0, but 400 mg/dL is well above threshold. Tm is the reabsorptive ceiling, not the excreted amount, and the kidney does not ignore reabsorption entirely.

distractorRationales.A: Glucose appears in urine once filtered load exceeds Tm; 100% reabsorption is not guaranteed.
distractorRationales.B: This ignores Tm reabsorption of 375 mg/min.
distractorRationales.C: Tm is reabsorbed, not excreted.

items.stem: Which sentence is closest to the commentator’s own conclusion rather than a view attributed to others?

choices.text: Officials called it a demonstration of service.
The fight had become, for a night, a question of illumination.
NORMALITY RETURNS.
The empty tram definitely shortened the dispute by frightening the board.

items.explanation: The last sentence, after dismissing both historian camps as less useful than the clerk, is the commentator’s distillation. A is attributed to officials. C is a headline. D is one camp the text refuses to settle. Identifying conclusion versus support or versus reported speech is the skill: B is the writer’s closing claim.

distractorRationales.A: Attributed to officials.
distractorRationales.C: A newspaper heading, not the commentator’s verdict.
distractorRationales.D: The text says historians disagree and prefers the clerk to either camp.

passage.title: Note on a cancelled tram
passage.body:
In the third week of the lockout the company ran a single tram, brightly lit, along the route at dusk, with no passengers permitted. Officials called it a demonstration of service. Strikers called it a lantern on a coffin. Children ran beside it anyway, as they had when the cars were working, and were photographed. The photograph was printed in the morning paper under the heading NORMALITY RETURNS, and in an overseas paper under the heading CHILDREN MOCK THE DEAD LINE.

A clerk in the tram office, years later, wrote that he had been told to leave the lights on even if the generator complained, because darkness would look like surrender. He added, without apparent bitterness, that surrender had already occurred in the timetable. What remained was a moving argument about who owned the look of a street at evening.
