Actin-ring assembly, which is what physically pulls sisters to opposite poles

items.explanation: Cohesin rings hold sister chromatids together from S phase until anaphase. The spindle checkpoint ultimately allows the anaphase-promoting complex to ubiquitinate securin; free separase then proteolyzes the kleisin subunit of cohesin, especially at centromeres, so sisters can disjoin. A separase loss-of-function after alignment therefore freezes cells in metaphase with intact cohesion. DNA licensing is a G1/S event, the nuclear envelope is already gone in animal metaphase, and the mitotic spindle of microtubules, not the cytokinetic actin ring, is what segregates chromatids.

distractorRationales.B: Replication occurs in S phase; it is not re-executed to trigger anaphase.
distractorRationales.C: Metaphase animal cells have already broken down the nuclear envelope.
distractorRationales.D: The actin contractile ring drives cytokinesis after chromatids have separated; it is not the anaphase chromatid engine.

items.stem: Among the isoelectronic species O2-, F-, Na+, and Mg2+, the ionic radius is largest for:

choices.text: Mg2+, because it has the most protons pulling on the electron cloud
Na+, because sodium is an alkali metal and alkali cations are always the largest isoelectronic species
O2-, because it has the smallest nuclear charge acting on the same number of electrons
F-, because fluorine is the most electronegative element

items.explanation: These four ions all have 10 electrons (the neon configuration). For a fixed electron count, radius decreases as nuclear charge Z increases, because the same cloud is pulled inward more strongly. Oxygen (Z = 8) has the fewest protons of the set, so O2- is the largest; then F- (Z = 9), then Na+ (Z = 11), then Mg2+ (Z = 12), which is the smallest. Electronegativity of the neutral atom is not the ranking tool for isoelectronic ionic radii, and extra protons shrink rather than expand the ion.

distractorRationales.A: More protons at fixed electron number shrink the ion. Mg2+ is the smallest member of this isoelectronic series, not the largest.
distractorRationales.B: Alkali-metal parentage does not override Zeff. Na+ is smaller than both O2- and F- because sodium has more protons (11) than O or F.
distractorRationales.D: Fluorine's high electronegativity describes the atom's pull on bonding electrons; it does not make F- the largest 10-electron ion. O2- has still fewer protons.

items.stem: A eukaryotic cell is treated with α-amanitin at a concentration that strongly inhibits RNA polymerase II but leaves RNA polymerase I largely unaffected. After a short 3H-uridine pulse, which class of newly made RNA is expected to decrease the most?

choices.text: Heterogeneous nuclear RNA that is processed into mRNA
45S precursor rRNA synthesized in the nucleolus
Most tRNAs, which are primary products of RNA polymerase I
The RNA component of mitochondrial ribosomes, made by RNA polymerase II imported into mitochondria

items.explanation: RNA polymerase II synthesizes pre-mRNA (hnRNA) and some snRNAs. α-Amanitin at classic concentrations binds Pol II with high affinity and blocks elongation, so pulse-labeled hnRNA collapses quickly. RNA polymerase I, which makes the 45S rRNA precursor in the nucleolus, is relatively resistant, so nucleolar rRNA labeling continues. tRNAs are made by RNA polymerase III, not Pol I, so choice C misassigns the polymerase. Mitochondrial rRNAs are transcribed by a distinct mitochondrial RNA polymerase, not by imported Pol II. The pulse-label design reports new synthesis, not the bulk of pre-existing rRNA.

distractorRationales.B: 45S pre-rRNA is an RNA polymerase I product. At a Pol II-selective amanitin dose, Pol I activity remains, so this class should not drop the most.
distractorRationales.C: Nuclear tRNAs are transcribed by RNA polymerase III, not polymerase I. The choice is wrong both as the expected decrease and as a polymerase assignment.
distractorRationales.D: Mitochondrial rRNA is made by the mitochondrial RNA polymerase, not by nuclear RNA polymerase II, so it is not the primary target of nuclear Pol II inhibition.

items.stem:
A student mixes 30.0 mL of 0.250 M HCl with 30.0 mL of 0.100 M NaOH. Both solutes are strong. Amounts before mixing and the total volume afterwards are:

Species | Amount (mmol) | After mixing
HCl | 7.50 | excess H+ remains
NaOH | 3.00 | fully consumed
Total volume | — | 60.0 mL

What is the pH of the final solution?
items.explanation: HCl supplies 30.0 mL × 0.250 M = 7.50 mmol of H+. NaOH supplies 30.0 mL × 0.100 M = 3.00 mmol of OH−. After neutralization, 4.50 mmol of H+ remains in 60.0 mL, so [H+] = 4.50 mmol / 60.0 mL = 0.0750 M. Then pH = −log10(0.0750) = 1.12. Equal volumes do not imply a neutral mixture because the acid is more concentrated. The leftover solute is a strong acid, so the pH is acidic, not 14 minus 1.12. Using the leftover millimoles in only 30.0 mL would give [H+] = 0.150 M and pH 0.82, which ignores dilution by the other aliquot.

distractorRationales.A: 0.82 is −log10(0.150), which uses leftover H+ in 30.0 mL instead of the combined 60.0 mL volume.
distractorRationales.C: pH 7 would require equal millimoles of strong acid and strong base. Here acid millimoles are larger (7.50 versus 3.00).
distractorRationales.D: 12.88 is what one would obtain if the leftover reagent were treated as OH− (pOH = 1.12). The leftover reagent is H+, so the solution is acidic.

items.stem: Two cities have the same citywide percentage of Black residents. In City A those residents are evenly spread across tracts; in City B nearly all live in three tracts. The index of dissimilarity is much higher in B. Asthma hospitalizations cluster in B’s segregated tracts despite similar citywide income. Which conclusion is most warranted?

choices.text: Evenness of groups across tracts cannot affect health if citywide composition is matched
Segregation can be measured only in majority-Black cities, so B’s index is invalid
The dissimilarity index measures income inequality only and cannot be computed for race
Residential segregation—the uneven spatial distribution of groups—can concentrate hazards and limit resources even when citywide composition is held constant

items.explanation: Spatial inequality includes how groups are arranged in space, not only each group’s citywide share. The index of dissimilarity quantifies how unevenly two groups are spread across neighborhoods; City B is more segregated despite an identical overall percentage. Segregated tracts can concentrate pollution, poor housing, and weak services, producing clustered asthma that a citywide average conceals. Dissimilarity is routinely computed for race and does not require a majority-Black city. Matching citywide composition is what makes the spatial arrangement the remaining explanation.

distractorRationales.A: The point of comparing A and B is that evenness can differ—and can track health—when composition is matched.
distractorRationales.B: Dissimilarity is defined for any pair of group shares; majority status is not a requirement.
distractorRationales.C: Dissimilarity is a segregation statistic for any two groups, including racial groups, not an income-Gini by another name.

items.stem: After a fatty meal, lymph in the thoracic duct is milky with chylomicrons. Surgical ligation of the thoracic duct near its junction with the left subclavian vein would be expected to:

choices.text: Increase delivery of dietary long-chain triglycerides into mixed venous blood
Block all intestinal glucose absorption, which is entirely lymph-dependent
Prevent hemoglobin recycling by macrophages as the duct’s primary cargo
Impair return of chylomicrons and interstitial lymph to the venous system, with backup of intestinal lymph

items.explanation: Enterocytes package long-chain fatty acids into chylomicrons that enter lacteals, not blood capillaries, and reach the circulation via the thoracic duct at the left subclavian vein. Ligating that duct therefore interrupts both dietary fat transport and a major route of lymph return, producing chylous backup. Glucose and amino acids use portal blood, so they are not duct-dependent. Hemoglobin from senescent RBCs is processed by macrophages and the liver, not as thoracic-duct chyle. The milky appearance after a fat meal is the clinical clue that the cargo is chylomicron lipid.

distractorRationales.A: Ligation reduces, not increases, chylomicron entry into venous blood.
distractorRationales.B: Monosaccharides are absorbed into mesenteric capillaries and the portal vein.
distractorRationales.C: The thoracic duct is not the primary hemoglobin-recycling pathway.

items.stem:
Nuclear processes are written as parent (Z, A) → daughter (Z, A):
Process 1: (92, 238) → (90, 234)
Process 2: (90, 234) → (91, 234)
Process 3: (91, 234) → (92, 234)
Process 4: (92, 234) → (90, 230)
Alpha emission decreases Z by 2 and A by 4. Beta-minus emission increases Z by 1 and leaves A unchanged.
Which processes are alpha emissions?

choices.text: 2 and 3
1 and 2
3 and 4
1 and 4

items.explanation: Process 1 drops Z by 2 and A by 4 (92 → 90, 238 → 234), the alpha signature. Process 4 does the same (92 → 90, 234 → 230). Processes 2 and 3 keep A = 234 while Z increases by 1 (90 → 91, then 91 → 92), which is beta-minus decay (a neutron converting to a proton). Mixing an alpha with a beta, or pairing the two betas, does not match the ΔZ, ΔA rules given in the stem.

distractorRationales.A: Processes 2 and 3 are β− (A unchanged, Z + 1), not alpha.
distractorRationales.B: Process 2 is β−; only process 1 of this pair is alpha.
distractorRationales.C: Process 3 is β−; only process 4 of this pair is alpha.

items.stem:
Two spherical cells are compared. Cell L has diameter 20 µm (radius 10 µm). Cell S has diameter 10 µm (radius 5 µm). Surface area = 4πr² and volume = (4/3)πr³, so the surface-to-volume ratio equals 3/r. Membrane transport capacity scales with surface area; metabolic demand scales with volume.
Which statement follows?

choices.text: Cell S is more transport-limited because its SA/V is 0.60 µm−1 versus 0.30 µm−1 for L.
The two cells are equally transport-limited because both are spheres with the same 3/r formula.
Cell L is more transport-limited because its SA/V is 0.30 µm−1, half that of cell S (0.60 µm−1).
Cell L is more transport-limited because it has the larger SA/V of 0.60 µm−1.

items.explanation: For a sphere, SA/V = 3/r. Cell L has r = 10 µm so SA/V = 0.30 µm−1; cell S has r = 5 µm so SA/V = 0.60 µm−1. The larger cell therefore has only half as much membrane per unit cytoplasm. Nutrient import, gas exchange, and waste export are more likely to limit L than S. Being spherical does not equalise the ratios, and 0.60 µm−1 belongs to the smaller cell, not L.

distractorRationales.A: A higher SA/V eases, rather than limits, membrane transport relative to volume; S is less limited.
distractorRationales.B: The same geometric formula still yields different numerical ratios when r differs.
distractorRationales.D: L’s SA/V is 0.30 µm−1, not 0.60 µm−1; the larger value belongs to S.

items.stem: The phrase “rights as an audition” most nearly suggests that

choices.text: legal rights at a border exist only when performed as a complete, sequential, appropriately tearful story for an official.
actors should replace border officials.
smiling manuals have abolished the need to persuade anyone that a life is plausible.
databases never contradict speech loosened by tea.

items.explanation: The second paragraph says rights that must be performed as a story—complete, sequential, tearful at approved moments—are rights as an audition. The inference is about the form of proof, not about hiring actors. Courtesy training does not remove the grammar of plausibility. Tea is later an instrument of the file, not a proof that contradiction never comes. Vocabulary here is the author’s compression of performance requirements into “audition.”

distractorRationales.B: Audition is a metaphor for the applicant’s burden, not a staffing proposal.
distractorRationales.C: Courtesy is disinfectant for raised voices; the deeper grammar remains.
distractorRationales.D: The tea sentence says speech can be loosened until it can be contradicted.

passage.title: Courtesy at the checkpoint
passage.body:
A border official is trained in courtesy as if courtesy were a disinfectant. Smile, use the family name, apologize for the wait. The training manuals are not cynical. They are trying to prevent the obvious cruelty of a raised voice. What they cannot prevent is the deeper grammar of the encounter: one person may leave, the other must persuade a stranger that her life is plausible.

Liberal theory likes to treat this grammar as an unfortunate delay on the way to a principle. In the principle, the stranger is already a rights-bearer; the checkpoint is a bureaucratic remainder. On the ground, the remainder is the event. Rights that must be performed as a story—complete, sequential, tearful at the approved moments—are rights as an audition. The official who says “help me to help you” is not necessarily a villain. He is naming the price of entry into a language that pretends it is only asking for facts.

Scholars of hospitality distinguish welcome from inspection. The distinction is cleaner on the page than in a queue. Inspection can dress as welcome, and welcome can become inspection the moment a detail fails to match a database. A cup of tea in an interview room is not the opposite of a file. It can be the file’s most efficient instrument, loosening speech until it can be contradicted.

None of this requires pretending that states have no legitimate interest in knowing who crosses. It requires noticing that “legitimate interest” is not a measuring cup. It expands. Yesterday’s emergency power is today’s ordinary form. Tomorrow’s form will be justified by the person who told her story too well, or too badly, last year. The archive of interviews becomes a training set for suspicion.

The courteous checkpoint is therefore not a milder politics. It is a politics that has learned to sound like a service. If we want a different politics, we will need a different distribution of who must be plausible to whom—not a warmer script for the same audition.

items.stem: A ball is launched from level ground at 20 m s−1 and 45° in a region where g = 10 m s−2 and air resistance is neglected. Take sin 45° = cos 45° = 1/√2, so the initial components are each 10√2 m s−1. Maximum height H = uy² / (2g), range R = u² sin 2θ / g, and time of flight T = 2 uy / g. Which set is correct?
items.explanation: uy = 10√2 m s−1, so H = (10√2)² / 20 = 200/20 = 10 m. At 45°, sin 2θ = 1, so R = u² / g = 400/10 = 40 m. T = 2(10√2)/10 = 2√2 s. Using uy = 20 m s−1 as if the launch were vertical would give H = 20 m and T = 4 s. Halving the range to 20 m confuses H with R/2 or uses only one velocity component in R = u t. Swapping 10 m and 40 m mixes height with range.

distractorRationales.B: H = 20 m and T = 4 s would require uy = 20 m s−1, i.e. a vertical launch, not 45°.
distractorRationales.C: The 10 m height is right, but R = u²/g = 40 m at 45°, not 20 m.
distractorRationales.D: 40 m is the range, not the height; 10 m is the height, not the range.

items.stem:
Initial uptake rates (nmol min−1 per milligram protein) versus external concentration [S]:
[S] = 0.5 mM: glucose 18, urea 2.1.
1.0 mM: glucose 32, urea 4.0.
2.0 mM: glucose 48, urea 8.1.
8.0 mM: glucose 58, urea 32.
16 mM: glucose 60, urea 64.
Which kinetic reading is correct?

choices.text: Both solutes cross by unsaturable simple diffusion, because both rates increase with [S].
Glucose uses a saturable facilitated carrier; urea crosses by unsaturable simple diffusion.
Urea uses an ATP pump, because its rate at 16 mM (64) exceeds that of glucose (60).
Glucose uses simple diffusion, because a plateau means the bilayer has become infinitely permeable.

items.explanation: Facilitated transporters saturate when binding sites are occupied. Glucose rises from 18 to 58 between 0.5 and 8 mM but only to 60 at 16 mM, so Vmax is about 60 nmol min−1 and Km is near 1 mM (rate 32 ≈ Vmax/2). Urea doubles whenever [S] doubles (2.1, 4.0, 8.1, 32, 64), a linear relation with no plateau, as expected for simple diffusion. A higher urea rate at 16 mM does not imply a pump; pumps would still saturate and would require an energy source, which is not indicated.

distractorRationales.A: Glucose clearly plateaus (58 then 60) while urea does not; an increase with [S] at low concentration occurs for both mechanisms.
distractorRationales.C: Simple diffusion can outrun a saturated carrier at high [S]; rate 64 versus 60 is not evidence of active pumping.
distractorRationales.D: A plateau is the signature of a limited number of carriers, not of infinite bilayer permeability.

items.stem: Starling filtration slightly exceeds venous reabsorption in most capillary beds; lymphatics return the difference plus leaked plasma protein. If lymphatics draining a limb are obliterated, the limb most likely develops:

choices.text: A fall in interstitial protein and dehydration of the subcutis
Arterial obstruction, because lymphatics are the sole path for erythrocytes to return to the heart
Lymphedema: accumulation of protein-rich interstitial fluid that cannot be cleared
Immediate cessation of ADH secretion, which is controlled by limb lymph flow

items.explanation: Blind-ended lymphatic capillaries collect excess filtrate and macromolecules that blood capillaries do not fully reabsorb, eventually returning them to veins. When that route is blocked (filariasis, surgery, congenital aplasia), protein-rich fluid accumulates as lymphedema. Interstitial oncotic pressure rises and worsens filtration, a vicious cycle. RBCs normally remain in the vascular space and return via veins, not lymph. ADH is regulated by plasma osmolarity and volume receptors, not limb lymphatics. The fluid is not protein-poor dehydration.

distractorRationales.A: Blocked lymphatics trap protein and fluid; they do not dehydrate the limb.
distractorRationales.B: Erythrocytes return through veins; lymph is not the RBC circuit.
distractorRationales.D: ADH is not slaved to limb lymphatic flow.

items.stem:
Acidified dichromate (orange Cr2O7 2− → green Cr3+) is used in excess, then the organic product is characterised.

Alcohol | dichromate colour | product IR after oxidation
CH3CH2OH | orange → green | 1710 cm−1 plus broad 3000 cm−1 (carboxylic acid)
(CH3)2CHOH | orange → green | 1715 cm−1 only (ketone)
(CH3)3COH | orange remains | unchanged 3300 cm−1 alcohol

Which oxidation-level account is correct?

choices.text: Primary ethanol oxidises through aldehyde to carboxylic acid; secondary propan-2-ol stops at the ketone; tertiary 2-methylpropan-2-ol has no C–H on the carbinol carbon and does not oxidise
Tertiary alcohols oxidise most easily, so the orange colour should have vanished
Secondary alcohols give carboxylic acids, matching the 1715 cm−1-only row
All three alcohols are at the same oxidation level because each contains one oxygen

items.explanation: Dichromate decolourisation (orange to green) means the alcohol reduced Cr(VI). Ethanol, primary, is oxidised all the way to ethanoic acid (carbonyl plus very broad O–H). Propan-2-ol, secondary, can lose its one carbinol hydrogen and stops at acetone (carbonyl, no acid O–H). tert-Butanol has no hydrogen on the carbon bearing OH, so Cr(VI) remains orange. Tertiary is therefore the least, not most, oxidisable under these conditions. A ketone IR without the broad acid band is not a carboxylic acid. One oxygen atom does not equalise oxidation levels: RCH2OH, R2CHOH and R3COH sit at different levels.

distractorRationales.B: The tertiary row keeps orange dichromate, experimental proof of no oxidation.
distractorRationales.C: The secondary product is a ketone (1715 cm−1 only), not an acid.
distractorRationales.D: The three different outcomes show three different oxidisabilities.

items.stem: A hydrolase exhibits a bell-shaped kcat versus pH profile with apparent pKa values near 4.5 and 6.5. Mutating a conserved active-site glutamate to glutamine collapses kcat across pH 5–8 to near the uncatalyzed baseline. The glutamate is most likely required as:

choices.text: A residue whose hydrogen-bond donor pattern is identical to glutamine, so the activity loss must be steric only
A carboxylate that must be deprotonated in the active enzyme and cannot ionize after the Gln substitution
The organic substrate itself, meaning the enzyme had been catalyzing glutamate conversion rather than peptide hydrolysis
A residue that sets the pKa of solvent water to 14, without participating in proton transfer

items.explanation: A bell-shaped kcat–pH curve implies that two ionizable groups must occupy specific protonation states during the rate-limiting step. An apparent pKa near 4.5 is in the carboxylic-acid range. Glutamate in the deprotonated form can act as a general base or stabilize a cation; glutamine is isosteric but cannot ionize, so it cannot supply that carboxylate and kcat collapses at all assay pH values. Gln still donates and accepts hydrogen bonds, so a purely H-bond-identical substitution would not explain total loss. The conserved residue is in the enzyme, not the substrate, and water’s pKa in bulk is already ~15.7; the data specifically implicate an ionizable carboxylate.

distractorRationales.A: Gln can mimic some H-bonds but not the negative charge or proton-shuttling of Glu; the activity collapse indicates ionization is essential.
distractorRationales.C: A conserved active-site glutamate is a catalytic residue of the hydrolase, not evidence that glutamate was the substrate.
distractorRationales.D: Bulk water already has a high pKa; the pH profile and the Glu→Gln phenotype point to a catalytic carboxylate.

items.stem: A homodimer is stabilized by an interfacial salt bridge between Arg80 and Glu120. The Glu120Lys mutant remains a single 30 kDa band on SDS-PAGE, but sedimentation equilibrium in native buffer shifts from a 60 kDa dimer toward a 30 kDa monomer. Which interpretation is most accurate?

choices.text: The mutation hydrolyzes peptide bonds, so SDS-PAGE should have shown fragments smaller than 30 kDa
The substitution selectively weakens quaternary assembly without changing covalent subunit mass
SDS-PAGE would show a 60 kDa band if the interface were real, so the wild-type dimer assignment was an artifact
Lysine cannot occupy a primary-structure position, so the mutant protein cannot be synthesized

items.explanation: SDS-PAGE reports covalent polypeptide mass after denaturation. An unchanged 30 kDa band means the backbone is intact and the substitution is a simple point mutant. Sedimentation in native buffer reports oligomeric state: loss of the attractive Arg–Glu pair in favor of Arg–Lys repulsion destabilizes the dimer, shifting the equilibrium toward monomer. That is a quaternary-structure defect. SDS always dissociates noncovalent dimers, so wild-type SDS-PAGE is also 30 kDa and does not refute the native dimer. Lysine is a standard encoded amino acid.

distractorRationales.A: A missense mutation does not proteolyze the chain; fragment bands are not expected.
distractorRationales.C: Noncovalent dimers routinely run as monomers on SDS-PAGE; native methods are required to see the oligomer.
distractorRationales.D: Lysine is genetically encoded and is commonly introduced by mutagenesis.

items.stem: A decarboxylation evolves 250 mL of CO2 collected at 300 K and 0.80 atm over water-free conditions and treated as ideal. Using R = 0.082 L atm K^-1 mol^-1, the amount of CO2 is closest to:

choices.text: 8.1 mmol
0.81 mmol
12 mmol
81 mmol

items.explanation: Rearrange PV = nRT to n = PV / RT. Convert 250 mL to 0.250 L, then n = (0.80 x 0.250) / (0.082 x 300) = 0.200 / 24.6 ≈ 0.0081 mol, which is 8.1 mmol. Ten-fold errors usually come from a misplaced milliliter-to-liter conversion. Using an inconsistent volume or dropping P from the numerator shifts the result toward the other distractors.

distractorRationales.B: This is 10-fold too small and typically reflects treating 250 mL as 0.025 L, or an equivalent decimal-place error in V.
distractorRationales.C: This overestimates n, for example by using a smaller T in the denominator or a larger effective V or P than the stem gives.
distractorRationales.D: This is 10-fold too large, as if 250 mL were entered as 2.50 L.

items.stem: Teachers are told, randomly, that certain pupils are “late bloomers.” Those children later gain more on an IQ test. Rosenthal and Jacobson’s Pygmalion study is a classroom instance of which process Merton named?

choices.text: Stereotype threat, because the children feared confirming a negative label of “ordinary”
A self-fulfilling prophecy: a false definition (the bloomer label) evokes behavior that makes the false definition come true
Fundamental attribution error about the teachers’ essays
Groupthink in the faculty lounge, which raises children’s IQ without expectancy

items.explanation: Merton’s self-fulfilling prophecy (building on the Thomas theorem) is a false public definition that elicits behavior confirming it. Rosenthal and Jacobson randomly labeled children; teachers’ expectancies then altered interaction and measured IQ—the prophecy fulfilled. Stereotype threat is the target’s worry about confirming a negative stereotype on a diagnostic test, a different design. FAE is an observer’s dispositional bias. Groupthink is concurrence-seeking in cohesive decision groups, not a teacher-expectancy effect.

distractorRationales.A: The manipulation was a positive teacher label, not a diagnostic-test threat to the child.
distractorRationales.C: No essay-constraint attribution task is involved.
distractorRationales.D: Faculty concurrence-seeking is not the Pygmalion mechanism.

items.stem: Which proposed Task B theme is too generic to be a theme, and which is personal enough to control a thirty-minute piece?

choices.text: Too generic: “Life is a journey.” Personal enough: “The cost of staying in a family that would only love a quieter version of me.”
Too generic: any first-person sentence. Personal enough: “Society today.”
Too generic: the family-silence theme. Personal enough: “The human condition in all cultures.”
Too generic: all Task B themes; the section is only for policy.

items.explanation: A personal theme still needs edges. “Life is a journey” and “the human condition” cannot generate a particular scene. “The cost of staying in a family that would only love a quieter version of me” can: a kitchen, a withheld sentence, a leaving that is also a silence. That is still Task B, not a Task A program. First-person grammar alone does not make a theme personal, and “society today” is the generic fog Task B must refuse. The section is not a policy paper; misfiling it as one is a task error. A is the pair that shows the difference in grain.

distractorRationales.B: First-person is not automatically generic, and “society today” is the broader fog, not the cure.
distractorRationales.C: This inverts the grain: family-silence can be written; “all cultures” cannot.
distractorRationales.D: Task B is the personal/social task; calling it policy-only misreads the paper.

items.stem: On a weak-acid + strong-base titration curve, which region is nearly flat (small ΔpH per mL of titrant) and why?

choices.text: The initial point only, because no acid has reacted yet.
The far-basic plateau after equivalence, which is flat because the solution is a perfect buffer of NaOH and water.
The vertical equivalence jump, which is flat by definition.
The buffer region around the half-equivalence point, where added OH− converts HA to A− without large pH change while both species remain.

items.explanation: Buffer action is maximal when [HA] and [A−] are both substantial, which occurs between the start and the equivalence point and is centered at half-equivalence (pH = pKa). Added strong base is consumed by HA, so pH = pKa + log([A−]/[HA]) changes only as the log ratio changes—slowly. The equivalence region is the opposite: a tiny increment of titrant swings the pH through many units (steep, not flat). After equivalence the curve tracks excess NaOH and rises, but that is not the HA/A− buffer. The initial weak-acid point is not a buffer until some A− has been generated.

distractorRationales.A: The starting weak-acid solution has almost no A− and is not well buffered; the first additions of base change pH faster than in the mid-buffer region.
distractorRationales.B: Excess strong base is not a conventional buffer; pH still changes with each added milliliter, though more slowly than at equivalence.
distractorRationales.C: The equivalence jump is the steepest part of the curve, used to locate the endpoint, not a flat region.

items.stem: The author suggests that a pedagogy that “can only hear what the metronome can hear” will most likely

choices.text: produce technically precise pitch-accountants and a thin audience for what notation leaks.
replace all universities with dance halls.
eliminate jazz because rhythm sections refuse to negotiate.
make recordings illegal in seminars.

items.explanation: The last paragraph names the consequence: excellent accountants of pitch and a thin audience for everything else—the leaked, unstill information. That is an implication of a pedagogy indexed to the metronome. B and D invent institutional abolitions. C misreads jazz rhythm sections, which the passage treats as evidence of negotiation rather than as a target for elimination. Extrapolation should stay inside the practical upshot the author actually draws.

distractorRationales.B: No replacement of universities is proposed; seminars are asked not to confuse maps with territory.
distractorRationales.C: Jazz rhythm sections illustrate living time, not a genre the pedagogy should wipe out.
distractorRationales.D: Recordings are criticised as a new paper, not banned.

passage.title: What the metronome cannot hear
passage.body:
Musicology has a long habit of treating the score as the work and the performance as a more or less obedient copy. The habit is understandable. Paper sits still. It can be compared, edited, and taught in rooms where no instrument is present. A performance disappears as it occurs, leaving only memory, a recording, or an argument.

Yet the stillness of paper is not neutrality. Notation is a technology with a history: it captures some relations (pitch against a staff, duration against a beat) and lets others leak away (the weight of a bow, the delay before a singer accepts a consonant, the social fact of who is allowed to ornament). When a textbook says a movement is “in three,” it is reporting a notational decision that a village dance may never have made in those terms. The metronome, arriving later still, offers a fantasy that time is a ruler laid beside sound. Dancers know otherwise. So do jazz rhythm sections, whose time is a negotiation, not a grid that failed.

Scholars who defend the score-as-work often point to the composer’s authority and to the need for a shared object of study. Without a text, they say, we are left with impressions. The worry is real in a university. It is less real in a tradition that already treats the night’s playing as the work, and the paper, if paper exists, as a prompt. To call that tradition incomplete because it will not sit still is to confuse the archive’s convenience with the art’s ontology.

Recordings seemed to solve the disappearance problem. They created a new paper: a fixed take that can be looped, transcribed, and worshipped. The solution smuggles in its own politics. Which night was recorded, from which seat, with which microphone aiming at which social center of the band? A “definitive” recording can freeze a hierarchy that a living scene would have kept in motion. The fan who owns every take may know more facts than a player and still know less about what the music is for.

The practical upshot is not to burn scores. Scores are superb tools, as maps are superb tools. The upshot is to stop calling the map the territory in order to make seminars easier to grade. A pedagogy that can only hear what the metronome can hear will keep producing excellent accountants of pitch and a thin audience for everything else. If musicology wants to study music rather than the paperwork of music, it will have to tolerate objects that do not hold still, and to admit that some of the most precise information arrives as a glance between players that no staff line was built to hold.

items.stem: In a coffee-cup calorimeter, 2.00 g of KNO3 (101.1 g mol−1) dissolves in 50.0 g of water. The temperature falls from 25.00 °C to 22.60 °C. Take the solution mass as 52.0 g and c = 4.18 J g−1 °C−1. What is ΔH_soln per mole of KNO3?

choices.text: −26.4 kJ mol−1, because any temperature change in a calorimeter is reported as a negative enthalpy
+52.2 kJ mol−1, using q = m c ΔT without dividing by moles
+26.4 kJ mol−1, because dissolution absorbed heat from the solution (endothermic) and q_rxn = −q_solution
+13.2 kJ mol−1, from accidentally doubling the number of moles

items.explanation: A coffee-cup calorimeter operates at constant pressure, so q_p = ΔH for the process inside. The solution’s temperature drop means the solution lost heat: q_solution = (52.0 g)(4.18 J g−1 °C−1)(−2.40 °C) = −522 J. Heat conservation requires q_rxn = −q_solution = +522 J, so dissolution is endothermic. Dividing by n = 2.00/101.1 = 0.0198 mol gives ΔH = +26.4 kJ mol−1. The sign tracks the observed cooling; omitting the mole conversion or doubling n produces the numeric traps.

distractorRationales.A: The calorimeter cools, which means the chemical process absorbed heat. ΔH_soln is positive, not negative.
distractorRationales.B: q_rxn ≈ +522 J is the enthalpy change for 2.00 g, not for one mole. Molar ΔH requires division by 0.0198 mol.
distractorRationales.D: Using n = 0.0396 mol (as if the formula weight were applied twice) halves the molar enthalpy to 13.2 kJ mol−1.

items.stem:
A microphone records the superposition of two nearby pure tones. A Fourier analysis of a 2.00 s recording lists:

Component | Frequency (Hz)
Tone 1 | 440
Tone 2 | 436

The beat frequency is |f1 − f2|. Intensity maxima occur once per beat period. How many loud intensity maxima occur in the 2.00 s recording, and what is the beat frequency?

choices.text: Beat frequency 4 Hz, so 8 maxima in 2.00 s.
Beat frequency 4 Hz, so 4 maxima in 2.00 s.
Beat frequency 438 Hz, so 876 maxima in 2.00 s.
Beat frequency 876 Hz, so 1752 maxima in 2.00 s.

items.explanation: The beat frequency is |440 − 436| = 4 Hz, so the intensity envelope repeats 4 times each second. In 2.00 s there are 4 × 2.00 = 8 loud maxima. Counting only 4 maxima in 2 s confuses the beat frequency with the number of events in 2 s (forgetting to multiply by the duration). The arithmetic mean 438 Hz is the average of the two tones, not the beat rate. The sum 876 Hz is an upper sideband of a nonlinear mixer, not the slow envelope. The table’s two frequencies are close, which is exactly the condition under which beats are heard as a slow wavering of loudness at the difference frequency.

distractorRationales.B: The beat frequency is 4 Hz, but 4 Hz means 4 maxima per second, hence 8 in 2.00 s, not 4. Duration must be multiplied in.
distractorRationales.C: 438 Hz is the mean of 440 and 436. Beats are heard at the difference, not at the average pitch.
distractorRationales.D: 876 Hz is the sum of the two frequencies. The slow loudness variation is the difference 4 Hz, not the sum.

items.stem: Which option shows emotional precision rather than sentimentality?

choices.text: Tears streamed down my face like rivers of liquid pain as my heart shattered into a million pieces.
I was so emotional; it was the most emotional day of my entire emotional life.
I was angry at him for dying in a rental, and ashamed of the anger, and then irritated at the agent for being the only person in the room with a workable next step.
I smiled bravely because love never dies and he is watching from a better place.

items.explanation: Precision names mixed, slightly unflattering states that can coexist: anger, shame at the anger, irritation at competence. That is tone control. Sentimentality inflates a single approved feeling (tears like rivers, love never dies) until it cannot be tested. “Emotional” repeated is a blank. Task B rewards the writer who can bear an awkward true combination. C could be false in a way that would matter; A and D cannot, because they are already at maximum. Markers read the difference as maturity of thought, not as a lack of feeling.

distractorRationales.A: The river-and-million-pieces pile is stock inflation; it blurs rather than specifies.
distractorRationales.B: Repeating “emotional” names no feeling at all.
distractorRationales.D: Consolation-card metaphysics replaces the awkward present tense of a rental with an untestable afterlife.

items.stem: A hand-therapy clinic maps just-noticeable differences for hidden grip-weights. Against a 200 g standard, patients first report a change when the increment is 6 g. Weber’s law is assumed to hold over this range. Which increment should be just noticeable against a 500 g standard?

choices.text: 15 g, because the ratio of increment to standard intensity is constant
6 g, because the just-noticeable difference is a fixed mass independent of the standard
2.4 g, because sensitivity improves linearly as the standard grows
500 g, because the comparison must equal the standard before a difference can be felt

items.explanation: Weber’s law states that the just-noticeable difference is a constant fraction of the standing intensity, ΔI/I = k. Here k = 6/200 = 0.03, so a 500 g standard requires about 15 g. Fechner later integrated that ratio into a logarithmic sensation scale, but the clinic’s prediction is the Weber fraction itself. Absolute threshold is detection from zero, not a difference from a standing weight. Signal-detection theory concerns hits and false alarms, not this ratio.

distractorRationales.B: A constant absolute increment is the opposite of Weber’s law; the increment must scale with the standard.
distractorRationales.C: Weber’s law makes the absolute increment larger, not smaller, as intensity rises (k held constant).
distractorRationales.D: Equality with the standard would be a 100 percent change, far above a typical Weber fraction.

items.stem: Which statement best captures what the extract as a whole is saying?

choices.text: Estate agents are uniquely cruel, and carpet cleaning is a form of theft from the bereaved.
Legal vacancy and a cleared rental can coexist with objects and habits that still assign tasks, so grief here is less a passing weather than an unanswered list.
The speaker decides that buying milk will bring her father back, and the poem proves supernatural continuance.
Poetry taped in cupboards is always a confession of a secret literary career the family refused to honour.

items.explanation: The piece moves from the agent's tidy phrase through remaining marks, a list, a poem about a week that never arrived, and a daughter who almost ticks milk. Its claim is that emptiness in law is not emptiness in the present tense of objects and unfinished care. It does not prosecute agents as thieves, promise resurrection by shopping, or unmask a hidden career. A main-claim answer must sit inside that modest, exact complaint about vacant possession and assigned tasks, which only B does.

distractorRationales.A: The speaker says the agent is not unkind and is on a clock; the target is a legal sentence, not a morality play about cruelty.
distractorRationales.C: Ticking milk is called a joke at her own expense and a ridiculous want, not a magical program; the poem addresses a week that never arrived.
distractorRationales.D: He is explicitly not a man who announced poems; the scrap is intimate remainder, not evidence of a suppressed vocation.

passage.title: Vacant possession
passage.body:
The rental had been emptied with the efficiency of people who did not live there. I arrived after the skip had gone. What remained were the marks of remaining: a paler rectangle on the wall where a calendar had blocked the sun, a screw in the kitchen plaster that had held nothing I could remember, a ring on the lino where a bin had sat long enough to become a climate. The agent called it "vacant possession." The phrase was legally tidy. It treated my father as a tenancy that had concluded.

I opened the cupboard above the kettle. Inside, taped to the wood, was a shopping list in his slanted capitals, and beneath it a scrap of verse I had never seen. He was not a man who announced poems. He had been a man who boiled water at the same hour, as if the day were a machine that required a particular ignition. The list wanted milk, soap, and a cheaper brand of tea. The last item was written twice, then crossed out, then written again, as if indecision were a kind of company.

The kettle still knew his hour.
I did not.
The cupboard kept a shopping list
addressed to a week that never arrived.
I ticked the milk as if the ticking
could make a future stand up.

I stood with a pen I had not meant to bring and put a mark beside milk, then stopped, because the gesture had the shape of care and the content of a joke at my own expense. Grief, in the pamphlets, is supposed to be a weather that passes over a landscape. In the cupboard it was more like a task left in a shared kitchen: unclaimed, slightly shameful, still assigned. I wanted, ridiculously, to buy the milk. I wanted not to be the kind of daughter who leaves a list unanswered.

The agent coughed in the hallway and mentioned carpet cleaning, then the bond, then the need to "move on" as if the room were a queue. I heard myself thank him. Courtesy was easier than explaining that the room was not empty, only unpopulated. He was not unkind. He was on a clock I did not share. Vacant possession, I thought, is a legal sentence that cannot conjugate the present tense of objects. The kettle, if it could speak, would not have used it. It would have asked why the hour had been cancelled without notice.

items.stem: A newly characterized hormone is hydrophobic, derived from cholesterol, and alters target-cell transcription over hours. It most likely:

choices.text: binds a Gs-coupled receptor and raises cAMP within seconds as its primary action
is stored for long periods in dense-core granules and released by exocytosis as its only option
diffuses across the plasma membrane and binds an intracellular receptor that regulates DNA transcription
cannot cross membranes and therefore must use a receptor tyrosine kinase

items.explanation: Cholesterol-derived steroid hormones are lipophilic, are not stored in secretory granules in the peptide fashion, and classically bind intracellular (often nuclear) receptors that act as transcription factors. That genomic mode matches a lag of hours. Rapid Gs-cAMP signaling is the peptide/catecholamine membrane-receptor pattern. Hydrophobicity is why the hormone can cross the bilayer rather than why it would be barred from doing so.

distractorRationales.A: Seconds-scale cAMP signaling is typical of hydrophilic hormones at GPCRs, not of classic steroid genomic action.
distractorRationales.B: Peptide hormones are granule-stored and exocytosed. Steroids are synthesized on demand from cholesterol and leave by diffusion.
distractorRationales.D: A hydrophobic cholesterol derivative can cross membranes; an RTK is the wrong receptor class for that chemistry.

items.stem: From Table 2, the initial velocity estimated from the 0 s and 20 s product concentrations is closest to which value?
items.explanation: Table 2 reports 19.6 μM product at 20 s and 0.0 μM at 0 s, so the early-time rate is 19.6/20 = 0.98 μM s^{-1}. That window is the one the experimenters would treat as an initial rate: Table 2 is still nearly linear through 20–30 s, whereas averaging to 120 s (102.4/120 ≈ 0.85 μM s^{-1}) already shows curvature from substrate depletion. The value 2.0 μM s^{-1} is the assay V_max expected from 80 nmol s^{-1} mg^{-1} times 0.025 mg in 1.00 mL at saturating S, not the rate at [S]_0 = K_m. 0.16 μM s^{-1} would follow if 2 μg rather than 25 μg of enzyme had been used. Only the 0 s and 20 s pair in Table 2 yields 0.98.

distractorRationales.A: 0.16 μM s^{-1} matches an assay loaded with 2 μg of enzyme at the Table 1 specific activity, not the 25 μg progress curve actually described.
distractorRationales.B: 0.85 μM s^{-1} is 102.4 μM divided by 120 s, an average over a curved progress trace rather than an initial slope from the 0–20 s points.
distractorRationales.D: 2.0 μM s^{-1} is the saturating-S assay V_max in the 1.00 mL cuvette (80 nmol s^{-1} mg^{-1} × 0.025 mg); Table 2 starts at [S] = K_m, so the initial rate should be near half of that ceiling.

passage.title: Reversible inhibitors of a cytosolic dehydrogenase
passage.body:
Investigators purified a cytosolic NAD+-dependent dehydrogenase that oxidizes a small-molecule metabolite S. Initial velocities were measured at 25 °C by following NADH formation in 1.00 mL assays. Nonlinear fits of v versus [S] produced the apparent Michaelis constants and maximal velocities in Table 1. When an inhibitor was present, its concentration was 2.0 μM in the assay mix. Dialysis that removed unbound compound restored full catalytic activity after incubation with P, Q, or R, indicating reversible binding rather than covalent inactivation. Active-site titration with a tight-binding stoichiometric inactivator found 4.0 nmol of catalytic sites per milligram of protein.

Table 1. Apparent kinetic parameters from initial-rate fits

| Condition | Apparent K_m (mM) | Apparent V_max (nmol s^{-1} mg^{-1}) |
|-----------|-------------------|--------------------------------------|
| No inhibitor | 0.50 | 80 |
| Compound P (2.0 μM) | 0.50 | 40 |
| Compound Q (2.0 μM) | 1.50 | 80 |
| Compound R (2.0 μM) | 0.25 | 40 |

In a separate progress-curve experiment, 25 μg of the same enzyme protein was mixed with 0.50 mM S and no inhibitor in a 1.00 mL reaction. Product concentration was recorded as a function of time (Table 2).

Table 2. Product appearance at [S]_0 = 0.50 mM without inhibitor

| Time (s) | [Product] (μM) |
|----------|----------------|
| 0 | 0.0 |
| 10 | 9.9 |
| 20 | 19.6 |
| 30 | 29.1 |
| 60 | 56.2 |
| 120 | 102.4 |

items.stem: The author's account of identical wave-forms wearing two moral uniforms is most nearly analogous to which of the following?

choices.text: A restaurant dress code that calls a laborer's boots 'unkempt' and a customer's distressed leather 'casual luxury' at the same scuff level.
A physics classroom that treats two equal amplitudes as identical regardless of instrument.
A ban on all urban sound in the name of a perfectly silent commons.
A medical study that measures sleep loss from compressors beside bedrooms.

items.explanation: The analogy has to map same intensity, different moral labels, tracking prestige. Dress codes that rename the same scuff according to who wears it preserve that structure. A physics classroom that refuses the distinction is the meter the author says officials are not; a total ban is the unlimited-noise opposite the fourth paragraph declines; compressor studies are the genuine public-health work the first paragraph grants. Hypothetical mapping fails if it erases the double uniform or if it substitutes the health concession for the hypocrisy claim. A keeps the hypocrisy without denying that some health measurements are real.

distractorRationales.B: That classroom is what a thermometer would do if it were only a thermometer; the author's point is that ordinances are not only meters.
distractorRationales.C: The author rejects both unlimited noise and the romance of the unregulated street; a total ban is not the analogue of two uniforms.
distractorRationales.D: Sleep-loss measurement is the legitimate health work distinguished from the sorting device; it does not analogize the two-uniform trick.

passage.title: Who may be loud
passage.body:
Noise ordinances are written as if they were thermometers. A number of decibels is named; a clock hour is named; a fine is attached. The language of public health does real work here: sleep is not a luxury, and a child whose window faces a compressor is not being precious. But the thermometer conceals a second instrument, which is a social sorting device. Cities do not merely suppress loudness. They decide which kinds of loudness will be classified as vitality and which as nuisance, and the decision tracks, with embarrassing regularity, the prestige of the people making the sound.

Walk a mixed street after dark and the taxonomy is audible. A licensed terrace with heaters and a playlist is "activation of the night-time economy." A storefront church whose singing lasts past the same hour is a complaint waiting to be logged. A terrace is a business; a congregation is a disturbance that happens to own a building. Street vendors packing ice and calling prices are "chaos"; a restaurant's Friday overflow onto the pavement is "vibrancy," provided the overflow has paid for a permit. The ear that writes the ordinance has already been trained to hear money as atmosphere and unpaid sound as aggression.

Defenders of the ordinances will say that the issue is volume, not culture. Sometimes it is. A speaker stack aimed at a bedroom is a harm whether the music is sacred or commercial. The author's claim is narrower and more awkward: when two sounds of similar intensity are sorted differently, the sorting is not acoustics. It is a theory of who belongs in the air. "Quiet" is then sold as a natural baseline, like clean water, when it is often an aesthetic associated with certain housing and certain hours of salaried rest. Night-shift workers returning at dawn, whose rest is real, rarely get to define the city's sonic morals. People who sleep when the ordinance writers sleep do.

None of this is a brief for unlimited noise, or for the romance of the unregulated street. A city that cannot protect sleep will punish the poorest first, because they cannot buy distance from compressors. The decent aim is not a louder city but a less hypocritical one: a city that admits that permission to be loud is a scarce good, distributed by licensing, policing, and taste, and that "quality of life" is never only a medical phrase. It is also a claim about whose life is the measure.

The rhetorical trick is hygiene. Once noise is framed as dirt, opposition to a particular sound can wear the costume of sanitation rather than of preference. Dirt, unlike preference, does not have to justify itself at a public meeting. It only has to be pointed at. That is why a campaign against a night market can speak the idiom of rats and refuse even when the photographs show swept stones, and why a campaign for a waterfront festival can speak the idiom of civic joy even when the sound spill is identical. The same wave-form, two moral uniforms.

If the argument holds, then reform is not a new app for logging complaints. It is a requirement that like sounds be given like reasons, and that exemptions be named as political choices rather than as nature. A hospital generator may deserve its exemption. So, perhaps, does a funeral that spills into a street. What cannot be defended is the pretense that the ordinance is only a meter reading. Meters do not know the difference between a hymn and a brand. Officials do, and they should have to say so.

items.stem:
A runner’s velocity–time graph consists of three straight-line segments:

Interval | v(t)
0 to 4.0 s | v increases linearly from 0 to 8.0 m s−1
4.0 to 10.0 s | v is constant at 8.0 m s−1
10.0 to 12.0 s | v decreases linearly from 8.0 m s−1 to 0

Displacement equals the signed area under a v–t graph. What is the runner’s displacement from t = 0 to t = 12.0 s?
items.explanation: The area is a triangle of base 4.0 s and height 8.0 m s−1, plus a rectangle 6.0 s by 8.0 m s−1, plus a triangle of base 2.0 s and height 8.0 m s−1. Those areas are (1/2)×4.0×8.0 = 16 m, 6.0×8.0 = 48 m, and (1/2)×2.0×8.0 = 8 m, which sum to 72 m. Using only the constant-speed rectangle gives 48 m. Omitting the final triangle gives 64 m. Multiplying the peak speed by the total time (8.0 × 12) gives 96 m, which would be valid only if v were 8.0 m s−1 for the whole 12 s. All three segments contribute positive area because v never reverses.

distractorRationales.A: 48 m is only the rectangular middle segment. The two triangular areas (16 m and 8 m) must be added.
distractorRationales.B: 64 m is the first triangle plus the rectangle, omitting the 8 m triangle during deceleration from 10 s to 12 s.
distractorRationales.D: 96 m is (8.0 m s−1)×(12 s), as if the runner held peak speed for the entire interval instead of accelerating and then stopping.

items.stem:
A sealed respirometer records gas exchange of isolated muscle fibres. Complete oxidation of glucose is C6H12O6 + 6 O2 → 6 CO2 + 6 H2O (respiratory quotient RQ = CO2 produced / O2 consumed = 1.00). Complete oxidation of palmitate is C16H32O2 + 23 O2 → 16 CO2 + 16 H2O (RQ = 16/23 ≈ 0.70).
Run 1: 12 mmol O2 consumed, 12 mmol CO2 produced.
Run 2: 10 mmol O2 consumed, 7 mmol CO2 produced.
Which fuel use is consistent with the two runs?

choices.text: Run 1 is carbohydrate oxidation (RQ = 1.00); Run 2 is close to fatty-acid oxidation (RQ = 0.70).
Run 1 is fatty-acid oxidation because equal moles of the two gases always indicate fat.
Run 2 is carbohydrate oxidation because more O2 than CO2 always indicates sugar.
Both runs have RQ = 1.00 once the 23 and 6 stoichiometric coefficients are ignored.

items.explanation: RQ is the measured mole ratio, not a count of carbons alone. Run 1 gives 12/12 = 1.00, matching glucose. Run 2 gives 7/10 = 0.70, matching the palmitate stoichiometry 16/23. Fat oxidation consumes extra O2 to oxidise the more reduced hydrocarbon chain, so CO2 < O2. Equal gas volumes do not diagnose fat; that pattern is carbohydrate. The coefficients 6 and 23 are exactly what generate the two distinctive RQ values.

distractorRationales.B: Equal moles of CO2 and O2 give RQ = 1, the carbohydrate signature, not the fat signature of ~0.70.
distractorRationales.C: Carbohydrate has RQ = 1, so O2 and CO2 match; Run 2’s excess O2 consumption is the fat pattern.
distractorRationales.D: Dropping the stoichiometric coefficients would erase the definition of RQ; the data already give 1.00 and 0.70.

items.stem: How is the author's admission that “some rooms change designs” best reconciled with the critique of participation rituals?

choices.text: It is a contradiction the passage never notices, because any revision would make attendance identical with consent.
It is a sarcastic aside that the author immediately withdraws by calling all ramps imaginary.
It is consistent: the target is the ambient theory that treats any revision as proof the process is sound and leftover grievance as noise, not the existence of occasional design changes.
It shows the author ultimately prefers photographs of crowded halls to written reasons, since ramps are photogenic.

items.explanation: Internal consistency turns on whether the concession cancels the thesis. The third paragraph says revisions matter and that a different piety would deny them, then names the actual target: the theory that any revision proves the process and that remaining grievance is leftover noise from people who had their chance. Attendance made to do the work of consent can coexist with occasional ramps. There is no later withdrawal of the ramp example, and the closing preference is for attributable 'proceeding anyway' over the listening-face photograph. The concession is therefore a scope limit, not a hidden reversal.

distractorRationales.A: The author denies that revision equals a sound process; noticing ramps does not force the identity of attendance and consent.
distractorRationales.B: Nothing in the text recasts the ramp, tree, or night bus as imaginary; they are granted as real and morally relevant.
distractorRationales.D: The closing paragraphs prefer the politically expensive sentence that admits a choice over the photograph that simulates listening without choosing.

passage.title: Minutes as consent
passage.body:
City governments have learned to speak the language of invitation. A new waterfront, a bus garage, a night-time licensing scheme: each arrives with a room, a facilitator, sticky notes, and a promise that "your voice will be heard." The promise is not empty in the way cynics assume. People do speak. Minutes are taken. A summary slide later reports that the community was "engaged." What the ritual converts, with almost chemical reliability, is dissent into attendance. The fact of having been in the room is then cited as evidence that the decision which followed was shared.

This conversion is the point, not an accidental side-effect. A planning authority that can display a photograph of a crowded hall has already performed legitimacy. The photograph does not record what was refused, only that refusal was given a chair. Once refusal has a chair, it can be filed. The file then travels upward as proof of consultation, and the project proceeds under the borrowed moral credit of those who came to object. Objectors discover, sometimes only at the groundbreaking, that they were extras in a scene titled participation.

The objection is not that consultation is a trick in every case. Some rooms change designs. A ramp is added; a tree is spared; a night bus is rerouted. Those revisions matter, and it would be a different piety to pretend they never occur. The trouble is the ambient theory that treats any revision as proof that the process is sound, and any remaining grievance as leftover noise from people who "had their chance." Attendance is thereby made to do the work of consent. Consent, if the word still means anything civic, is not the same as having been scheduled.

Oral comments at a microphone illustrate the substitution with painful clarity. Three minutes are allotted. A timer is visible. The speaker is thanked. The next speaker is invited. The form is courteous and the structure is a funnel: complexity is shaved to fit the slot, and what cannot be shaved is classified as repetition. Staff later write that "themes" emerged. Themes are what survive the funnel. They are not necessarily what the speakers thought they had said. A person who came to argue that the garage should not be built at all finds herself listed under "requests for mitigation." The minutes have translated abolition into upholstery.

Digital portals repeat the same conversion with a friendlier interface. A comment box invites "feedback." Character limits and dropdown menus decide in advance which kinds of sentence will count as input. The resident who types a structural objection is asked, before submitting, to rate the project from one to five stars. The rating is the datum that will be averaged; the paragraph is optional texture. When officials later announce that the "average rating was 3.7," they are not lying about the arithmetic. They are treating a coerced metric as a public will.

A more honest practice would not abandon rooms or portals. It would stop narrating them as consent machines. It would publish the unedited record beside the decision, including the proposals that were not adopted, and it would say plainly: we heard you and we are proceeding anyway, for these reasons. That sentence is politically expensive, which is why the photograph of the hall is preferred. The photograph allows a government to be seen listening without being seen choosing. Democracy, however, is not a listening face. It is the willingness to let a choice remain attributable, especially when the choice disappoints the people who were invited to speak.

items.stem: A resident is sure her team sees her as “the awkward one,” feels shame, and withdraws, although 360-degree comments are actually warm. Cooley’s looking-glass self explains the self-feeling as arising from which sequence?

choices.text: Mead’s “I” spontaneously emits shame without any imagined other
Marcia’s foreclosure: she has committed without exploration because a parent ordered the shame
Piagetian conservation failure, so she cannot reverse the team’s comments
We imagine our appearance to others, imagine their judgment, and the imagined judgment produces a self-feeling (here, shame)—even if the imagination is inaccurate

items.explanation: Cooley’s looking-glass self is the three-step process: imagined appearance, imagined judgment, and resulting self-feeling. The “glass” can distort; what matters is the imagined view, which matches the warm comments plus unwarranted shame. Mead’s “I” is the novel, subject pole of the self, not a shame generator that skips the other. Marcia’s identity statuses (foreclosure, moratorium, achievement, diffusion) classify exploration/commitment, not this reflected-appraisal mechanism. Conservation is a physical-quantity operation, not social self-feeling.

distractorRationales.A: Mead’s I is not Cooley’s reflected-appraisal sequence.
distractorRationales.B: Foreclosure is premature commitment, not a misread 360 review.
distractorRationales.C: Piaget’s conservation does not explain imagined social judgment.

items.stem: Participants hold a pen either in the teeth, which recruits smile muscles, or in the lips, which prevents a smile, while rating cartoons. They cannot see their own faces, and autonomic recordings do not differ between conditions. Cartoon ratings are higher in the teeth condition. The result most directly implicates which claim about emotion’s components?

choices.text: Pure autonomic arousal is sufficient, because a pen cannot affect the face
The behavioral/expressive component can feed back onto the subjective component, as in a facial-feedback account
Unexplained epinephrine was labeled using a confederate, as required by Schachter–Singer theory
Universal-emotion recognition of another person’s face is required, so an audience must have been present

items.explanation: Emotion is typically parsed into physiological, behavioral/expressive, and cognitive/subjective components that can influence one another. Forcing a smile-like contraction without a visible audience and without a change in autonomic arousal isolates the expressive component. Higher amusement ratings then indicate feedback from face to feeling, the facial-feedback hypothesis. The design does not manipulate epinephrine or a confederate, and it does not require recognizing someone else’s expression. Autonomic sufficiency is ruled out if recordings are matched across conditions.

distractorRationales.A: Matched autonomic recordings mean arousal was not the manipulated cause; the pen posture was.
distractorRationales.C: No unexplained drug arousal and no mood confederate were described, so two-factor misattribution is not the mechanism under test.
distractorRationales.D: Participants could not see their own faces and no audience is required for a facial-feedback effect on one’s own ratings.

items.stem: The polite caption “We'll call you when your number becomes a priority” relates to the image most accurately as

choices.text: a literal operating instruction that the drawing merely illustrates without friction.
a courteous administrative idiom whose calm is in tension with dotted patients, a door-sized ticket, a handless clock, and a board listening to a till.
a promise that number 1847 will be seen immediately, which the cash register confirms.
a caption that contradicts the image by proving the board is facing the patients.

items.explanation: Caption-versus-image items ask whether words soothe, ironise, or duplicate the drawing. The typeface is described as polite; the sentence is the familiar postponement of waiting rooms. The image refuses the courtesy: patients are not fully drawn, time has no hands, the ticket is monstrous, the board's ears point at money. That is tension, not illustration without friction. The caption does not promise immediacy, and the board is explicitly not facing patients. The joke is the mismatch between civilised delay and what the picture shows delay is for.

distractorRationales.A: If the drawing only illustrated the caption, the board would be listening to patients; the till and dotted lines create friction.
distractorRationales.C: 1847 and a handless clock work against immediacy; the till is the competing listener, not a confirmation of care.
distractorRationales.D: The description states the board figures are not facing the patients; the caption does not reverse that.

passage.title: When your number becomes a priority
passage.body:
[Image]
A waiting-room drawn as a long, low shed. The bench is actually the tubing of a giant stethoscope, coiled so that patients must sit on the instrument that is supposed to listen to them. Two figures in dark suits, labelled BOARD, wear the earpieces. They are not facing the patients. They lean together toward a cash register whose receipt paper unspools across the floor like a white carpet. The patients are drawn in broken dotted lines, as if they were still being sketched. One solid figure is a child holding a numbered ticket as tall as a door. The ticket number is 1847. A clock on the wall has no hands.

[Caption, in a polite typeface beneath the frame]
"We'll call you when your number becomes a priority."

items.stem:
Hydrogen and iodine reach the equilibrium H2(g) + I2(g) ⇌ 2 HI(g). After a long wait at constant volume and temperature, the equilibrium concentrations are:

Species | Equilibrium concentration (mol L−1)
H2 | 0.20
I2 | 0.20
HI | 1.60

Using Kc = [HI]^2 / ([H2][I2]), what is Kc for this reaction at this temperature?
items.explanation: Kc uses equilibrium concentrations in the mass-action expression. Substituting the table values gives Kc = (1.60)^2 / (0.20 × 0.20) = 2.56 / 0.040 = 64. The numerical value is unitless for this equal-mole reaction. Omitting a concentration in the denominator, forgetting to square [HI], or squaring incorrectly produces 8, 16, or 256. Because the system is stated to be at equilibrium, these table entries are the values that belong in Kc, not in a nonequilibrium Q.

distractorRationales.A: 8.0 is [HI] / ([H2][I2]) or a similar expression that fails to square the product concentration.
distractorRationales.B: 16 is (1.60)^2 / 0.20, which drops one of the two reactant concentrations from the denominator.
distractorRationales.D: 256 would require an extra factor of 4 in the numerator or an erroneously small denominator such as (0.10)^2.

items.stem: A student has two minutes to replace a generic sentence. Which substitution best keeps thought while adding particularity?

choices.text: Replace “I felt sad” with a list of ten synonyms for sad.
Replace “I felt sad” with “I washed his mug and left it on the drying rack, then moved it back to the cupboard because the rack looked like a claim.”
Replace “I felt sad” with a quotation from a famous published memoir used as if it were the student’s life.
Replace “I felt sad” with “Sadness is a socio-economic construct in late capitalism,” and stop.

items.explanation: Particularity is not a thesaurus and not a costume of theory. The mug, the rack, and the fear that a drying object looks like a claim turn sadness into a decision in a kitchen—thought plus scene. Synonyms stall. Borrowing a famous memoir’s life as if it were yours is both generic and a integrity problem; this bank uses original scenes only. A theory slogan without a life attached is Task A jargon on a Task B body. The particular should still mean; B’s last clause is the meaning. That is why it wins.

distractorRationales.A: A synonym list is still generic; it does not locate the feeling in an action.
distractorRationales.C: Famous memoir language would not be the student’s particular life, and this trainer does not use copyrighted essays as models to copy.
distractorRationales.D: A theory caption without a scene abandons Task B’s demand for lived grain.

items.stem: A high-poverty tract is cut off by a highway from a job corridor. Survey networks show few overlapping ties with higher-opportunity tracts. Citywide employment rises in a boom year, but unemployment in the isolated tract barely moves. Which spatial-inequality mechanism is most consistent with this pattern?

choices.text: A pure individual self-efficacy deficit with no role for place
Concentrated disadvantage and spatial mismatch/isolation that can trap residents out of labor markets even when the wider city adds jobs
Social loafing inside factories, which built the highway to reduce effort
Cannon–Bard emotion theory as a predictor of unemployment

items.explanation: Spatial inequality is not only pollution; it is also isolation from jobs, schools, and bridging social networks. Spatial mismatch and concentrated poverty describe neighborhoods physically and socially cut off from opportunity, so a citywide boom need not reach them. That is a place-level mechanism, not a claim that self-efficacy is irrelevant, but it cannot be reduced to self-efficacy alone. Factory loafing and Cannon–Bard theory do not explain highway barriers or truncated networks.

distractorRationales.A: A tract-level failure to share in a citywide boom, with a physical barrier and thin bridging ties, is a spatial pattern rather than a lone personality score.
distractorRationales.C: Highways are infrastructure, not a loafing strategy by workers.
distractorRationales.D: Simultaneity of feeling and arousal does not place jobs on the far side of a highway.

items.stem:
A randomly mating population of 10 000 diploid adults is genotyped at an autosomal locus:

Genotype | Number
AA | 6400
Aa | 3200
aa | 400

Allele frequency of A is counted as (2×AA + Aa) / 20 000. Are the data consistent with Hardy–Weinberg proportions, and what is p(A)?

choices.text: p = 0.80, but HWE requires 8000 AA : 1800 Aa : 200 aa
p = 0.32, the heterozygote frequency, which already equals Hardy–Weinberg
p = 0.64, and the population is not in HWE because 6400 ≠ 0.80² × 10 000
p = 0.80, expected counts are 6400 : 3200 : 400, so the sample matches HWE

items.explanation: p = (2×6400 + 3200) / 20 000 = 16 000 / 20 000 = 0.80, so q = 0.20. Hardy–Weinberg expectations are p²N = 0.64 × 10 000 = 6400, 2pqN = 0.32 × 10 000 = 3200, q²N = 0.04 × 10 000 = 400, identical to the counts. Using p = 0.64 confuses the AA genotype frequency with the allele frequency. The 8000:1800:200 split would correspond to different p or to a selection-distorted sample, not to p = 0.80.

distractorRationales.A: Those counts would require a much higher p or a deficit of heterozygotes; they are not the HWE prediction for p = 0.80.
distractorRationales.B: Heterozygote frequency 0.32 equals 2pq only after p is known; p itself is 0.80, not 0.32.
distractorRationales.C: 0.64 is the frequency of AA, not of allele A; with p = 0.80 the 6400 AA individuals are exactly p²N.

items.stem: An electron (q = −1.6 × 10−19 C, m = 9.1 × 10−31 kg) moves at 2.0 × 10^6 m s−1 perpendicular to B = 0.50 T. F = |q| v B, and the orbital radius is r = m v / (|q| B). What are F and r? (Use m ≈ 9.0 × 10−31 kg for rounding.)

choices.text: F = 0 because a magnetic field never does work, so it never exerts a force

items.explanation: F = (1.6×10−19)(2.0×10^6)(0.50) = 1.6×10−13 N. Then r = (9.0×10−31 × 2.0×10^6) / (1.6×10−19 × 0.50) = 1.8×10−24 / 8.0×10−20 = 2.25×10−5 m ≈ 2.3×10−5 m. A millimetre-scale 10−2 m would need a much smaller B or larger v. Using |q| alone as the force ignores vB. Magnetic forces do no work because F is perpendicular to v, but the force itself is not zero; it only changes direction, producing circular motion.

distractorRationales.A: The force is right, but r is 2.3 × 10−5 m, not 2.3 cm; the 10−31/10−19 ratio already supplies 10−12 before v/B.
distractorRationales.B: 1.6 × 10−19 N is the charge’s magnitude written as a force, omitting v B = 1.0 × 10^6 T m s−1.
distractorRationales.C: No-work means ΔKE = 0, not F = 0; the centripetal magnetic force is 1.6 × 10−13 N.

items.stem: Isolated mitochondria are given pyruvate plus ADP. When matrix NADH and acetyl-CoA are raised experimentally, pyruvate consumption falls. Which enzyme is the principal site of this feedback, and which reaction does it catalyze?

choices.text: Citrate synthase; condensation of two acetyl-CoA molecules to acetoacetate
Pyruvate carboxylase; decarboxylation of pyruvate to acetaldehyde
The pyruvate dehydrogenase complex; oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA
Malate dehydrogenase; oxidation of malate that is stimulated by NADH

items.explanation: Pyruvate enters mitochondrial oxidative metabolism through the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, which converts pyruvate, CoA, and NAD+ to acetyl-CoA, CO2, and NADH. High NADH and acetyl-CoA are the immediate products of that reaction and inhibit PDH (product inhibition and, via PDH kinase, phosphorylation). That feedback slows pyruvate consumption when the cell is already reduced and acetyl-CoA-rich. Citrate synthase does not consume pyruvate and does not condense two acetyl-CoA units to acetoacetate. Pyruvate carboxylase makes oxaloacetate, not acetaldehyde. NADH inhibits, rather than stimulates, NAD+-dependent malate oxidation.

distractorRationales.A: Citrate synthase condenses acetyl-CoA with oxaloacetate to citrate, not two acetyl-CoA molecules to acetoacetate. It also does not consume pyruvate, so it is not the site that explains falling pyruvate use.
distractorRationales.B: Pyruvate carboxylase carboxylates pyruvate to oxaloacetate and is activated, not inhibited, by acetyl-CoA. It does not produce acetaldehyde.
distractorRationales.D: Malate dehydrogenase uses NAD+; a high NADH/NAD+ ratio drives the reaction toward malate, so NADH does not stimulate malate oxidation or explain reduced pyruvate uptake as the primary gate.

items.stem: 25.0 mL of 0.10 M HCl is titrated with 0.10 M NaOH. At the equivalence point the pH is 7.0, and the curve is nearly vertical from about pH 4 to 10. Which statement correctly contrasts this curve with the acetic acid titration curve?

choices.text: Both curves have a half-equivalence buffer plateau at pH = pKa of the acid being titrated; for HCl that pKa is 7.
The strong-acid curve starts near pH 1, has no weak-acid buffer region, and the equivalence pH is 7 because the salt is NaCl, which does not hydrolyze.
The strong-acid curve starts near pH 5 and is identical to the weak-acid curve after the first 1 mL of base.
Strong-acid titrations have two equivalence points because HCl is diprotic.

items.explanation: 0.10 M HCl has pH 1.0 at the start. As NaOH is added, [H3O+] falls, but there is no HA/A− buffer plateau because HCl is fully dissociated. At equivalence the solute is NaCl; Cl− is the conjugate of a strong acid and Na+ is the conjugate of a strong base, so the pH is 7. The vertical region is wider than for a weak acid, which is why many indicators work. HCl is monoprotic and has no aqueous pKa near 7. The acetic acid curve, by contrast, starts near pH 3, buffers around pH 4.7, and ends basic at equivalence.

distractorRationales.A: HCl has no useful weak-acid pKa in water and no half-equivalence buffer at pH 7. pH 7 is the equivalence point, not a pKa.
distractorRationales.C: The strong-acid start is pH 1, not 5, and the early part of the curve is not a weak-acid buffer.
distractorRationales.D: HCl donates one proton; diprotic curves (H2SO4, H2CO3) are a different class.

items.stem: 3-Oxobutanoic acid (acetoacetic acid) evolves CO2 on gentle warming and leaves acetone. Hexanoic acid is unchanged under the same conditions. Which mechanistic feature explains the difference?

choices.text: Every carboxylic acid decarboxylates below 100 °C; hexanoic acid is simply slower for steric reasons
Only acids with a quaternary α-carbon can lose CO2, and hexanoic acid is secondary at C2
The β-ketone permits a six-membered cyclic transition state that transfers the carboxyl proton to the ketone oxygen as C–C cleavage releases CO2, giving an enol that tautomerizes to acetone
The ketone is reduced to an alcohol by the departing CO2, a redox decarboxylation unique to fatty acids

items.explanation: β-Keto acids decarboxylate thermally through a cyclic, concerted transition state: the carboxyl hydrogen hydrogen-bonds to the β-carbonyl oxygen as the Cα–CO2H bond breaks, producing CO2 and a ketone enol that tautomerizes to acetone. Hexanoic acid lacks a β-carbonyl and cannot form that six-membered array, so it does not lose CO2 on gentle heating. Ordinary fatty acids require much harsher conditions or enzymatic activation (as in metabolic decarboxylations) to lose carbon dioxide. The α-carbon need not be quaternary, and the process is not a reduction of the ketone by CO2.

distractorRationales.A: Simple alkanoic acids do not decarboxylate on a steam bath. The β-keto functional group is essential for the mild thermal reaction.
distractorRationales.B: Malonic acid and acetoacetic acid decarboxylate with primary or secondary α-carbons. Quaternary substitution is not the requirement.
distractorRationales.D: The ketone oxidation state is preserved: the product is acetone, not an alcohol. CO2 is not a reductant in this reaction.

items.stem:
Successive ionisation energies (kJ mol−1) of element Q in period 3:

IE1 590 | IE2 1150 | IE3 4910 | IE4 6480 | IE5 8110

A large jump marks removal of an electron from a new, much more stable shell. Which inference is justified, and what is the most likely ground-state valence configuration of the neutral atom?

choices.text: The jump after IE2 shows two valence electrons; Q is a group-2 metal with valence ns2
The jump after IE2 shows Q is a halogen with valence ns2 np5
IE values increase smoothly, so Q is a noble gas with ns2 np6
The jump after IE5 shows five valence electrons, so Q is group 15 with ns2 np3

items.explanation: IE3 is more than four times IE2 (4910 versus 1150), while IE1 and IE2 are comparable. That pattern means the third electron comes from a complete inner shell, so only two electrons are valence electrons: a group-2 configuration ns2 (Mg-like in period 3). A halogen would show a jump after seven valence ionisations. A noble-gas atom would have a very high IE1. A jump after IE5 is not present; IE3 is already the cliff. The configuration therefore cannot be np5, np6, or np3.

distractorRationales.B: A halogen has seven valence electrons, so the first large jump would appear after IE7, not after IE2.
distractorRationales.C: IE1 of Q is only 590 kJ mol−1, far too low for a noble gas, and the series is not smooth: IE3 is a cliff.
distractorRationales.D: The cliff is at IE3, not after five electrons; group 15 would jump after IE5.

items.stem: An uncoupler collapses the proton motive force of a motile Gram-negative rod. Flagellar rotation stops within seconds even though cytoplasmic ATP remains high for several minutes. In a control, demembranated sperm axonemes continue to beat when ATP is supplied. Bacterial flagellar rotation in this organism is powered by:

choices.text: ATP hydrolysis at a dynein-like ATPase built into the basal body, identical to the axoneme
GTP hydrolysis by FtsZ rings at the pole, which turn the filament
Actin polymerization against the cell wall, which pushes the hook
Proton (or in some species sodium) flux through Mot proteins of the rotary motor in the envelope

items.explanation: The bacterial flagellum is a rotary motor. Torque is generated by ion flow, usually protons, through MotA/MotB stator complexes in the inner membrane, dissipating the proton motive force.
