choices.text: Conflict theory in the Marxian sense, emphasizing surplus extraction by a bourgeois board
Symbolic interactionism (Blumer), which refuses any analysis above a dyad’s gestures
Structural functionalism: institutions are analyzed by the functions they perform for system stability
Rational-choice theory, which treats the hospital as a single utility-maximizing shopper

items.explanation: Functionalism, from Durkheim’s social facts and organic solidarity through Parsons’s AGIL systems, analyzes institutions by the functions they serve for cohesion and equilibrium—the organ analogy is textbook. Marxian conflict theory would ask which class benefits and how contradictions drive change. Symbolic interactionism (Mead/Blumer) inspects meaning in face-to-face interaction, not system organs. Rational choice models individual utility, not a hospital-as-organism metaphor.

distractorRationales.A: A board extracting surplus is conflict analysis, not the equilibrium-organ frame.
distractorRationales.B: Blumer’s premises are about meaning, not societal organs.
distractorRationales.D: A utility-maximizing shopper is not Durkheim’s functional analysis.

items.stem: The extract's tone shifts most clearly when the speaker

choices.text: moves from dry inventory and legal phrasing into self-implicating want—the ridiculous impulse to buy milk—and then back into courtesy with the agent.
begins in rage at the agent and ends in religious consolation.
maintains a single satirical attack on carpet-cleaning advertisements from first sentence to last.
shifts from celebrating vacant possession as freedom to condemning her father for writing lists.

items.explanation: The opening is inventory and a legally tidy phrase. After the poem, the register turns inward and slightly comic-painful: a pen she had not meant to bring, a joke at her own expense, a ridiculous want. The agent's cough returns her to courtesy, which is easier than explaining. That is a detectable turn, not a rage-to-hymn plot, not a satire of advertisements, and not a celebration of vacancy. Tone-shift items require locating where the temperature changes; here it is the cupboard gesture, framed by cooler legal language on either side.

distractorRationales.B: The agent is not initially attacked in rage, and nothing in the close is religious consolation.
distractorRationales.C: Carpet cleaning is one mention in the agent's clocked speech, not a sustained satirical target.
distractorRationales.D: Vacant possession is never celebrated as freedom, and the father is not condemned for the list; the daughter fears being the one who leaves it unanswered.

passage.title: Vacant possession
passage.body:
The rental had been emptied with the efficiency of people who did not live there. I arrived after the skip had gone. What remained were the marks of remaining: a paler rectangle on the wall where a calendar had blocked the sun, a screw in the kitchen plaster that had held nothing I could remember, a ring on the lino where a bin had sat long enough to become a climate. The agent called it "vacant possession." The phrase was legally tidy. It treated my father as a tenancy that had concluded.

I opened the cupboard above the kettle. Inside, taped to the wood, was a shopping list in his slanted capitals, and beneath it a scrap of verse I had never seen. He was not a man who announced poems. He had been a man who boiled water at the same hour, as if the day were a machine that required a particular ignition. The list wanted milk, soap, and a cheaper brand of tea. The last item was written twice, then crossed out, then written again, as if indecision were a kind of company.

The kettle still knew his hour.
I did not.
The cupboard kept a shopping list
addressed to a week that never arrived.
I ticked the milk as if the ticking
could make a future stand up.

I stood with a pen I had not meant to bring and put a mark beside milk, then stopped, because the gesture had the shape of care and the content of a joke at my own expense. Grief, in the pamphlets, is supposed to be a weather that passes over a landscape. In the cupboard it was more like a task left in a shared kitchen: unclaimed, slightly shameful, still assigned. I wanted, ridiculously, to buy the milk. I wanted not to be the kind of daughter who leaves a list unanswered.

The agent coughed in the hallway and mentioned carpet cleaning, then the bond, then the need to "move on" as if the room were a queue. I heard myself thank him. Courtesy was easier than explaining that the room was not empty, only unpopulated. He was not unkind. He was on a clock I did not share. Vacant possession, I thought, is a legal sentence that cannot conjugate the present tense of objects. The kettle, if it could speak, would not have used it. It would have asked why the hour had been cancelled without notice.

items.stem: A monomeric enzyme contains no cysteine. Incubation with β-mercaptoethanol in native buffer leaves the far-UV circular-dichroism spectrum unchanged, whereas 6 M guanidine hydrochloride abolishes the 222 nm helical signal. What do the two treatments together indicate about conformational stability?

choices.text: The fold is locked by disulfides that β-mercaptoethanol somehow cannot reach
β-Mercaptoethanol is a stronger denaturant than guanidine hydrochloride for helical proteins
Guanidine hydrochloride hydrolyzes peptide bonds, and the CD change reports chain cleavage
Secondary structure is maintained by noncovalent interactions, not by disulfides

items.explanation: The protein has no cysteine, so it cannot contain disulfides, and a reductant is not expected to alter its fold—matching the unchanged CD in β-mercaptoethanol. Guanidine hydrochloride is a chaotrope that disrupts the hydrophobic effect and hydrogen bonding; loss of 222 nm ellipticity shows that α-helix (a noncovalent secondary structure) requires those interactions. Guanidine at 6 M does not hydrolyze the backbone on the timescale of a CD experiment, and a reductant is not a stronger general denaturant than GdnHCl. The contrast isolates noncovalent stabilization.

distractorRationales.A: There are no cysteines, so there are no disulfides to lock the fold or to be inaccessible.
distractorRationales.B: The data show the opposite: GdnHCl unfolds the protein and the reductant does not.
distractorRationales.C: Chaotropes unfold proteins noncovalently; peptide-bond hydrolysis requires strong acid or proteases.

items.stem: In the photoelectric effect, monochromatic light already above the metal's threshold frequency has its intensity doubled while frequency is held fixed. The principal result is that:

choices.text: the maximum kinetic energy of ejected electrons doubles
the number of electrons ejected per second doubles, while KE_max is unchanged
the work function of the metal is halved
KE_max drops to zero because intensity, not frequency, now governs the effect

items.explanation: Each photoelectron's maximum kinetic energy is KE_max = h f − φ, which depends on photon frequency and the metal's work function, not on intensity. Intensity at fixed frequency is photon flux, so doubling intensity doubles the number of photons arriving per second and therefore doubles the number of electrons ejected per second (above threshold). The work function is a property of the metal surface; shining brighter light does not change φ. Below threshold, raising intensity still ejects no electrons, but this beam is already above threshold, so rate scales with intensity and KE_max does not.

distractorRationales.A: KE_max is set by photon energy h f minus φ. Intensity does not appear in that equation, so doubling brightness does not double electron kinetic energy.
distractorRationales.C: The work function is characteristic of the metal (and its surface condition), not of the lamp brightness. Intensity does not retune φ.
distractorRationales.D: Above threshold, intensity controls rate, not whether electrons have kinetic energy. KE_max remains h f − φ and is unchanged at fixed f.

items.stem: Radiolabeled hormone X produces autoradiographic grains over nuclei of uterine cells. Hormone Y produces grains only at the plasma membrane of hepatocytes and never over nuclei. X and Y are most consistent with:

choices.text: X a steroid (or thyroid hormone) and Y a peptide
X a peptide and Y a steroid
both peptides that must enter the nucleus to work
both steroids that act only at membrane ion channels

items.explanation: Nuclear accumulation is the classic autoradiographic signature of steroid or thyroid hormones bound to intracellular receptors. Peptide hormones bind plasma-membrane receptors and do not appear over nuclei as the intact labeled ligand. Swapping X and Y inverts that topology. Two peptides would both decorate membranes, and two steroids acting only as membrane-channel ligands would not concentrate over nuclei as X does.

distractorRationales.B: This swaps the compartments. Nuclear grains belong to the lipophilic/nuclear-receptor class, not to peptides.
distractorRationales.C: Peptides do not have to enter the nucleus; they signal from the cell surface. Y's membrane-only pattern is the peptide pattern.
distractorRationales.D: X's nuclear grains contradict an only-at-the-membrane steroid model, and Y's membrane-only pattern is wrong for classic genomic steroids.

items.stem: Benzaldehyde is treated with NH4Cl and KCN, and the isolated aminonitrile is heated in aqueous acid. What is the organic product, and what is its stereochemical character?

choices.text: Enantiopure (S)-phenylglycine, because cyanide approaches only the Re face of the imine
Racemic phenylglycine (2-amino-2-phenylacetic acid), because the uncatalyzed Strecker sequence generates a new stereocenter without facial control
A β-amino acid, because cyanide adds to the carbonyl carbon that becomes C3
Benzylamine, because the nitrile is reduced rather than hydrolyzed in acid

items.explanation: In the Strecker synthesis an aldehyde is converted to an imine (or iminium), which is attacked by cyanide to give an α-aminonitrile. Acidic hydrolysis then converts the nitrile into a carboxylic acid, producing an α-amino acid whose side chain was the aldehyde’s R group—here phenylglycine. The imine is achiral, and cyanide adds to both faces equally, so the product is racemic unless a chiral catalyst or auxiliary is introduced. The new carbon is the α-carbon, not a β-carbon, and aqueous acid hydrolyzes nitriles rather than reducing them to amines.

distractorRationales.A: Without a chiral catalyst or enzyme, both faces of the imine are equivalent. Classic Strecker chemistry is racemic.
distractorRationales.C: Cyanide adds to the imine carbon that becomes C2 (the α-carbon) of the amino acid, not C3.
distractorRationales.D: Hot aqueous acid hydrolyzes the nitrile to a carboxylic acid. Reduction to an amine would require a reductant such as LiAlH4, which is not present.

items.stem: In poem 2, “I, traitor, waved” most nearly implies that

choices.text: the speaker committed a legal crime on the jetty.
answering the wave colludes with a future self the speaker has not become, a small betrayal of the present.
the coins were stolen.
the boat has changed species in a biological sense.

items.explanation: The wave comes from someone greeting a person the speaker has not yet become; calling the return wave treason compresses guilt about becoming, not a statute. Animal is metaphor for the boat’s changed feel. Coins’ edges versus faces belong to recognition, not a theft plot. Reading between the lines in the lyric means taking traitor as moral-self language attached to the wave, which is the only action tagged that way.

distractorRationales.A: No law or arrest is in the poem; traitor is tonal.
distractorRationales.C: Edges versus faces is about recognition of coins, not theft.
distractorRationales.D: “Different animal” is figurative estrangement of the same boat.

passage.title: Two short poems: Ferry
passage.body:
Poem 1 — “Ticket”
I bought a ticket to the other bank
as if the river were a problem in change.
The ferryman took coins that had known other pockets.
He did not ask what I was leaving.
The water did, in small repeated questions
against the hull.

Poem 2 — “Return”
On the way back the same boat
was a different animal.
I recognised the coins by their edges
and not the faces.
Someone on the far jetty waved
at a person I had not yet become
and I, traitor, waved.

items.stem: Suppose the student had measured each L to the bottom of the bob rather than to its centre. On a plot of T² against that recorded length, how would the intercept change relative to the Table 1 procedure?

choices.text: The vertical intercept would remain zero, because a constant length error cannot affect a T² versus L graph.
The vertical intercept would become positive and equal in magnitude to T² at L = 0.400 m, because the whole data set would shift upward.
The vertical intercept would become negative (approximately −0.060 s²), because each recorded L is 0.015 m larger than the length that belongs in T² = (4π²/g) L_centre.
The vertical intercept would become positive and the gradient would double, because diameter rather than radius would now be the length unit.

items.explanation: The bob diameter is 3.0 cm, so the radius is 0.015 m. Length to the bottom is L_centre + 0.015 m. The physical relation is T² = k L_centre with k = 4π²/g ≈ 4.03 s² m^{-1} from Table 1. Substituting L_recorded = L_centre + 0.015 m gives T² = k L_recorded − 0.015k, a line of unchanged slope with vertical intercept −0.015 × 4.03 ≈ −0.060 s². Table 1, measured to the centre, is consistent with a near-zero intercept; measuring to the bottom systematically overstates L and slides every point to the right. A constant length offset is a classic intercept error, not a doubling of gradient and not an upward shift in T².

distractorRationales.A: A systematic additive error in the abscissa is precisely what produces a nonzero intercept; Table 1’s near-origin behaviour would not survive that mis-measure.
distractorRationales.B: T² does not increase when L is overstated; the points move right along the L axis, which makes the intercept more negative, not equal to the first T² value.
distractorRationales.D: Using the bottom rather than the centre adds one radius, not a change of units to diameters, and it does not double 4π²/g.

passage.title: Period of a simple pendulum and the value of g
passage.body:
A student determines the gravitational field strength g from the small-angle period of a simple pendulum. Length L is measured from the support to the centre of a spherical bob of diameter 3.0 cm. For each length the student times 20 oscillations and divides by 20 to obtain the period T; the procedure is repeated three times and the mean is recorded. The timing uncertainty on each 20-oscillation interval is estimated as ±0.20 s from reaction time, so the uncertainty in a single mean T is about ±0.010 s. All runs in Table 1 used a maximum angular displacement of about 5°. Take 4π² = 39.48. For an ideal simple pendulum, T² = (4π²/g) L, so a graph of T² against L should be a straight line through the origin with gradient 4π²/g.

Table 1. Mean period versus length (θ ≈ 5°)

| L (m) | Mean T (s) | T² (s²) |
|-------|------------|---------|
| 0.400 | 1.269 | 1.610 |
| 0.500 | 1.419 | 2.012 |
| 0.600 | 1.554 | 2.415 |
| 0.700 | 1.678 | 2.817 |
| 0.800 | 1.794 | 3.220 |

The student then holds L fixed at 0.600 m and varies the release angle (Table 2).

Table 2. Period versus amplitude at L = 0.600 m

| Maximum angular displacement θ (°) | Mean T (s) |
|------------------------------------|------------|
| 5 | 1.554 |
| 10 | 1.557 |
| 20 | 1.571 |
| 30 | 1.595 |

items.stem: Relative to the image, the caption “The system is coping” functions as

choices.text: a neutral clinical observation confirmed by the matching clocks.
an official sentence the picture contradicts, so the caption is ironic rather than descriptive.
proof that the fifth clock is broken and should be replaced under warranty.
the letter-writer’s own words.

items.explanation: Nothing in the panel shows coping: time is unsynchronised, public time is blank, triage is reduced to sitting up, a clock is face-down. The caption therefore vents an official line against the drawing. It is not the letter, which is a separate text. Warranty and matching clocks are inventions. Caption-versus-image questions in this exam style ask whether the line underwrites or undercuts the drawing; here it undercuts by remaining serene.

distractorRationales.A: The clocks do not match, and the wall clock has no hands.
distractorRationales.C: The face-down clock is a visual of discarded time, not a consumer complaint.
distractorRationales.D: The letter is attributed to Concerned, Upper Shore; the caption sits under the cartoon.

passage.title: Cartoon: Clinic time
passage.body:
A single-panel cartoon, unsigned, published on a letters page.

Foreground: a waiting-room bench. Four people sit. Above each head a small clock; the hands are at 1:10, 2:40, 4:15, and 9:50. None of the clocks match the large wall clock, which has no hands.

On the wall, a framed motto: WE VALUE YOUR TIME. The frame is gold. The glass is cracked.

To the right, a receptionist window. The receptionist smiles with many teeth and holds a clipboard titled TRIAGE (PRIVATE). On the clipboard the only visible line is: “Can they still sit up?” A potted plant on the sill is fake; its price tag remains.

Under the bench, a fifth clock, face-down.

Caption, in small type: “The system is coping.”

A letter printed beneath, from “Concerned, Upper Shore”: “Cartoons like this undermine dedicated staff. If people arrived on time and did not bring relatives, clocks would match.”

items.stem: An investigator inserts a single extra nucleotide immediately after the AUG start codon of a bacterial ORF that previously encoded a 300-residue protein. No compensating mutation is present. Which outcome is most likely?

choices.text: Every amino acid remains identical because degeneracy lets the ribosome skip extra bases at wobble positions.
Translation initiates at the next in-frame AUG, producing a protein that lacks only the N-terminal residue.
The insertion is spliced out of the bacterial transcript as a nuclear intron, restoring the original frame.
The reading frame shifts by one nucleotide, so downstream codons are systematically misread until a stop is encountered, typically yielding a truncated nonfunctional polypeptide.

items.explanation: The genetic code is read as nonoverlapping triplets from a fixed initiation codon. Inserting one nucleotide immediately after AUG regroups every subsequent base, so all downstream codons differ from the original frame. Premature stop codons appear frequently in the new frame, truncating the chain well before 300 residues. Degeneracy does not authorize skipping nucleotides. There is no general mechanism that simply reinitiates at the next AUG to rescue a one-base frameshift across a long ORF, and typical bacterial protein-coding sequences are not spliced by a nuclear spliceosome.

distractorRationales.A: Degeneracy and wobble affect synonymous third-position pairing; they do not cause the ribosome to ignore an inserted nucleotide.
distractorRationales.B: A +1 insertion after the start does not leave the remainder of the original ORF in frame, so the product is not a single-residue N-terminal truncation.
distractorRationales.C: Bacteria lack the nuclear spliceosome that removes eukaryotic introns from pre-mRNA; a genomic +1 insertion remains in the mRNA.

items.stem: An enzyme is assayed with lactate as the only organic substrate. No product forms unless NAD+ is present; the organic product is pyruvate and the dinucleotide is reduced to NADH. According to enzyme classification by reaction type, the protein is:

choices.text: A hydrolase that adds water across the C–C bond of lactate
A ligase that condenses two lactates with concomitant ATP hydrolysis
An isomerase that rearranges lactate to pyruvate without a redox cofactor
An oxidoreductase that uses NAD+ as the electron acceptor

items.explanation: Oxidoreductases catalyze electron transfer. Conversion of lactate (a secondary alcohol) to pyruvate (a ketone) with stoichiometric reduction of NAD+ to NADH is hydride transfer to a nicotinamide cofactor, the defining LDH reaction and EC class 1. Hydrolases add water and do not require NAD+. Ligases join two molecules using NTP hydrolysis, which is not described. An isomerase would rearrange atoms within one molecule without a net redox change or a requirement for NAD+. The obligatory NAD+ dependence and NADH production assign the enzyme as an oxidoreductase.

distractorRationales.A: No water is added, and NAD+ would be unnecessary for a hydrolase.
distractorRationales.B: ATP is not mentioned, and two lactates are not condensed.
distractorRationales.C: Isomerases do not reduce NAD+; the observed cofactor change is a redox signature.

items.stem: An experimenter depolarizes the middle of an unmyelinated axon to threshold with an extracellular electrode. Action potentials:

choices.text: travel only toward the soma
travel only toward the synaptic terminal
fail to start, because spikes can be initiated only in dendrites
propagate in both directions away from the stimulus site

items.explanation: A patch of axon brought to threshold opens local voltage-gated Na+ channels and depolarizes both neighboring regions. There is no refractory wake yet on either side, so two action potentials travel away from the artificial site, one orthodromic and one antidromic. Physiologic initiation at the hillock looks unidirectional only because the soma/dendrite side is a poor regenerative axon and because a refractory region develops behind a naturally traveling spike. Dendrites are not the unique legal site of spike initiation, and the axon membrane itself is fully excitable.

distractorRationales.A: Nothing about a mid-axon shock forbids the terminal-directed spike. Both directions are available at the instant of stimulation.
distractorRationales.B: The soma-directed (antidromic) spike also propagates on that axon; unidirectionality is not an intrinsic one-way valve in the membrane.
distractorRationales.C: Axons, especially the hillock and nodes, are the usual spike-initiation zones. Dendrites are not required to start this experimentally evoked AP.

items.stem: A 2.0 kg cart travelling at 6.0 m s−1 collides with a stationary 4.0 kg cart. For a perfectly inelastic collision they move together at v = (m1 u1) / (m1 + m2). Kinetic energies: KE = (1/2) m v². What is the common speed, and how much KE is lost?

choices.text: v = 2.0 m s−1; KE is conserved at 36 J
v = 3.0 m s−1; KE lost is 0
v = 2.0 m s−1; KE falls from 36 J to 12 J, so 24 J is lost
v = 6.0 m s−1; KE is conserved at 36 J

items.explanation: Momentum conservation: 2.0 × 6.0 = (6.0) v, so v = 2.0 m s−1. Initial KE = 0.50 × 2.0 × 36 = 36 J. Final KE = 0.50 × 6.0 × 4.0 = 12 J. The missing 24 J is dissipated as heat and deformation, which is allowed in a perfectly inelastic collision. Speed is not unchanged, and KE is not conserved for the inelastic case. A 3.0 m s−1 guess is the mean of 6 and 0 without mass weighting. Elastic formulae would give a rebound of the light cart, not a common 2.0 m s−1.

distractorRationales.A: The common speed 2.0 m s−1 is right, but (1/2)×6×4 = 12 J, not 36 J, so KE is not conserved.
distractorRationales.B: Mass-weighted momentum gives 2.0 m s−1, not the unweighted average 3.0 m s−1, and inelastic collisions do lose KE.
distractorRationales.D: The 4.0 kg cart must gain momentum, so the 2.0 kg cart must slow; v cannot stay 6.0 m s−1 if they stick.

items.stem: Malonate, a competitive analog of succinate, is added to respiring mitochondria supplied with pyruvate. Which pair of matrix changes is most likely?

choices.text: Succinate falls and fumarate rises because the block is after fumarase.
Succinate accumulates and conversion of succinate to fumarate decreases.
Isocitrate is depleted because aconitase is the malonate target.
α-Ketoglutarate is converted exclusively to glutamate, fully bypassing the cycle.

items.explanation: Malonate is a classic competitive inhibitor of succinate dehydrogenase, occupying the succinate-binding site so that succinate cannot be oxidized to fumarate. The substrate of the blocked step therefore accumulates, and the product fumarate (and downstream malate/oxaloacetate) declines. Upstream cycle intermediates can also back up. Aconitase is not the malonate target, so isocitrate depletion as a primary event is wrong. Fumarase is downstream of SDH; blocking SDH cannot raise fumarate while lowering succinate. Transamination of α-ketoglutarate may increase if the cycle stalls, but that is not a complete enzymatic bypass of the malonate block.

distractorRationales.A: Malonate inhibits succinate dehydrogenase, which is before fumarase. Succinate should rise and fumarate from that step should fall, not the reverse.
distractorRationales.C: Malonate is a succinate analog aimed at SDH, not aconitase. Isocitrate would not be the depleted substrate of the inhibited enzyme.
distractorRationales.D: Glutamate formation from α-ketoglutarate can increase when the cycle backs up, but it does not ‘exclusively’ replace the cycle or remove the SDH block.

items.stem: Pyridine is readily protonated by dilute aqueous acid (pKa of pyridinium ≈ 5.2), whereas pyrrole is not (pKa of the conjugate acid ≈ −4). Which orbital analysis explains the difference?

choices.text: Pyridine’s nitrogen lone pair occupies an sp2 orbital in the plane of the ring and is not part of the 6π aromatic sextet, so it can bind H+ without destroying aromaticity; pyrrole’s lone pair is part of the sextet
Pyrrole is more basic because its nitrogen is sp3 and has a higher-energy lone pair
Neither heterocycle is aromatic, so basicity tracks only the electronegativity of nitrogen
Pyridine is not aromatic; protonation creates aromaticity, which is why it is basic

items.explanation: Both rings are aromatic with 6π electrons (Hückel 4n+2). In pyridine the nitrogen contributes one electron to the π system from its p orbital, exactly as a CH group would; the lone pair sits in an sp2 orbital in the plane and is available for protonation. In pyrrole the nitrogen already contributes two electrons (the lone pair) to the π sextet. Protonating pyrrole on nitrogen would remove those two electrons from conjugation and destroy aromaticity, so pyrrole is an extremely weak base (and is instead weakly acidic at N–H). Pyrrole’s nitrogen is not sp3 in the aromatic structure.

distractorRationales.B: Pyrrole is far less basic than pyridine. Its nitrogen is planar and sp2, with the lone pair in the aromatic π system.
distractorRationales.C: Both are aromatic. Electronegativity alone cannot explain a ~9-unit pKa gap between two azine/azole nitrogens.
distractorRationales.D: Pyridine is already aromatic before protonation. Aromaticity is preserved, not created, when the in-plane lone pair binds H+.

items.stem: Blood is modeled as an ideal incompressible fluid in a horizontal artery that enters a stenosis with half the upstream cross-sectional area. Compared with the wide segment, the stenosis has:

choices.text: lower speed and higher hydrostatic pressure
higher speed and lower hydrostatic pressure
higher speed and higher hydrostatic pressure
lower speed and lower hydrostatic pressure

items.explanation: Continuity requires the product of area and speed to stay constant, so halving area doubles speed. Bernoulli's equation at constant height then says that an increase in dynamic pressure 1/2 rho v squared must be paid for by a decrease in hydrostatic pressure. The stenosis is therefore the fast, low-pressure region. The opposite pairing of speed and pressure would violate either continuity or energy conservation along a streamline.

distractorRationales.A: Lower speed would require a larger area, not a stenosis. Higher pressure with lower speed can occur in a dilation, not a narrowing.
distractorRationales.C: Speed does rise in the stenosis, but Bernoulli then requires hydrostatic pressure to fall, not rise, at the same height.
distractorRationales.D: Speed does not fall where area falls. Continuity forces the opposite speed change.

items.stem: Two climbers of equal skill fall on the same pitch. The one who had rated “I can complete this route if I persist” returns to practice the move the next day. The one who had rated “I am just not a lead-climbing person” avoids the wall for weeks. Which construct most directly predicts the difference in persistence?

choices.text: Global self-esteem (overall worth) rather than any task belief
External locus of control, which always increases practice after failure
Self-efficacy: belief in capability for this task predicts practice and persistence after failure
Social identity as “climber” must be absent in anyone who falls

items.explanation: Bandura’s self-efficacy is a judgment that one can organize and execute the actions required in a specific domain. High efficacy after a fall supports return to practice; a trait-like “I am not that kind of person” statement functions as low efficacy and predicts withdrawal. Global self-esteem may not differ between the two climbers. External locus (“outcomes are luck”) would not uniquely predict more practice. A fall does not strip a social identity; identities can include being a climber who is currently struggling.

distractorRationales.A: The ratings in the stem are about completing this route, not about being a worthy person in general.
distractorRationales.B: External locus typically reduces, rather than increases, instrumental practice, because effort is seen as irrelevant.
distractorRationales.D: Identity categories survive setbacks; the predictor here is capability belief, not deletion of the climber identity.

items.stem:
A liver homogenate is fractionated by differential centrifugation. Marker quantities are reported per milligram of protein:
1000 g nuclear pellet: succinate dehydrogenase 4 units, acid phosphatase 3 units, NADPH–cytochrome c reductase 5 units, DNA 82 µg.
10 000 g pellet: SDH 96, acid phosphatase 8, reductase 6, DNA 4.
20 000 g pellet: SDH 7, acid phosphatase 88, reductase 9, DNA 2.
100 000 g microsomal pellet: SDH 3, acid phosphatase 6, reductase 91, DNA 1.
Final supernatant: SDH 2, acid phosphatase 5, reductase 4, DNA 0.
Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.text: The 10 000 g pellet is enriched in mitochondria, because succinate dehydrogenase peaks there.
The 20 000 g pellet is nuclei, because acid phosphatase is a nuclear-envelope marker.
The microsomal pellet is nuclei, because it has the highest DNA (91 units of reductase).
The supernatant contains the mitochondria, because succinate dehydrogenase is a soluble cytosolic enzyme.

items.explanation: Succinate dehydrogenase sits in the inner mitochondrial membrane, so its specific activity traces mitochondria. That activity is 96 units mg−1 in the 10 000 g pellet and only 2–7 in the other fractions, so mitochondria sediment there. Acid phosphatase at 88 units marks lysosomes in the 20 000 g pellet; NADPH–cytochrome c reductase at 91 units marks endoplasmic reticulum microsomes; DNA at 82 µg mg−1 marks nuclei. The cytosol is not the mitochondrial compartment. The table therefore assigns mitochondria to the 10 000 g fraction.

distractorRationales.B: Acid phosphatase is a lysosomal hydrolase, not a nuclear marker; nuclei track with DNA in the 1000 g pellet.
distractorRationales.C: The 91-unit peak is the ER reductase, not DNA; microsomal DNA is only 1 µg mg−1.
distractorRationales.D: Succinate dehydrogenase is membrane-bound in mitochondria; the supernatant has only 2 units.

items.stem: A surgical skills lab finds that a simple interrupted suture is performed fastest under high evaluative arousal, whereas a delicate microvascular anastomosis is most accurate at moderate arousal and degrades when the attending stares. This pattern is the Yerkes–Dodson law. Which statement captures it?

choices.text: Performance is a strictly rising linear function of arousal for every task
Hull’s drive reduction predicts that only hunger, not evaluative arousal, can change skill
Performance follows an inverted U with arousal, and the optimal point is lower for more difficult tasks
Maslow’s hierarchy forbids any arousal effect until self-actualization is complete

items.explanation: Yerkes and Dodson described an inverted-U relation between arousal and performance, with complex tasks peaking at lower arousal than simple ones. That matches fast simple suturing under high arousal and fragile fine anastomosis under an audience. A strictly linear “more arousal is always better” rule is the common trap. Hull’s drive-reduction theory concerns tissue deficits and habit strength, not this arousal–complexity interaction. Maslow’s need hierarchy does not ban arousal effects on motor skill.

distractorRationales.A: The law is an inverted U, not a monotonic rise, especially for hard tasks.
distractorRationales.B: Drive reduction is a different motivational theory and does not uniquely own skill-arousal curves.
distractorRationales.D: Maslow does not prohibit Yerkes–Dodson effects in a skills lab.

items.stem: In a Trier Social Stress Test, salivary α-amylase, a sympathetic marker, peaks within minutes of a judged speech, whereas salivary cortisol peaks about twenty minutes after the speech ends. Which physiological account is best?

choices.text: Cortisol is always released first because the adrenal cortex fires before the medulla
Both peaks are produced by the same postganglionic acetylcholine release at the heart, so they must coincide
The sympathetic–adrenal-medullary axis releases catecholamines rapidly, while the HPA axis releases cortisol more slowly after CRH and ACTH
The cortisol lag proves the speech was appraised as irrelevant and therefore not a stressor

items.explanation: Acute psychosocial threat rapidly engages the sympathetic–adrenal-medullary axis, raising catecholamines and markers such as salivary α-amylase within minutes. The hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal cascade requires hypothalamic CRH, pituitary ACTH, and then adrenocortical cortisol, so the glucocorticoid peak is slower, often on the order of tens of minutes in saliva. The cortex-first claim reverses adrenal anatomy and timing. Cardiac acetylcholine does not generate the cortisol curve. A cortisol rise is evidence that the HPA axis treated the speech as a stressor, not as an irrelevant event.

distractorRationales.A: Medullary catecholamines are faster than cortical cortisol; the stem’s amylase-then-cortisol order matches that, not a cortex-first rule.
distractorRationales.B: Cortisol is an endocrine HPA product, not a burst of cardiac acetylcholine, so the peaks need not coincide.
distractorRationales.D: A delayed cortisol peak is the expected HPA time course for a stressor, not a sign that the event was appraised as irrelevant.

items.stem: A focal demyelinating lesion increases internodal membrane capacitance and decreases internodal transmembrane resistance. Compared with adjacent myelinated axon, action potential propagation through the plaque is most likely to:

choices.text: Speed up, because saltatory jumps become longer when myelin is lost
Convert the axon into an electrical synapse with no need for voltage-gated sodium channels
Increase the density of internodal sodium channels above nodal levels within minutes as the only repair
Slow or fail, because local-circuit current leaks across internodal membrane instead of depolarizing the next node to threshold

items.explanation: Myelin increases effective membrane resistance and decreases capacitance, so internodal membrane does not waste depolarizing current. Voltage-gated Na+ channels are concentrated at nodes of Ranvier; the action potential jumps from node to node. Demyelination lets current leak through internodes, lowering the length constant and slowing charging of the next node, which can block conduction. Saltatory conduction is not faster without myelin. Loss of myelin does not create a gap junction, and internodal Na-channel redistribution, when it occurs, is a slow plastic response rather than an immediate rescue that speeds conduction above normal.

distractorRationales.A: Myelin loss shortens the effective jump and slows conduction; it does not lengthen saltatory steps.
distractorRationales.B: The axon remains a chemically/electrically excitable cable with Na channels; it does not become a gap-junction synapse.
distractorRationales.C: Channel redistribution is not an instantaneous, complete replacement of myelin, and internodes do not immediately exceed nodal Na-channel density to speed spikes.

items.stem: Light traveling in glass (n = 2.0) strikes a glass–air interface. The critical angle for total internal reflection is:
items.explanation: Total internal reflection can occur only when light in a higher-index medium meets a lower-index medium, as in glass to air. The critical angle satisfies n1 sin θc = n2 sin 90°, so sin θc = n2 / n1 = 1.0 / 2.0 = 1/2 and θc = 30°. At angles of incidence larger than 30° there is no transmitted ray in air. The 45° value is the critical angle for n = √2, a common memorized special case that does not match n = 2. Sixty degrees would be 90° minus 30° or arcsin(√3/2), not arcsin(1/2).

distractorRationales.A: This is half of 30° without a physical basis. The inverse sine of 1/2 is 30°, not 15°.
distractorRationales.C: sin 45° = 1/√2, which would be θc if n1 were √2. For n = 2 the sine of the critical angle is 1/2, not 1/√2.
distractorRationales.D: This is 90° − 30° or the angle whose sine is √3/2. Snell's law at the critical angle uses sin θc = n2/n1 = 1/2, which is 30°.

items.stem: Fibroblasts from a peroxisome-biogenesis disorder still carry out mitochondrial beta-oxidation of palmitate but accumulate very-long-chain fatty acids. The defective organelles normally:

choices.text: oxidize very-long-chain fatty acids and detoxify hydrogen peroxide via catalase
attach complex oligosaccharides to secretory proteins in the Golgi stack
generate the inner-membrane proton gradient used by ATP synthase
splice pre-mRNA inside the nucleus

items.explanation: Peroxisomes shorten very-long-chain fatty acids and house catalase (and other H2O2-metabolizing enzymes). Mitochondria handle the bulk of long-chain (for example palmitate) beta-oxidation, so those pathways can remain intact when peroxisomes fail—matching the stem. Golgi glycosylation, oxidative phosphorylation, and nuclear splicing are other organelles' jobs and would not specifically spare palmitate oxidation while stacking VLCFA.

distractorRationales.B: N- and O-glycosylation of secretory proteins is a Golgi (and ER) function, not a peroxisomal one.
distractorRationales.C: The proton-motive force for ATP synthase is mitochondrial. The stem already implies mitochondria can still oxidize palmitate.
distractorRationales.D: Splicing is nuclear. Peroxisome failure does not present as a primary spliceosome defect with VLCFA buildup.

items.stem: A human primary spermatocyte has 46 chromosomes and 4C DNA. Immediately after meiosis I, each secondary spermatocyte has:

choices.text: 23 chromosomes (each a dyad of sister chromatids) and 2C DNA
46 chromosomes and 4C DNA, unchanged because meiosis I is equational
23 single chromatids and 1C DNA, the haploid sperm genome
46 unpaired G1 chromosomes with 2C DNA, as in a somatic G1 cell

items.explanation: Meiosis I is reductional: homologs disjoin, so chromosome number falls from 46 to 23, but each chromosome still consists of two sister chromatids. DNA content therefore falls from 4C to 2C, not to 1C. Meiosis II is the equational division that splits sisters, producing 1C haploid spermatids. Treating meiosis I as if it were mitosis (46 chromosomes remaining) or as if sisters had already separated (1C) are the two standard counting errors. A somatic G1 cell is 2C with 46 unreplicated chromosomes, which is not a secondary spermatocyte.

distractorRationales.B: Meiosis I reduces ploidy; it is not equational, so neither chromosome number nor DNA content stays 46/4C.
distractorRationales.C: 1C 23-chromatid products appear after meiosis II, not after meiosis I.
distractorRationales.D: Secondary spermatocytes still have replicated dyads, not G1 unreplicated chromosomes.

items.stem: How many stereoisomers exist for 2-bromo-3-chlorobutane, CH3CHBrCHClCH3?
items.explanation: C2 and C3 are both stereocenters, and they are not identically substituted (one bears Br, the other Cl). The 2^n rule therefore gives 2^2 = 4 stereoisomers: a pair of enantiomers with the (2R,3R)/(2S,3S) relative configuration and a second diastereomeric pair (2R,3S)/(2S,3R). There is no meso form because the two centers are different, so none of the four is achiral. Two would describe a single stereocenter; three is the count for a molecule such as 2,3-dibromobutane that has a meso isomer; eight would require three independent stereocenters.

distractorRationales.A: Two stereoisomers would be expected for a molecule with only one stereocenter (a single enantiomeric pair).
distractorRationales.B: Three is the stereoisomer count for 2,3-dibromobutane, which has two identically substituted centers and therefore one meso form plus one enantiomeric pair.
distractorRationales.D: Eight stereoisomers would require three unrelated stereocenters (2^3). This chain has only two.

items.stem: A drug blocks nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in autonomic ganglia. The expected result is:

choices.text: selective loss of parasympathetic output with fully intact sympathetic output
impaired transmission in both sympathetic and parasympathetic pathways
increased firing of both divisions' postganglionic neurons
blockade of steroid-hormone nuclear receptors in the adrenal cortex

items.explanation: Both sympathetic and parasympathetic ganglia use acetylcholine onto nicotinic receptors on postganglionic neurons (the sympathetic adrenal medulla is a related nicotinic target). A ganglionic nicotinic blocker therefore hits both autonomic divisions. It is not selective for craniosacral outflow, it does not excite postganglionic cells, and nicotinic ACh receptors are ligand-gated ion channels, not nuclear steroid receptors.

distractorRationales.A: Sympathetic ganglia are also nicotinic. Selectivity for parasympathetic only would require a different receptor distribution than the one that exists.
distractorRationales.C: Antagonists decrease, not increase, ganglionic transmission.
distractorRationales.D: This confuses nicotinic ion channels with intracellular steroid receptors, which are a different protein family and a different signaling logic.

items.stem: A mutant HIV-1 reverse transcriptase has kcat for dNTP incorporation reduced 80-fold with an unaltered Km for dNTPs. In newly infected CD4 T cells, compared with wild-type virus, synthesis of full-length proviral DNA is expected to be:

choices.text: Faster, because a lower kcat always means higher fidelity and therefore fewer pauses
Unchanged, because host replicative DNA polymerase copies the viral RNA genome directly
Replaced by integrase polymerization, which does not require reverse transcriptase
Slower, because minus- and plus-strand DNA synthesis from the RNA template is catalyzed by reverse transcriptase at a rate set by kcat

items.explanation: Retroviruses package reverse transcriptase so that the single-stranded RNA genome can be converted into double-stranded DNA before integrase inserts a provirus. The enzyme's kcat is the catalytic turnover per active site; dropping it 80-fold slows chain elongation even when dNTP binding (Km) is normal and dNTP pools are saturating. Host DNA polymerases do not copy incoming viral RNA as mRNA into DNA. Integrase catalyzes concerted insertion of already-made DNA ends, not polymerization of the genome. Fidelity can change with some RT mutants, but a pure kcat drop does not make DNA synthesis faster.

distractorRationales.A: Catalytic rate and fidelity are different parameters; slowing chemistry lengthens the time to a complete provirus.
distractorRationales.B: Cellular DNA polymerases act on DNA templates; reverse transcription is the viral enzyme's job.
distractorRationales.C: Integrase cannot substitute for DNA polymerization from RNA.

items.stem: A linear double-stranded DNA viral genome is hydrolyzed completely to mononucleotides. Adenine accounts for 18% of all bases. A student reports that guanine must also be 18% because ‘purines are equal.’ Which value is the actual percentage of guanine, and why was the student wrong?

choices.text: 18%, because Chargaff’s rules set A equal to G in duplex DNA.
32%, because A pairs with T so A = T = 18%, leaving G = C = 32%.
36%, because G must equal A + T in a Watson–Crick duplex.
64%, because G + C equals A and the remaining bases are all guanine.

items.explanation: In double-stranded DNA, Watson–Crick pairing enforces A = T and G = C, not A = G. If adenine is 18% of all bases, thymine is also 18%, so A + T = 36%. The remaining 64% of bases are G + C, split equally, so guanine is 32%. The student’s purine-equality claim confuses the two purines with each other; Chargaff’s rules pair each purine with a pyrimidine. These equalities do not apply to single-stranded genomes, but the stem specifies a duplex molecule, so the calculation is determined.

distractorRationales.A: Chargaff’s rules set A equal to T and G equal to C, not A equal to G. Equal purine percentages would be coincidental, not required.
distractorRationales.C: There is no rule that G equals A + T. After assigning A = T = 18%, G and C share the remaining 64% equally (32% each).
distractorRationales.D: G + C is 64%, but that sum is split between guanine and cytosine; guanine alone is 32%, not 64%.

items.stem: A hospital deploys a new mRNA platform within months, while consent templates, kinship rules about stored samples, and malpractice doctrine lag by years. Ogburn’s concept that names this gap is which of the following?

choices.text: Culture shock, which is a society-level legal delay rather than an individual’s strain in a new culture
McDonaldization (Ritzer) as a synonym for delayed ethics committees
Cultural lag: material culture (technology) changes faster than nonmaterial culture (norms, laws, meanings)
Assimilation, because lag is defined as English-only signage

items.explanation: Ogburn’s cultural lag is the delay of nonmaterial culture behind material invention—the classic cars-before-traffic-laws example, here mRNA before updated consent and kinship norms. Culture shock is an individual’s disorientation in an unfamiliar culture. Ritzer’s McDonaldization is efficiency, calculability, predictability, and control, not lag per se. Assimilation is absorption of a minority into a dominant culture, not a technology–norm gap.

distractorRationales.A: Culture shock is not Ogburn’s macrosocial lag of laws behind gadgets.
distractorRationales.B: McDonaldization is a rationalization thesis, not the name of the delay.
distractorRationales.D: Assimilation is a different cultural process than material/nonmaterial mismatch.

items.stem: In a residency interview, an applicant uses flattery of the program (ingratiation) and mentions first-author papers (self-promotion), then looks concerned when describing a patient’s death (exemplification of virtue). Jones and Pittman’s taxonomy of impression-management strategies would classify this as which overall project?

choices.text: Unconscious Freudian displacement of oral drives onto the interviewer
Strategic self-presentation: selecting behaviors to shape an attributed identity (likable, competent, moral)
Asch conformity to a wrong line length
Mere exposure (Zajonc) to the interviewer’s face as the sole cause of liking

items.explanation: Impression management is the attempt to control attributed identities. Jones and Pittman distinguished ingratiation (liking), self-promotion (competence), exemplification (moral worth), intimidation, and supplication. The applicant’s mix is strategic self-presentation, compatible with Goffman’s broader dramaturgy. Displacement is a defense mechanism, not this taxonomy. Asch is majority influence on a perceptual judgment. Mere exposure is liking from repeated neutral exposure, not a one-shot interview script.

distractorRationales.A: Psychodynamic displacement is not Jones and Pittman’s strategy list.
distractorRationales.C: No confederate majority on line lengths is present.
distractorRationales.D: Mere exposure does not explain flattery and CV displays as tactics.

items.stem: A fibroblast line coexpresses wild-type EGFR and a truncated EGFR that binds EGF but lacks the intracellular tyrosine kinase domain. EGF-stimulated MAPK phosphorylation is strongly suppressed relative to cells that express only wild-type receptor. The truncated receptor acts as a dominant negative because it:

choices.text: Sequesters ligand and forms nonproductive dimers in which trans-autophosphorylation cannot occur
Hydrolyzes GTP on Ras more rapidly than GAP, thereby silencing MAPK independently of dimerization
Constitutively phosphorylates STAT proteins in the absence of EGF
Translocates to the nucleus and functions as a steroid-hormone receptor repressor of cyclin genes

items.explanation: EGFR is a receptor tyrosine kinase that must dimerize so that partner kinase domains can trans-autophosphorylate, creating phosphotyrosine docking sites for adaptor-driven Ras-MAPK activation. A kinase-deleted ectodomain still binds EGF and still dimerizes, so it poisons mixed dimers and also competes for ligand. The result is dominant-negative blockade even though some wild-type chains are present. The truncation has no kinase, so it cannot hyperphosphorylate STATs, it is not a Ras GAP, and RTKs are not nuclear steroid receptors.

distractorRationales.B: Dominant-negative EGFR acts at the receptor-dimer step, not by becoming a Ras GTPase.
distractorRationales.C: Without a kinase domain the mutant cannot phosphorylate STATs.
distractorRationales.D: EGFR signaling is membrane-proximal tyrosine phosphorylation, not steroid-receptor transcription as the primary truncated mechanism.

items.stem: In the sentence “A coverage estimate can become a footnote that licenses the headline number,” the author is primarily

choices.text: accusing statisticians of fabricating the fifty million figure out of whole cloth.
describing how an honest error model can still function rhetorically as permission to treat a compromise as a photograph.
claiming that appendices are illegal unless read aloud in parliament.
denying that post-enumeration surveys ever occur.

items.explanation: The paragraph grants that professionals name error, then shows the public-facing split: fifty million in the ear, a compromise in the appendix. Licensing is rhetorical permission, not a charge of invention from nothing. The photograph metaphor is the author's name for that misuse. A ignores the grant that compromise is not a crime. C invents a legal rule. D contradicts the explicit mention of surveys. The argumentative move is to separate technical candor from public enchantment.

distractorRationales.A: The author calls the total a compromise among models, not a fabrication, and says compromise is not a crime.
distractorRationales.C: No legal requirement about reading appendices is proposed.
distractorRationales.D: Post-enumeration surveys are cited as part of the professional ethic the author is distinguishing from headline use.

passage.title: The census of the uncounted
passage.body:
Political arithmetic began as a courtly hobby: a way of estimating how many subjects a prince could tax, feed, or send to war. Its early practitioners treated people as a kind of harvest. What could be enumerated could be extracted. What could not be enumerated was, for administrative purposes, a rumor.

The modern census inherited the appetite and dressed it as representation. To be counted is now advertised as a civic right, a way of appearing in the distribution of schools, clinics, and parliamentary seats. The advertisement is not false. Under-counted neighborhoods do lose clinics. The advertisement is incomplete. A census is also a machine for deciding which kinds of life will be treated as facts and which will remain anecdotes told to a volunteer with a clipboard.

Consider the category. Every census must invent boxes. The boxes are not discovered in nature; they are negotiated among ministries, churches, and, later, identity movements. A person who lives in two houses, or in none, or who works in a language the form does not print, must be forced into a box or dropped. Dropping looks like a clerical mishap. It is often a theory of the state: some lives are too expensive to verify, too mobile to locate, too politically inconvenient to add to a total that will be used against the ministry next year.

Statisticians reply that they already know this, that they publish coverage estimates and post-enumeration surveys, that the professional ethic is to name the error. Naming the error is not the same as refusing the uses of the total. A coverage estimate can become a footnote that licenses the headline number. The public hears fifty million; the appendix whispers that the fifty million is a compromise among several less flattering models. Compromise is not a crime. Treating the compromise as a photograph is.

There is a further twist. Groups that have been historically erased often demand better counting, and they are right to. Visibility in a dataset can be a precondition of funds. Yet the same groups may later discover that a sharper count is also a sharper target: for policing, for debt collection, for the allocation of blame when a service fails. The census does not choose the policy. It does make the policy cheaper to aim.

None of this is an argument for ignorance. A state that refuses to count will invent its numbers in the back room and call the invention common sense. The argument is for a less enchanted relationship to the table. Read the boxes as arguments. Read the missing as a constituency. And when a politician says the numbers speak for themselves, notice that speech is exactly what numbers cannot do until someone supplies a sentence.

items.stem: Groups brainstorm uses for a brick. When ideas are pooled anonymously, unique ideas per person fall relative to working alone. When each idea is tagged with a name on a shared screen, per-person output matches the alone condition. The identifiability effect is best explained as:

choices.text: Social loafing that shrinks when contributions are identifiable
Social facilitation of a novel creative task, which should always rise in groups
Deindividuation causing more ideas when people are anonymous
Bystander apathy toward a medical crisis

items.explanation: Brainstorming in a pool is a collective task. When credit is anonymous, individuals can hide, and unique output per person drops—social loafing. Tagging names restores accountability, so effort returns to the alone baseline. Facilitation of a poorly learned or complex generative task would, if anything, predict impairment from an audience, not a benefit of anonymity. Deindividuation would predict more unrestrained output when anonymous, which is the opposite of fewer ideas. No emergency is present.

distractorRationales.B: Idea generation is not a well-learned dominant response that an audience should automatically improve; the drop when anonymous is loafing.
distractorRationales.C: Anonymity reduced, rather than increased, idea counts, which is not a deindividuation-disinhibition pattern.
distractorRationales.D: The task is idea listing, not helping a victim.

items.stem:
Three C6 hydrocarbons are treated with bromine in the dark in CCl4, then with Br2/FeBr3.

Sample | Br2/CCl4 (dark) | Br2/FeBr3
Cyclohexane | orange persists | orange persists (very slow)
Cyclohexene | orange decolourises instantly | (already reacted)
Benzene | orange persists | substitution, HBr fumes, pale product

Which bonding description is supported?

choices.text: Benzene is a typical alkene, because it eventually reacts with bromine
Cyclohexane is unsaturated, which is why FeBr3 is required
All three are aromatic, differing only in colour
Cyclohexene undergoes rapid electrophilic addition; benzene’s delocalised π system resists addition and instead substitutes under Lewis-acid catalysis; cyclohexane has no π bond

items.explanation: Instant decolourisation in the dark is addition to an isolated C=C, the cyclohexene row. Benzene leaves Br2/CCl4 untouched, proving it does not add like an alkene, but does undergo catalysed substitution with FeBr3, the aromatic electrophilic-substitution signature. Cyclohexane, with only σ bonds, does neither on this timescale. Reaction of benzene under forcing catalytic conditions is substitution, not evidence that benzene is ‘a typical alkene’. Cyclohexane’s inertness in both tests is the saturated-alkane pattern. Aromaticity is unique to benzene in this set.

distractorRationales.A: A typical alkene would decolourise Br2 in the dark, which benzene does not.
distractorRationales.B: Cyclohexane fails both tests; FeBr3 is the aromatic-substitution catalyst for benzene.
distractorRationales.C: Cyclohexane and cyclohexene are not aromatic; their Br2 behaviour differs sharply from benzene.

items.stem: A city museum digitizes a seized drum, equalizes the audio of a 1960s field tape to concert-hall norms, and files the file under “world music.” Applying the passage, the author would most likely say this

choices.text: is a purely technical rescue that completes nothing, because digits have no font.
can complete the seizure in a gentler font: readability as art in the receiving capital without restoring a right of refusal.
is identical to leaving a lacuna as a paler mute on a medieval panel.
proves consultation is always theater and should stop.

items.explanation: The colonial paragraph says cleaning into a style that makes objects readable as art in the receiving capital completes the seizure in a gentler font, especially without a right of refusal. Concert-hall equalization and a “world music” file are that readability. A denies the paragraph. C analogizes to a different editorial aesthetic without the colonial mechanism. D overreads the theater warning into abolition of consultation. Application should carry the seizure-and-readability principle, not a random conservation technique.

distractorRationales.A: The author treats technical rescue without restored refusal as completion of seizure, font or no font.
distractorRationales.C: Leaving a lacuna is an editorial honesty example, not the colonial-readability mechanism.
distractorRationales.D: Consultation may be theater and is still called a different verb from rescue; the author does not end it.

passage.title: The museum as a verb
passage.body:
Conservation used to mean stopping time. A painting was a patient; varnish was a bandage; the ideal was to return the object to a single authentic hour and then prevent further hours from occurring. That ideal had a hidden historiography. It assumed the authentic hour was already known, usually as the artist’s last brushstroke, and that later repairs, soot, liturgy, and even damage were noise.

A newer conservation talk prefers verbs. To museum an object is to keep choosing which traces will remain legible. Cleaning is not the removal of history; it is the promotion of one history over another. The nineteenth-century restorer who “completed” a medieval panel was not more ideological than the twenty-first-century restorer who leaves the lacuna as a paler mute. Both are editors. They differ in which audience they imagine and in how proudly they sign the edit.

Critics of reversible methods sometimes complain that visible fills and honest seams break the spell. They want the old miracle: an untouched past that happens to hang at eye level under LEDs. The complaint is aesthetically sincere and philosophically confused. The spell was always produced with scaffolding, attributions, and lighting. Reversibility is not a refusal of beauty. It is a refusal to trap the next generation inside today’s certainty about what the object “really” was.

There is a colonial edge. Objects that arrived by seizure were often cleaned into a style that made them readable as art in the receiving capital, which is to say, cleaned of the uses that had made them un-museumlike. To restore the pigment without restoring the right of refusal is to complete the seizure in a gentler font. Some institutions now consult source communities about smoke, wear, and whether an object should be seen at all. Consultation is slow and can be theater. It is still a different verb from rescue.

If this sounds like relativism, notice what it does not say. It does not say that all edits are equal, or that pigment chemistry is a matter of taste. It says that technical competence cannot supply the missing decision about which past is being kept available. The decision will be made. Calling it science does not make it less a decision. Calling it care does not either. The more honest museum is the one that can show its verbs.

items.stem: A Task B essay on belonging mentions silence at a table, a passport metaphor from the set, and a later city share-house, but never lets those three touch. Which revision would integrate them?

choices.text: Keep them in separate paragraphs labelled Childhood, Symbol, Adult, with no cross-reference.
Show that the share-house key-in-a-bowl was a learned substitute for the table’s silence: a practice of belonging that still flinched from speech, so the passport stamp was never the real document.
Drop two of the three so the essay cannot be accused of having ideas.
Add a fourth thread about climate policy to prove range.

items.explanation: Integration on Task B is often temporal and metaphorical: a later practice revealed as a translation of an earlier silence, with a comment’s image (passport) used to name what still was not a document. B makes the three threads one argument. Separate labelled boxes are a list of themes. Dropping material to avoid thought is not craft. A climate-policy bolt-on is range as scatter, usually a Task A hijack. The reader should feel the pieces requiring one another. That requirement is the score. B is the only revision that creates it.

distractorRationales.A: Labels without contact are the problem restated as a plan.
distractorRationales.C: Fewer images without relation still fail; the issue is contact, not count.
distractorRationales.D: An extra policy thread would likely disintegrate the personal piece, not unify it.

items.stem: A lambda lysogen is exposed to UV doses that activate RecA. RecA stimulates autocleavage of the lambda cI repressor. The expected immediate outcome for the prophage is:

choices.text: Permanent silencing of all phage genes with no virion production, because cI cleavage locks lysogeny
Excision of the prophage and induction of the lytic cycle, producing progeny phage and usually lysing the host
Conversion of the phage genome into a prion that seeds in the cytoplasm without DNA replication
Immediate reverse transcription of lambda DNA into an RNA provirus that integrates at a new site

items.explanation: In lysogeny, cI repressor occupies operators and prevents lytic transcription while the prophage rides along in the bacterial chromosome. DNA damage activates RecA, which facilitates cI autocleavage, dropping repressor occupancy. Lytic genes including excisionases then fire, the prophage excises, and the phage replicates, packages, and lyses the cell. Cleavage of cI is the switch out of lysogeny, not a lock into it. Lambda is a dsDNA phage and does not reverse-transcribe, and induction is not prion conversion.

distractorRationales.A: cI cleavage removes repression; it does not deepen lysogeny.
distractorRationales.C: Prophage induction is a DNA recombination and transcription program, not a prion disease.
distractorRationales.D: Reverse transcription is a retrovirus strategy; lambda replicates as DNA.

items.stem:
The water–gas shift reaction CO(g) + H2O(g) ⇌ CO2(g) + H2(g) has Kc = 10.0 at 800 K, with Kc = ([CO2][H2]) / ([CO][H2O]). A 1.0 L vessel at 800 K is at equilibrium with the first row of the table. A pulse of extra CO2 then raises [CO2] instantly to the second-row value; the other three concentrations are unchanged at that instant.

Stage | [CO] | [H2O] | [CO2] | [H2]  (all mol L−1)
Equilibrium | 0.50 | 0.50 | 1.58 | 1.58
Immediately after adding CO2 | 0.50 | 0.50 | 3.16 | 1.58

What is Q after the pulse, and what net reaction restores equilibrium?

choices.text: Q remains 10.0, so adding a product cannot shift a system that is already at equilibrium.
Q = 5.0, less than Kc, so the forward reaction produces still more CO2 and H2.
Q = 20, greater than Kc, so the reverse reaction consumes CO2 and H2 and forms CO and H2O.
Q = 20, greater than Kc, so the forward reaction continues because Kc must rise to match the new Q.

items.explanation: The equilibrium row satisfies Kc: (1.58 × 1.58) / (0.50 × 0.50) = 2.496 / 0.25 ≈ 10.0. After the CO2 pulse, Q = (3.16 × 1.58) / 0.25 = 4.993 / 0.25 ≈ 20, which is greater than Kc. The reverse reaction therefore proceeds, consuming CO2 and H2. That is Le Chatelier’s response to adding a product. Kc is unchanged at 800 K; Q, not Kc, is what jumps when a concentration is suddenly altered.

distractorRationales.A: Adding CO2 changes the numerator of Q immediately. Q is then 20, not 10, so a net reverse reaction occurs.
distractorRationales.B: Q after the pulse is about 20, not 5. Q > Kc drives the reverse reaction, which consumes CO2 rather than producing more of it.
distractorRationales.D: Q is 20, but Kc does not chase Q. Temperature is still 800 K, so Kc stays 10 and the reverse reaction lowers Q back to 10.

items.stem: A seizure is staged over an intercom. Help is faster and more likely when the participant believes they are the only listener than when they believe four other students also hear the seizure. Which mechanism is the best explanation?

choices.text: Social facilitation of helping as a dominant well-learned response that should increase in a group
Bystander effect via diffusion of responsibility: more co-witnesses reduce each person’s sense of personal obligation
Deindividuation from wearing a mask, which was not part of the procedure
Normative peer pressure to match a helpful in-group, which predicts more helping when more peers are present

items.explanation: Darley and Latané’s seizure study is the textbook bystander effect: the presence of other witnesses lowers helping. The proposed mediator is diffusion of responsibility—each person feels less uniquely accountable when others could act. Facilitation would predict better performance of a dominant helping response in a group, which is the wrong direction. Deindividuation was not manipulated with anonymity costumes. A helpful peer-pressure account predicts the opposite of what the intercom design finds.

distractorRationales.A: Helping fell, not rose, as the believed audience of co-helpers grew, which is the opposite of facilitation of a dominant help response.
distractorRationales.C: No mask or anonymity costume is described; the variable is believed number of witnesses.
distractorRationales.D: Normative pressure to be helpful in a group would increase helping with more peers, not decrease it.

items.stem: A keto ester must have its ketone preserved while the ester is reduced to a primary alcohol with LiAlH4. Which protecting-group sequence succeeds, and why?

choices.text: Use 0.5 equivalent of LiAlH4; ketones always reduce more slowly than esters, so the ketone survives
Convert the ketone to a cyclic acetal with ethylene glycol and acid, reduce the ester with LiAlH4, then hydrolyze the acetal with aqueous acid
Use NaBH4 in methanol, because borohydride reduces esters rapidly and leaves ketones untouched
Form the acetal, then reduce with LiAlH4, which also cleaves acetals, simultaneously freeing the ketone as an alcohol

items.explanation: LiAlH4 reduces both ketones and esters, so an unprotected ketone would be destroyed. A cyclic acetal (1,3-dioxolane) is formed under acid catalysis from the ketone and ethylene glycol. Acetals are stable to hydride and to basic nucleophiles, so LiAlH4 then reduces only the ester to the alcohol. Mild aqueous acid hydrolyzes the acetal back to the ketone. NaBH4 actually shows the opposite chemoselectivity: it reduces ketones much faster than esters. Acetals are not cleaved by LiAlH4; that is why they are useful protecting groups.

distractorRationales.A: Ketones are generally more electrophilic than esters and are reduced at least as readily by LiAlH4. Half an equivalent will not spare the ketone.
distractorRationales.C: NaBH4 reduces aldehydes and ketones, not ordinary esters. That reagent would destroy the ketone and leave the ester.
distractorRationales.D: Hydride does not hydrolyze acetals. Acidic water, not LiAlH4, is what restores the ketone after reduction.

items.stem: A lab presents a sudden loud noise while recording a startle blink and a continuous self-report dial of fear. Felt fear and the blink both begin within a few hundred milliseconds, and neither measure reliably precedes the other. Palmar skin-conductance change lags by one to two seconds. Which theory is most consistent with near-simultaneity of feeling and the fast motor sign, and with the slowness of the viscera?

choices.text: James–Lange theory, which requires that visceral change be perceived before any feeling can start
Opponent-process theory, which requires a delayed opposite emotion before fear is reported
Cannon–Bard theory, which holds that a central process triggers experience and bodily responses together, so slow viscera cannot be the source of the feeling
Schachter–Singer theory, which requires a waiting-room confederate to assign a label before feeling can start

items.explanation: Cannon argued that the viscera are too slow and too undifferentiated to be the origin of distinct, rapidly felt emotions. Cannon–Bard theory therefore places a central (thalamic) process that simultaneously generates the conscious feeling and the bodily pattern. Fast coincidence of reported fear and a motor sign, with skin conductance trailing, matches that architecture and undercuts a strictly visceral James–Lange sequence. Opponent-process theory is about a later opposite state, not latency of the first feeling. Two-factor theory is an arousal-plus-label account and does not require a confederate for every fear episode.

distractorRationales.A: A visceral-first James–Lange sequence is strained when feeling begins before, or without waiting for, the slow skin-conductance change.
distractorRationales.B: Opponent-process theory predicts a subsequent opposite feeling (for example, relief), not that fear itself must be delayed until an opposite appears.
distractorRationales.D: Schachter–Singer theory uses context to label unexplained arousal; it does not require a confederate before any fear can be felt in a startle paradigm.

items.stem:
Dipole moments and boiling points of 1,2-dichloroethene isomers:

Isomer | μ (D) | bp (°C)
cis | 1.9 | 60
trans | 0.0 | 48

Both have Mr = 97. Which explanation is consistent with polarity and packing?

choices.text: Cis is non-polar, which is why μ is listed as 1.9 D
Cis C–Cl dipoles add, raising intermolecular dipole–dipole attraction and bp; trans dipoles cancel, leaving a non-polar molecule with the lower bp
Trans has the higher bp because μ = 0 means stronger forces
The 12 °C gap is a molecular-mass difference

items.explanation: In the cis isomer both chlorines lie on the same side so the C–Cl vectors reinforce (1.9 D), producing dipole–dipole attractions on top of dispersion and a 60 °C boiling point. In trans the vectors oppose (0.0 D), so only dispersion remains and the boiling point is 12 °C lower. Zero dipole moment means weaker, not stronger, polar attractions. The isomers share Mr = 97. A 1.9 D dipole is the definition of a polar molecule, so cis is polar.

distractorRationales.A: μ = 1.9 D is a substantial dipole; cis is polar.
distractorRationales.C: The trans bp is 48 °C, lower than cis 60 °C; μ = 0 removes dipole–dipole forces.
distractorRationales.D: Both isomers are C2H2Cl2, identical mass.

items.stem: Medical students give serial morning samples during a six-week examination block. In week 1, catecholamines and cortisol surge and sleep collapses. In weeks 2–5, cortisol stays high but exam performance recovers. In the week after finals, several students develop viral illness and show blunted cortisol reactivity to a laboratory speech. Which general-adaptation-syndrome sequence is illustrated?

choices.text: Exhaustion, then alarm, then resistance, because the illnesses came at the end of the term
Resistance only; later infection shows they never mounted a stress response
Primary then secondary appraisal, which are the named stages of GAS
Alarm (acute surge), resistance (sustained high cortisol with recovered function), then exhaustion (illness and hyporeactivity)

items.explanation: Selye’s general adaptation syndrome orders the organism’s response to a persistent stressor as alarm, resistance, and exhaustion. The first week’s catecholamine and cortisol spike with functional disruption is alarm. Continued glucocorticoid elevation with restored performance is resistance. Later infection and blunted reactivity fit exhaustion, when adaptive systems are depleted or dysregulated. Appraisal terms come from Lazarus, not from GAS stage names. Reversing the order, or treating infection as proof that no stress response occurred, misreads the timeline in the stem.

distractorRationales.A: Illness after prolonged demand is the last stage, not the first; alarm is the initial surge.
distractorRationales.B: A documented catecholamine and cortisol surge is a mounted stress response; later illness does not erase it.
distractorRationales.C: Primary and secondary appraisal are Lazarus’s cognitive steps, not Selye’s GAS stages.

items.stem: “Failed fence” at noon versus “crowd that has agreed not to face you” at dusk most nearly implies that

choices.text: the steel changes alloy at sunset.
the same spacing can be read as broken exclusion or as a turned community, depending on light and the viewer’s metaphor.
the memorial is only open at dusk.
tourists are absent at noon.

items.explanation: The critic offers two appearances of the same uprights. Implication from diction: fence is exclusion that failed; crowd-not-facing is a social body that withholds. Light cues the shift, not a metallurgical one. Opening hours and tourist schedules are not given. The diction pair is doing the interpretive work the exam means by implication from word choice.

distractorRationales.A: Alloy does not change; reading does.
distractorRationales.C: Noon and dusk are both used; no closing time is stated.
distractorRationales.D: Tourists are not timed to dusk only.

passage.title: On the new memorial
passage.body:
The memorial is a corridor of rusted uprights, each the height of a person, irregularly spaced so that you must turn sideways to pass. At noon they look like a failed fence. At dusk they look like a crowd that has agreed not to face you. There are no names. A small plaque at the exit says only: THEY WERE NOT LATE. THEY WERE PREVENTED.

Tourists complain that they do not know whom to pity. School groups count the uprights and get different numbers, because some are so close they read as one. A veteran interviewed on the steps said he hated it, then stood there until the lights came on, then said he hated that he did not hate it enough.

The sculptor, in a panel discussion, refused the word healing. “If it heals,” she said, “it has failed at being a door you cannot swagger through.” Critics split between those who call this moral bullying in Cor-Ten steel and those who call the tourists’ complaint the point.

I went through twice. The second time a child asked why the fence was broken. His father said it was not a fence. The child, satisfied with a new category, ran. I was not satisfied. Prevention is a bureaucratic word. In the corridor it becomes a body insisting on its width.

items.stem: Use PV = n R T with R = 8.0 J mol−1 K−1. n = 2.0 mol, T = 300 K, V = 0.050 m³. Average translational KE per molecule is (3/2) k T. If T is doubled at constant V and n, what happens to P and to the average KE?

choices.text: P = 96 kPa initially; doubling T doubles both P and the average molecular KE
P = 96 kPa; doubling T doubles P but leaves KE unchanged
P = 9.6 kPa; doubling T has no effect at constant V
P = 96 kPa; doubling T doubles KE but halves P to keep PV = nRT

items.explanation: P = nRT/V = 2.0 × 8.0 × 300 / 0.050 = 4800 / 0.050 = 96 000 Pa = 96 kPa. Gay-Lussac / Charles in the form P ∝ T at fixed V, n, so 2T implies 2P. Kinetic theory identifies P with molecular KE density, and (3/2)kT itself is linear in T, so mean KE also doubles. A missed factor of 10 in V would give 9.6 kPa. Mean KE cannot stay fixed if T changes. P does not fall when T rises at constant V. The two statements (P and KE) therefore move together.

distractorRationales.B: ⟨KE⟩ = (3/2) k T must double when T doubles; that is the kinetic-theory definition of temperature here.
distractorRationales.C: V = 0.050 m³ already yields 96 kPa, and P ∝ T at constant V.
distractorRationales.D: PV = nRT at constant V means P rises with T, it does not fall.

items.stem: Which of the following situations is most analogous to the author's contrast between receiving a text and recruiting it?

choices.text: A kitchen that only 'hosts' a visiting cook after rewriting every recipe until guests cannot tell the food was ever foreign, then advertises the guest's name as proof of cosmopolitan taste.
A library that stocks facing-page bilingual editions so that delays in reading are mechanically impossible.
A publisher that refuses to print any translation, on the ground that all rendering is recruitment.
A teacher who requires students to look up every word in a bilingual dictionary before class, treating the dictionary as a moral test.

items.explanation: Receiving, in the passage, would leave a trace of the guest; recruiting makes the page a mirror with a foreign name attached, using prestige to ratify what the host already believed. The kitchen that erases every foreign mark and then sells the guest's name maps that structure: hospitality is advertised while the guest's difference is removed. Bilingual editions, a ban on translation, and dictionary-as-moral-test each invert or ignore a local claim (delay can be honest; translation remains necessary; dictionaries are not moral instruments). The analogy must preserve both the erasure and the prestige-borrowing, which only A does.

distractorRationales.B: The author values some delay as information; an edition designed to make delay impossible would be closer to the fluency ideal being criticized, not an analogue of receiving.
distractorRationales.C: The author refuses abandonment of translation and the calque museum alike; a ban would not model receiving.
distractorRationales.D: That teacher is the figure the closing paragraph tells us to stop being; it is an analogue of a rejected piety, not of receiving-versus-recruiting.

passage.title: The courtesy of untranslatability
passage.body:
