Historians of language like to treat translation as a pipe: meaning enters one end, equivalent wording exits the other, and any turbulence is a defect in the plumber. The figure is flattering to publishers, who can then sell fluency as fidelity, and it is flattering to readers, who can then consume a foreign argument as if it had always been written in their kitchen. The figure is also false. A translation is not a transfer of a stable cargo. It is a series of decisions about which silences will remain audible and which will be paved over so that a page turns without snagging.

Consider the ordinary boast that a novel has been rendered into "perfectly natural" English. Natural for whom? The boast treats the target language as a climate rather than as a historically specific set of habits, class markers, and tolerated opacities. When a rural insult is recast as a metropolitan joke, or a liturgical cadence is recast as a magazine paragraph, the text has not been rescued from awkwardness. It has been enrolled in a local etiquette. The reader who thanks the translator for making the book "not feel translated" is thanking the translator for hiding the fact that hospitality occurred. Hospitality, if it is more than a smile, leaves a trace of the guest.

This is not an argument for wooden calques or for the museum of untranslated words left standing like exhibits. Those tactics can become their own piety, a performance of difficulty that congratulates the reader for enduring it. The more serious failure is the opposite one: the belief that a text which does not delay us has therefore been understood. Delay is sometimes the only honest report of a conceptual mismatch. A legal term that organizes a whole civic world cannot be swapped for a near-synonym without smuggling in the civic world of the synonym. To refuse the delay is to pretend that the two worlds already agreed.

Publishers will object that readers abandon books that snag. They are not wrong about the market. They are wrong to treat the market as a theory of meaning. A culture that will only receive what has already been made to sound like itself is not receiving; it is recruiting. The translated page then becomes a mirror with a foreign name on the title page, and the prestige of the foreign name is used to ratify what the reader already believed. That is why "accessible" can function as a political adjective. It names not a reading level but a refusal of conceptual immigration.

None of this requires contempt for the reader. It requires a different courtesy: the courtesy of letting a sentence remain slightly foreign so that the reader can notice the foreignness as information rather than as a stain. The translator's invisibility, long praised as professionalism, is in this light a kind of disappearance of evidence. We might instead want translators to be visibly responsible for their choices, not as celebrities, but as people who can be asked why a silence was kept or filled.

The practical consequence is modest and severe. Reviewers should stop treating smoothness as a synonym for accuracy. Teachers should stop treating a bilingual dictionary as a moral instrument. And readers who want to be hosts rather than consumers should learn to tolerate, even to prize, the small resistances that prove a text has not been entirely naturalized. What cannot be made to sound like us is often the part that most needed to travel.

items.stem: Nascent RNA chains isolated from a rapidly growing bacterial culture are still hydrogen-bonded to the DNA template and are also bound to ribosomes. Which conclusion fits bacterial gene expression?

choices.text: A spliceosome must finish removing introns before any ribosome can bind bacterial mRNA.
Bacterial mRNA is fully capped and exported from a nucleus before translation begins.
Transcription and translation are spatially separated, so ribosomes cannot occupy an incomplete RNA.
Ribosomes can initiate on the 5′ end of a bacterial mRNA while RNA polymerase is still elongating the 3′ end.

items.explanation: Bacteria lack a nuclear envelope, and their primary transcripts generally lack spliceosomal introns and 5′ caps of the eukaryotic type. As soon as a ribosome-binding site and start codon emerge from RNA polymerase, ribosomes can initiate. The resulting coupling of transcription and translation is observed as DNA–RNA–ribosome complexes. Eukaryotic mRNA, by contrast, is processed and exported before cytosolic translation. The experimental observation in the stem is therefore diagnostic of prokaryotic expression and is not explained by nuclear capping, spliceosome dependence, or spatial separation of the two processes.

distractorRationales.A: Bacterial protein-coding RNAs are not processed by a eukaryotic spliceosome, and ribosomes do not wait for intron removal that generally does not occur.
distractorRationales.B: Bacteria have no nucleus and do not cap and export mRNA in the eukaryotic manner; translation occurs in the same compartment as transcription.
distractorRationales.C: The isolation of ribosomes on nascent, DNA-associated RNA directly contradicts spatial separation in this organism.

items.stem: Relative rates of hydrolysis (neutral water, 25 °C) decrease in the order acetyl chloride ≫ acetic anhydride > ethyl acetate ≫ acetamide. Which analysis best explains that ranking?

choices.text: Better leaving groups and less n→π* donation into the carbonyl make the acyl carbon more electrophilic: Cl− > RCO2− > RO− > R2N−
Amides hydrolyze fastest because nitrogen is more electronegative than chlorine
Esters cannot undergo nucleophilic acyl substitution at all, so the ranking is an artifact
Acid chlorides are the least electrophilic because chlorine is a π donor as strong as NH2

items.explanation: Nucleophilic acyl substitution rate tracks two coupled effects. First, resonance donation from the heteroatom into the carbonyl (n→π*) is strongest for nitrogen, weaker for oxygen, and weakest for chlorine, so the acyl carbon of an amide is the least electrophilic. Second, the leaving group in the tetrahedral intermediate must depart: Cl− is an excellent leaving group, carboxylate is fair, alkoxide is poor, and amide anion is very poor. Those trends place acid chlorides at the top of the reactivity scale and amides at the bottom. Esters do hydrolyze, just more slowly than anhydrides and chlorides. Nitrogen is less electronegative than chlorine, not more.

distractorRationales.B: Nitrogen is less electronegative than chlorine and donates more strongly by resonance. Amides are the least, not most, reactive common carboxylic derivatives.
distractorRationales.C: Esters undergo nucleophilic acyl substitution (saponification, acid hydrolysis, transesterification); they are simply slower than anhydrides and acid chlorides.
distractorRationales.D: Chlorine is a weak resonance donor compared with NH2. Acid chlorides are the most, not least, electrophilic in this series.

items.stem: A point mutation in the Shine–Dalgarno sequence of a bacterial mRNA reduces complementarity to the 3′ end of 16S rRNA. Ribosome profiling shows fewer 30S subunits at the authentic AUG and increased use of a downstream AUG in a different frame. Which explanation is best?

choices.text: Bacteria use 5′-cap scanning as the default mechanism; the mutation merely shortens the 5′ UTR so the first AUG is skipped.
The Shine–Dalgarno sequence encodes N-formylmethionine; mutating it changes the initiator amino acid without affecting initiation frequency.

Base-pairing between the Shine–Dalgarno sequence and 16S rRNA positions the 30S subunit so that fMet-tRNA^fMet can bind the start codon in the P site; weaker pairing permits alternative AUG selection.
Elongation factor EF-G requires the Shine–Dalgarno sequence to translocate after every peptide bond, so elongation rather than initiation is primarily affected.

items.explanation: The 3′ end of 16S rRNA base-pairs with the Shine–Dalgarno motif in the 5′ UTR, docking the 30S subunit so that the start AUG occupies the P site for fMet-tRNA^fMet. Weakening that pairing reduces authentic initiation and allows 30S subunits to occupy other AUGs, including out-of-frame starts, matching the profiling result. Bacteria do not rely on eukaryotic 5′-cap scanning as the default. The Shine–Dalgarno sequence is a ribosome-binding RNA motif, not a codon for fMet. EF-G drives translocation during elongation and does not reread the initiation Shine–Dalgarno sequence at every codon.

distractorRationales.A: Cap-dependent scanning is eukaryotic; bacterial start-site selection is driven by 16S–Shine–Dalgarno pairing and initiator tRNA, not by 5′ cap recognition.
distractorRationales.B: fMet is encoded by AUG (or occasionally GUG/UUG) and is carried by tRNA^fMet; the Shine–Dalgarno sequence is not translated as fMet.
distractorRationales.D: The phenotype is altered start-codon occupancy by 30S subunits, an initiation defect, not an EF-G translocation requirement at each codon.

items.stem: Same waiting/time comments as a typical Task A set. Which opening is an argumentative thesis rather than a survey or a delay?

choices.text: There are many interesting views on waiting, and people have disagreed since the dawn of time.
Queues can be fair or unfair depending on a range of factors that this essay will now list.

Public waiting is not a neutral leftover of logistics: when a clock is owned by those who will never sit in the queue, delay becomes a way of distributing dignity, and speed for the already-served is not automatically care.
In this essay I will discuss comments 1 through 5 in order and then conclude.

items.explanation: An argumentative thesis takes an evaluable position a reader could resist. C says waiting distributes dignity, that ownership of the clock matters, and that speed is not automatically care—three contestable claims that still leave room for a counterargument about neglect. A and B refuse to land. D is a table of contents, the inventorying ACER does not reward. Task A is not a summary of the prompt. The thesis should be visible early enough that examples have a job. C is the only opening that already argues.

distractorRationales.A: A survey of eternal disagreement is a delay, not a position; “dawn of time” is also a generic inflate.
distractorRationales.B: “Depending on a range of factors” postpones the evaluation the task asks for.
distractorRationales.D: Promising to walk through comments in order is the checklist method, not a thesis.

items.stem: Two applicants have identical GPAs. The one who can talk museum internships, chamber music, and “concerted cultivation” interview banter (Lareau) is rated more “collegial” on the MMI. Bourdieu would treat that edge as which kind of resource, and to what reproductive effect?

choices.text: Marxian raw labor power only, which is identical to knowing Brahms
Davis–Moore functionalist proof that the rating is a pure scarcity rent for talent
Cultural capital: embodied tastes and institutional credentials that schools and professions reward, reproducing class advantage beyond wages
Weberian party membership in a political machine, which is the only capital Bourdieu named

items.explanation: Bourdieu distinguished economic, social, and cultural capital. Cultural capital (embodied habitus, objectified goods, institutionalized degrees) is converted into advantages in educational and professional fields, a mechanism of social reproduction. Marx’s labor power is not exhausted by high-culture fluency, though conflict theory more broadly cares about class. Davis–Moore would read unequal reward as functional for talent allocation—the view Bourdieu opposes here. Weber’s class/status/party triad is related stratification language, but “cultural capital” is Bourdieu’s term.

distractorRationales.A: Knowing Brahms is not “labor power” in Marx’s technical sense.
distractorRationales.B: The identical-GPA design is meant to show a non-merit, class-cultured bonus.
distractorRationales.D: Bourdieu named cultural (and social, economic) capital, not only party.

items.stem: A Task B draft opens with three paragraphs of warm-up (“What is belonging, really?”) and puts the only kitchen scene in the last four minutes. What is the structural diagnosis?

choices.text: The warm-up is the true close, so the kitchen should be deleted.
The piece inverts the needed order: under time, the particular scene should arrive early enough to be thought with, and the abstract question should not consume the opening rent.
The diagnosis is that Task B forbids kitchens.
The diagnosis is that thirty minutes require at least six scenes.

items.explanation: Openings that ask unanswerable What-is-X questions pay rent without furniture. The kitchen is where this paper’s thought would live; parking it in the last four minutes means the close cannot use it and the middle had nothing to develop. Structure is the management of when particularity appears. Deleting the scene would worsen the fog. Forbidding kitchens is invented. Six scenes would guarantee skimming. The fix is to start in the room and let the question arise from it. That is still an opening-development-close model, just not a philosophy-first one. B is the diagnosis a marker’s timing would reward.

distractorRationales.A: The kitchen is the asset; the warm-up is what should shrink.
distractorRationales.C: Domestic scenes are core Task B material.
distractorRationales.D: More scenes would thin attention; one or two developed moments beat a montage.

items.stem: A polar, water-soluble alkaloid has a boiling point of 255 °C at 1 atm and begins to polymerize above 190 °C. It is contaminated only with nonvolatile inorganic salts. Which purification method is most appropriate?

choices.text: Simple distillation at atmospheric pressure, because salts are nonvolatile
Fractional distillation at atmospheric pressure, because a fractionating column always prevents thermal decomposition
Steam distillation, because every high-boiling organic is carried over with water near 100 °C
Vacuum distillation, because lowering the external pressure lowers the boiling temperature below the decomposition threshold

items.explanation: A liquid boils when its vapor pressure equals the applied pressure. Reducing the pressure therefore lowers the boiling temperature (Clausius–Clapeyron), so the alkaloid can distill below 190 °C and avoid polymerization. Atmospheric simple or fractional distillation still requires the flask to reach 255 °C. Steam distillation relies on two immiscible liquids each contributing vapor pressure; a water-soluble polar alkaloid does not form that two-phase system, so steam is the wrong tool here. The nonvolatile salts remain in the pot under reduced pressure as well.

distractorRationales.A: Atmospheric simple distillation still boils the compound at 255 °C, well above the 190 °C decomposition onset.
distractorRationales.B: A fractionating column improves separation of close-boiling volatiles; it does not lower the boiling temperature of a single compound at 1 atm.
distractorRationales.C: Steam distillation is for water-immiscible high-boiling organics. A water-soluble polar alkaloid will not codistill by that mechanism.

items.stem: A student-athlete bombs a chemistry quiz in the locker room and later bricks a free throw during lecture. In a twenty-statements task, self-description after the quiz emphasizes “athlete”; after the miss it emphasizes “pre-med.” Which identity claim does this pattern best support?

choices.text: People have only one self-concept, so the shift must be a scoring error
This is demographic transition of the self from stage 2 to stage 4
Looking-glass self requires a one-way mirror, which was not present, so identity cannot change
People hold multiple social identities whose salience shifts with context, sometimes protecting self-concept after a threat to one identity

items.explanation: Self-concept is a working collection of identities (student, athlete, friend) rather than a single static list. Self-categorization and social-identity approaches predict that the identity made salient will track cues and motives, including the motive to downplay a just-threatened identity and foreground an intact one. That is compatible with the quiz-then-athlete and miss-then-pre-med switch. It is not a population fertility model, not dependent on laboratory mirrors, and not evidence that only one identity exists.

distractorRationales.A: The twenty-statements shift is evidence for multiple, context-weighted identities, not for a single frozen list.
distractorRationales.B: Demographic transition refers to national birth and death rates, not to which identity is listed first.
distractorRationales.C: Reflected appraisals can occur without a piece of glass; the stem is about identity salience, not about mirrors.

items.stem: Penicillin’s antibacterial activity depends on acylation of a serine in bacterial D-alanine transpeptidase. Ordinary unstrained amides do not acylate that serine at a useful rate. Which property of the β-lactam is most responsible?

choices.text: The β-lactam is actually an ester, and esters always outrun amides in nucleophilic acyl substitution
The four-membered ring is aromatic (4n+2), so it behaves like an acid chloride
The lactam nitrogen is so basic that it deprotonates serine before any acyl transfer
Ring strain and reduced amide resonance (the nitrogen cannot be fully coplanar with the carbonyl) make the lactam carbonyl unusually electrophilic

items.explanation: A normal amide is unreactive because the nitrogen lone pair conjugates with the carbonyl, lowering electrophilicity and making R2N− a terrible leaving group. In a fused β-lactam the four-membered ring prevents that geometry: the N–C(O) system cannot be fully planar, resonance is diminished, and opening the ring relieves angle strain. The serine hydroxyl can therefore perform nucleophilic acyl substitution, covalently inactivating the transpeptidase. The functional group remains an amide, not an ester; it is not aromatic (4 π electrons would be 4n, anti-aromatic if planar); and the chemistry is acyl transfer, not a preliminary deprotonation of serine by the lactam nitrogen as a base.

distractorRationales.A: Penicillin’s reactive carbonyl is a cyclic amide (β-lactam), not an ester. Strain, not a change of functional-group class to ester, is the key.
distractorRationales.B: Hückel aromaticity requires 4n+2 π electrons in a planar conjugated loop. A saturated β-lactam is not an aromatic ring.
distractorRationales.C: Amide nitrogens are poor bases (the lone pair is tied up, even if less so in a β-lactam). The lethal step is acylation of serine, not acid–base deprotonation.

items.stem: In the intrinsic apoptotic pathway, mitochondrial outer-membrane permeabilization allows a heme protein of the intermembrane space to enter the cytosol, where it helps assemble the apoptosome with Apaf-1 and procaspase-9. Which protein is released, and where does it normally function in respiration?

choices.text: Complex I iron–sulfur subunits, which normally reduce NAD+ in the matrix
The F1 domain of ATP synthase, which normally synthesizes ATP in the cytosol
Ubiquinone, a peripheral protein of the outer membrane that donates electrons to oxygen
Cytochrome c, which normally shuttles electrons from Complex III to Complex IV

items.explanation: Cytochrome c is a small soluble heme protein in the intermembrane space. In healthy mitochondria it carries electrons from the cytochrome bc1 complex (Complex III) to cytochrome c oxidase (Complex IV). After Bax/Bak-dependent outer-membrane permeabilization, cytosolic cytochrome c binds Apaf-1, enabling apoptosome assembly and caspase-9 activation. Complex I subunits are integral/matrix-facing and reduce ubiquinone from NADH rather than reduce NAD+. ATP is made in the matrix by inner-membrane ATP synthase, not by cytosolic F1. Ubiquinone is a lipid-soluble inner-membrane carrier, not an outer-membrane protein that reduces oxygen.

distractorRationales.A: Complex I oxidizes NADH and is not the IMS heme protein that nucleates the apoptosome. It also reduces Q, rather than reducing NAD+.
distractorRationales.B: ATP synthase is inner-membrane/matrix-facing; F1 does not synthesize ATP in the cytosol, and it is not the canonical apoptosome trigger.
distractorRationales.C: Ubiquinone is a hydrophobic inner-membrane pool, not a peripheral outer-membrane protein, and it does not reduce O2 (Complex IV does).

items.stem:
Osmolality (mOsm kg−1) along a long-looped nephron with and without ADH:

Site | with ADH | without ADH
Bowman’s capsule | 300 | 300
Hairpin of loop | 1200 | 1200
Early distal tubule | 100 | 100
Final urine | 1200 | 100

The thick ascending limb actively exports NaCl and is impermeable to water. Which statement follows?

choices.text: Without ADH the loop cannot concentrate the hairpin, because the table would then show 300 at the hairpin
ADH is required to dilute the early distal fluid to 100 mOsm kg−1
Final urine is always 1200 mOsm kg−1 in a long-looped nephron
The loop still generates a medullary gradient without ADH, but only ADH makes the collecting duct water-permeable so urine can equilibrate to 1200 mOsm kg−1

items.explanation: The hairpin is 1200 in both columns, so countercurrent multiplication does not require ADH. Early distal fluid is 100 in both columns, the signature of salt extraction without water in the ascending limb (diluting segment). The columns diverge only at the collecting duct: with ADH, water follows the medullary gradient to 1200; without ADH the duct stays impermeable and urine remains as dilute as the distal load (100). Therefore ADH gates water permeability of the collecting duct, not loop function or distal dilution.

distractorRationales.A: The hairpin is 1200 with and without ADH, so the gradient is intact.
distractorRationales.B: Early distal osmolality is already 100 in the no-ADH column, so dilution is ADH-independent.
distractorRationales.C: The no-ADH urine is 100 mOsm kg−1, so long loops do not force concentrated urine without ADH.

items.stem: A simple pendulum has length 1.0 m. Take g = 10 m s−2 so T = 2π √(L/g) = 2π √0.10. √0.10 ≈ 0.32, hence T ≈ 2.0 s. The same pendulum is taken to a planet where g' = 2.5 m s−2, and a second pendulum of length 4.0 m is left on Earth. Which period pairing is correct?

choices.text: Both remain 2.0 s, because a pendulum’s period is a universal constant
Planet: about 4.0 s; 4.0 m Earth pendulum: about 4.0 s
Planet: about 1.0 s; 4.0 m Earth pendulum: about 1.0 s
Planet: about 4.0 s; 4.0 m Earth pendulum: about 2.0 s

items.explanation: T scales as √(L/g). Reducing g from 10 to 2.5 is a factor of 1/4, so √(1/g) grows by 2 and T doubles to ~4.0 s. Lengthening L from 1.0 to 4.0 m at fixed g also multiplies T by 2, giving ~4.0 s. The two changes are therefore equivalent. If T scaled as g or as 1/L, the planet pendulum would be faster. The 4.0 m Earth pendulum is not still 2.0 s. Period is not a universal constant independent of L and g; that is why pendulums measure g.

distractorRationales.A: T = 2π√(L/g) depends on both length and gravity; neither change can be ignored.
distractorRationales.C: Weaker gravity lengthens, not shortens, T; a longer pendulum is also slower, not faster.
distractorRationales.D: The planet value is right, but √4 = 2 so the 4.0 m Earth pendulum is ~4.0 s, not ~2.0 s.

items.stem: The veteran’s sequence (hate, remain until lights, hate the insufficiency of hate) suggests an attitude of

choices.text: simple dismissal.
unwilling entanglement: the work gets under a refusal without offering a comfortable approval.
cheerful tourism.
agreement with the tourists who want someone to pity by name.

items.explanation: He hates it, stays, then hates not hating enough: that is resistance that fails to stay clean. Not dismissal, not cheer, and not the tourists’ demand for a pity-object. Speaker attitude is mixed and self-reproachful. Tone items should track the three-step interview, which the critic reports because it matches a door you cannot swagger through.

distractorRationales.A: Staying until lights and revising the hate contradicts simple dismissal.
distractorRationales.C: Hate and self-reproach are not cheer.
distractorRationales.D: He does not mention names or pity; tourists do.

passage.title: On the new memorial
passage.body:
The memorial is a corridor of rusted uprights, each the height of a person, irregularly spaced so that you must turn sideways to pass. At noon they look like a failed fence. At dusk they look like a crowd that has agreed not to face you. There are no names. A small plaque at the exit says only: THEY WERE NOT LATE. THEY WERE PREVENTED.

Tourists complain that they do not know whom to pity. School groups count the uprights and get different numbers, because some are so close they read as one. A veteran interviewed on the steps said he hated it, then stood there until the lights came on, then said he hated that he did not hate it enough.

The sculptor, in a panel discussion, refused the word healing. “If it heals,” she said, “it has failed at being a door you cannot swagger through.” Critics split between those who call this moral bullying in Cor-Ten steel and those who call the tourists’ complaint the point.

I went through twice. The second time a child asked why the fence was broken. His father said it was not a fence. The child, satisfied with a new category, ran. I was not satisfied. Prevention is a bureaucratic word. In the corridor it becomes a body insisting on its width.

items.stem: Which evaluation of Letter B's reasoning is most accurate?

choices.text: It is airtight, because any policy that mentions graduates' duties is by definition a sermon rather than an argument.
It usefully relocates staffing failure from character to conditions, but it overreaches if it treats a bond and liveable postings as mutually exclusive rather than as possibly joint instruments.
It has no empirical suggestions at all, because housing and isolation are not conditions.
It secretly agrees with Letter A that towns are a lifestyle choice doctors may decline.

items.explanation: B's strongest move is the misdiagnosis claim: empty clinics share causes with other missing staff, so a character story about the young is a convenient error. “Coercion is cheaper than housing” names a political incentive. The reasoning thins where a bond is identified with hostage-taking as such, as if furnishing rooms and some recoupment could not be combined. False dichotomy is the gap; it is not the case that B offers no conditions, nor that B accepts A's lifestyle-choice line. Evaluating strength means keeping the good causal relocation and naming the overreach.

distractorRationales.A: Calling all duty-language a sermon is itself a dismissal, not an evaluation of B's actual causal claims.
distractorRationales.C: Housing costs, school deserts, isolation, and locum markets are empirical-type conditions B explicitly lists.
distractorRationales.D: B rejects parking a resentful beginner as justice; it does not adopt A's claim that towns are a sport one may decline.

passage.title: Return-of-service bond: two letters
passage.body:
Two letters appeared in the same metropolitan daily after the health minister proposed a "return-of-service" bond: new doctors whose training was publicly subsidised would owe three years in designated underserved clinics before they could take an unrestricted urban post.

Letter A
A public scholarship is not a gift ribbon. It is a wager the public makes on a scarce skill. If the graduate then sells that skill immediately to the densest private market, the wager has been privatised without a receipt. Three years is not indenture; it is the time in which a clinic learns a name and a name learns a clinic. Those who call the bond a "mobility tax" speak as if mobility were a natural right unpolluted by the taxes that built the teaching hospitals. Rights that forget their invoices are just appetites with better stationery. Underserved towns are not a lifestyle choice the profession may decline, like a sport. They are the other half of the ledger.

Letter B
The minister has misdiagnosed a staffing failure as a character failure in the young. Clinics are empty of doctors for the same reasons they are empty of radiographers and nurses: housing costs, school deserts, professional isolation, and locum markets that pay more for a weekend than a bonded year pays for a winter. A bond does not staff a town; it parks a resentful beginner there and calls the parking "justice." Meanwhile the budget that should have made the posting liveable is spared the embarrassment of being seen. Coercion is cheaper than housing. If the public wants doctors in those rooms, it should furnish the rooms, not hostage the people it trained. A ledger that counts only the graduate's debt, and never the state's, is not a ledger. It is a sermon.

Editor's note: Letter A was signed by a retired regional physician; Letter B by a recent graduate now in a metropolitan hospital.

items.stem: A five-year-old watches juice poured from a short wide beaker into a tall thin cylinder and insists there is now “more to drink.” Piaget’s stage account attributes the error to which limitation of the preoperational period?

choices.text: Centration and irreversibility, so height is attended and the transformation cannot be mentally reversed
Failure of object permanence, as in the sensorimotor A-not-B error
Lack of hypothetical-deductive reasoning that defines the formal operational stage
An already-intact conservation operation that the child simply refuses to verbalize

items.explanation: Conservation of liquid is a concrete-operational achievement (about 7–11 years). Preoperational children (about 2–7) fail it because they center on a salient dimension (height) and cannot reverse the pour in thought. Object permanence is a sensorimotor issue in infants, not this liquid task. Formal operations concern abstract hypothesis testing in adolescence, not beaker conservation. The child’s explicit “more” is a genuine conservation failure, not a hidden competence they decline to state.

distractorRationales.B: Object permanence is a sensorimotor milestone; this is a conservation failure years later.
distractorRationales.C: Formal operations are not required for liquid conservation; concrete operations suffice.
distractorRationales.D: Piaget treats the typical five-year-old’s judgment as a real operational gap, not mere tacit knowledge.

items.stem: A school rewards sitting still, raising a hand, and deferring to the teacher’s clock more consistently than it rewards unusual scientific curiosity. Bowles and Gintis interpret this hidden curriculum as which institutional function of education?

choices.text: A purely meritocratic filter that Davis and Moore would say is unrelated to class
Correspondence with workplace authority relations, reproducing class structure through schooling as an institution
Weber’s Protestant ethic as the official math syllabus
Parsons’s sick role applied to children who sit still

items.explanation: The hidden curriculum is the unofficial lessons of school (punctuality, obedience, hierarchy). Bowles and Gintis’s correspondence principle claims those lessons mirror capitalist workplace relations and thus contribute to social reproduction. Davis–Moore functionalist meritocracy is the rival story this critique targets. Weber’s Protestant ethic is a thesis about capitalism’s cultural origins, not a math syllabus. The sick role is a medical-institution concept, not a description of classroom docility.

distractorRationales.A: Bowles and Gintis deny that school is a class-neutral merit sieve.
distractorRationales.C: The Protestant ethic is not the hidden-curriculum claim.
distractorRationales.D: Sitting still in class is not Parsons’s influenza role.

items.stem: A sleep-lab montage 12 minutes after lights-out shows 12–14 Hz bursts, occasional high-amplitude biphasic waves, mixed-frequency EEG, moderate EMG, and no rapid eye movements. Which stage of non-REM sleep, in the standard Rechtschaffen–Kales / AASM mapping, is this?

choices.text: N1, defined by vertex waves and a purely theta background without spindles
N3 slow-wave sleep, defined by high-voltage delta occupying much of the epoch
N2, defined by sleep spindles and K-complexes
REM sleep, defined by low EMG, sawtooth EEG, and bursts of rapid eye movements

items.explanation: Sleep spindles (about 12–14 Hz) and K-complexes are the defining graphoelements of N2 (formerly stage 2). N1 is light theta without those markers. N3 requires abundant delta. REM requires atonia, a wake-like low-voltage EEG, and REMs—the opposite of moderate EMG and no eye movements. Aserinsky and Kleitman described REM as a distinct state; this epoch is still non-REM N2, the stage that occupies much of a typical night after sleep onset.

distractorRationales.A: N1 lacks the spindles and K-complexes listed in the montage.
distractorRationales.B: N3 is scored on delta percentage, not on spindles as the main features.
distractorRationales.D: REM requires eye movements and atonia, both absent here.

items.stem: Two patients with the same diabetes regimen and similar household income differ in neighborhood. Patient N lives where street lighting is poor and violent crime after dark is high; accelerometer counts are low and HbA1c is higher. Patient S lives on well-lit streets with active night sports fields and has the reverse pattern. Which spatial-inequality claim is best?

choices.text: Only genetics can explain the HbA1c gap, because both patients have the same prescription
Neighborhood safety is a spatial constraint on health behavior and can therefore shape clinical outcomes
Social facilitation by potential offenders improves exercise, so N should have been more active
The difference is a looking-glass-self illusion with no behavioral pathway

items.explanation: Neighborhood safety is a standard spatial-inequality topic because the local risk of violence and the quality of public space constrain whether people walk, play, or travel for care. If two similar patients differ in those exposures, activity and a behavior-sensitive marker such as HbA1c can diverge without any change in the written regimen. Genetics-only and “illusion” accounts ignore the measured activity gap. An audience of potential offenders is not a social-facilitation helper that improves a well-learned exercise skill.

distractorRationales.A: A matched prescription does not cancel differences in whether the neighborhood makes activity feasible.
distractorRationales.C: Fear of crime reduces, rather than facilitates, outdoor activity in this design.
distractorRationales.D: Accelerometer differences are a behavioral path, not a purely reflective-appraisal illusion.

items.stem: A clean lesion of the ventral root of a spinal nerve, with the dorsal root left intact, most directly:

choices.text: blocks motor outflow in the corresponding myotome while sparing sensory inflow through that spinal level
blocks sensory inflow from the dermatome while sparing motor outflow
severs the dorsal-column nuclei in the medulla
destroys the contralateral primary motor cortex

items.explanation: Ventral roots carry efferent axons (somatic motor and some autonomic) out of the cord. Dorsal roots carry afferents in. Cutting only the ventral root therefore weakens or paralyzes the myotome while leaving sensation from the dorsal root intact (a pattern historically associated with ventral-root lesions). The lesion is peripheral to the cord and does not ablate medullary nuclei or cerebral cortex.

distractorRationales.B: This describes a dorsal-root lesion, the opposite root.
distractorRationales.C: Dorsal-column nuclei (gracile and cuneate) sit in the caudal medulla, not in a spinal ventral root.
distractorRationales.D: Motor cortex is intracranial. A spinal ventral root is a lower-motor-neuron outflow, not a cortical lesion.

items.stem: The speaker’s attitude in poem 1 toward the ferryman is best described as

choices.text: furious accusation that he should have asked.
observant, slightly chilled: he takes worn coins and does not ask, while the water does.
comic delight in overcharging.
religious awe at a miracle crossing.

items.explanation: The ferryman’s not asking is stated without insult; the water’s questions supply what the official exchange omits. Attitude is cool notice, a chill rather than a rant. Nothing comic about price appears, and no miracle. Tone is in the contrast between human unasking and hull-questions, which is dry rather than devout or enraged.

distractorRationales.A: There is no outburst; the leaving is unnamed, not prosecuted.
distractorRationales.C: Coins from other pockets suggest circulation, not a joke about fraud.
distractorRationales.D: The ticket-as-change opening is secular and slightly ironic, not hymnic.

passage.title: Two short poems: Ferry
passage.body:
Poem 1 — “Ticket”
I bought a ticket to the other bank
as if the river were a problem in change.
The ferryman took coins that had known other pockets.
He did not ask what I was leaving.
The water did, in small repeated questions
against the hull.

Poem 2 — “Return”
On the way back the same boat
was a different animal.
I recognised the coins by their edges
and not the faces.
Someone on the far jetty waved
at a person I had not yet become
and I, traitor, waved.

items.stem: A simple pendulum of length 10 m and bob mass 2 kg executes small-amplitude oscillations. Take g = 10 m/s^2. If the bob is replaced by a 4 kg bob of the same size, the period is closest to:
items.explanation: For small angles the simple-pendulum period is T = 2π sqrt(L/g), which does not depend on mass. With L = 10 m and g = 10 m/s^2, sqrt(L/g) = 1 s and T = 2π ≈ 6.3 s. Doubling the bob from 2 kg to 4 kg therefore leaves T unchanged. The result also does not depend on amplitude provided the motion stays in the small-angle regime. Omitting the 2π, using π only, or doubling T with mass are the usual errors.

distractorRationales.A: This is sqrt(L/g) with the 2π omitted, or T = 2 s from a misremembered T = 2 sqrt(L). The full factor is 2π.
distractorRationales.B: This is π sqrt(L/g) ≈ 3.1 s, missing a factor of two. The period of a simple pendulum is 2π sqrt(L/g), not π sqrt(L/g).
distractorRationales.D: This doubles 6.3 s on the (incorrect) idea that T scales with mass, or it is 4π sqrt(L/g). Mass cancels in the pendulum derivation.

items.stem: Which hypothetical is most analogous to the author’s comparison of the nineteenth-century “completing” restorer and the restorer who leaves a lacuna?

choices.text: Two translators, one smoothing a joke into local slang and one leaving a footnote that a joke depended on an untranslatable feast day; both are editing for an imagined reader.
A chemist who measures pigment and a chemist who refuses to measure because taste rules.
A thief and a conservator, because all museums are theft.
A metronome and a census box, because both are paper.

items.explanation: The author says both restorers are editors who differ in imagined audience and in how they sign the edit, not that one is science and the other ideology. Translators smoothing versus footnoting replay that structure. B reintroduces the taste mistake the last paragraph rejects. C collapses the colonial edge into a slogan the passage does not universalize. D grabs other essays’ props. Analogy items should map the relation (two edits, different audiences) rather than the topic (paint).

distractorRationales.B: The passage denies that pigment chemistry is taste and denies that all edits are equal.
distractorRationales.C: Seizure is a specific edge, not a claim that every museum act is theft.
distractorRationales.D: No such identification is made; the analogy would be empty.

passage.title: The museum as a verb
passage.body:
Conservation used to mean stopping time. A painting was a patient; varnish was a bandage; the ideal was to return the object to a single authentic hour and then prevent further hours from occurring. That ideal had a hidden historiography. It assumed the authentic hour was already known, usually as the artist’s last brushstroke, and that later repairs, soot, liturgy, and even damage were noise.

A newer conservation talk prefers verbs. To museum an object is to keep choosing which traces will remain legible. Cleaning is not the removal of history; it is the promotion of one history over another. The nineteenth-century restorer who “completed” a medieval panel was not more ideological than the twenty-first-century restorer who leaves the lacuna as a paler mute. Both are editors. They differ in which audience they imagine and in how proudly they sign the edit.

Critics of reversible methods sometimes complain that visible fills and honest seams break the spell. They want the old miracle: an untouched past that happens to hang at eye level under LEDs. The complaint is aesthetically sincere and philosophically confused. The spell was always produced with scaffolding, attributions, and lighting. Reversibility is not a refusal of beauty. It is a refusal to trap the next generation inside today’s certainty about what the object “really” was.

There is a colonial edge. Objects that arrived by seizure were often cleaned into a style that made them readable as art in the receiving capital, which is to say, cleaned of the uses that had made them un-museumlike. To restore the pigment without restoring the right of refusal is to complete the seizure in a gentler font. Some institutions now consult source communities about smoke, wear, and whether an object should be seen at all. Consultation is slow and can be theater. It is still a different verb from rescue.

If this sounds like relativism, notice what it does not say. It does not say that all edits are equal, or that pigment chemistry is a matter of taste. It says that technical competence cannot supply the missing decision about which past is being kept available. The decision will be made. Calling it science does not make it less a decision. Calling it care does not either. The more honest museum is the one that can show its verbs.

items.stem: A car’s speedometer reads 72 km h−1. Convert to m s−1 using 1 km = 1000 m and 1 h = 3600 s. A heater runs at 2.0 kW for 3.0 h. Energy in kWh is P × t, and 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10^6 J. Which pair is correct?
items.explanation: 72 km h−1 = 72 × 1000 / 3600 = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m s−1. Energy = 2.0 kW × 3.0 h = 6.0 kWh = 6.0 × 3.6×10^6 = 2.16×10^7 J. Leaving the speed as 72 mixes km/h with m/s. 6.0 J ignores the 3.6 MJ per kWh. 2.0 m s−1 would be 7.2 km/h. 6.0 × 10^3 J is 6.0 kJ, a kW·s style slip (2.0×10^3 W × 3 s) rather than 3 hours. Unit conversion is therefore two independent, both necessary, scalings.

distractorRationales.A: 72 is the km/h figure, not m/s; 6.0 kWh is millions of joules, not 6 J.
distractorRationales.B: 72 × 1/36 = 2.0 would be an arithmetic error; energy is 2.0 × 3.0 = 6.0 kWh, not 5.0.
distractorRationales.C: The 20 m s−1 is right, but 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ, so 6.0 kWh is 2.16 × 10^7 J, not 6.0 kJ.

items.stem: A synthetic analog that geometrically mimics the tetrahedral intermediate of a peptide-bond hydrolysis reaction binds a serine protease with a Kd 1000-fold lower than that of the corresponding ground-state substrate, yet the analog is not turned over. This observation is most consistent with which statement about catalysis?

choices.text: The enzyme is designed to bind substrate more tightly than the transition state, which is why chemistry is slow without analog
The analog functions as a dissociable redox cofactor that the protease reduces before each turnover
The active site is complementary to the transition state, so a transition-state mimic binds unusually tightly
Tight analog binding proves that the protease hydrolyzes peptide bonds by a radical chain mechanism

items.explanation: Pauling’s principle is that enzymes accelerate reactions by binding the transition state more tightly than the substrate, thereby lowering the activation energy. A chemically stable analog that resembles the tetrahedral intermediate therefore acts as a high-affinity inhibitor (a transition-state analog) and is not a substrate. Preferential ground-state binding would raise the barrier, the opposite of catalysis. Serine proteases are hydrolytic, not redox enzymes, and do not require a radical cofactor for this chemistry. The Kd difference is direct evidence of transition-state complementarity.

distractorRationales.A: Tighter substrate than transition-state binding would slow the reaction; enzymes do the reverse.
distractorRationales.B: A non-turned-over analog is an inhibitor, not a redox cofactor of a hydrolase.
distractorRationales.D: Serine proteases use covalent nucleophilic catalysis, not a radical chain; affinity alone does not imply radicals.

items.stem: When, if at all, is a letter form a good optional choice for Task B?

choices.text: Whenever the student is bored of paragraphs, including when the letter is only a vehicle for rhymed slogans with no thought.

When addressing an absent person (a parent, a younger self) lets the writer do work that a report could not—voice, withheld sentences, what cannot be said in the room—and the thinking remains visible.
Never; ACER automatically fails any non-essay shape.
Only if the letter is addressed to a politician with a five-point policy appendix.

items.explanation: Creative form is optional and must serve thought. A letter to an absent person can make silence and address part of the meaning, which a generic essay on “family” cannot. It fails when form is a gimmick: rhyme without a mind, a screenplay of jokes, a shape chosen from panic. ACER does not automatically fail letters; it also does not reward them as such. A politician-plus-appendix is Task A in costume. The test is whether the form is doing a job the content needs. B is the only option that states that test.

distractorRationales.A: Boredom and slogan-rhyme are gimmick, the case in which form should not be used.
distractorRationales.C: The topic is optional creative form when it serves thought; an automatic-fail rule is invented.
distractorRationales.D: A policy appendix is the wrong task’s register; it would not make the letter a good Task B.

items.stem: A coil of N = 50 turns has flux changing from 0.080 Wb to 0.020 Wb in 0.10 s. Faraday: |ε| = N |ΔΦ|/Δt. A transformer with Np = 100 and Ns = 20 is fed with 240 V rms on the primary. Vs / Vp = Ns / Np. Which pair is correct?

choices.text: Coil emf = 30 V; Vs = 240 V because transformers cannot change voltage
Coil emf = 30 V; transformer Vs = 48 V
Coil emf = 0.60 V (N omitted); Vs = 48 V
Coil emf = 30 V; Vs = 1200 V (turns ratio inverted)

items.explanation: |ΔΦ| = 0.060 Wb in 0.10 s, so |dΦ/dt| = 0.60 V per turn and N × 0.60 = 30 V. The transformer steps down by 20/100 = 1/5, so 240 × 1/5 = 48 V. Omitting N leaves 0.60 V. Inverting the turns ratio would step up to 1200 V. Transformers exist precisely to change ac voltage in the Ns/Np ratio, so Vs is not stuck at 240 V. Lenz’s minus sign sets direction, not the magnitude asked here.

distractorRationales.A: Vs = Vp × Ns/Np = 48 V; a 1:1 transformer would be needed to keep 240 V.
distractorRationales.C: Faraday multiplies by the number of turns; 50 × 0.60 V = 30 V.
distractorRationales.D: The 30 V coil figure is right, but Ns < Np is a step-down, 48 V, not a step-up to 1200 V.

items.stem: For the cartoon’s joke to land, which unstated assumption must the viewer grant?

choices.text: That a board’s true object of attention is revealed by what its listening-tool is aimed at, so aiming a stethoscope at a till means revenue outranks patients.
That children should not be allowed numbered tickets.
That cash registers are medically more accurate than stethoscopes.
That clocks without hands keep better time than clocks with hands.

items.explanation: Unstated assumptions are what must be true for the satire to mean. The image only works if aiming the earpieces is a sign of what the institution values. Without that convention, the till is just furniture. The caption’s postponement until a number becomes a priority then reads as: patients are not yet the valued object. B, C, and D are not required: the oversized ticket is scale-symbol, not a policy about children; the till is not claimed as a better diagnostic; the handless clock symbolises frozen time, not superior horology. The assumption is institutional, which is why a social waiting-room cartoon still turns on a hidden premise about attention.

distractorRationales.B: The child’s ticket is a symbol of waiting scale, not a premise that children must be ticketless.
distractorRationales.C: The cartoon does not ask us to believe tills auscultate better; it uses mis-aimed listening as irony.
distractorRationales.D: A handless clock is frozen time, not a claim about accuracy of timekeeping.

passage.title: When your number becomes a priority
passage.body:
[Image]
A waiting-room drawn as a long, low shed. The bench is actually the tubing of a giant stethoscope, coiled so that patients must sit on the instrument that is supposed to listen to them. Two figures in dark suits, labelled BOARD, wear the earpieces. They are not facing the patients. They lean together toward a cash register whose receipt paper unspools across the floor like a white carpet. The patients are drawn in broken dotted lines, as if they were still being sketched. One solid figure is a child holding a numbered ticket as tall as a door. The ticket number is 1847. A clock on the wall has no hands.

[Caption, in a polite typeface beneath the frame]
"We'll call you when your number becomes a priority."

items.stem: A clinic randomizes reminder messages about a new vaccine. Among patients who will be offered the shot this week and who score high on need for cognition, intention tracks argument quality (trial data versus anecdote) and is unaffected by whether the spokesperson wears a white coat. Among other patients, a white coat and an attractive spokesperson shift intention more than argument quality. Which factor set is illustrated?

choices.text: Target characteristics (motivation, ability) determine whether message characteristics or source characteristics dominate, as in the elaboration-likelihood model
Only source attractiveness can ever change health attitudes, so the high-involvement result is impossible
Cognitive dissonance requires a one-dollar payment, which was absent, so no attitude change can occur
Social facilitation: a white coat is an audience that always improves argument scrutiny

items.explanation: Attitude-change theories distinguish features of the message (evidence quality), the source (expertise cues, attractiveness), and the target (motivation, ability, need for cognition). ELM says those target features select the route: involved, able targets use message arguments (central) and discount superficial source cues; uninvolved targets use source cues (peripheral). The split results match that interaction. Claiming that only attractiveness works, that dissonance pay is required for any change, or that a coat is an “audience” that forces scrutiny, cannot explain both groups.

distractorRationales.B: High-involvement patients did change with argument quality; attractiveness is not the only possible lever.
distractorRationales.C: Dissonance is one attitude-change theory, not a prerequisite payment for all persuasion.
distractorRationales.D: Social facilitation concerns arousal and dominant responses in the presence of others, not white-coat heuristic cues in an ad.

items.stem:
Take c_water = 4.0 kJ kg−1 K−1. Two samples are heated 10 K:
2.0 kg of water, and 2.0 kg of aluminium (c_Al = 0.90 kJ kg−1 K−1).
Q = m c ΔT. Which heat comparison is correct?

choices.text: Aluminium requires more heat because metals feel hotter
Water requires 8.0 kJ; aluminium 18 kJ (c_water used as 0.40)
Water requires 80 kJ; aluminium requires 18 kJ
Both require 80 kJ because masses and ΔT match

items.explanation: Q_water = 2.0 × 4.0 × 10 = 80 kJ. Q_Al = 2.0 × 0.90 × 10 = 18 kJ. Specific heat, not mass or ΔT alone, distinguishes the samples: water’s large c stores more energy per kelvin. Equal mass and equal ΔT therefore do not equalise Q. Thermal conductivity (how hot metal feels) is not specific heat. Using c_water = 0.40 would undercount water by ten. The ratio 80:18 is exactly 4.0:0.90, the c ratio.

distractorRationales.A: Metals often feel hotter because they conduct, not because they have larger c; aluminium’s Q is the smaller one.
distractorRationales.B: c_water is 4.0 kJ kg−1 K−1 here, giving 80 kJ not 8.0 kJ.
distractorRationales.D: Q also contains c, which is 4.0 versus 0.90 kJ kg−1 K−1.

items.stem:
Annual energy fluxes (kJ m−2 yr−1) in a grassland:

Flux | value
Gross primary production (GPP) | 20 000
Autotrophic respiration | 10 000
Herbivore ingestion | 1 000
Herbivore respiration + faeces + urine | 900
Carnivore ingestion | 100

Net primary production NPP = GPP − autotrophic respiration. Ecological efficiency at a step is ingestion at that step divided by production at the step below. Which pair is correct?

choices.text: NPP = 10 000; herbivore efficiency 90% because 900 is respired
NPP = 9 000; carnivore efficiency 1% of GPP only
NPP = 10 000; herbivore efficiency 10%; carnivore efficiency 10% of herbivore ingestion (100/1000)
NPP = 20 000; both consumer efficiencies 50%

items.explanation: NPP = 20 000 − 10 000 = 10 000 kJ m−2 yr−1. Herbivores ingest 1000 of that 10 000, so 10% transfer into the herbivore step. Herbivore production available to carnivores is ingestion minus the 900 lost to respiration and wastes, i.e. 100, and carnivores ingest that entire 100, which is 10% of herbivore ingestion (or 100% of net herbivore production). Using GPP as NPP ignores plant respiration. Treating the 900 loss as an efficiency of 90% inverts the meaning of transfer efficiency. NPP is not 9000 on these figures.

distractorRationales.A: The 900 is energy not passed to the next trophic level; efficiency of transfer is 100/1000 or 1000/10 000, not 900/1000.
distractorRationales.B: NPP is 10 000; quoting carnivores as 1% of GPP (200) would be 200, not the 100 listed, and mixes a basal GPP denominator with a two-step climb.
distractorRationales.D: NPP is GPP minus autotrophic respiration, so 10 000 not 20 000; 1000/10 000 is 10% not 50%.

items.stem: In a Jones and Harris-style design, clerks read essays that were assigned to be pro- or anti-a hospital merger; they still rate the assigned-pro authors as personally in favor of the merger. This correspondence bias is the fundamental attribution error. Which description is correct?

choices.text: Observers overweight dispositional causes and underweight situational constraints (here, the assignment)
Actors explain their own success by the situation and their failure by traits (self-serving bias)
People always use Kelley’s high-consensus information, which forces an external attribution here
The just-world hypothesis requires that merger views be attributed to luck only

items.explanation: The fundamental attribution error (Jones and Harris’s correspondence bias) is the observer’s tendency to infer a corresponding attitude even when the writer had no choice. Situational constraint is underused. Self-serving bias is a different pattern about one’s own outcomes. Kelley’s covariation model would, with an assignment (high consensus, situational demand), point external—exactly what FAE violators fail to do. Just-world thinking is a justice motive, not this essay-constraint finding.

distractorRationales.B: Self-serving bias concerns actors’ own successes and failures, not observers of assigned essays.
distractorRationales.C: FAE is a failure to use the situational/consensus information Kelley would highlight.
distractorRationales.D: Just-world theory is not the Jones–Harris result.

items.stem: A student uses irony to say the opposite of what they feel, then never removes the mask. Why is that a problem for emotional precision, and which move would help?

choices.text: It is not a problem; irony is always more precise than naming. Help: add more sarcasm.
It is a problem because the marker cannot tell the difference between defence and thought. Help: one un-ironic clause that admits the uncool feeling the irony was protecting.
It is a problem because Task B forbids humour. Help: delete every particular.
It is a problem because feelings must be listed as bullet points. Help: format as a table.

items.explanation: Irony can be precise when it is a known distance from a named feeling. If the mask never drops, the essay may look controlled while remaining unavailable. One un-ironic clause—I was lonely; I hated needing them—gives the irony a floor. More sarcasm thickens the mask. Humour is not forbidden; fog is. Bullet-point feelings are a form, not precision. The topic is tone control, not a ban on wit. B states the diagnostic and the smallest repair that still sounds like a person. That is what thirty minutes can afford.

distractorRationales.A: Unrelieved irony is often a defence; it is not automatically more exact than a named state.
distractorRationales.C: Humour can serve precision; the failure is concealment, and deleting particulars would worsen it.
distractorRationales.D: A table of feelings is not ACER’s demand and usually kills voice.

items.stem: Skeletal muscle is forced to work under strictly anaerobic conditions. Glycolytic flux from glucose continues, and lactate accumulates. Which process most directly permits GAPDH to keep turning over?

choices.text: Faster entry of pyruvate into the TCA cycle, which oxidizes NADH in mitochondria
Lactate dehydrogenase regeneration of NAD+ by reducing pyruvate to lactate
The oxidative pentose phosphate pathway, which is the cell’s source of NAD+ for GAPDH
Oxidative phosphorylation, which is required to reoxidize NADH whenever glycolysis runs

items.explanation: GAPDH requires NAD+ each time it oxidizes glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate. Under anaerobic conditions the electron-transport chain cannot reoxidize NADH. Cytosolic lactate dehydrogenase transfers those electrons to pyruvate, producing lactate and regenerating NAD+, which is why lactate accumulates and why glycolysis can continue. Pyruvate does not enter a running TCA cycle without oxygen-dependent NADH oxidation. The pentose phosphate pathway produces NADPH, not the NAD+ pool used by GAPDH. Oxidative phosphorylation is precisely what is unavailable in the anaerobic vignette.

distractorRationales.A: Anaerobiosis prevents net TCA/ETC function; accelerating pyruvate oxidation in mitochondria is not available.
distractorRationales.C: Oxidative PPP makes NADPH and CO2; it does not supply the NAD+ that GAPDH needs.
distractorRationales.D: Oxidative phosphorylation requires oxygen; it cannot be the NAD+ source in this experiment.

items.stem: In this problem take 1 u c² = 900 MeV. A fusion sketch is 2_1H + 3_1H → 4_2He + 1_0n. Masses: 2.014 u + 3.016 u = 5.030 u on the left; 4.002 u + 1.009 u = 5.011 u on the right. What is the mass defect and the energy released?

choices.text: Defect 0; energy 0, because nucleon number 5 is conserved
Defect 0.019 u; energy ≈ 17 MeV
Defect 0.019 u; energy ≈ 0.019 MeV (c² omitted)
Defect 0.041 u (adding instead of subtracting); energy ≈ 37 MeV

items.explanation: Mass defect = 5.030 − 5.011 = 0.019 u. Energy = 0.019 × 900 ≈ 17 MeV released, because the product nuclei sit in a deeper binding well. Omitting the 900 MeV u−1 conversion leaves a meaningless 0.019 MeV. Adding the masses as a ‘defect’ double-counts. Conserving nucleon number does not conserve mass; the 0.019 u is that relativistic mass difference. Fission and fusion both release energy when products have higher binding energy per nucleon than reactants.

distractorRationales.A: A is conserved at 5, but mass is not; the 0.019 u deficit is the 17 MeV.
distractorRationales.C: Each unified mass unit corresponds to 900 MeV here, so 0.019 u is 17 MeV, not 0.019 MeV.
distractorRationales.D: Defect is left minus right, 0.019 u, not the sum 0.041 u.

items.stem: A secreted heterodimer consists of a 22 kDa chain and a 38 kDa chain joined by a single interchain disulfide. SDS-PAGE is run on identical samples with or without dithiothreitol (DTT). Which banding pattern is expected?

choices.text: Without DTT, one band near 60 kDa; with DTT, bands near 22 kDa and 38 kDa
Both gels show only 22 kDa and 38 kDa bands, because SDS oxidatively cleaves disulfides
Without DTT, bands at 22 kDa and 38 kDa; with DTT, a new 60 kDa cross-link appears
Both gels show a single 22 kDa band, because SDS equalizes all protein masses

items.explanation: SDS denatures polypeptides and coats them with a nearly uniform negative charge per mass, so mobility reports polypeptide mass, not native charge. SDS does not reduce cystine. Without DTT the covalent heterodimer remains intact and migrates near 22 + 38 = 60 kDa. DTT reduces the interchain disulfide, releasing the two chains, which then migrate at 22 kDa and 38 kDa. DTT does not create a larger cross-link, and SDS does not magically assign every protein the same mass.

distractorRationales.B: SDS is a denaturing detergent, not a reductant. Disulfides survive SDS unless a thiol such as DTT or β-mercaptoethanol is added.
distractorRationales.C: This reverses the chemistry: DTT breaks, rather than forms, disulfides. The 60 kDa species is the oxidized covalent dimer.
distractorRationales.D: SDS equalizes charge-to-mass ratio, not mass itself. Different chain lengths still separate.

items.stem: During DNA chain elongation the 3′ end of the primer attacks an incoming dNTP. Which description of the organic chemistry is correct?

choices.text: The primer 3′-OH performs nucleophilic substitution at the α-phosphate of the dNTP, releasing pyrophosphate from the β and γ phosphates
The primer 5′-OH attacks the incoming dNTP, so chains grow 3′→5′
The nucleobase of the primer displaces pyrophosphate in an SN1 reaction at carbon
The incoming dNTP’s 3′-OH attacks a 5′-monophosphate on the primer, and no pyrophosphate is released

items.explanation: DNA polymerases catalyze nucleophilic attack by the primer’s terminal 3′-hydroxyl on the α-phosphorus of a complementary dNTP. The leaving group is pyrophosphate (the β and γ phosphates), and a new 3′–5′ phosphodiester is formed. That geometry forces 5′→3′ growth. A free 5′-OH on the primer is not the nucleophile, the base is not the nucleophile, and the electrophilic site is phosphorus, not a carbon of the sugar. Hydrolysis of the released PPi by pyrophosphatase pulls the equilibrium toward polymerization.

distractorRationales.B: Primers present a 3′-OH, not a nucleophilic 5′-OH, and biological DNA synthesis is 5′→3′, not 3′→5′.
distractorRationales.C: The nucleophile is an alcohol oxygen, and the electrophilic atom is phosphorus. This is not an SN1 reaction at carbon.
distractorRationales.D: The electrophile is a triphosphate, not a primer 5′-monophosphate, and pyrophosphate is the obligatory leaving group.

items.stem:
Serum antibody titres after two injections of the same protein antigen on day 0 and day 40:

Day | IgM titre | IgG titre
0 | <10 | <10
7 | 80 | 20
14 | 40 | 160
40 (pre-boost) | 10 | 80
47 | 40 | 2560
54 | 20 | 1280

Which conclusion is best supported?

choices.text: The primary response is IgM-led and modest; the secondary response is a large, rapid IgG rise, the signature of immunological memory and class switching
IgM is the memory isotype, because it is highest on day 47
No class switch occurred, because IgM never falls to zero
The day-47 IgG titre of 2560 is a primary response to a new antigen contaminating the boost

items.explanation: After the first injection IgM appears first (80 at day 7) while IgG is still 20, then IgG overtakes (160 at day 14): primary class switching. After the day-40 boost IgG rockets to 2560 within a week while IgM only reaches 40, which is the quantitative definition of a secondary, memory, IgG-dominant response to the same antigen. IgM is not higher than IgG on day 47. Persistence of a little IgM does not deny class switch. A contaminant would not selectively inflate IgG 32-fold over the pre-boost baseline in seven days as a first exposure.

distractorRationales.B: On day 47 IgG is 2560 versus IgM 40, so IgG, not IgM, dominates the memory response.
distractorRationales.C: IgG already exceeds IgM by day 14 and explodes after the boost; that is class switching even if some IgM remains.
distractorRationales.D: A primary response to a new antigen would look like days 7–14 (modest IgM then IgG), not a 2560 IgG spike.

items.stem: The raw 2-minute count of 800 at t = 10 min (software includes background) is

choices.text: impossible, because net is 400 min−1.
consistent with about 400 net min−1 plus 12 min−1 background: (400+12)×2 ≈ 824, so 800 is a plausible rounded total.
proof background is 400 min−1.
a half-life of 2 min.

items.explanation: Expected raw ≈ (net + background) × live time = 412 × 2 = 824. A displayed 800 is within ordinary rounding, dead time, or a slightly different 2-minute window. Not impossible, not a 400 background, not a new half-life. Uncertainty and bookkeeping of gross versus net is the point; students often forget to put background back when checking an integral count.

distractorRationales.A: Gross should be net plus background times live time, about 824, so 800 is slightly low, not impossible.
distractorRationales.C: Overnight background was 12 min−1.
distractorRationales.D: Counting window length is not t½.

passage.title: Counting a short-lived sample
passage.body:
A detector records decays from a small source. Background, measured overnight with the source removed, is 12 counts per minute. The table is net rate after subtracting that background (already done by the software). Clock time starts when the sample is placed.

t / min | net counts per minute
0 | 800
5 | 566
10 | 400
15 | 283
20 | 200
25 | 141
40 | 50

The software also reports a 2-minute count at t = 10 min as 800 counts (raw, including background). A student wants the half-life from any two points and also wants activity in Bq.

items.stem: In wild-type E. coli, MutH nicks the unmethylated strand of a hemimethylated GATC near a mismatch shortly after replication. A dam-null strain lacks GATC methylation entirely and shows a strong mutator phenotype. Which mechanism best explains the increased mutation rate?

choices.text: MutH becomes hyperactive and double-nicks every GATC, killing cells that then mutate only during SOS repair of the resulting double-strand breaks.

Without a methylation mark, MutH cannot discriminate parental from daughter DNA, so mismatch repair fails to nick the correct strand or nicks randomly, allowing mutations to be fixed on either strand.
Dam methylase is the endonuclease that excises mismatches; its absence leaves MutS permanently bound and blocks all replication forks.
Unmethylated DNA cannot be transcribed, so error-prone translesion polymerases become the only remaining polymerases and mutagenize the genome uniformly.

items.explanation: Immediately after replication, GATC sites are hemimethylated: the parental strand carries Dam methylation and the daughter strand does not. MutS/MutL activate MutH to nick the unmethylated strand, directing excision to the newly synthesized DNA so that the parental sequence is used as template. In a dam-null cell both strands lack the mark, strand discrimination collapses, and mismatches are either left unrepaired or repaired using the wrong strand, producing a mutator phenotype. Dam is a methyltransferase, not the mismatch endonuclease, and unmethylated DNA is still a competent template for transcription and high-fidelity replication.

distractorRationales.A: The dam-null mutator reflects loss of strand discrimination, not obligatory lethal double-nicking at every GATC followed by SOS mutagenesis as the sole source of mutations.
distractorRationales.C: Dam methylates GATC adenines; MutH is the nicking endonuclease. Replication is not globally blocked in dam mutants.
distractorRationales.D: Transcription and replicative polymerases do not require GATC methylation; translesion polymerases are not the default genome-wide polymerase in dam-null cells.

items.stem: The passage's closing image of a busy counter most nearly suggests

choices.text: that civic routine can eclipse the demand for moral theatre
that the clerk was punished with extra work
that lost property should be privatised
that the owner was lying about the letter

items.explanation: Asked about recognition, the clerk would say the counter was busy: ordinary work refuses the test of whether virtue needs thanks. That is a cultural-critical shrug at moral theatre, not a labour-discipline plot, a policy pitch, or an accusation that the owner lied.

distractorRationales.B: Busy is the clerk's understatement, not a punishment.
distractorRationales.C: No privatisation argument is made.
distractorRationales.D: The owner collecting the purse does not make the letter a lie.

passage.title: On keeping a promise to a stranger
passage.body:
When the magistrate asked why he had returned the purse, the clerk did not say honesty. He said habit. He had been taught, in a household that measured virtue by small repetitions, that a found object remains someone else's until the world has been given a fair chance to reclaim it. The purse contained little money and a letter, unsealed, beginning: I will not be there when you arrive. He did not finish it. To finish it, he thought, would convert a duty into a story, and stories have a way of making the finder important.

Philosophers like to treat this as a puzzle about property and knowledge. If he does not know the owner, is the duty weaker? If the letter would have saved a marriage, does withholding it become a harm? The clerk would have found the questions indecent. He was not refusing knowledge so much as refusing a role. The city had clerks for lost property; it did not have clerks for other people's farewells.

A later commentator, writing after the clerk was dead, praised him as a Kantian saint: he acted from a maxim he could will as universal. The praise is too clean. The clerk's maxim was local and slightly ashamed. He did not want to be the man who had read the letter. Shame, not universality, kept his eyes off the page. That is not a lesser ethics. It is an ethics that knows how quickly curiosity dresses itself as concern.

The owner collected the purse the next morning and did not thank him. In the commentary this becomes a test of whether virtue needs recognition. The clerk, if asked, would have said only that the counter was busy.

items.stem: (2R,3R)-2,3-dibromobutane and (2R,3S)-2,3-dibromobutane are compared. Which statement about their physical properties is correct?

choices.text: They are enantiomers, so they have identical melting points and identical magnitudes of optical rotation.
They are constitutional isomers, so they have different atom connectivities.
They are identical (the same compound), so every physical constant matches.
They are diastereomers, so they can have different melting points, boiling points, and dipole moments; only the chiral (2R,3R) isomer is optically active.

items.explanation: Both compounds share the same connectivity (2,3-dibromobutane) but differ at only one of two stereocenters, so they are diastereomers. Diastereomers are different compounds: they pack differently in crystals and have different intermolecular interactions, hence different melting points, boiling points, and often different dipole moments. The (2R,3S) isomer of this symmetric molecule is meso and optically inactive, while (2R,3R) is chiral. Enantiomers would require opposite configuration at every stereocenter, as in (2R,3R) versus (2S,3S). The connectivity is the same, so they are not constitutional isomers.

distractorRationales.A: Enantiomers differ at every stereocenter. These two differ at only one center (and one is meso), so they are diastereomers, not enantiomers.
distractorRationales.B: Constitutional isomers differ in connectivity (for example 1,2- versus 2,3-dibromobutane). Both structures here are 2,3-dibromobutane.
distractorRationales.C: Different CIP labels at C3 mean they are not the same compound.

items.stem: When the author says the manuals “are not cynical,” the rhetorical effect is to

choices.text: excuse every checkpoint outcome as good intentions.
grant the anti-cruelty aim so the critique can move to grammar, audition, and service-sounding politics rather than to cartoon villainy.
mock trainers for believing in smiles.
argue that raised voices are the only remaining problem.

items.explanation: The concession isolates what courtesy can do (prevent a raised voice) from what it cannot (change who must be plausible). That is a tone of precision, not sarcasm at trainers and not a blanket excuse. D is the limited prevention the manuals achieve, which the author says is not the deeper problem. Rhetoric questions should hear why a concession is placed early: to retire the easy target.

distractorRationales.A: The rest of the essay criticizes audition, expanding emergency powers, and service-sounding politics.
distractorRationales.C: The manuals are granted a non-cynical aim; the author is not sneering at smiles as such.
distractorRationales.D: Raised voices are the obvious cruelty the manuals address; the essay’s subject is the grammar underneath.

passage.title: Courtesy at the checkpoint
passage.body:
A border official is trained in courtesy as if courtesy were a disinfectant. Smile, use the family name, apologize for the wait. The training manuals are not cynical. They are trying to prevent the obvious cruelty of a raised voice. What they cannot prevent is the deeper grammar of the encounter: one person may leave, the other must persuade a stranger that her life is plausible.

Liberal theory likes to treat this grammar as an unfortunate delay on the way to a principle. In the principle, the stranger is already a rights-bearer; the checkpoint is a bureaucratic remainder. On the ground, the remainder is the event. Rights that must be performed as a story—complete, sequential, tearful at the approved moments—are rights as an audition. The official who says “help me to help you” is not necessarily a villain. He is naming the price of entry into a language that pretends it is only asking for facts.

Scholars of hospitality distinguish welcome from inspection. The distinction is cleaner on the page than in a queue. Inspection can dress as welcome, and welcome can become inspection the moment a detail fails to match a database. A cup of tea in an interview room is not the opposite of a file. It can be the file’s most efficient instrument, loosening speech until it can be contradicted.

None of this requires pretending that states have no legitimate interest in knowing who crosses. It requires noticing that “legitimate interest” is not a measuring cup. It expands. Yesterday’s emergency power is today’s ordinary form. Tomorrow’s form will be justified by the person who told her story too well, or too badly, last year. The archive of interviews becomes a training set for suspicion.

The courteous checkpoint is therefore not a milder politics. It is a politics that has learned to sound like a service. If we want a different politics, we will need a different distribution of who must be plausible to whom—not a warmer script for the same audition.

items.stem: A chief resident is expected, in that single status, to be both a rapid discharger of patients and an unrushed listener. Separately, the same person is on call as resident while also being the parent of a febrile toddler. Goode’s and Merton’s role vocabulary would label those two tensions how?

choices.text: Both are role exit, because she is leaving medicine
Both are master-status racial ascription, which is the only role term Merton used
Both are primary-group bonds in Cooley’s sense, which abolish roles
In-role incompatible demands are role strain; conflict between resident and parent statuses is role conflict

items.explanation: Role strain is tension among expectations attached to one status (the resident torn between speed and listening). Role conflict is tension between two statuses (resident vs parent). Role exit is leaving a status, not described here. A master status is a dominating identity (race, disability, occupation in some settings), not the name of these two tensions. Cooley’s primary groups are intimate, enduring associations; they do not erase role analysis.

distractorRationales.A: Nothing in the stem describes leaving the profession.
distractorRationales.B: Master status is not Merton’s term for strain versus conflict.
distractorRationales.C: Primary groups do not make role strain/conflict unstatable.

items.stem: A perception lab shows three black “Pac-man” inducers whose mouths face inward. Most observers report a bright white triangle with sharp edges covering the gaps, even though no triangle is drawn. Which Gestalt principle, associated with Wertheimer’s grouping laws, most directly names this completion?

choices.text: Closure (and Prägnanz), because the visual system completes a simple enclosed form from incomplete contours
Common fate, because the Pac-men appear to move as one flock
Absolute threshold, because the triangle is a real luminance increment at detection threshold
Place theory, because each inducer maps to a different cochlear position

items.explanation: The Kanizsa triangle is a textbook illusory-contour display. Gestalt psychologists (Wertheimer, later Kanizsa) argued that perception organizes toward simple, closed, good forms (Prägnanz) and fills gaps (closure). No physical triangular luminance edge is required. Common fate groups by shared motion, which is not presented. Absolute threshold concerns detecting a weak real stimulus. Place theory is auditory frequency mapping and does not explain visual illusory contours.

distractorRationales.B: Common fate requires common motion; the stem is a static grouping display.
distractorRationales.C: The triangle is constructed, not a near-threshold physical luminance patch.
distractorRationales.D: Place theory is a cochlear map, unrelated to visual contour completion.

items.stem: In a four-stage demographic-transition teaching model, a country’s crude death rate falls from 30 to 12 per 1,000 over two decades while the birth rate remains near 38. Population grows rapidly. Which stage is this, and what typically drives the death-rate drop?

choices.text: Stage 2: mortality falls first (sanitation, nutrition, basic medicine) while fertility stays high
Stage 1: both rates still high, so growth remains near zero
Stage 3: fertility has already fallen to match mortality
Stage 4: both rates are low and the boom is over

items.explanation: In the standard four-stage demographic transition, stage 1 has high birth and death rates. Stage 2 is the mortality decline—public health, food, and infectious-disease control—while fertility remains high, producing explosive growth. Stage 3 is the later fertility decline. Stage 4 is low-low with slower growth. Five-stage variants add a possible stage-5 below-replacement fertility; they do not relocate the first mortality drop out of the early-transition boom described here.

distractorRationales.B: Stage 1 would not show a collapsed death rate with a still-high birth rate.
distractorRationales.C: Stage 3 is when births fall, which has not yet happened in the stem.
distractorRationales.D: Stage 4 is low fertility and low mortality, not a 38 birth rate.
