items.stem: Which statement about computer-based S2 typing is most accurate as craft advice?

choices.text: Spelling will be invisibly corrected, so muddy thinking will look precise.
You should spend the first ten minutes designing an elaborate outline with numbered subsections you will not have time to fill.
Assume little rescue from later proofreading: prefer one claim per sentence, read a paragraph back once for dropped words, and do not chase ornamental vocabulary you cannot spell under pulse.
Type with your eyes closed to simulate authenticity.

items.explanation: The craft topic is clarity under timed typing, including sentence control without treating spellcheck as a substitute for thought. Whether a given sitting offers light correction or none, ornamental words you cannot securely type will cost you. One claim per sentence is a hedge against dropped subjects and lost verbs. A giant outline that is never filled is a common computer-exam failure. Eye-closed typing is a joke, not a method. The accurate advice is modest: readable units, one pass for missing words, vocabulary you can actually produce. C states that. It is retrieval of how the task works, not a request to write the essay here.

distractorRationales.A: Relying on invisible correction to launder unclear thought is exactly the false comfort this topic warns against.
distractorRationales.B: Over-outlining is a time thief; structure should be light enough to fill.
distractorRationales.D: Authenticity is not produced by not looking at the screen.

items.stem: Free aspartic acid (pKa ≈ 2.0, 3.9, and 9.9) is loaded onto a cation-exchange resin, which bears immobilized negative charges, in a pH 7.0 buffer. The amino acid flows through without binding. Which explanation is best?

choices.text: At pH 7 aspartate has a net negative charge and is electrostatically repelled by the resin
At pH 7 aspartate is a zwitterion of net charge zero and therefore has no ionic interaction with the resin
At pH 7 aspartate is net positive and binds so tightly that it cannot be loaded onto the column in the first place
Cation-exchange resins bind amino acids only through aromatic stacking, and aspartate lacks an aromatic ring

items.explanation: At pH 7 both carboxyl groups of aspartate (α-carboxyl pKa ~2 and side-chain pKa ~4) are deprotonated, while the α-amino group (pKa ~10) remains protonated, giving a net charge of −1. A cation exchanger presents negative charges intended to bind cations. A net-negative solute is repelled and appears in the flow-through. Aspartate’s isoelectric point is acidic (average of the two carboxyl pKa values, near 3), so pH 7 is well above the pI and the anion predominates. Cation-exchange chromatography is electrostatic, not aromatic stacking.

distractorRationales.B: The net-zero form of aspartate exists near pH 3, not at pH 7, where the net charge is −1.
distractorRationales.C: A net-positive aspartate would require pH below the pI; at pH 7 the residue is anionic, not tightly bound.
distractorRationales.D: Cation exchangers separate by charge. Aromatic stacking is not the binding mode of a sulfonate or carboxylate resin.

items.stem: A premature neonate produces insufficient pulmonary surfactant. Alveolar surface tension remains high. Which set of mechanical consequences is expected?

choices.text: High surface tension, alveolar collapse (atelectasis), and decreased lung compliance, raising the work of inflation
Increased compliance so that small alveoli overexpand while large ones empty
A higher FEV1/FVC ratio as the primary surfactant deficiency phenotype, identical to asthma
A right shift of the hemoglobin-O2 curve as surfactant’s main chemical role

items.explanation: Surfactant, largely dipalmitoyl phosphatidylcholine from type II pneumocytes, lowers alveolar surface tension gamma. Laplace's relation P = 2 gamma / r says that without that reduction, small alveoli generate large collapsing pressures, empty into larger ones, and the lung becomes stiff (low compliance). Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome is the clinical picture: atelectasis and high work of breathing. Asthma is an obstructive FEV1/FVC fall, not a surfactant-deficient restrictive pattern. Surfactant is not a hemoglobin allosteric effector. Compliance falls, it does not rise.

distractorRationales.B: High tension decreases compliance and promotes collapse of small alveoli, the opposite of easy overexpansion.
distractorRationales.C: Surfactant deficiency is restrictive physiology, not an asthma-like obstructive ratio increase as the core lesion.
distractorRationales.D: The O2 dissociation curve is not controlled by alveolar surfactant lipids.

items.stem: In a Baddeley working-memory clinic task, repeating “the, the, the” aloud (articulatory suppression) abolishes the phonological-similarity effect for visually presented letter strings, while Corsi block span is unchanged. Which component was occupied, and which was spared?

choices.text: The phonological loop (articulatory rehearsal) was occupied; the visuospatial sketchpad was spared
The visuospatial sketchpad was occupied; the phonological loop was spared
Long-term episodic memory was occupied, which is why Corsi span survived
Sensory iconic memory was occupied, which is the only store Baddeley named

items.explanation: Baddeley’s multicomponent model assigns verbal rehearsal to the phonological loop. Articulatory suppression fills that rehearsal process, removing phonological confusions among letters. Corsi blocks load the visuospatial sketchpad and the central executive’s spatial control, so they should survive a purely verbal suppressor. Long-term episodic memory is not the working-memory buffer under test. Iconic memory is a brief sensory register in the older modal model, not the named Baddeley loop.

distractorRationales.B: The suppressor is verbal; it loads the loop, not the sketchpad.
distractorRationales.C: Corsi span is a working-memory spatial index, not proof that long-term memory was the occupied store.
distractorRationales.D: Baddeley’s model is loop, sketchpad, central executive (and later episodic buffer), not iconic memory alone.

items.stem:
Halogen data:

Element | covalent radius (pm) | IE1 (kJ mol−1) | electron affinity (kJ mol−1, exothermic as negative)
F | 64 | 1680 | −328
Cl | 99 | 1255 | −349
Br | 114 | 1140 | −325

Electron affinity here is the enthalpy of X(g) + e− → X−(g). Which reading is supported?

choices.text: F has the most exothermic EA because it has the highest IE1
Br is the smallest halogen, which is why its IE1 is lowest
EA becomes steadily more exothermic from F to Br as radius increases
Radius and ease of removing an electron both increase down the group, but Cl has the most exothermic EA because F’s compact 2p shell raises electron–electron repulsion in F−

items.explanation: Covalent radius increases 64 → 99 → 114 pm and IE1 falls 1680 → 1255 → 1140, the standard down-group weakening of attraction to valence electrons. Electron affinity, however, is most negative for Cl (−349), not F (−328): adding an electron to tiny F crowding a 2p subshell is less favourable than adding to Cl. EA is therefore not a monotone function of IE1 or of radius. Br is the largest listed atom, not the smallest, which is why its IE1 is the lowest of the three.

distractorRationales.A: F’s EA is −328, less exothermic than Cl’s −349, so the highest IE1 does not produce the most exothermic EA.
distractorRationales.B: Br’s radius 114 pm is the largest in the table.
distractorRationales.C: EA goes −328, −349, −325, a peak at Cl, not a steady trend toward Br.

items.stem: A premed still endorses the cultural goal of a physician’s income and prestige but, facing a bottleneck of seats, begins selling stolen exam banks. In Merton’s strain (anomie) typology, this adaptation is which cell?

choices.text: Innovation: accepting the cultural goal while rejecting legitimate means
Ritualism: rejecting the goal while clinging to legitimate means (endless MCAT retakes with no career aim)
Retreatism: rejecting both goals and means (dropping out into isolation)
Rebellion: substituting a new goal–means pair (founding an alternative school)

items.explanation: Merton’s strain theory says anomie arises when culturally approved goals (here, professional success) are not matched by equally available legitimate means. Innovation keeps the goal and uses illegitimate means—the stolen banks. Ritualism is going through the motions without the goal. Retreatism abandons both. Rebellion replaces both with a new set. Conformity, the fifth cell, would keep both goals and legal means. Durkheim’s broader anomie idea is the parent of this typology, but the named cells are Merton’s.

distractorRationales.B: Ritualism drops the success goal; this student still wants the prestige.
distractorRationales.C: Retreatism would abandon the career goal, not cheat toward it.
distractorRationales.D: Rebellion would try to change the goal–means framework, not privately cheat within it.

items.stem: A labeled mRNA is transcribed in a cultured eukaryotic cell, then nuclear-pore export of that mRNA is blocked. The most likely observation is that:

choices.text: translation of that mRNA increases in the cytosol
the mRNA remains nuclear and protein produced from that mRNA falls
the mRNA is imported into mitochondria and translated on mitochondrial ribosomes
cytosolic ribosomes enter the nucleus and translate the mRNA on chromatin

items.explanation: Eukaryotic mRNA must exit through nuclear pores to meet cytosolic ribosomes. Blocking export traps the transcript in the nucleus, so cytosolic translation of that message falls. Mitochondria do not import random nuclear mRNAs for translation, and cytosolic ribosomes do not routinely enter the nucleoplasm to translate chromatin-associated mRNA. Increased cytosolic translation would require successful export, the step that was blocked.

distractorRationales.A: Without export, cytosolic ribosomes never see the mRNA, so translation of it cannot increase.
distractorRationales.C: Mitochondrial translation is reserved for the mitochondrial genome's own RNAs, not stranded nuclear mRNAs.
distractorRationales.D: Translation of nuclear-encoded mRNA is cytosolic. Pore blockade does not relocate the ribosome machinery onto DNA.

items.stem:
A 900-nucleotide coding sequence (300 amino acids, no introns) is mutated. Experimental readouts:

Mutant | DNA change | mRNA length | protein
W | TGG at codon 80 → TGA | 900 nt | 79 amino acids
X | TGG at codon 80 → TGC | 900 nt | 300 amino acids, one residue different
Y | +1 bp insertion in codon 10 | 901 nt | 18 amino acids
Z | promoter −10 box ATATAA → GGATCC | none detected | none

TGG = Trp, TGA = stop, TGC = Cys. Which assignment is correct?

choices.text: W deletion of the gene; X silent; Y inversion; Z RNA editing
W nonsense; X missense; Y frameshift to a premature stop; Z promoter loss of transcription
W missense; X nonsense; Y silent; Z frameshift
W splice defect; X conservative substitution only if Cys equals Trp; Y promoter mutation; Z missense

items.explanation: TGG → TGA converts Trp to stop at codon 80, truncating translation after 79 residues while leaving a full-length mRNA: nonsense. TGG → TGC is Trp → Cys with a 300-residue protein: missense. A +1 insertion near codon 10 scrambles the reading frame and typically hits a stop soon after (here at residue 18) with an mRNA one nucleotide longer: frameshift. Destroying the −10 promoter box abolishes transcription, so no mRNA and no protein. The table does not show splicing (no introns), gene deletion, or RNA editing.

distractorRationales.A: W still produces 900 nt mRNA so the gene is present; X changes an amino acid; Y is an insertion; Z is transcriptional failure.
distractorRationales.C: W creates a stop, not a missense change; X is Cys not a stop; Y is not silent; Z is not a frameshift in coding DNA.
distractorRationales.D: There are no introns, so W is not splicing; Cys ≠ Trp so X is a real missense; Y is coding-sequence insertion; Z is not missense.

items.stem: Okonkwo's sociological point about the census is that it

choices.text: already selects which details may represent a life, leaving other household facts unasked
should be abolished in favour of poetry
accurately records the age of stairs
is written by kettles

items.explanation: She says a census already poetizes by deciding what may stand for a life and what remains unasked. That is a sociological claim about classification. She does not abolish counts, and the poem's joke is that stairs are not asked their age — the census does not record that.

distractorRationales.B: She says the poem is not anti-data.
distractorRationales.C: The poem notes that nobody asked the stairs their age.
distractorRationales.D: The kettle is a proxy image, not an author.

passage.title: Two ways of hearing a census
passage.body:
Poem (untitled, 2019)

We counted rooms as if rooms were people.
The spare one kept its coat on.
In the column for language we wrote the kettle.
Nobody asked the stairs their age.

Commentary by L. Okonkwo, catalogue essay for an exhibition of household inventories:
The poem is easy to misread as anti-data. It is not. It notices that a census already poetizes: it decides what may stand for a life (rooms, language, age) and what must remain downstairs, unasked. The coat on the spare room is not a joke about furniture. It is a figure for surplus — the part of a household that official forms cannot rent. When the poem puts a kettle in the language column, it is not claiming kettles speak. It is showing how quickly a form will accept a proxy if the proxy is small and warm.

A table printed beside the poem in the gallery listed visitors by hour and by whether they photographed the stairs:
Hour 10: 14 visitors, 2 photographed stairs
Hour 11: 31 visitors, 18 photographed stairs
Hour 12: 9 visitors, 0 photographed stairs (docent talk in progress)
The curator captioned the table: Attention is not the same as attendance.

A radio host later called the exhibition “political because it made a kettle into a citizen.” Okonkwo's essay had already refused that flattening. The political cut, for her, is not enfranchising objects. It is noticing which human details a state is willing to miss.

items.stem:
Clearance C = U V / P, with U urine concentration, V urine flow, P plasma concentration. Simultaneous measurements:

Marker | P | U | V
Inulin | 4.0 mg L−1 | 200 mg L−1 | 2.0 mL min−1
PAH | 2.0 mg L−1 | 1000 mg L−1 | 2.0 mL min−1

Inulin clearance estimates GFR. PAH clearance estimates effective renal plasma flow. What are GFR, RPF, and filtration fraction GFR/RPF?

choices.text: GFR 50 mL min−1; RPF 500 mL min−1; FF 0.10
GFR 100 mL min−1; RPF 200 mL min−1; FF 0.50
GFR 100 mL min−1; RPF 1000 mL min−1; FF 0.10
GFR 1000 mL min−1; RPF 100 mL min−1; FF 10

items.explanation: Convert V to 0.0020 L min−1. Inulin: C = 200 × 0.0020 / 4.0 = 0.40 / 4.0 = 0.10 L min−1 = 100 mL min−1. PAH: C = 1000 × 0.0020 / 2.0 = 2.0 / 2.0 = 1.0 L min−1 = 1000 mL min−1. Filtration fraction = 100/1000 = 0.10. Swapping the two clearances inverts FF to an impossible 10. Halving both would require using V = 1.0 mL min−1. Using U/P without V for PAH gives 500, not 1000 mL min−1, and 200 mL min−1 would be a typical RBF mis-scale.

distractorRationales.A: Those values would follow if V were taken as 1.0 mL min−1 instead of 2.0.
distractorRationales.B: RPF 200 mL min−1 underuses the PAH U/P ratio of 500 together with the 2 mL min−1 flow.
distractorRationales.D: That pair swaps inulin and PAH clearances and makes FF = 10, which cannot be a fraction of plasma filtered.

items.stem:
The slope of a velocity–time graph is acceleration. A cart’s v–t record is:

Interval | v(t)
0.0 to 3.0 s | v decreases linearly from 12.0 m s−1 to 0
3.0 to 5.0 s | v = 0 (at rest)
5.0 to 8.0 s | v increases linearly from 0 to 6.0 m s−1

What is the acceleration in the interval 0.0–3.0 s?

choices.text: 0 m s−2

items.explanation: Acceleration is Δv/Δt. From 12.0 m s−1 to 0 in 3.0 s, a = (0 − 12.0)/3.0 = −4.0 m s−2. The negative sign means the velocity is decreasing (the cart is slowing while still moving in the original positive direction). Zero acceleration applies to the 3–5 s rest interval, not to 0–3 s. The later +2.0 m s−2 is (6.0 − 0)/3.0 for 5–8 s. Dropping the sign and quoting +4.0 m s−2 reports the magnitude of the first interval’s acceleration but not the signed kinematic value asked for.

distractorRationales.B: Zero slope occurs only while the cart is at rest (3–5 s). The 0–3 s segment has a clear negative slope.
distractorRationales.C: +2.0 m s−2 is the slope of the 5–8 s segment, not of 0–3 s.
distractorRationales.D: +4.0 m s−2 is the magnitude of the first interval’s acceleration with the sign omitted. Velocity is decreasing, so a is negative.

items.stem: A conducting rod of length ℓ = 0.20 m slides at 4.0 m s−1 on rails in B = 0.50 T, B perpendicular to the area. Motional emf ε = B ℓ v. The circuit resistance is 2.0 Ω. Induced current I = ε/R. The magnetic drag is F = B I ℓ. What are ε, I, and F?

choices.text: ε = 0.40 V; I = 0.20 A; F = 0.020 N opposing the motion (Lenz)
ε = 0.40 V; I = 0.20 A; F = 0, because magnetic fields do no work
ε = 0.40 V; I = 2.0 A (R omitted as 0.20 Ω); F = 0.20 N

items.explanation: ε = 0.50 × 0.20 × 4.0 = 0.40 V. I = 0.40/2.0 = 0.20 A. F = 0.50 × 0.20 × 0.20 = 0.020 N. Lenz’s law requires that force to oppose the change in flux, i.e. to drag against the imposed velocity, so a pulling agent must do mechanical work that becomes I²R heat. ‘Magnetic fields do no work’ refers to F·v on individual charges in the B field, not to the external agent. Dropping a factor of 10 in Bℓv gives 4.0 V. Using R = 0.20 Ω instead of 2.0 Ω inflates I tenfold.

distractorRationales.B: The 0.40 V and 0.20 A are right, but the current-carrying rod in B feels 0.020 N opposing the motion; the hand pulling the rod does the work.
distractorRationales.C: ε = Bℓv = 0.40 V, not 4.0 V; the later I and F scale from that error.
distractorRationales.D: R is 2.0 Ω, so I = 0.20 A not 2.0 A; F then is 0.020 N.

items.stem: Oxidation numbers in Cr2O7 2− + 3 SO2 + 2 H+ → 2 Cr3+ + 3 SO4 2− + H2O are assigned with O as −2 and H as +1. In Cr2O7 2− each Cr is +6; in SO2 each S is +4; in SO4 2− each S is +6; Cr3+ is +3. How many electrons are transferred per dichromate ion, and which species is the oxidising agent?

choices.text: Three electrons; SO2 is the oxidising agent
Six electrons; SO2 is the oxidising agent because sulfur’s number rises
Zero electrons; oxidation numbers are book-keeping only and no transfer occurs
Six electrons; Cr2O7 2− is the oxidising agent (each of two Cr gains three electrons)

items.explanation: Each chromium falls from +6 to +3, a gain of three electrons, and two chromium atoms per dichromate give six electrons gained. Those six electrons come from three SO2 molecules, each sulfur rising from +4 to +6 (loss of two electrons each). The species that is reduced (Cr2O7 2−) is the oxidising agent. SO2 is oxidised, so it is the reducing agent. Three electrons would count only one chromium. The balanced equation exists precisely because electrons are transferred; the oxidation numbers track that transfer.

distractorRationales.A: Three electrons counts a single Cr; the formula has two. SO2 is oxidised, not reduced.
distractorRationales.B: Six electrons is the right count, but the oxidising agent is the dichromate that accepts them, not the sulfur that loses them.
distractorRationales.C: A change of six in the chromium oxidation-number total is the definition of a six-electron redox process.

items.stem: A smoking-cessation trial finds that baseline self-efficacy, number of smoking friends, and cigarettes remaining in the house each predict lapse. A lapse then lowers self-efficacy and increases time spent with smoking friends. Which social-cognitive claim does this pattern illustrate?

choices.text: One-way environmental determinism: only the house and friends cause behavior
Central-route persuasion by printed nicotine facts
Reciprocal determinism: person (cognition), behavior, and environment continuously influence one another
General adaptation syndrome exhaustion as the only pathway to a lapse

items.explanation: Social cognitive theory’s reciprocal determinism says personal factors (beliefs such as self-efficacy), behavior (smoking or abstinence), and environment (cues, peers, available cigarettes) are ongoing causes of one another rather than a one-way chain. The trial’s bidirectional links—cognition and setting predict lapse, and lapse then reshapes cognition and setting—are that loop. A purely environmental account drops self-efficacy. ELM is about message routes, not this triad. GAS exhaustion is a stress-physiology sequence, not the SCT model of health-behavior change.

distractorRationales.A: Self-efficacy is a personal cognition that also predicts lapse, so environment is not the sole cause.
distractorRationales.B: No message-elaboration manipulation is described.
distractorRationales.D: A lapse can have many proximal causes in SCT; exhaustion is not required and is not what the measured loop shows.

items.stem: A protease isolated from a mammalian pancreas hydrolyzes peptides composed of L-amino acids with a measured kcat/Km of 2×10^5 M−1 s−1. A chemist synthesizes the identical sequence using only D-amino acids and incubates it with the same enzyme under otherwise identical buffer, pH, and temperature. Which outcome is most likely, and why?

choices.text: Little or no cleavage, because the active site is stereospecific for the L configuration at Cα
Faster cleavage, because D-residues experience less steric hindrance at the scissile bond
Uncatalyzed hydrolysis in water that is faster for D-peptides than for L-peptides, so the enzyme is unnecessary
The enzyme first racemizes each D-residue to L and then cleaves at the usual rate

items.explanation: Mammalian digestive proteases evolved to recognize L-amino acids, the configuration found in ribosomally synthesized proteins. The active-site pockets and catalytic residues present a chiral environment that orients the scissile peptide bond of an L-substrate for nucleophilic attack. A D-peptide is the mirror image and generally cannot make the same contacts, so kcat/Km collapses. Peptide bonds of D- and L-peptides have essentially the same intrinsic chemical stability in water, and proteases do not racemize residues before cleavage. Therefore the D-peptide remains largely intact.

distractorRationales.B: Steric bulk is not systematically lower for D-residues; the issue is mismatched chirality, not a smaller side chain.
distractorRationales.C: Uncatalyzed peptide hydrolysis is extremely slow for both configurations; D-peptides are not intrinsically labile.
distractorRationales.D: Proteases catalyze hydrolysis of peptide bonds; they do not invert Cα configuration as a prerequisite to cleavage.

items.stem: Inside-out plasma-membrane vesicles are given ATP on the ATPase side of the Na+/K+ pump. In 1.00 min the vesicles hydrolyse 3.0 nmol ATP and catalyse net movement of 9.0 nmol Na+ outward and 6.0 nmol K+ inward. Ouabain, a pump blocker, reduces ATP hydrolysis and both ion fluxes to ≤0.2 nmol. Which stoichiometry matches the measurements?

choices.text: 1 Na+ and 1 K+ moved per ATP, because 9 and 6 are both larger than 3.
2 Na+ out and 3 K+ in per ATP (the ratios 9/3 and 6/3 reversed).
3 Na+ out and 2 K+ in per ATP hydrolysed.
The ions diffuse independently of ATP, because 9, 6, and 3 are different numbers.

items.explanation: Dividing the ion fluxes by ATP hydrolysed gives 9.0/3.0 = 3 Na+ and 6.0/3.0 = 2 K+ per ATP. That is the textbook Na+/K+ ATPase stoichiometry and it is electrogenic (net +1 charge out). Ouabain collapsing all three measurements together shows the fluxes are pump-coupled, not independent leaks. Unequal Na and K counts are required by the 3:2 mechanism; they do not imply 1:1 cycling or a reversed 2:3 pump.

distractorRationales.A: 9/3 = 3 and 6/3 = 2, not 1 and 1; being larger than 3 nmol does not set the ratio to 1.
distractorRationales.B: That swaps the measured 3 Na : 2 K ratio.
distractorRationales.D: Ouabain zeros ATP hydrolysis and both ion movements together, so the fluxes are pump-dependent.

items.stem: In the sentence that calls “accessible” a political adjective naming “a refusal of conceptual immigration,” the phrase conceptual immigration most nearly means

choices.text: the physical relocation of translators across national borders as a labor-market fact.
the entry of distinctions and civic worlds that have not already been recast to sound like the host language's habits.
the use of immigration statutes as a plot device inside the novels being translated.
a reader's duty to memorize untranslated legal terms as if they were visa documents.

items.explanation: The surrounding contrast is receiving versus recruiting: a culture that will only take what already sounds like itself is not receiving. “Accessible” is said to name not a reading level but a refusal of conceptual immigration, so the metaphor is about ideas and civic worlds crossing into a language without being fully naturalized. It is not about translators' passports, novelistic plots about immigration law, or a homework program of memorizing terms. The phrase's meaning is fixed by the recruiting/receiving antithesis and by the legal-term example of smuggled civic worlds.

distractorRationales.A: The passage's immigration figure is conceptual, not a claim about translators as migrant workers.
distractorRationales.C: No argument is made about immigration law as subject matter inside fiction; the civic world belongs to the legal term being translated.
distractorRationales.D: Teachers are warned against treating dictionaries as moral instruments; the author does not redefine immigration as a memorization duty.

passage.title: The courtesy of untranslatability
passage.body:
Historians of language like to treat translation as a pipe: meaning enters one end, equivalent wording exits the other, and any turbulence is a defect in the plumber. The figure is flattering to publishers, who can then sell fluency as fidelity, and it is flattering to readers, who can then consume a foreign argument as if it had always been written in their kitchen. The figure is also false. A translation is not a transfer of a stable cargo. It is a series of decisions about which silences will remain audible and which will be paved over so that a page turns without snagging.

Consider the ordinary boast that a novel has been rendered into "perfectly natural" English. Natural for whom? The boast treats the target language as a climate rather than as a historically specific set of habits, class markers, and tolerated opacities. When a rural insult is recast as a metropolitan joke, or a liturgical cadence is recast as a magazine paragraph, the text has not been rescued from awkwardness. It has been enrolled in a local etiquette. The reader who thanks the translator for making the book "not feel translated" is thanking the translator for hiding the fact that hospitality occurred. Hospitality, if it is more than a smile, leaves a trace of the guest.

This is not an argument for wooden calques or for the museum of untranslated words left standing like exhibits. Those tactics can become their own piety, a performance of difficulty that congratulates the reader for enduring it. The more serious failure is the opposite one: the belief that a text which does not delay us has therefore been understood. Delay is sometimes the only honest report of a conceptual mismatch. A legal term that organizes a whole civic world cannot be swapped for a near-synonym without smuggling in the civic world of the synonym. To refuse the delay is to pretend that the two worlds already agreed.

Publishers will object that readers abandon books that snag. They are not wrong about the market. They are wrong to treat the market as a theory of meaning. A culture that will only receive what has already been made to sound like itself is not receiving; it is recruiting. The translated page then becomes a mirror with a foreign name on the title page, and the prestige of the foreign name is used to ratify what the reader already believed. That is why "accessible" can function as a political adjective. It names not a reading level but a refusal of conceptual immigration.

None of this requires contempt for the reader. It requires a different courtesy: the courtesy of letting a sentence remain slightly foreign so that the reader can notice the foreignness as information rather than as a stain. The translator's invisibility, long praised as professionalism, is in this light a kind of disappearance of evidence. We might instead want translators to be visibly responsible for their choices, not as celebrities, but as people who can be asked why a silence was kept or filled.

The practical consequence is modest and severe. Reviewers should stop treating smoothness as a synonym for accuracy. Teachers should stop treating a bilingual dictionary as a moral instrument. And readers who want to be hosts rather than consumers should learn to tolerate, even to prize, the small resistances that prove a text has not been entirely naturalized. What cannot be made to sound like us is often the part that most needed to travel.

items.stem: A winch pulls a crate horizontally at a constant 2 m/s. The tension in the cable is a constant 10 N. The instantaneous mechanical power delivered by the tension is:

choices.text: 0 W, because kinetic energy is not changing
5 W

items.explanation: Instantaneous power delivered by a force is P = F · v = F v when force and velocity are parallel. Here P = (10 N)(2 m/s) = 20 W. Constant speed means the net force on the crate is zero, so friction (or another opposing force) cancels the 10 N and net work is zero, but the tension still does positive work at rate F v. The opposing force does an equal negative work, which is why KE stays constant. Over any 1 s interval the tension does 20 J of work, which is 20 W of power from that one force.

distractorRationales.A: Zero net work (and unchanging KE) does not mean every force delivers zero power. Tension does +20 W; the opposing force does −20 W.
distractorRationales.B: This is F/v = 10/2. Power is the product F v, not the quotient; N/(m/s) is not a watt.
distractorRationales.D: This is 2 F v, perhaps inserting a leftover 2 from (1/2) m v^2. That factor does not belong in P = F v.

items.stem: Taken together, cartoon and letter most nearly comment on

choices.text: how public language of coping and valued time can coexist with private ranking of bodies, and how critics of the picture may protect that language.
the need to ban letters pages.
horticulture in clinics.
why gold frames improve health outcomes.

items.explanation: The cartoon shows valued-time rhetoric against triage that asks who can sit, unmatched private times, and a coping caption. The letter defends staff by restoring a manners explanation. Together they sketch a political argument about whose time counts and how dissent is moralised as ingratitude. B, C, and D shrink to props or censorship. Social-argument items should stay at the level of public language versus ranking, which both texts stage.

distractorRationales.B: The pairing uses the letter; it does not campaign against letters pages.
distractorRationales.C: The fake plant is a satirical prop, not a gardening thesis.
distractorRationales.D: Gold is ostentation against cracked glass, not an outcomes claim.

passage.title: Cartoon: Clinic time
passage.body:
A single-panel cartoon, unsigned, published on a letters page.

Foreground: a waiting-room bench. Four people sit. Above each head a small clock; the hands are at 1:10, 2:40, 4:15, and 9:50. None of the clocks match the large wall clock, which has no hands.

On the wall, a framed motto: WE VALUE YOUR TIME. The frame is gold. The glass is cracked.

To the right, a receptionist window. The receptionist smiles with many teeth and holds a clipboard titled TRIAGE (PRIVATE). On the clipboard the only visible line is: “Can they still sit up?” A potted plant on the sill is fake; its price tag remains.

Under the bench, a fifth clock, face-down.

Caption, in small type: “The system is coping.”

A letter printed beneath, from “Concerned, Upper Shore”: “Cartoons like this undermine dedicated staff. If people arrived on time and did not bring relatives, clocks would match.”

items.stem:
Haemoglobin–oxygen saturation on two dissociation curves at the same PO2 values:

PO2 (mmHg) | sat % at P50 = 26 mmHg | sat % at P50 = 32 mmHg (low pH / high 2,3-BPG)
100 | 97 | 95
40 | 75 | 60
26 | 50 | 38

Venous muscle PO2 is 40 mmHg; arterial PO2 is 100 mmHg. Which statement about oxygen unloading is supported?

choices.text: The right shift prevents unloading because saturation at 40 mmHg is lower
Arterial saturation falling from 97% to 95% is the main physiological effect of a P50 increase
P50 is the PO2 at 100% saturation, so 26 mmHg already represents full loading
The right-shifted curve unloads more O2 in tissue (35 percentage points versus 22) with little change in arterial loading

items.explanation: Unloading is arterial minus venous saturation. For P50 = 26 mmHg: 97 − 75 = 22 points. For P50 = 32 mmHg: 95 − 60 = 35 points. The Bohr/2,3-BPG right shift therefore delivers more oxygen at a venous PO2 of 40 mmHg, while arterial loading at 100 mmHg barely changes (97 vs 95). Lower venous saturation means more, not less, unloading. P50 is the PO2 at 50% saturation by definition, not at 100%.

distractorRationales.A: A lower saturation at 40 mmHg is exactly greater unloading if arterial saturation remains near 95–97%.
distractorRationales.B: The 2-point arterial change is trivial beside the 15-point extra venous desaturation.
distractorRationales.C: The table itself shows 50% saturation at 26 mmHg on the first curve; that is the definition of P50.

items.stem: Developing mouse paws treated with a pan-caspase inhibitor retain interdigital webbing that normally regresses before birth. DNA from the untreated interdigital mesenchyme shows internucleosomal ladders. The morphogenetic process that was blocked is:

choices.text: Mitotic expansion of ectoderm that physically pushes digits apart
Ossification of the radius, which secondarily erases webbing
Programmed cell death (apoptosis) of interdigital mesenchymal cells
Fertilization of residual polar bodies in the limb bud

items.explanation: Digit separation in mice depends on apoptosis of the interdigital mesenchyme. Caspases execute that program; inhibiting them leaves a bat-like web. Internucleosomal DNA cleavage (ladders) is a biochemical hallmark of apoptosis, distinct from random necrotic smears. The process is spatially patterned death, not a requirement that ectoderm outgrow the web or that the radius ossify to cut the tissue. Polar-body fertilization is unrelated to limb morphogenesis. Comparative anatomy (webbed duck feet have less interdigital apoptosis) is the same mechanism in another species.

distractorRationales.A: Digits are sculpted by death of cells between them, not by mitotic wedging alone.
distractorRationales.B: Radius ossification does not explain caspase-sensitive webbing or DNA ladders in the mesenchyme.
distractorRationales.D: Polar bodies are meiotic products in the ovary/zygote, not limb-bud cells.

items.stem:
Four nuclides are listed as (Z, A):
P: (17, 35); Q: (17, 37); R: (18, 37); S: (16, 32).
Isotopes are nuclides with the same proton number Z and different mass number A. Neutron number is A − Z.
Which pair are isotopes of the same element?

choices.text: Q and R, because both have A = 37
P and R, because neutron numbers are 18 and 19, nearly equal
P and Q, because both have Z = 17
R and S, because 18 − 16 = 37 − 32

items.explanation: Z is the proton count and defines the element. P and Q both have Z = 17, with A = 35 and 37, so they are isotopes (17 protons; neutrons 18 and 20). Q and R share A = 37 but differ in Z (17 vs 18); those are isobars, not isotopes. Nearly equal neutron numbers do not make P and R the same element (Z = 17 vs 18). An accidental equality of two differences for R and S is not the isotope definition.

distractorRationales.A: Same A and different Z are isobars (here 37Cl and 37Ar), not isotopes.
distractorRationales.B: P has 18 neutrons and R has 19, but Z differs (17 vs 18), so they are different elements.
distractorRationales.D: Subtracting Z and A between two nuclides is not a test for isotopes; R and S have different Z and A.

items.stem: A 400-Da fluorescent tracer is added to the apical bath of a polarized MDCK monolayer. In wild-type cultures the tracer remains apical for hours. Monolayers lacking claudin-1 allow the tracer to appear in the basolateral compartment within minutes without any drop in transcellular transporter activity. The missing epithelial structure is the:

choices.text: Gap junction plaque, whose connexin channels normally seal the paracellular route
Hemidesmosome, which is the only barrier to small solutes between apical and basolateral baths
Tight junction (zonula occludens), whose claudin strands form the paracellular seal
Focal adhesion, which occludes the lateral intercellular space at the apical pole

items.explanation: Polarized epithelia separate apical and basolateral compartments with tight junctions. Claudins polymerize into anastomosing strands that limit paracellular flux of small solutes; losing claudin-1 opens that shunt so an apical tracer reaches the basolateral bath. Gap junctions (connexins) couple the interiors of adjacent cells and do not form the apical seal. Hemidesmosomes and focal adhesions attach cells to the basement membrane or matrix and are not the permeability barrier between apical and basolateral media. Unchanged transcellular transport shows the leak is paracellular, not a collapse of pumps and channels.

distractorRationales.A: Connexin channels permit ion and metabolite exchange between cytoplasms; they do not occlude the paracellular path.
distractorRationales.B: Hemidesmosomes link basal keratin to laminin in the basement membrane and are not the apical paracellular gate.
distractorRationales.D: Focal adhesions are integrin-based matrix contacts, typically basal, and do not create the epithelial tight seal.

items.stem:
Isometric tetanic tension of a skeletal fibre versus sarcomere length (relative tension, 100 = plateau):

Length (µm) | tension (%)
1.5 | 55
2.0 | 100
2.2 | 100
2.6 | 80
3.6 | 0

Thick filaments are 1.6 µm; thin filaments from each Z-line are 1.0 µm; the H-zone has no thin-filament overlap. Which mechanical interpretation fits?

choices.text: The plateau at 2.0–2.2 µm means no cross-bridges attach in that range
Tension at 1.5 µm is low because thin filaments have detached from Z-lines
3.6 µm is zero overlap so zero force; 2.0–2.2 µm is optimal overlap; 1.5 µm is excessive overlap that impairs force
Force is maximum at 3.6 µm because cross-bridges have the most room to swing

items.explanation: At 3.6 µm a 1.6 µm thick filament plus two 1.0 µm thin filaments end-to-end span 3.6 µm, so overlap—and force—is zero, matching the table. The 2.0–2.2 µm plateau is the region of constant maximal overlap of cross-bridge zones. At 1.5 µm opposite thin filaments crash into each other and thick filaments hit Z-lines, reducing force to 55%, not because Z-line attachments are lost. Maximum force is therefore at intermediate, not extreme stretched, length. The plateau is maximal attachment, not zero attachment.

distractorRationales.A: 100% tension on the plateau is the maximum number of active bridges, not zero.
distractorRationales.B: Thin filaments remain anchored at Z-lines; force falls at short length because of double overlap and compression, as the 1.5 µm row shows residual 55% tension.
distractorRationales.D: The 3.6 µm row is 0% tension; there is no overlap for cross-bridges to swing on.

items.stem: In guinea pigs, black (B) is dominant to brown (b) and rough coat (R) is dominant to smooth (r). The loci assort independently. A dihybrid BbRr is crossed to another BbRr. Among 160 offspring, how many are expected to be black and smooth (B_ rr), and what fraction of all offspring are brown and rough (bb R_)?

choices.text: 10 black-smooth; 1/16 brown-rough
40 black-smooth; 1/4 brown-rough
30 black-smooth; 1/16 brown-rough
30 black-smooth; 3/16 brown-rough

items.explanation: Independent assortment gives 9:3:3:1 among the four phenotypic classes of a double heterozygote self-cross. Black-smooth is B_ rr = (3/4)×(1/4) = 3/16, and 3/16 × 160 = 30. Brown-rough is bb R_ = (1/4)×(3/4) = 3/16, not 1/16 (that is bb rr) and not 1/4 (that is a single recessive class). Ten would be 1/16 of 160. Forty would be 1/4 of 160, the combined recessive-at-one-locus count if the other locus were ignored incorrectly.

distractorRationales.A: 10 is 1/16 × 160, the double-recessive class, not B_ rr.
distractorRationales.B: 40 is 1/4 × 160, which would be all smooth coats regardless of colour, not the black-smooth subset.
distractorRationales.C: The headcount 30 is right, but brown-rough is 3/16, not the 1/16 double recessive.

items.stem: Glycogen and cellulose are both homopolymers of D-glucose. Glycogen is readily mobilized by glycogen phosphorylase in animals; cellulose is not digested by human enzymes and forms rigid fibrils. Which chemical difference is most responsible?

choices.text: Cellulose uses α-1,6 branches every 8–12 residues; glycogen is an unbranched β-1,4 polymer.
Cellulose is composed of galactose, the C4 epimer of glucose; glycogen uses glucose, so only glycogen matches phosphorylase specificity.

Glycogen has α-1,4 chains with α-1,6 branches, producing a helical, hydrated polymer with many nonreducing ends; cellulose has β-1,4 linkages that form straight, hydrogen-bonded sheets resistant to human amylases and phosphorylase.
The two polymers are chemically identical; only the organism of origin determines whether human enzymes can hydrolyze them.

items.explanation: Glycosidic stereochemistry dictates polymer conformation and enzyme specificity. α-1,4 linkages in glycogen curve the chain into a hydrated helix, and α-1,6 branches create many nonreducing ends for phosphorylase. β-1,4 linkages in cellulose produce extended chains that hydrogen-bond into fibrils; human amylases and glycogen phosphorylase do not hydrolyze β-1,4 glucans. Both polymers are poly-D-glucose, not galactose. Branching is a glycogen feature, not a cellulose feature, and digestibility is a chemical-recognition issue rather than a mere label of plant versus animal origin.

distractorRationales.A: This swaps the architectures: glycogen is the branched α polymer; cellulose is unbranched β-1,4.
distractorRationales.B: Cellulose is a glucose homopolymer; galactose is not the repeating unit, and C4 epimerization is not the glycogen/cellulose distinction.
distractorRationales.D: The polymers differ in anomeric configuration and branching; those chemical differences, not the source organism alone, explain enzyme resistance.

items.stem: Which paraphrase of “stories have a way of making the finder important” best fits the passage?

choices.text: Narrating a found letter tends to centre the finder rather than the owner
Fiction is more legally binding than lost-property rules
The clerk wanted celebrity for returning the purse
All letters in purses are fictional

items.explanation: The clerk stops reading because finishing the letter would convert a duty into a story that makes the finder important. The paraphrase must keep that shift from anonymous duty to self-centred narrative. He is not seeking celebrity; he is avoiding a role. Legal ranking of fiction and a claim that the letters are fake are not in the text.

distractorRationales.B: No comparison of fiction to law is made.
distractorRationales.C: He refuses the story that would make him important.
distractorRationales.D: The letter is treated as real correspondence, not a fiction.

passage.title: On keeping a promise to a stranger
passage.body:
When the magistrate asked why he had returned the purse, the clerk did not say honesty. He said habit. He had been taught, in a household that measured virtue by small repetitions, that a found object remains someone else's until the world has been given a fair chance to reclaim it. The purse contained little money and a letter, unsealed, beginning: I will not be there when you arrive. He did not finish it. To finish it, he thought, would convert a duty into a story, and stories have a way of making the finder important.

Philosophers like to treat this as a puzzle about property and knowledge. If he does not know the owner, is the duty weaker? If the letter would have saved a marriage, does withholding it become a harm? The clerk would have found the questions indecent. He was not refusing knowledge so much as refusing a role. The city had clerks for lost property; it did not have clerks for other people's farewells.

A later commentator, writing after the clerk was dead, praised him as a Kantian saint: he acted from a maxim he could will as universal. The praise is too clean. The clerk's maxim was local and slightly ashamed. He did not want to be the man who had read the letter. Shame, not universality, kept his eyes off the page. That is not a lesser ethics. It is an ethics that knows how quickly curiosity dresses itself as concern.

The owner collected the purse the next morning and did not thank him. In the commentary this becomes a test of whether virtue needs recognition. The clerk, if asked, would have said only that the counter was busy.

items.stem: Which of the following is the conclusion Letter A is principally trying to establish, as distinct from a supporting move?

choices.text: Teaching hospitals were built with public money.
Some critics use the phrase “mobility tax.”
The proposed three-year bond is a legitimate completion of a public wager rather than indenture, because underserved towns are the other half of the ledger.
Private urban posts exist and pay.

items.explanation: Letter A piles reasons—scholarship as wager, names learned in clinics, invoices behind mobility, towns as ledger not lifestyle—toward a verdict on the bond: it is not indenture but the public's due. Teaching-hospital funding, the critics' phrase, and the existence of private posts are materials in that case, not the destination. Distinguishing conclusion from support means asking what would still need proving if those facts were granted. A wants the reader to accept the bond as just recoupment. That evaluative landing is C.

distractorRationales.A: Public building of teaching hospitals is offered as an invoice behind mobility, a premise, not the letter's landing claim.
distractorRationales.B: Naming the opposing slogan is a setup for rebuttal, not A's own conclusion.
distractorRationales.D: Urban private markets are the scene of the alleged privatised wager, a circumstance, not what A is trying to prove.

passage.title: Return-of-service bond: two letters
passage.body:
Two letters appeared in the same metropolitan daily after the health minister proposed a "return-of-service" bond: new doctors whose training was publicly subsidised would owe three years in designated underserved clinics before they could take an unrestricted urban post.

Letter A
A public scholarship is not a gift ribbon. It is a wager the public makes on a scarce skill. If the graduate then sells that skill immediately to the densest private market, the wager has been privatised without a receipt. Three years is not indenture; it is the time in which a clinic learns a name and a name learns a clinic. Those who call the bond a "mobility tax" speak as if mobility were a natural right unpolluted by the taxes that built the teaching hospitals. Rights that forget their invoices are just appetites with better stationery. Underserved towns are not a lifestyle choice the profession may decline, like a sport. They are the other half of the ledger.

Letter B
The minister has misdiagnosed a staffing failure as a character failure in the young. Clinics are empty of doctors for the same reasons they are empty of radiographers and nurses: housing costs, school deserts, professional isolation, and locum markets that pay more for a weekend than a bonded year pays for a winter. A bond does not staff a town; it parks a resentful beginner there and calls the parking "justice." Meanwhile the budget that should have made the posting liveable is spared the embarrassment of being seen. Coercion is cheaper than housing. If the public wants doctors in those rooms, it should furnish the rooms, not hostage the people it trained. A ledger that counts only the graduate's debt, and never the state's, is not a ledger. It is a sermon.

Editor's note: Letter A was signed by a retired regional physician; Letter B by a recent graduate now in a metropolitan hospital.

items.stem: A T-even bacteriophage is grown so that its DNA is labeled with 32P and its capsid protein with 35S. After adsorption to bacteria and shear that strips empty coats, 32P is recovered in the bacterial pellet while 35S remains in the supernatant. The structural implication is that:

choices.text: Capsid protein is injected as the genetic material and DNA remains outside
The phage envelope fuses with the bacterial plasma membrane, mixing 35S into the cytoplasm
The nucleic acid genome enters the cell while the protein capsid stays outside, so DNA, not protein, is the injected hereditary material
Both labels enter equally because the entire virion is taken up by phagocytosis

items.explanation: Tailed bacteriophages are nucleoprotein particles: DNA (or sometimes RNA) is condensed inside a protein capsid, and a tail apparatus punctures the envelope to inject the genome. 32P traces nucleic acid into the cell; 35S traces methionine/cysteine in coat protein that remains extracellular after blending. That partition shows the capsid is a delivery device, not the hereditary substance. Typical T-even phages are non-enveloped and are not taken up whole by bacterial phagocytosis. Protein staying outside is the opposite of protein-as-gene.

distractorRationales.A: The pellet is 32P-rich and the supernatant 35S-rich, which is DNA in and protein out, not the reverse.
distractorRationales.B: T-even phages are naked; fusion of a lipid envelope is not how they deliver DNA, and 35S did not enter.
distractorRationales.D: Bacteria do not phagocytose intact T-even virions in this protocol; the labels separate.

items.stem: A chemist measures the specific rotation of enantiopure (R)-2-butanol as −13.9°. A second sample of 2-butanol is prepared as a 1:1 mixture of the R and S enantiomers. What optical rotation is expected for the second sample under the same conditions?
items.explanation: Enantiomers rotate plane-polarized light by equal magnitudes in opposite directions. In a racemate the two enantiomers are present in equal concentration, so the rotations cancel and the observed rotation is zero. The mixture is not optically active even though each molecule is chiral. The −13.9° value is the rotation of the pure R enantiomer; the S enantiomer would read +13.9°; doubling to −27.8° has no physical basis. Optical purity (ee) of zero is the defining optical property of a racemic mixture.

distractorRationales.A: That is the rotation of enantiopure (R)-2-butanol, not of a racemate.
distractorRationales.B: That would be the rotation of enantiopure (S)-2-butanol, not of an equal mixture.
distractorRationales.D: Rotations of enantiomers cancel rather than add; a racemate does not double the magnitude.

items.stem: An ethereal solution contains equimolar benzoic acid (pKa ≈ 4.2), 4-methylphenol (pKa ≈ 10.3), and naphthalene. The solution is shaken with saturated aqueous NaHCO3 and the layers are separated. Which species is found predominantly in the aqueous layer?

choices.text: Sodium benzoate, because bicarbonate is basic enough to deprotonate the carboxylic acid but not the phenol
Sodium 4-methylphenolate, because phenols are stronger acids than carboxylic acids
Naphthalene, because it is the least polar and therefore prefers water
All three solutes, because NaHCO3 is a general organic-soluble detergent

items.explanation: Aqueous bicarbonate is a weak base whose conjugate acid (carbonic acid) has pKa near 6.4. Proton transfer HA + HCO3− ⇌ A− + H2CO3 is favorable only when pKa(HA) is below that value. Benzoic acid meets that criterion and is extracted as water-soluble benzoate. 4-Methylphenol (pKa ≈ 10) is not deprotonated by bicarbonate and remains in ether, as does non-ionizable naphthalene. The complementary extraction of the phenol requires a stronger base such as NaOH. Carboxylic acids are stronger acids than phenols, not the reverse.

distractorRationales.B: Phenols are weaker acids than carboxylic acids (pKa ~10 vs ~4–5). Bicarbonate does not generate phenolate in useful amounts.
distractorRationales.C: Naphthalene is a nonpolar hydrocarbon and partitions into ether, not into aqueous bicarbonate.
distractorRationales.D: Bicarbonate is not a detergent that solubilizes all organics; it ionizes only sufficiently acidic solutes.

items.stem: Ksp(PbCl2) = 1.6 × 10−5 = [Pb2+][Cl−]2. Equal volumes of 0.20 M Pb(NO3)2 and 0.20 M HCl are mixed, so immediately after mixing, before any precipitation, [Pb2+] = 0.10 M and [Cl−] = 0.10 M. The reaction quotient Q = [Pb2+][Cl−]2. Does PbCl2 precipitate?

choices.text: No; Q = 0 because solids have activity 1
Yes; Q = 1.0 × 10−3, which exceeds Ksp = 1.6 × 10−5
No; Q = 1.0 × 10−3, which is less than Ksp
Yes; Q = 0.10, set equal to [Pb2+] alone

items.explanation: After equal-volume mixing both ions are 0.10 M, so Q = (0.10)(0.10)2 = 0.10 × 0.010 = 1.0 × 10−3. Ksp is 1.6 × 10−5, and 1.0 × 10−3 > 1.6 × 10−5, so the solution is supersaturated and PbCl2 precipitates. Q is not smaller than Ksp. Omitting the square on chloride gives 0.010, still > Ksp, but the listed distractor 0.10 ignores chloride entirely. Q for the dissolved ions is not zero; the solid’s activity is 1 only once the solid is present at equilibrium, which is the state the comparison is testing for.

distractorRationales.A: Q is computed from the ion concentrations before precipitation; it is 1.0 × 10−3, not 0.
distractorRationales.C: 1.0 × 10−3 is larger than 1.6 × 10−5, so the inequality predicts precipitation.
distractorRationales.D: Q must include [Cl−]2; using [Pb2+] alone is not the Ksp expression.

items.stem: A lineage tracer injected into a single cell of embryonic ectoderm after gastrulation later labels spinal-cord neurons and epidermal keratinocytes but never cardiomyocytes, skeletal muscle, or hepatocytes. The labeled clone was restricted to:

choices.text: Mesoderm, which produces epidermis and the neural tube
Endoderm, which produces the entire central nervous system
Ectoderm, which generates both surface epidermis and neuroectoderm
Trophectoderm only, which forms the embryo proper rather than extraembryonic tissues

items.explanation: After gastrulation the three germ layers are allocated. Ectoderm produces the epidermis and, after neural induction, the neural plate/tube (CNS neurons). Mesoderm produces heart, skeletal muscle, and many internal supporting tissues; endoderm produces hepatocytes and gut epithelium. A clone that marks epidermis plus spinal neurons and excludes heart and liver is therefore ectodermal. Trophectoderm is extraembryonic (placenta) and is not the source of the embryo proper's neurons. Mixing up which organs come from which layer is the usual error.

distractorRationales.A: Mesoderm makes muscle and heart, not epidermis and CNS neurons.
distractorRationales.B: Endoderm makes gut-derived viscera such as liver, not the neural tube.
distractorRationales.D: Trophectoderm is extraembryonic; it does not produce spinal neurons or epidermis of the embryo proper.

items.stem: 2,4-Dinitrophenol is added to mitochondria that had been synthesizing ATP from ADP + Pi while oxidizing succinate. Which set of immediate effects is expected?

choices.text: The proton gradient increases, ATP synthesis rises, and oxygen consumption falls.
ATP synthesis rises because protons enter more rapidly through ATP synthase.
Oxygen consumption falls to zero because Complex IV is inhibited by DNP.
The proton-motive force collapses, ATP synthesis falls, and oxygen consumption increases as electron transport is uncoupled from phosphorylation.

items.explanation: 2,4-Dinitrophenol is a protonophore: it shuttles protons across the inner membrane, dissipating ΔpH and Δψ. ATP synthase requires that proton-motive force, so ATP synthesis falls even though ADP and Pi are present. With the back-pressure of the gradient gone, electron transport accelerates and oxygen consumption rises; energy is released as heat rather than captured as ATP. DNP does not inhibit cytochrome oxidase, and it does not route extra protons through F0 in a way that increases ATP. The same pattern is seen with UCP1 in brown adipose tissue, a physiologic uncoupler.

distractorRationales.A: Uncouplers decrease, not increase, the proton gradient. ATP synthesis therefore falls while respiration typically speeds up, opposite this choice.
distractorRationales.B: Protons re-enter through the uncoupler, not productively through ATP synthase, so phosphorylation decreases rather than rises.
distractorRationales.C: DNP does not block Complex IV. Oxygen consumption increases because electron flow is no longer limited by the proton gradient.

items.stem: Standard reduction potentials: NAD+ / NADH, E°′ = −0.32 V; a typical enzyme-bound FAD / FADH2, E°′ = 0.00 V; ½ O2 / H2O, E°′ = +0.82 V. Using ΔG°′ = −nFΔE°′ with n = 2, which statement follows for oxidation of the two carriers by O2?

choices.text: FADH2 oxidation is more exergonic because its E°′ is closer to that of oxygen
The two oxidations have identical ΔG°′ because both ultimately reduce O2
NADH cannot reduce oxygen because its potential is negative
NADH oxidation has the larger ΔE°′ (1.14 V vs 0.82 V) and therefore the more negative ΔG°′, consistent with NADH electrons entering the chain at a higher-energy (more reducing) level than FADH2

items.explanation: Electrons flow from the more negative to the more positive couple. For NADH to O2, ΔE°′ = 0.82 − (−0.32) = 1.14 V. For FADH2 to O2, ΔE°′ = 0.82 − 0.00 = 0.82 V. Because ΔG°′ = −nFΔE°′, the larger ΔE°′ makes NADH oxidation more exergonic. That extra free energy is why NADH feeds Complex I and supports more proton pumping than FADH2, which enters at Complex II. A negative E°′ for NAD+/NADH means NADH is a strong reductant, not that it is forbidden from reducing oxygen through the chain. Sharing O2 as the terminal acceptor does not equalize ΔE°′.

distractorRationales.A: A smaller gap to oxygen means a smaller ΔE°′ and a less negative ΔG°′. FADH2 is the lower-energy reductant.
distractorRationales.B: The donor potentials differ, so ΔE°′ and ΔG°′ differ even though both paths end at O2.
distractorRationales.C: A negative E°′ identifies a good reductant. NADH reduces the chain, and ultimately oxygen, with a large positive ΔE°′.

items.stem: Using the uninhibited V_max in Table 1 and the active-site titration result, k_cat of the dehydrogenase is closest to
items.explanation: Turnover number is V_max expressed per mole of catalytic sites. Table 1 lists uninhibited V_max as 80 nmol of product per second per milligram of protein. The passage states that active-site titration found 4.0 nmol of catalytic sites per milligram, so k_cat = 80 nmol s^{-1} mg^{-1} divided by 4.0 nmol mg^{-1} = 20 s^{-1}. The milligram units cancel, and the result does not use the inhibitor rows. Treating the V_max number as already a first-order rate constant, multiplying by the site titer, or inverting the ratio all ignore one of the two experimental numbers the passage supplies.

distractorRationales.A: 80 s^{-1} copies the V_max magnitude while dropping the site-titer division; V_max in nmol s^{-1} mg^{-1} is not k_cat until it is normalized per site.
distractorRationales.C: 320 s^{-1} multiplies V_max by the 4.0 nmol mg^{-1} titer instead of dividing, which has the wrong dimensions for a first-order rate constant.
distractorRationales.D: 0.050 s^{-1} is the inverted ratio 4.0/80; that construction does not convert a specific activity into a turnover number.

passage.title: Reversible inhibitors of a cytosolic dehydrogenase
passage.body:
Investigators purified a cytosolic NAD+-dependent dehydrogenase that oxidizes a small-molecule metabolite S. Initial velocities were measured at 25 °C by following NADH formation in 1.00 mL assays. Nonlinear fits of v versus [S] produced the apparent Michaelis constants and maximal velocities in Table 1. When an inhibitor was present, its concentration was 2.0 μM in the assay mix. Dialysis that removed unbound compound restored full catalytic activity after incubation with P, Q, or R, indicating reversible binding rather than covalent inactivation. Active-site titration with a tight-binding stoichiometric inactivator found 4.0 nmol of catalytic sites per milligram of protein.

Table 1. Apparent kinetic parameters from initial-rate fits

| Condition | Apparent K_m (mM) | Apparent V_max (nmol s^{-1} mg^{-1}) |
|-----------|-------------------|--------------------------------------|
| No inhibitor | 0.50 | 80 |
| Compound P (2.0 μM) | 0.50 | 40 |
| Compound Q (2.0 μM) | 1.50 | 80 |
| Compound R (2.0 μM) | 0.25 | 40 |

In a separate progress-curve experiment, 25 μg of the same enzyme protein was mixed with 0.50 mM S and no inhibitor in a 1.00 mL reaction. Product concentration was recorded as a function of time (Table 2).

Table 2. Product appearance at [S]_0 = 0.50 mM without inhibitor

| Time (s) | [Product] (μM) |
|----------|----------------|
| 0 | 0.0 |
| 10 | 9.9 |
| 20 | 19.6 |
| 30 | 29.1 |
| 60 | 56.2 |
| 120 | 102.4 |

items.stem: The paragraph that begins “The rhetorical trick is hygiene” primarily functions to

choices.text: abandon the earlier claim that volume can be a real harm, replacing it with a theory that all sanitation language is fraudulent.
explain how the social sorting described earlier can wear a public-health costume, so that preference need not justify itself as preference.
introduce a new thesis that night markets are medically dirtier than waterfront festivals.
define hygiene as the only legitimate basis for any noise rule, including brand-sponsored festivals.

items.explanation: The hygiene paragraph does not replace the opening concession that sleep and compressors matter. It supplies the rhetorical mechanism that lets unequal sorting look like sanitation: once noise is dirt, pointing replaces justifying. That mechanism binds the thermometer opening, the vitality/nuisance walk, and the identical wave-form wearing two moral uniforms. Integration of parts means seeing this paragraph as the how of the sorting claim, not as a medical finding about markets or as a withdrawal of the sleep concession. The festival/market pair is illustrative of uniforms, not a dirt ranking.

distractorRationales.A: The first paragraph insists public-health language does real work; the later trick is misuse of that language, not a denial that sleep is a good.
distractorRationales.C: The author says campaigns can speak the idiom of rats even when photographs show swept stones; the point is costume, not a dirt comparison.
distractorRationales.D: Hygiene-as-dirt is the trick being unmasked, not the author's recommended sole basis for rules; festivals in the civic-joy idiom are the matching uniform.

passage.title: Who may be loud
passage.body:
Noise ordinances are written as if they were thermometers. A number of decibels is named; a clock hour is named; a fine is attached. The language of public health does real work here: sleep is not a luxury, and a child whose window faces a compressor is not being precious. But the thermometer conceals a second instrument, which is a social sorting device. Cities do not merely suppress loudness. They decide which kinds of loudness will be classified as vitality and which as nuisance, and the decision tracks, with embarrassing regularity, the prestige of the people making the sound.

Walk a mixed street after dark and the taxonomy is audible. A licensed terrace with heaters and a playlist is "activation of the night-time economy." A storefront church whose singing lasts past the same hour is a complaint waiting to be logged. A terrace is a business; a congregation is a disturbance that happens to own a building. Street vendors packing ice and calling prices are "chaos"; a restaurant's Friday overflow onto the pavement is "vibrancy," provided the overflow has paid for a permit. The ear that writes the ordinance has already been trained to hear money as atmosphere and unpaid sound as aggression.

Defenders of the ordinances will say that the issue is volume, not culture. Sometimes it is. A speaker stack aimed at a bedroom is a harm whether the music is sacred or commercial. The author's claim is narrower and more awkward: when two sounds of similar intensity are sorted differently, the sorting is not acoustics. It is a theory of who belongs in the air. "Quiet" is then sold as a natural baseline, like clean water, when it is often an aesthetic associated with certain housing and certain hours of salaried rest. Night-shift workers returning at dawn, whose rest is real, rarely get to define the city's sonic morals. People who sleep when the ordinance writers sleep do.

None of this is a brief for unlimited noise, or for the romance of the unregulated street. A city that cannot protect sleep will punish the poorest first, because they cannot buy distance from compressors. The decent aim is not a louder city but a less hypocritical one: a city that admits that permission to be loud is a scarce good, distributed by licensing, policing, and taste, and that "quality of life" is never only a medical phrase. It is also a claim about whose life is the measure.

The rhetorical trick is hygiene. Once noise is framed as dirt, opposition to a particular sound can wear the costume of sanitation rather than of preference. Dirt, unlike preference, does not have to justify itself at a public meeting. It only has to be pointed at. That is why a campaign against a night market can speak the idiom of rats and refuse even when the photographs show swept stones, and why a campaign for a waterfront festival can speak the idiom of civic joy even when the sound spill is identical. The same wave-form, two moral uniforms.

If the argument holds, then reform is not a new app for logging complaints. It is a requirement that like sounds be given like reasons, and that exemptions be named as political choices rather than as nature. A hospital generator may deserve its exemption. So, perhaps, does a funeral that spills into a street. What cannot be defended is the pretense that the ordinance is only a meter reading. Meters do not know the difference between a hymn and a brand. Officials do, and they should have to say so.

items.stem:
Fick’s law is written V̇gas = (A / T) × D × ΔP. Three lung conditions are compared at the same ΔP and D:
Healthy: A = 70 m², T = 0.5 µm, relative rate = 100.
Emphysema: A = 35 m², T = 0.5 µm.
Fibrosis: A = 70 m², T = 1.0 µm.
What are the relative diffusion rates for emphysema and fibrosis?

choices.text: Both remain 100, because ΔP is unchanged
Emphysema 50; fibrosis 50
Emphysema 200; fibrosis 50, because thinning always accompanies emphysema
Emphysema 50; fibrosis 200, because thicker barriers conduct faster

items.explanation: Rate scales with A/T. Healthy A/T = 70 / 0.5 = 140 (in m² µm−1). Emphysema halves area at the same thickness, so A/T = 70, half the healthy value (relative 50). Fibrosis doubles thickness at the same area, A/T = 70, again half (relative 50). The stem holds T fixed in emphysema and A fixed in fibrosis, so one should not invent extra thinning or argue that thicker tissue conducts faster. Unchanged ΔP does not cancel a change in A/T.

distractorRationales.A: Fick’s law still contains A/T; holding ΔP constant isolates that geometric factor, which did change.
distractorRationales.C: The emphysema row keeps T = 0.5 µm; doubling rate would require doubling A/T, which does not occur.
distractorRationales.D: T is in the denominator, so doubling thickness halves, rather than doubles, rate.

items.stem: A toxin disrupts tight junctions in an otherwise intact intestinal epithelium. The most immediate functional consequence is:

choices.text: conversion of apical microvilli into motile cilia
collapse of every mitochondrion in the sheet
extraction of all membrane cholesterol
increased paracellular flux of solutes between lumen and basolateral space

items.explanation: Tight junctions (zonula occludens) seal the paracellular route and help maintain apical-basolateral polarity of the barrier. When they open, solutes and water can leak between cells rather than being forced through transcellular transporters. Microvilli, mitochondria, and cholesterol content are not the junction's direct structural products, so they are not the immediate readout of a tight-junction toxin.

distractorRationales.A: Microvilli are actin-supported apical specializations. Tight-junction loss does not transdifferentiate them into axonemal cilia.
distractorRationales.B: Mitochondria are intracellular organelles; a junctional toxin does not globally collapse them as its primary action.
distractorRationales.C: Cholesterol is a bilayer lipid. Junction disruption is a protein-complex event, not a bulk delipidation.

items.stem: A reversible inhibitor is added to a Michaelis–Menten enzyme. Double-reciprocal plots with and without inhibitor intersect on the ordinate; the apparent Km increases while Vmax is unchanged. Which mechanistic description fits these data?

choices.text: Uncompetitive inhibition in which inhibitor binds only the ES complex
Pure noncompetitive inhibition in which inhibitor binds E and ES with equal affinity
Irreversible active-site titration that permanently lowers the concentration of functional enzyme
Competitive inhibition in which inhibitor and substrate compete for free enzyme

items.explanation: Competitive inhibitors bind free enzyme in a manner that overlaps substrate binding, so they can be overcome by high [S]: Vmax is unchanged and apparent Km rises. On a Lineweaver–Burk plot that pattern is a shared y-intercept (1/Vmax) and a larger x-intercept magnitude. Uncompetitive inhibition lowers both Km and Vmax and gives parallel lines. Pure noncompetitive inhibition lowers Vmax without changing Km (shared x-intercept). Irreversible inactivation lowers Vmax because active enzyme concentration falls and is not reversed by substrate in the same way. The ordinate intersection with higher Km is the competitive signature.

distractorRationales.A: Uncompetitive lines are parallel; both apparent Km and Vmax decrease, unlike these plots.
distractorRationales.B: Noncompetitive inhibition decreases Vmax; the y-intercept would increase, not stay fixed.
distractorRationales.C: Irreversible loss of enzyme molecules reduces Vmax; substrate cannot restore the original maximum velocity.

items.stem: Comparing Civic Daily and Harbour Post on this table, the most defensible contrast is

choices.text: Civic Daily’s speech-verbs cluster in challenge (claimed, insisted); Harbour Post’s cluster in concession (admitted).
Harbour Post did not use “said.”
they are identical except for “revealed.”
Civic Daily is overseas and Harbour Post is not.

items.explanation: Civic Daily: claimed 8, insisted 4, said only 3. Harbour Post: admitted 6, said 7, claimed 1. That is a contrast in stance verbs over one announcement. B is false (said = 7). C is false. D is not in the data. Quote-set or table comparison still needs a contrast the numbers license, not extra biography.

distractorRationales.B: Harbour Post has seven “said.”
distractorRationales.C: Several columns differ, not only revealed (both 0).
distractorRationales.D: Locations are not given.

passage.title: Table: Verbs in the morning
passage.body:
A media researcher counts finite verbs in the first paragraphs of four papers on the same Monday, all covering the same ministry announcement.

Paper | “said” | “claimed” | “admitted” | “revealed” | “insisted” | Other verbs of speaking
North Evening | 12 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 2
Civic Daily | 3 | 8 | 1 | 0 | 4 | 1
Harbour Post | 7 | 1 | 6 | 0 | 0 | 3
The Signal | 2 | 2 | 0 | 9 | 1 | 2

Caption under the table, written by the researcher: “Speaking is never only speaking. The ministry released one statement. The city woke in four grammars.”

A talkback host that night: “This is just synonyms. Nobody is doing politics with a verb chart. Grow up.”

items.stem: A blastomere from the prospective neural plate of an early gastrula is transplanted into ventral epidermis of a same-stage host and differentiates as epidermis. The equivalent cell taken from a late neurula and transplanted ventrally still forms neural tissue. These results show that:

choices.text: Determination has occurred by the later stage, so fate is no longer redirected by the new environment
Totipotency increases as development proceeds, which is why the older transplant ignores host cues
Induction never occurs, because the early transplant could change fate
The late transplant undergoes apoptosis and the host then makes a ghost neural tube

items.explanation: Specification and determination are operationally defined by transplantation. An undetermined cell is competent to follow inductive cues in a new location (here, ventral epidermis). Once determined, the cell's developmental commitment is stable and it differentiates according to its original identity (neural) even in a foreign environment. That is a restriction of potency over time, not an increase in totipotency. The early result actually demonstrates that induction/environment can still assign fate. The assay scores differentiated neural tissue from the graft, not host apoptosis artifacts.

distractorRationales.B: Potency generally decreases; totipotency does not rise after gastrulation.
distractorRationales.C: The early cell's change of fate is evidence that inductive environment still acts.
distractorRationales.D: The experiment's point is autonomous neural differentiation of the late graft, not cell death.

items.stem: A peptide (amide) C–N bond does not rotate freely at room temperature, so the six atoms of the amide unit lie in a plane. Which hybridization statement best explains that restricted rotation?

choices.text: The carbonyl carbon is sp3 and the nitrogen is sp3, producing a purely sigma C–N bond that happens to be short.
Only hydrogen bonding between N–H and C=O, not orbital hybridization, can prevent C–N rotation.
The carbonyl carbon is sp and the nitrogen is unhybridized, producing a linear C–N–H array.
Resonance donation from nitrogen into the carbonyl makes both the carbonyl carbon and the amide nitrogen sp2, giving the C–N linkage partial double-bond character.

items.explanation: The amide resonance contributor that places a lone pair from nitrogen into the C=O π* orbital gives a C=N double-bond picture with charge-separated O− and N+. Both the carbonyl carbon and the nitrogen therefore have three electron domains and are treated as sp2, and the C–N bond order is between 1 and 2. Partial double-bond character creates a substantial rotational barrier, which is why the peptide unit is planar. Hydrogen bonding can stabilize secondary structure, but it is not required to explain the amide rotational barrier in a simple peptide bond.

distractorRationales.A: An sp3–sp3 single bond would rotate freely and would not force planarity of the six amide atoms.
distractorRationales.B: Hydrogen bonding is important in proteins but is not the origin of the amide C–N rotational barrier; isolated amides are still planar.
distractorRationales.C: An sp carbonyl carbon would be linear (as in ketene or CO2), which does not match the trigonal planar amide carbon.

items.stem: Observers read a briefly flashed, degraded clinic note in which several letters are ink-smudged. They still report the intended words when the sentence is medically plausible, but they misread the same marks in a scrambled letter string. Richard Gregory’s constructivist account treats this as which kind of processing?

choices.text: Pure bottom-up feature detection, because Hubel and Wiesel cells finish the job before knowledge acts
Top-down processing, in which stored knowledge and context generate perceptual hypotheses that disambiguate incomplete sensory data
Gibsonian direct pickup of optic-array invariants, which needs no hypothesis testing
Weber scaling of ink density, which uniquely determines each letter

items.explanation: Gregory argued that perception is hypothesis-testing: incomplete retinal data are interpreted using memory and context (top-down, constructivist). Sentence meaning helping smudged letters is that influence. Strict bottom-up feature detection would not improve once the same marks sit in a meaningful sentence. Gibson’s ecological theory emphasizes direct invariants and downplays such inference. Weber’s law scales intensity differences; it does not read words.

distractorRationales.A: Context changing the percept of identical marks is the signature that bottom-up feature maps are not sufficient.
distractorRationales.C: Gibsonian direct perception denies the need for knowledge-driven hypotheses that the stem demonstrates.
distractorRationales.D: Weber fractions do not explain lexical restoration of smudged letters.

items.stem: A 2 kg point mass sits at x = 0 and a 6 kg point mass sits at x = 4 m, both on the x-axis and otherwise isolated. The x-coordinate of the system's center of mass is:

choices.text: 1 m
2 m
3 m
4 m

items.explanation: The center of mass of two point masses is the mass-weighted average x_cm = (m1 x1 + m2 x2) / (m1 + m2). Substituting gives (2 kg)(0) + (6 kg)(4 m) all over 8 kg, which is 24/8 = 3 m. The center of mass therefore lies closer to the heavier 6 kg mass than to the 2 kg mass, as expected, but it is not at the 6 kg mass itself. Equal-mass averaging would put it at the geometric midpoint 2 m, which does not apply here.

distractorRationales.A: This inverts the mass weighting or uses (2/8)*4 m. The heavier mass should pull x_cm toward 4 m, not toward 0.
distractorRationales.B: This is the geometric midpoint, correct only if the two masses were equal. The 6 kg mass outweighs the 2 kg mass three to one.
distractorRationales.D: The center of mass coincides with a mass only if the other mass is zero or is located at the same point. The 2 kg mass still shifts x_cm left of 4 m.

items.stem:
Standard enthalpies of formation (kJ mol−1): CH4(g) −75; CO2(g) −394; H2O(l) −286; O2(g) 0. For CH4 + 2 O2 → CO2 + 2 H2O(l), ΔH = Σ ΔHf(products) − Σ ΔHf(reactants).
What is ΔH?

choices.text: −891 kJ mol−1
−966 kJ mol−1 (forgetting to subtract ΔHf of CH4)
+891 kJ mol−1
−75 kJ mol−1, the formation enthalpy of methane

items.explanation: Products: −394 + 2(−286) = −394 − 572 = −966 kJ. Reactants: −75 + 2(0) = −75 kJ. ΔH = −966 − (−75) = −891 kJ mol−1. Methane combustion is strongly exothermic, matching the negative sign. Dropping the methane term leaves −966, which is only the product sum. The formation enthalpy −75 kJ is the methane building reaction from C and H2, not this combustion.

distractorRationales.B: Σ ΔHf(products) is −966 kJ; Hess’s law still subtracts ΔHf of CH4 (−75).
distractorRationales.C: Heat is released (combustion), so ΔH is negative.
