distractorRationales.D: −75 kJ mol−1 is ΔHf of methane, not ΔH of burning methane in oxygen.

items.stem: A receiving country finds that first-generation immigrant women have higher total fertility than native-born women, but by the second generation TFR has largely converged. Working-age in-migration also lowers the aged-dependency ratio for a decade. Which statement is best?

choices.text: Migration cannot affect a population’s age structure, only its language
Fertility, mortality, and migration jointly determine demographic structure; immigrant fertility often assimilates across generations, while in-migration can temporarily rejuvenate the age pyramid
Only catastrophes can change TFR, so the first-generation elevation is measurement error
Stage 1 populations are the only ones that migrate, so the second generation cannot exist

items.explanation: The demographic equation is births, deaths, and net migration. Migrants are often concentrated in working ages, which lowers aged dependency in the short run. Fertility of immigrant cohorts frequently moves toward the host-country pattern in subsequent generations, a standard finding in demographic structure. Migration therefore belongs beside fertility and mortality as a determinant of age composition. Catastrophes are not the only TFR shifter, and the existence of a second generation shows that migration is not confined to hypothetical stage-1 isolates.

distractorRationales.A: Age-selective in-migration is a classic way to change the pyramid; language change is a separate acculturation issue.
distractorRationales.C: Fertility responds to many social factors, including migration and assimilation, not only disasters.
distractorRationales.D: People migrate from and into countries at every transition stage; children of immigrants are a normal cohort.

items.stem: Which register best matches Task A, and which mismatch is most damaging?

choices.text: Match: controlled public argument, concrete cases, no fake intimacy. Damaging mismatch: “lol queues r dumb, ministers r trash, subscribe for more takes.”
Match: baby-talk. Damaging mismatch: any complete sentence.
Match: a private love letter to the marker. Damaging mismatch: mentioning a public institution.
Match: as many Latinate abstractions as possible with no case. Damaging mismatch: a specified clinic.

items.explanation: Register is fitness of language to task. Task A is a civic argument for an educated stranger: serious without being stuffed, concrete without being chatty. A blog-rant with lol and subscribe is the wrong public. Baby-talk, love letters to markers, and abstraction-only fog are also mismatches, but the question’s best pair is the rant versus controlled argument. A specified clinic is appropriate, not a mismatch. The damaging pattern in real scripts is often online voice leaking into a paper that is still a formal task. A names that leak. Matching register is not the same as being pompous.

distractorRationales.B: Complete sentences are not a mismatch; baby-talk would be.
distractorRationales.C: A love letter is the wrong intimacy; public institutions are Task A’s natural furniture.
distractorRationales.D: Abstraction without a case is a register failure of emptiness, and a clinic is a virtue here, not a vice.

items.stem: A temperature-sensitive E. coli ligA mutant is shifted to 42 °C during rapid growth. After a brief 3H-thymidine pulse, alkaline sucrose-gradient centrifugation places the radioactivity in ~1000–2000 nucleotide pieces rather than in chromosomal-length DNA. Return to 30 °C chases the label into high-molecular-weight DNA. Which interpretation is most accurate?

choices.text: Lagging-strand Okazaki fragments are synthesized but cannot be sealed at 42 °C; alkaline denaturation reveals the nicks that ligase would otherwise close.
Helicase denatures at 42 °C, so both strands are copied only as abortive RNA primers that ligase later joins into chromosomal DNA.
DNA polymerase III loses 5′→3′ polymerase activity at 42 °C, leaving only initiator RNAs that become 1000-nucleotide DNA after the downshift.
DNA gyrase cannot decatenate daughters at 42 °C, mechanically shearing chromosomes into gene-sized pieces independently of ligation.

items.explanation: DNA ligase seals nicks after polymerase I has removed RNA primers and filled Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand. At the nonpermissive temperature those fragments remain unjoined. Alkaline sucrose gradients denature duplexes, converting nicked molecules into single strands whose length matches bacterial Okazaki pieces. Restoring ligase activity at 30 °C allows sealing and a chase into chromosomal DNA. Helicase failure, loss of Pol III catalytic activity, or a decatenation defect would not produce this reversible pile-up of discrete, pulse-labeled fragments of Okazaki length.

distractorRationales.B: Helicase failure would halt fork progression rather than generate a reversible pool of DNA-length Okazaki pieces that chase after ligase is restored.
distractorRationales.C: The pulse labels DNA, not RNA primers, and the mutation is in ligase, not the Pol III polymerase site.
distractorRationales.D: Decatenation acts on fully replicated circles; it does not create a pulse-labeled 1–2 kb nascent-DNA ladder that chases when ligase is restored.

items.stem: Adult hemoglobin (α2β2) binds 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate in a central cavity lined by cationic residues including βHis143. Fetal hemoglobin (α2γ2) has serine at the analogous γ position and binds 2,3-BPG more weakly. What is the physiological consequence of that binding difference?

choices.text: Fetal Hb has higher O2 affinity than adult Hb at the same 2,3-BPG concentration, favoring O2 transfer from maternal to fetal blood
Fetal Hb has lower O2 affinity, so the fetus unloads oxygen into maternal blood
2,3-BPG is oxidized by fetal heme to 3-phosphoglycerate, a glycolytic intermediate, so HbF is an enzyme
Serine covalently phosphorylates 2,3-BPG, irreversibly locking fetal Hb in the T state

items.explanation: 2,3-BPG is a polyanion that binds deoxyhemoglobin and stabilizes the low-affinity T state, shifting the O2 isotherm to the right. Weaker binding to HbF therefore leaves fetal hemoglobin closer to the high-affinity R-like curve of stripped Hb. At a shared PO2 in the placenta, maternal HbA (more 2,3-BPG-stabilized) unloads oxygen that HbF can bind. This is a reversible allosteric binding function, not catalysis of 2,3-BPG oxidation or a covalent phosphorylation of the effector by serine.

distractorRationales.B: Weaker 2,3-BPG binding raises, rather than lowers, O2 affinity. Transfer is from mother to fetus, not the reverse.
distractorRationales.C: Hemoglobin’s job here is reversible O2 transport modulated by a ligand. It does not metabolize 2,3-BPG to 3-phosphoglycerate as its primary function.
distractorRationales.D: Serine143 is a substitution that removes a cation; it does not phosphorylate 2,3-BPG or covalently lock the T state.

items.stem:
Sulfuryl chloride decomposes: SO2Cl2(g) ⇌ SO2(g) + Cl2(g), with Kp = 0.30 atm at a stated T and Kp = (P_SO2 P_Cl2) / P_SO2Cl2. A mixture in a rigid bulb has the partial pressures below.

Gas | Partial pressure (atm)
SO2Cl2 | 0.50
SO2 | 0.20
Cl2 | 0.20

What is Qp, and which net process occurs at this T?

choices.text: Qp = 0.080, which is less than Kp, so SO2Cl2 decomposes net.
Qp = 0.080, which is less than Kp, so SO2 and Cl2 combine net.
Qp = 0.80, which is greater than Kp, so SO2Cl2 decomposes net.
Qp = 0.30 = Kp, so the mixture is already at equilibrium.

items.explanation: Qp uses the same expression as Kp with the instantaneous partial pressures: Qp = (0.20 × 0.20) / 0.50 = 0.040 / 0.50 = 0.080. Because Qp < Kp, the numerator must increase relative to the denominator, which means net decomposition of SO2Cl2. The comparison is made at the given T, so Kp is fixed at 0.30 atm. Adding the partial pressures of the products instead of multiplying them, or treating the mixture as if Qp automatically equals Kp, produces the distractor values.

distractorRationales.B: Qp is 0.080, but Qp < Kp implies the forward (decomposition) direction, not combination of the products.
distractorRationales.C: Qp = 0.80 comes from adding the product pressures (0.20 + 0.20) / 0.50. Partial pressures are multiplied in Kp, and 0.80 would actually be greater than Kp, which is the wrong comparison as well as the wrong arithmetic.
distractorRationales.D: Equality of Qp and Kp would require (P_SO2 P_Cl2) / P_SO2Cl2 = 0.30. The table gives 0.080, so the system is not at equilibrium.

items.stem: For the weak acid–strong base titration above, the steep jump at equivalence is centered near pH 8.7. Which indicator is appropriate?

choices.text: Methyl orange (color change ≈ pH 3.1–4.4)
Bromophenol blue (color change ≈ pH 3.0–4.6)
Phenolphthalein (color change ≈ pH 8.2–10.0)
An indicator is unnecessary because the equivalence pH is 7.0 and the eye can detect neutrality.

items.explanation: An indicator is a weak acid whose color change interval should overlap the steep portion of the titration curve. For acetic acid/NaOH that jump lies in the alkaline region around pH 8–10, which matches phenolphthalein’s window. Methyl orange and bromophenol blue change in the acidic range, well before equivalence, so they would signal an endpoint after only partial neutralization (near the buffer region). The equivalence pH is not 7, and visual “neutrality” is not a substitute for an indicator whose pKa matches the jump.

distractorRationales.A: Methyl orange would change color in the acetic acid buffer region, far before the true equivalence point.
distractorRationales.B: Bromophenol blue likewise changes while substantial HA remains; it is used for some strong-acid endpoints, not this weak-acid case.
distractorRationales.D: Equivalence is basic, not pH 7, and unassisted vision cannot locate a specific pH.

items.stem: In the 1H NMR spectrum of bromoethane (CH3CH2Br), the signal for the CH3 group is a:

choices.text: singlet, because methyl protons do not couple
doublet, because the methyl group has one neighboring carbon
triplet, because the methyl protons have two equivalent neighbors on the CH2Br carbon (n+1 rule)
quartet, because there are four hydrogens in the ethyl fragment

items.explanation: Vicinal 1H–1H coupling follows the n+1 rule for first-order spectra: a proton (or equivalent set) with n equivalent neighbors appears as n+1 lines. The CH3 protons of bromoethane have two equivalent neighbors on the methylene carbon, so the methyl signal is a triplet (2+1). The CH2Br protons have three methyl neighbors and appear as a quartet; that pattern belongs to the downfield methylene, not the methyl. Coupling is to neighboring hydrogens, not to 'number of carbons' or the molecule's total hydrogen count. Methyl protons do couple when an adjacent CH2 is present.

distractorRationales.A: Methyl singlets occur when there are no neighboring hydrogens (for example a tert-butyl or an isolated methoxy). Adjacent CH2Br protons split the CH3 of bromoethane.
distractorRationales.B: The n in n+1 is the number of equivalent neighboring hydrogens, not the number of neighboring carbons. One adjacent carbon that bears two hydrogens gives a triplet, not a doublet.
distractorRationales.D: A quartet is the CH2Br resonance (three methyl neighbors). Total hydrogen count in the ethyl group is not what the n+1 rule uses.

items.stem: Two groups run in place for 60 seconds so that heart rate is equally elevated, then immediately watch either a comedy clip or a horror clip. Comedy viewers report amusement; horror viewers report fear, despite matched residual arousal. Which theory most cleanly accounts for the divergence?

choices.text: James–Lange theory, because equal heart rate must produce identical feelings
Cannon–Bard theory, because running already produced a thalamic emotion, so the films cannot change reports
Schachter–Singer two-factor theory: comparable residual arousal is labeled using the clip’s context
Selye’s general adaptation syndrome: amusement is the alarm stage and fear is the exhaustion stage

items.explanation: When residual arousal is experimentally equated, James–Lange reasoning that distinct feelings require distinct bodily signatures has little to work with. Two-factor theory predicts that the same leftover sympathetic activation will be experienced as different emotions once it is interpreted against different situational cues—the comedy versus horror clip. Cannon–Bard theory does not claim that a prior bout of running freezes later emotional quality so that films are irrelevant. GAS stages describe a time course of stress physiology, not a mapping of amusement onto alarm and fear onto exhaustion.

distractorRationales.A: Equal heart rate with unequal reports is a problem for a strictly visceral James–Lange account, not support for it.
distractorRationales.B: Cannon–Bard allows later stimuli to drive new central emotional events; it does not predict that films are powerless after exercise.
distractorRationales.D: GAS is a stress-response sequence, not a theory that assigns film genres to alarm versus exhaustion.

items.stem: A sample contains 80 g of a pure radioisotope whose half-life is 2 days. The mass of that isotope remaining after 6 days is:

choices.text: 8 g

items.explanation: Each half-life halves the remaining quantity of the parent isotope. Six days is 6/2 = 3 half-lives, so the remaining mass is 80 × (1/2)^3 = 80 × 1/8 = 10 g. Daughter nuclides may accumulate, but the question asks for the mass of the original isotope, which follows the exponential decay law. One half-life would leave 40 g and two would leave 20 g; stopping at those counts undercounts the elapsed half-lives. Linear subtraction (for example 80 − 10 × 6) is not how half-life works.

distractorRationales.B: This is two half-lives (80 → 40 → 20). Six days at 2 days per half-life is three halvings, not two.
distractorRationales.C: This is a single half-life (2 days), not 6 days. Remaining parent after one t1/2 is 40 g; after three it is 10 g.
distractorRationales.D: This divides 80 by 10 rather than by 2 three times. Half-life is a factor of 1/2 per interval, which is 1/8 overall, not 1/10.

items.stem: Spouses who have been primary caregivers for a partner with dementia for more than two years, compared with age-matched non-caregivers, show slower punch-biopsy wound healing, lower antibody titers after vaccination, and higher evening cortisol. Which interpretation is most consistent with chronic-stress physiology?

choices.text: Repeated acute sympathetic bursts that enhance vaccine responses for months
Prolonged HPA activation associated with impaired immune function, as in exhaustion or allostatic overload
Secondary appraisal of the wound as a challenge, which by itself slows collagen deposition
Emotion-focused humor that directly lyses lymphocytes

items.explanation: Sustained caregiving is a chronic stressor that keeps HPA output elevated. Glucocorticoids in that range are immunosuppressive: they can slow wound healing and blunt vaccine titers, matching an exhaustion or allostatic-overload picture rather than a short-lived adaptive burst. Acute sympathetic activation can transiently mobilize innate immunity, but it does not explain months of poorer antibody responses. Appraisal of a biopsy as a “challenge” is not a mechanism that replaces endocrine–immune pathways. Humor is an emotion-focused strategy, not a direct cytolytic signal.

distractorRationales.A: Enhanced, durable vaccine responses are the opposite of the lower titers described under chronic load.
distractorRationales.C: Challenge appraisal does not by itself dictate collagen kinetics; the stem’s cortisol and immune measures point to HPA–immune coupling.
distractorRationales.D: No evidence in the stem links humor to lymphocyte lysis; that is not a standard coping mechanism.

items.stem:
A one-step bacteriophage growth experiment reports plaque-forming units (PFU) per millilitre after a synchronous infection of 10³ cells mL−1:

Time (min) | extracellular PFU | intracellular PFU (after chloroform)
0 | 10 | 10³
10 | 8 | 10³
20 | 6 | 10³
30 | 1.0 × 10⁵ | 1.0 × 10⁵
40 | 1.0 × 10⁵ | 1.0 × 10⁵

Which statement is supported?

choices.text: Burst size is 10⁵ because that is the final PFU
Phage never enter an intracellular phase, because extracellular PFU is never zero
The latent period is 10 min, equal to the first listed time point after zero
The eclipse lasts at least 20 min with a burst size of about 100 phage per cell, and lysis has occurred by 30 min

items.explanation: During 0–20 min almost no infectious phage are outside cells (PFU ~10), while chloroform-released intracellular counts stay at the 10³ infected-cell input: new virions are not yet assembled (eclipse). At 30 min both extra- and intracellular PFU jump to 10⁵, so lysis has released a burst of 10⁵/10³ = 100 phage per cell. Residual extracellular PFU of 6–10 is unadsorbed inoculum, not evidence that infection failed. The latent period ends at the rise (30 min), not at the arbitrary 10 min row.

distractorRationales.A: 10⁵ is the population burst, not the per-cell burst size; dividing by 10³ infected cells gives 100.
distractorRationales.B: Intracellular PFU of 10³ during eclipse shows phage are inside cells; extracellular counts are leftover free virions.
distractorRationales.C: Infectious centres do not increase at 10 min; the latent period extends until the 30 min jump.
